import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// EyebrowProps configures a small uppercase overline label rendered above a
// title. Eyebrows read as status, not decoration: use them to anchor the eye
// before a headline (e.g. "DNS block · 12:47:03" above a page title).
type EyebrowProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Text string
}

// DefaultEyebrowProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultEyebrowProps() EyebrowProps {
	return EyebrowProps{}
}

// Eyebrow renders a small monospace uppercase overline label. Rendered
// neutral gray by default; pass an accent color via BaseProps.Class
// (e.g. Class: "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400") to make it the tonal
// signal of a page family. Renders nothing when Text is empty.
//
//	@display.Eyebrow(display.EyebrowProps{Text: "Deploy #142 · production"})
templ Eyebrow(props EyebrowProps) {
	if props.Text != "" {
		<p
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("font-mono text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.18em] text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			{ props.Text }
		</p>
	}
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// GridCols is a typed enum for the responsive column count of a Grid. Unknown
// values fall back to GridCols3 (graceful degradation — never panic).
type GridCols string

const (
	GridCols1 GridCols = "1"
	GridCols2 GridCols = "2"
	GridCols3 GridCols = "3"
	GridCols4 GridCols = "4"
	GridCols5 GridCols = "5"
	GridCols6 GridCols = "6"
	// GridColsAutoFit uses CSS auto-fit + minmax() instead of fixed breakpoints.
	// The grid responds to container width, not viewport. Requires MinColWidth.
	GridColsAutoFit GridCols = "auto-fit"
	// GridColsDefault is the canonical default (3 columns at the lg breakpoint).
	GridColsDefault GridCols = GridCols3
)

// GridGap is a typed enum for the gap spacing between grid items.
// Unknown values fall back to GridGapMD (graceful degradation — never panic).
type GridGap string

const (
	GridGapSM GridGap = "sm" // gap-2 (0.5rem)
	GridGapMD GridGap = "md" // gap-4 (1rem) — default
	GridGapLG GridGap = "lg" // gap-6 (1.5rem)
	GridGapXL GridGap = "xl" // gap-8 (2rem)
	// GridGapDefault is the canonical default.
	GridGapDefault GridGap = GridGapMD
)

// gridGapLookup maps each GridGap value to its Tailwind gap utility class.
var gridGapLookup = map[GridGap]string{
	GridGapSM: "gap-2",
	GridGapMD: "gap-4",
	GridGapLG: "gap-6",
	GridGapXL: "gap-8",
}

func gridGapClass(gap GridGap) string {
	return utils.Lookup(gridGapLookup, gap, gridGapLookup[GridGapDefault])
}

// gridColsLookup maps each GridCols value to the responsive Tailwind classes
// that stack on mobile and expand at sm/lg breakpoints. This is a pure class
// lookup, so the map+fallback pattern applies.
var gridColsLookup = map[GridCols]string{
	GridCols1: "grid grid-cols-1",
	GridCols2: "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2",
	GridCols3: "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3",
	GridCols4: "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4",
	GridCols5: "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4 xl:grid-cols-5",
	GridCols6: "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-6",
}

// gridColsContainerLookup maps each GridCols value to container-query-based
// Tailwind classes (@sm:, @lg:) that respond to the parent container's width
// instead of the browser viewport. Used when ContainerAware is true.
var gridColsContainerLookup = map[GridCols]string{
	GridCols1: "grid grid-cols-1",
	GridCols2: "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2",
	GridCols3: "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2 @lg:grid-cols-3",
	GridCols4: "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2 @md:grid-cols-3 @lg:grid-cols-4",
	GridCols5: "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2 @md:grid-cols-3 @lg:grid-cols-4 @xl:grid-cols-5",
	GridCols6: "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2 @lg:grid-cols-3 @xl:grid-cols-6",
}

// gridClass returns the responsive Tailwind class string for a column count,
// falling back to GridColsDefault for unknown values.
func gridClass(cols GridCols) string {
	return utils.Lookup(gridColsLookup, cols, gridColsLookup[GridColsDefault])
}

// gridAutoFitClass returns the auto-fit/minmax template class. The minimum
// column width is NOT concatenated into the class: a runtime-composed
// arbitrary value is invisible to Tailwind's source scanner, so the utility
// is never generated and every auto-fit grid silently collapses to a single
// column. The class stays a complete literal and reads the width from the
// --tc-grid-min custom property that gridAutoFitStyle sets.
func gridAutoFitClass() string {
	return "grid [grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(var(--tc-grid-min),1fr))]"
}

// gridAutoFitStyle returns the inline custom-property declaration carrying the
// minimum column width for an auto-fit grid, defaulting to 240px. It is the
// runtime half of gridAutoFitClass (documented inline-style exemption, same
// shape as the chart and heatmap width/height properties).
func gridAutoFitStyle(minColWidth string) string {
	if minColWidth == "" {
		minColWidth = "240px"
	}

	return "--tc-grid-min:" + minColWidth
}

// gridContainerClass returns the container-query-based Tailwind class string
// for a column count, falling back to GridColsDefault for unknown values.
func gridContainerClass(cols GridCols) string {
	return utils.Lookup(gridColsContainerLookup, cols, gridColsContainerLookup[GridColsDefault])
}

// GridProps configures a responsive grid layout. Use Grid to lay out cards,
// stat cards, or any repeating content with consistent responsive breakpoints
// without repeating the long `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3`
// utility string on every page.
//
// Children require a templ render context: Grid receives its cells through
// the templ children slot, so rendering the component directly into a plain
// writer (`Component.Render(ctx, &buf)` from Go, outside a templ tree) emits
// the grid shell with EMPTY cells — valid HTML, silently missing content.
// Pass the items through a templ template (even a trivial one that ranges
// over a slice) so the children context exists. The same limitation applies
// to every children-carrying component in this library (Card's slots,
// Modal/Drawer content, Accordion items with nested markup, …).
type GridProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Cols controls the responsive column count. Defaults to GridCols3 when
	// empty or unknown.
	Cols GridCols
	// Gap controls the spacing between grid items. Defaults to GridGapMD (gap-4).
	Gap GridGap
	// ContainerAware, when true, renders the grid inside an @container
	// wrapper so column counts respond to the container's width instead of
	// the browser viewport. Opt-in: the struct-literal zero value is
	// viewport-based; DefaultGridProps() sets it true. Set it explicitly
	// (true or false) whenever a bare GridProps{...} literal is used.
	ContainerAware bool
	// MinColWidth sets the minimum column width for auto-fit grids. Used only
	// when Cols is GridColsAutoFit. Include units ("190px", "12rem"); empty
	// means 240px. The value travels as the --tc-grid-min custom property so
	// the emitted class stays a literal Tailwind can see — never hand-compose
	// an arbitrary class from a prop, the scanner will not generate it.
	// Ignored for fixed column counts. When Cols is GridColsAutoFit,
	// ContainerAware is ignored (auto-fit already responds to container
	// width via CSS minmax).
	MinColWidth string
}

// DefaultGridProps returns sensible defaults (GridCols3).
func DefaultGridProps() GridProps {
	return GridProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Cols:           GridColsDefault,
		ContainerAware: true,
	}
}

// Grid renders a responsive grid container that stacks on mobile and expands
// at sm/lg breakpoints. Pass grid items as children.
//
//	@display.Grid(display.GridProps{Cols: display.GridCols3}) {
//	   for _, u := range users {
//	     @display.Card(display.CardProps{Title: u.Name}) { <p>{ u.Email }</p> }
//	   }
//	}
//
// For container-query-based responsiveness (grid adapts to its parent container,
// not the viewport):
//
//	@display.Grid(display.GridProps{Cols: display.GridCols3, ContainerAware: true}) {
//	   // items
//	}
//
// HYBRID RENDERING CAVEAT (strings.Builder path): Grid is a children-slot
// component. When a component is rendered OUTSIDE a templ file — e.g. a
// hybrid renderer calling component.Render(ctx, w) straight into a
// strings.Builder — the { children... } slot renders EMPTY: templ only
// captures children when the component is invoked from another templ
// template. Escape hatch: pass children programmatically via
// templ.WithChildren(ctx, child) before Render (pinned by
// TestGridHybridChildrenViaWithChildren). Details:
// docs/recipes/hybrid-strings-builder-rendering.md.
templ Grid(props GridProps) {
	{{
		cols := props.Cols
		if cols == "" {
			cols = GridColsDefault
		}
		gap := gridGapClass(props.Gap)
		baseGrid := gridClass(cols)
		gridStyle := ""
		if cols == GridColsAutoFit {
			baseGrid = gridAutoFitClass()
			gridStyle = gridAutoFitStyle(props.MinColWidth)
		} else if props.ContainerAware {
			baseGrid = gridContainerClass(cols)
		}
		gridClasses := utils.Class(baseGrid, gap, props.Class)
	}}
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@gridInner(props, gridClasses, gridStyle) {
				{ children... }
			}
		</div>
	} else {
		@gridInner(props, gridClasses, gridStyle) {
			{ children... }
		}
	}
}

// gridInner renders the grid element itself, shared by the container-query and
// viewport layouts so the attribute contract (id, class, runtime style, aria
// label, consumer attrs, children) cannot drift between them.
templ gridInner(props GridProps, gridClasses, gridStyle string) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ gridClasses }
		if gridStyle != "" {
			style={ gridStyle }
		}
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ children... }
	</div>
}
package display

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// Heatmap renders a CSS-based grid heatmap — no JavaScript, no SVG.
// Each cell's background opacity reflects its value relative to the maximum.
// The heatmap is responsive, dark-mode aware, and uses native table semantics
// for accessibility.
//
//	@display.Heatmap(display.HeatmapProps{
//	   Rows: []display.HeatmapRow{
//	       {Label: "Mon", Cells: []display.HeatmapCell{
//	           {Value: 5}, {Value: 12}, {Value: 0}, {Value: 8},
//	       }},
//	       {Label: "Tue", Cells: []display.HeatmapCell{
//	           {Value: 3}, {Value: 20}, {Value: 7}, {Value: 2},
//	       }},
//	   },
//	   ColumnLabels: []string{"00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00"},
//	   HighlightPeak: true,
//	})
templ Heatmap(props HeatmapProps) {
	{{
		rows := props.Rows
		colorVar := props.ColorVar
		if colorVar == "" {
			colorVar = defaultHeatmapColorVar
		}
		cellSize := props.CellSize
		if cellSize == "" {
			cellSize = defaultHeatmapCellSize
		}
		emptyMsg := props.EmptyMessage
		if emptyMsg == "" {
			emptyMsg = defaultEmptyMsg
		}
		valueFmt := props.ValueFormat
		if valueFmt == nil {
			valueFmt = func(v float64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f", v) }
		}
		maxVal := heatmapMax(rows, props.Max)
		peakRow, peakCol := -1, -1
		if props.HighlightPeak {
			peakRow, peakCol = heatmapPeakLocation(rows)
		}
	}}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		<p
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		>{ emptyMsg }</p>
	} else {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("overflow-x-auto", props.Class) }
		>
			<table
				class="min-w-full border-collapse text-xs"
				aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, heatmapFallbackName) }
			>
				if len(props.ColumnLabels) > 0 {
					<thead>
						<tr>
							<th class="px-2 py-1"></th>
							for _, colLabel := range props.ColumnLabels {
								<th class="px-1 py-1 text-center font-medium text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
									{ colLabel }
								</th>
							}
						</tr>
					</thead>
				}
				<tbody>
					for ri, row := range rows {
						<tr>
							<td class="whitespace-nowrap px-2 py-1 text-end font-medium text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300">
								{ row.Label }
							</td>
							for ci, cell := range row.Cells {
								if cell.Value > 0 {
									if ri == peakRow && ci == peakCol {
										<td
											class={ utils.Class("px-1 py-1 text-center tabular-nums ring-2 ring-[var(--ds-brand)] ring-offset-1", cellSize) }
											style={ heatmapCellBackground(cell.Value, maxVal, colorVar) }
											title={ cell.Label }
										>
											if props.ShowValues {
												{ valueFmt(cell.Value) }
											}
										</td>
									} else if cell.Href != "" {
										<td class="px-1 py-1 text-center">
											<a
												href={ templ.SafeURL(cell.Href) }
												class={ utils.Class("block rounded", cellSize) }
												style={ heatmapCellBackground(cell.Value, maxVal, colorVar) }
												title={ cell.Label }
											></a>
										</td>
									} else {
										<td
											class={ utils.Class("px-1 py-1 text-center tabular-nums", cellSize) }
											style={ heatmapCellBackground(cell.Value, maxVal, colorVar) }
											title={ cell.Label }
										>
											if props.ShowValues {
												{ valueFmt(cell.Value) }
											}
										</td>
									}
								} else {
									<td class="px-1 py-1 text-center text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-700" title={ cell.Label }>
										&middot;
									</td>
								}
							}
						</tr>
					}
				</tbody>
			</table>
		</div>
	}
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for hover card position classes
var hoverCardPositionMap = map[Position]string{
	PositionTop:    "bottom-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 mb-2",
	PositionBottom: "top-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 mt-2",
	PositionStart:  "inset-e-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 me-2",
	PositionEnd:    "inset-s-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 ms-2",
}

func hoverCardPositionClass(pos HoverCardPosition) string {
	return utils.Lookup(hoverCardPositionMap, pos, hoverCardPositionMap[PositionBottom])
}

// HoverCardProps configures a hover-activated card with rich content.
// The card appears on hover and focus, using pure CSS (no JavaScript).
// Accessible: the card content is linked to the trigger via aria-details
// (rich supplementary content — a hover card is not a tooltip, so no
// role="tooltip").
// This is the reference implementation for the CSS-only overlay pattern —
// see ADR-0017 for the broader Popover API migration strategy.
type HoverCardProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Content  templ.Component
	Position HoverCardPosition
}

// DefaultHoverCardProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultHoverCardProps() HoverCardProps {
	return HoverCardProps{
		Position: HoverCardPositionBottom,
	}
}

// HoverCard wraps a trigger element in a hover-activated card with rich
// content.
//
// Base path (every engine): the card appears on :hover and :focus-within
// via pure CSS opacity transitions, absolutely positioned in the flow.
//
// Enhancement path (engines with the Popover + Interest Invokers APIs): the
// card is a `popover="hint"` panel and the trigger carries `interestfor` —
// the browser promotes it to the top layer on hover (escaping every
// overflow/z-index ancestor) and the shared popover-positioning script
// anchors it to the trigger with viewport clamping and edge flipping. The
// popover attribute is inert where unsupported, so the two paths never
// fight: a closed popover is display:none, which overrides the CSS hover
// visibility entirely.
//
//	@display.HoverCard(display.HoverCardProps{Position: display.HoverCardPositionTop}) {
//	   <button>Hover me</button>
//	}
//	@display.HoverCard.HoverCardContent(display.HoverCardProps{Content: ...})
templ HoverCard(props HoverCardProps) {
	{{ id := utils.EnsureID("hovercard", props.ID) }}
	{{ triggerID := id + "-trigger" }}
	<div
		class={ utils.Class("relative inline-block", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div
			id={ triggerID }
			class="peer"
			aria-details={ id }
			tabindex="0"
			interestfor={ id }
		>
			{ children... }
		</div>
		<div
			id={ id }
			popover="hint"
			data-tc-anchor={ triggerID }
			data-tc-position={ string(props.Position) }
			class={ utils.Class(
				hoverCardPositionClass(props.Position),
				"w-64 rounded-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 p-4 shadow-lg dark:shadow-black/20 opacity-0 invisible peer-hover:opacity-100 peer-hover:visible peer-focus-within:opacity-100 peer-focus-within:visible transition-opacity motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0",
			) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
		>
			if props.Content != nil {
				@props.Content
			}
		</div>
	</div>
	@popoverPositionScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// ImageProps configures an <img> element with lazy loading, aspect-ratio
// dimensions, and optional fallback source. The fallback is handled via a
// CSP-safe singleton script (no inline onerror handler) that swaps the src
// when the original fails to load.
type ImageProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Src is the primary image URL.
	Src string
	// Alt text for accessibility. Required for non-decorative images.
	Alt string
	// SrcSet defines multiple image sources for responsive delivery.
	// Example: "photo-1x.jpg 1x, photo-2x.jpg 2x" or
	// "photo-480w.jpg 480w, photo-800w.jpg 800w".
	SrcSet string
	// Sizes defines the intended display width at different breakpoints.
	// Example: "(max-width: 600px) 480px, 800px".
	// Pair with a width-descriptor srcset for responsive images.
	Sizes string
	// Width in CSS pixels. When set, the img tag includes a width attribute
	// and helps prevent layout shift (CLS).
	Width int
	// Height in CSS pixels. When set, the img tag includes a height attribute.
	Height int
	// FallbackSrc, when non-empty, is used if Src fails to load. Handled via
	// a CSP-safe event-delegation script — no inline onerror handler.
	FallbackSrc string
	// Lazy controls the loading attribute AND the fetch priority. When true
	// (default) the img gets loading="lazy" and NO fetchpriority attribute;
	// set it to false for the above-the-fold LCP image, which then gets
	// loading="eager" plus fetchpriority="high".
	//
	// fetchpriority="low" is deliberately never emitted: pairing it with
	// loading="lazy" is a documented anti-pattern (Modern Web Guidance
	// "optimize-image-priority" makes it MANDATORY not to) — lazy images
	// already load at normal priority when they enter the viewport, and an
	// explicit low priority delays them further.
	Lazy bool
	// Rounded, when true, adds rounded-full for circular images (avatars, icons).
	// Defaults to false (rounded-md).
	Rounded bool
	// Placeholder, when non-empty, is a tiny image URL (a 10-30px thumbhash
	// or thumbnail) rendered blurred BEHIND the main image — the zero-JS
	// blur-up pattern. The placeholder fills the box while Src loads and is
	// covered the moment the full image paints (no JavaScript, no animation
	// timing to race). Consumer generates the tiny image; the library adds
	// only CSS.
	Placeholder string
}

// DefaultImageProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultImageProps() ImageProps {
	return ImageProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Lazy: true,
	}
}

// Image renders an <img> with lazy loading, optional dimensions, and optional
// fallback source. The fallback swap is CSP-safe: a data-tc-img-fallback
// attribute on the img tag is consumed by a singleton error-capture listener.
//
// For responsive images with multiple resolutions, use SrcSet and Sizes:
//
//	@display.Image(display.ImageProps{
//	    Src:    "/photo.jpg",
//	    SrcSet: "/photo-480w.jpg 480w, /photo-800w.jpg 800w",
//	    Sizes:  "(max-width: 600px) 480px, 800px",
//	    Alt:    "Profile photo",
//	})
//
//	@display.Image(display.ImageProps{Src: "/photo.jpg", Alt: "Profile photo", Width: 128, Height: 128, FallbackSrc: "/placeholder.jpg"})
templ Image(props ImageProps) {
	if props.Src != "" && props.Placeholder != "" {
		<span
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("relative inline-block max-w-full overflow-hidden", utils.Ternary(props.Rounded, "rounded-full", "rounded-md"), props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			<img
				src={ props.Placeholder }
				alt=""
				aria-hidden="true"
				class="absolute inset-0 h-full w-full scale-110 object-cover blur-lg"
			/>
			<img
				src={ props.Src }
				alt={ props.Alt }
				if props.SrcSet != "" {
					srcset={ props.SrcSet }
				}
				if props.Sizes != "" {
					sizes={ props.Sizes }
				}
				loading={ utils.Ternary(props.Lazy, "lazy", "eager") }
				decoding="async"
				if !props.Lazy {
					fetchpriority="high"
				}
				if props.Width > 0 {
					width={ props.Width }
				}
				if props.Height > 0 {
					height={ props.Height }
				}
				if props.FallbackSrc != "" {
					data-tc-img-fallback={ props.FallbackSrc }
				}
				class="relative h-auto w-full"
			/>
		</span>
	} else if props.Src != "" {
		<img
			src={ props.Src }
			alt={ props.Alt }
			if props.SrcSet != "" {
				srcset={ props.SrcSet }
			}
			if props.Sizes != "" {
				sizes={ props.Sizes }
			}
			loading={ utils.Ternary(props.Lazy, "lazy", "eager") }
			decoding="async"
			if !props.Lazy {
				fetchpriority="high"
			}
			if props.Width > 0 {
				width={ props.Width }
			}
			if props.Height > 0 {
				height={ props.Height }
			}
			if props.FallbackSrc != "" {
				data-tc-img-fallback={ props.FallbackSrc }
			}
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class(utils.Ternary(props.Rounded, "max-w-full h-auto rounded-full", "max-w-full h-auto rounded-md"), props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		/>
	}
	if props.FallbackSrc != "" {
		@imageFallbackScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
	}
}
package display

import (
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// KanbanCard is one work item in a KanbanBoard column. ID is the
// consumer-supplied stable identity used by the move exchange — a card
// without an ID renders fine but is not draggable (the server could not
// route the move).
type KanbanCard struct {
	// ID is the stable card identity submitted as the move's card field.
	// It must survive re-renders (never auto-generate it per request).
	ID string
	// Title is the card's heading text.
	Title string
	// Href, when set, links the card title to a detail page.
	Href string
	// Content renders arbitrary card body below the title (labels, avatars,
	// metadata). Compose with Badge, Avatar, RelativeTime, … — the proven
	// anatomy (identity badges, 2+N tag overflow, assignee stack, one-line
	// description preview) is docs/recipes/kanban-card-anatomy.md; the
	// compiling composition is ExampleKanbanBoard_cardAnatomy.
	Content templ.Component
	// Class overrides the card's Tailwind classes.
	Class string
}

// KanbanColumn is one swimlane of a KanbanBoard. Like cards, columns need a
// stable ID to be droppable targets of the move exchange.
type KanbanColumn struct {
	// ID is the stable column identity submitted as the move's column field.
	ID string
	// Title is the column heading.
	Title string
	// Cards renders in order, top to bottom.
	Cards []KanbanCard
	// Action is an optional affordance rendered in the column header after
	// the count badge — the standard "add card" spot. The consumer owns the
	// whole element: compose display.Button (its Wire field for transport
	// wiring), a plain link, or any templ markup — and owns its
	// accessibility too: whatever renders there must be keyboard-reachable
	// (a real button or link, not a hover-only div). nil omits it; boards
	// without it render byte-identical to before.
	Action templ.Component
	// Tone is an optional status color rendered as a small dot before the
	// column title (todo=blue, done=green, …). The zero value (and any
	// unknown value) renders no dot — see KanbanTone.
	Tone KanbanTone
	// Class overrides the column's Tailwind classes.
	Class string
}

// KanbanTone selects the semantic color of a KanbanColumn's status dot,
// mirroring StatTone's palette. Unlike StatTone, the zero value is
// toneless: an empty or unknown Tone renders no dot at all (columns are
// not required to carry status semantics).
type KanbanTone string

// Column dot tones. Match the palette of Badge/BadgeType and StatTone:
// gray, blue, green, yellow, red, purple.
const (
	KanbanToneGray   KanbanTone = "gray"
	KanbanToneBlue   KanbanTone = "blue"
	KanbanToneGreen  KanbanTone = "green"
	KanbanToneYellow KanbanTone = "yellow"
	KanbanToneRed    KanbanTone = "red"
	KanbanTonePurple KanbanTone = "purple"
)

// KanbanToneIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined KanbanTone
// constants. The zero value is intentionally invalid — a toneless column
// renders no dot.
func KanbanToneIsValid(v KanbanTone) bool {
	_, ok := kanbanToneLookup[v]

	return ok
}

// kanbanToneLookup maps each KanbanTone onto the status-dot background
// classes. Unknown/empty tones resolve to "" — the signal to render no
// dot — rather than falling back to a color.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table, same pattern as statTileLookup
var kanbanToneLookup = map[KanbanTone]string{
	KanbanToneGray:   "bg-gray-400 dark:bg-gray-500",
	KanbanToneBlue:   "bg-blue-500 dark:bg-blue-400",
	KanbanToneGreen:  "bg-green-500 dark:bg-green-400",
	KanbanToneYellow: "bg-yellow-500 dark:bg-yellow-400",
	KanbanToneRed:    "bg-red-500 dark:bg-red-400",
	KanbanTonePurple: "bg-purple-500 dark:bg-purple-400",
}

// KanbanBoardProps configures a Kanban board: horizontal swimlanes of
// draggable cards, movable via HTML5 drag-and-drop or per-card keyboard
// buttons, under either transport.
//
// The move exchange: when Wire is set (non-empty URL), the component
// renders a hidden form carrying the Wire attributes plus three hidden
// inputs — card, column, index. Every move (drop or keyboard button) fills
// those inputs and submits the form, so the request travels as a plain form
// POST under htmx (hx-post) and Datastar (@post with form encoding) alike.
// The documented response is the freshly rendered board element itself:
// under htmx the component auto-targets its own id with hx-swap="outerHTML";
// under Datastar wrap the endpoint in wire.Handler with
// PatchTarget{Selector: "#<board id>", Mode: wire.PatchModeOuter}. Decode
// submissions with ParseKanbanMove.
//
// A board without Wire (or with an empty Wire.URL) is a read-only view: no
// drag handles, no move buttons, no script.
//
// Moves apply optimistically: the card moves in the DOM the moment the move
// is submitted (before the request resolves) and wears a pending register
// (tc-kanban-pending spinner + aria-busy) until the server's re-render
// replaces it. A failed move (4xx/5xx, network error) is reverted to its
// original position, flashed with tc-kanban-move-failed, and announced
// through a role="alert" region. See ADR-0041 for the decision.
type KanbanBoardProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Columns renders left to right (right to left under dir="rtl").
	Columns []KanbanColumn
	// Wire is the move exchange. nil or empty URL renders a read-only board.
	// Method defaults to POST, Event to submit, ContentType to form
	// encoding; under htmx, Target defaults to the board root with
	// hx-swap="outerHTML".
	//
	// Sorted views: the submitted index is advisory — the server owns the
	// real ordering. On a server-sorted view (by priority, created-at, …)
	// reject same-column moves in the handler; the sort re-asserts on
	// re-render and would otherwise make the drop look broken. See
	// docs/recipes/kanban-card-anatomy.md ("Moves on a sorted view").
	Wire *wire.Action
	// EmptyColumnText shows inside a column with no cards. Default "No cards".
	EmptyColumnText string
	// CSRFToken, when set, renders a hidden CSRF input (name from
	// CSRFTokenName) inside the move form so submissions pass token checks.
	CSRFToken string
	// CSRFTokenName is the hidden input's name. Default "csrf_token".
	CSRFTokenName string
}

// kanbanEmptyColumnTextDefault is the muted placeholder for empty columns.
const kanbanEmptyColumnTextDefault = "No cards"

// kanbanColumnClass returns the Tailwind classes for a board column.
func kanbanColumnClass(extra string) string {
	return utils.Class("flex w-72 shrink-0 flex-col rounded-lg border border-gray-200 bg-gray-50 p-3 dark:border-gray-700 dark:bg-gray-900", extra)
}

// kanbanColumnBodyClass returns the Tailwind classes for a column's drop
// zone (the card list). relative anchors the drop indicators, min-h keeps
// empty columns droppable.
func kanbanColumnBodyClass() string {
	return "relative flex min-h-24 flex-col gap-2 list-none m-0 p-0"
}

// kanbanCardClass returns the Tailwind classes for a card.
func kanbanCardClass(extra string) string {
	return utils.Class("group relative cursor-grab rounded-lg border border-gray-200 bg-white p-3 shadow-sm hover:border-accent-300 active:cursor-grabbing dark:border-gray-700 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:border-accent-600", extra)
}

// kanbanMoveButtonClass returns the Tailwind classes for the per-card
// keyboard move buttons.
func kanbanMoveButtonClass() string {
	return "inline-flex h-6 w-6 items-center justify-center rounded text-gray-400 hover:bg-gray-100 hover:text-gray-600 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-500 dark:text-gray-500 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 dark:hover:text-gray-300 dark:focus-visible:ring-accent-400"
}

// DefaultKanbanBoardProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultKanbanBoardProps() KanbanBoardProps {
	return KanbanBoardProps{
		CSRFTokenName: "csrf_token",
	}
}

// KanbanBoard renders a kanban board: horizontally scrolling columns of
// cards. With Wire set, cards drag between columns (HTML5 drag-and-drop,
// CSP-safe singleton script) and carry per-card "move to previous/next
// column" buttons so the board is fully keyboard operable; both affordances
// submit the same hidden form.
//
//	@display.KanbanBoard(display.KanbanBoardProps{
//	   Columns: []display.KanbanColumn{
//	     {ID: "todo", Title: "To do", Cards: []display.KanbanCard{{ID: "c1", Title: "Write docs"}}},
//	     {ID: "done", Title: "Done"},
//	   },
//	   Wire: &wire.Action{URL: "/api/kanban/move"},
//	})
templ KanbanBoard(props KanbanBoardProps) {
	{{ boardID := utils.EnsureID("kanban", props.ID) }}
	{{ moveAttrs := kanbanWireAttributes(props.Wire, boardID) }}
	{{ wired := len(moveAttrs) > 0 }}
	<div
		id={ boardID }
		data-tc-kanban
		class={ utils.Class("min-w-0 rounded-xl", props.Class) }
		role="region"
		aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Kanban board") }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if wired {
			<form
				data-tc-kanban-form
				method="POST"
				action={ templ.SafeURL(props.Wire.URL) }
				class="hidden"
				{ moveAttrs... }
			>
				<input type="hidden" name={ kanbanFieldCard } value="" data-tc-kanban-f-card/>
				<input type="hidden" name={ kanbanFieldColumn } value="" data-tc-kanban-f-column/>
				<input type="hidden" name={ kanbanFieldIndex } value="" data-tc-kanban-f-index/>
				if props.CSRFToken != "" {
					<input
						type="hidden"
						name={ utils.Coalesce(props.CSRFTokenName, "csrf_token") }
						value={ props.CSRFToken }
					/>
				}
			</form>
			<p data-tc-kanban-live class="sr-only" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p>
			<p data-tc-kanban-alert class="sr-only" role="alert"></p>
		}
		<div class="flex gap-4 overflow-x-auto pb-2">
			for ci, col := range props.Columns {
				{{ colID := kanbanColumnID(boardID, ci, col) }}
				{{ draggable := wired && col.ID != "" }}
				<section
					if col.ID != "" {
						data-tc-kanban-column={ col.ID }
					}
					class={ kanbanColumnClass(col.Class) }
					aria-labelledby={ colID + "-title" }
				>
					<div class="mb-3 flex items-center justify-between gap-2 px-1">
						<h3 id={ colID + "-title" } class="truncate text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
							if dotClass := utils.Lookup(kanbanToneLookup, col.Tone, ""); dotClass != "" {
								<span
									class={ "me-1.5 inline-block h-2 w-2 rounded-full align-middle", dotClass }
									aria-hidden="true"
								></span>
							}
							{ col.Title }
						</h3>
						if col.Action != nil {
							<div class="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2">
								@kanbanColumnCount(len(col.Cards))
								@col.Action
							</div>
						} else {
							@kanbanColumnCount(len(col.Cards))
						}
					</div>
					<ul
						if col.ID != "" {
							data-tc-kanban-column-body={ col.ID }
							data-tc-kanban-col-title={ col.Title }
						}
						aria-label={ col.Title + ": " + kanbanCountLabel(len(col.Cards)) }
						class={ kanbanColumnBodyClass() }
					>
						// data-tc-kanban-empty lets the move script hide the placeholder
						// while a card is optimistically placed into this column.
						if len(col.Cards) == 0 {
							<li data-tc-kanban-empty class="rounded-lg py-6 text-center text-sm text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400">
								{ utils.Coalesce(props.EmptyColumnText, kanbanEmptyColumnTextDefault) }
							</li>
						}
						for _, card := range col.Cards {
							if draggable && card.ID != "" {
								<li
									data-tc-kanban-card={ card.ID }
									draggable="true"
									class={ kanbanCardClass(card.Class) }
								>
									@kanbanCardInner(card, ci, len(props.Columns), wired)
								</li>
							} else {
								<li class={ utils.Class(kanbanCardClass(card.Class), "cursor-default") }>
									@kanbanCardInner(card, ci, len(props.Columns), wired)
								</li>
							}
						}
					</ul>
				</section>
			}
		</div>
		if wired {
			@kanbanScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
		}
	</div>
}

// kanbanColumnCount renders a column's card-count badge. The data-tc-kanban-count
// hook lets the move script keep the badge honest while a move is pending
// (optimistic ±1) and after a failed move is reverted (recompute from DOM).
templ kanbanColumnCount(count int) {
	<span
		data-tc-kanban-count
		class="inline-flex items-center rounded-md bg-gray-100 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-gray-800 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:text-gray-300"
	>
		{ strconv.Itoa(count) }
	</span>
}

// kanbanCardInner renders a card's content plus, on a wired board, the
// keyboard move buttons. The tc-kanban-buttons wrapper hides them until
// hover or keyboard focus — EXCEPT on coarse pointers (touch), where the
// custom.css pointer:coarse rule keeps them visible (no hover exists).
templ kanbanCardInner(card KanbanCard, columnIndex, columnCount int, wired bool) {
	<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-1">
		<div class="min-w-0">
			if card.Href != "" {
				<a
					href={ templ.SafeURL(card.Href) }
					data-tc-kanban-title
					class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 hover:text-accent-600 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-500 dark:text-white dark:hover:text-accent-400 dark:focus-visible:ring-accent-400"
				>
					{ card.Title }
				</a>
			} else {
				<span data-tc-kanban-title class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
					{ card.Title }
				</span>
			}
			if card.Content != nil {
				<div class="mt-1.5">
					@card.Content
				</div>
			}
		</div>
		if wired && (columnIndex > 0 || columnIndex < columnCount-1) {
			<div class={ "tc-kanban-buttons flex shrink-0 gap-0.5 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 group-focus-within:opacity-100", utils.TransitionFast }>
				if columnIndex > 0 {
					<button
						type="button"
						data-tc-kanban-move="prev"
						class={ kanbanMoveButtonClass() }
						aria-label={ "Move " + card.Title + " to previous column" }
					>
						<svg
							class="h-4 w-4 rtl:rotate-180"
							fill="none"
							viewBox="0 0 24 24"
							stroke-width="1.5"
							stroke="currentColor"
							aria-hidden="true"
						>
							<path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d={ svg.PathArrowLeft }></path>
						</svg>
					</button>
				}
				if columnIndex < columnCount-1 {
					<button
						type="button"
						data-tc-kanban-move="next"
						class={ kanbanMoveButtonClass() }
						aria-label={ "Move " + card.Title + " to next column" }
					>
						<svg
							class="h-4 w-4 rtl:rotate-180"
							fill="none"
							viewBox="0 0 24 24"
							stroke-width="1.5"
							stroke="currentColor"
							aria-hidden="true"
						>
							<path stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" d={ svg.PathArrowRight }></path>
						</svg>
					</button>
				}
			</div>
		}
	</div>
}
// Lightbox component: a native <dialog> image viewer with thumbnail
// triggers, prev/next navigation, rotate and zoom — extracted from
// DiscordSync's image thumbnails and nsfw-classifier's image viewer
// (2026-10-10 analysis, TODO_LIST #396). Zero framework JS: one CSP-safe
// singleton script; Escape, focus trap, and backdrop dismissal come from the
// native dialog.
package display

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// LightboxImage is one viewable image.
type LightboxImage struct {
	// Src is the full-size image URL.
	Src string
	// Alt is the image's alternative text (required for a11y).
	Alt string
	// Caption optionally renders under the image.
	Caption string
	// ThumbSrc optionally overrides the thumbnail source (TriggerLabel
	// button mode uses Src when empty).
	ThumbSrc string
}

// LightboxProps configures the lightbox.
type LightboxProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Images renders in order; the viewer navigates them with wrap-around.
	Images []LightboxImage
	// TriggerLabel renders one opener button with this text (Thumbnails
	// overrides it). Empty + no Thumbnails renders the dialog only —
	// open it yourself via tcOpenLightbox("<id>-dialog", index).
	TriggerLabel string
	// Thumbnails renders one opener button per image (using ThumbSrc/Src
	// as its thumbnail) instead of a single TriggerLabel button.
	Thumbnails bool
}

// DefaultLightboxProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultLightboxProps() LightboxProps {
	return LightboxProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
		TriggerLabel: "View images",
	}
}

// lightboxJS returns the CSP-safe singleton script: open/navigate/rotate/zoom
// on [data-tc-lightbox] roots via event delegation. Escape and backdrop
// dismissal are native <dialog> behavior (backdrop detection is shared with the
// other overlays); rotate and zoom compose on the image's transform (JS-set
// styles are not blocked by style-src).
func lightboxJS() string {
	return `if(!window.tcLightboxAttached){window.tcLightboxAttached=true;` +
		`window.tcLightboxApply=function(img){` +
		`var r=img.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-rot')||'0';` +
		`var z=img.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-zoom')==='1'?' scale(2)':'';` +
		`img.style.transform='rotate('+r+'deg)'+z;};` +
		`window.tcShowLightbox=function(dlg,idx){` +
		`var imgs=dlg.querySelectorAll('[data-tc-lightbox-img]');if(!imgs.length)return;` +
		`if(idx<0)idx=imgs.length-1;if(idx>=imgs.length)idx=0;` +
		`for(var k=0;k<imgs.length;k++){imgs[k].hidden=k!==idx;}` +
		`var cap=dlg.querySelector('[data-tc-lightbox-caption]');` +
		`if(cap)cap.textContent=imgs[idx].getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-cap')||'';` +
		`var img=imgs[idx];img.style.transform='';img.setAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-rot','0');img.setAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-zoom','0');img.classList.remove('cursor-zoom-out');` +
		`dlg.setAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-index',String(idx));` +
		`if(!dlg.open)dlg.showModal();};` +
		`window.tcOpenLightbox=function(id,idx){var d=document.getElementById(id);if(d)window.tcShowLightbox(d,idx||0);};` +
		`document.addEventListener('click',function(e){` +
		`var opener=e.target.closest('[data-tc-lightbox-open]');` +
		`if(opener){var root=opener.closest('[data-tc-lightbox]');if(!root)return;` +
		`var dlg=document.getElementById(root.id+'-dialog');if(!dlg)return;` +
		`window.tcShowLightbox(dlg,parseInt(opener.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-open'),10)||0);return;}` +
		`var nav=e.target.closest('[data-tc-lightbox-prev],[data-tc-lightbox-next]');` +
		`if(nav){var dr=nav.closest('dialog');if(!dr)return;` +
		`var cur=parseInt(dr.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-index')||'0',10);` +
		`window.tcShowLightbox(dr,cur+(nav.hasAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-next')?1:-1));return;}` +
		`var rot=e.target.closest('[data-tc-lightbox-rotate]');` +
		`if(rot){var rr=rot.closest('dialog');if(!rr)return;` +
		`var ri=rr.querySelectorAll('[data-tc-lightbox-img]')[parseInt(rr.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-index')||'0',10)];` +
		`if(ri){var r=(parseInt(ri.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-rot')||'0',10)+90)%360;` +
		`ri.setAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-rot',String(r));tcLightboxApply(ri);}return;}` +
		`var zoom=e.target.closest('[data-tc-lightbox-zoom]');` +
		`if(zoom){var zr=zoom.closest('dialog');if(!zr)return;` +
		`var zi=zr.querySelectorAll('[data-tc-lightbox-img]')[parseInt(zr.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-index')||'0',10)];` +
		`if(zi){zi.setAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-zoom',zi.getAttribute('data-tc-lightbox-zoom')==='1'?'0':'1');` +
		`zi.classList.toggle('cursor-zoom-out');tcLightboxApply(zi);}}` +
		`});}` +
		`(function(){` + dialogBackdropOutsideJS() + `var dlgs=document.querySelectorAll('dialog[data-tc-lightbox-dialog]');` +
		`for(var i=0;i<dlgs.length;i++){var dlg=dlgs[i];` +
		`dlg.addEventListener('click',function(e){` +
		`if(e.target.closest('[data-tc-close]'))this.close();});` +
		backdropDismissJS("dlg") + `}})();`
}
package display

import (
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// lightboxControlClass is the shared control-button style (prev/next/rotate/
// zoom/close): ghost buttons over the dark overlay.
const lightboxControlClass = "inline-flex h-10 w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-white/10 text-white hover:bg-white/20 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-accent-400 transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0 cursor-pointer"

// Lightbox renders a native-dialog image viewer.
//
//	@display.Lightbox(display.LightboxProps{
//		Images: []display.LightboxImage{
//			{Src: "/img/1.jpg", Alt: "Front view", Caption: "Front"},
//			{Src: "/img/2.jpg", Alt: "Back view"},
//		},
//	})
//
// Thumbnails mode renders one opener per image:
//
//	@display.Lightbox(display.LightboxProps{Thumbnails: true, Images: images})
templ Lightbox(props LightboxProps) {
	{{ rootID := utils.EnsureID("lightbox", props.ID) }}
	<div
		id={ rootID }
		data-tc-lightbox
		class={ utils.Class("inline-block", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Thumbnails {
			<div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
				for i, img := range props.Images {
					<button
						type="button"
						data-tc-lightbox-open={ strconv.Itoa(i) }
						class="group cursor-pointer overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-gray-200 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-500 dark:border-gray-700 dark:focus-visible:ring-accent-400"
						aria-label={ "Open image: " + img.Alt }
					>
						<img
							src={ templ.SafeURL(utils.Coalesce(img.ThumbSrc, img.Src)) }
							alt={ img.Alt }
							class="h-20 w-20 object-cover transition-transform group-hover:scale-105 motion-reduce:transform-none motion-reduce:transition-none"
							loading="lazy"
						/>
					</button>
				}
			</div>
		} else if props.TriggerLabel != "" {
			<button
				type="button"
				data-tc-lightbox-open="0"
				class="inline-flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-semibold text-white hover:bg-accent-700 dark:hover:bg-accent-400 focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-accent-400 transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0"
			>
				@icons.Icon(icons.Photo, "h-4 w-4")
				{ props.TriggerLabel }
			</button>
		}
		<dialog
			id={ rootID + "-dialog" }
			data-tc-lightbox-dialog
			closedby="any"
			class="tc-overlay tc-modal bg-black/90 p-4 dark:bg-black/90"
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			} else {
				aria-label="Image viewer"
			}
		>
			<div class="flex min-h-[80vh] min-w-[80vw] flex-col items-center justify-center gap-3">
				<figure class="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
					for i, img := range props.Images {
						<img
							src={ templ.SafeURL(img.Src) }
							alt={ img.Alt }
							data-tc-lightbox-img
							data-tc-lightbox-cap={ img.Caption }
							if i > 0 {
								hidden
							}
							class="max-h-[70vh] max-w-full cursor-zoom-in object-contain"
						/>
					}
					<figcaption data-tc-lightbox-caption class="text-sm text-gray-200 dark:text-gray-200"></figcaption>
				</figure>
				<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
					if len(props.Images) > 1 {
						<button type="button" data-tc-lightbox-prev class={ lightboxControlClass } aria-label="Previous image">
							@icons.Icon(icons.ChevronLeft, "h-5 w-5")
						</button>
						<button type="button" data-tc-lightbox-next class={ lightboxControlClass } aria-label="Next image">
							@icons.Icon(icons.ChevronRight, "h-5 w-5")
						</button>
					}
					<button type="button" data-tc-lightbox-rotate class={ lightboxControlClass } aria-label="Rotate image">
						@icons.Icon(icons.ArrowPath, "h-5 w-5")
					</button>
					<button type="button" data-tc-lightbox-zoom class={ lightboxControlClass } aria-label="Zoom image">
						@icons.Icon(icons.Search, "h-5 w-5")
					</button>
					<button type="button" data-tc-close class={ lightboxControlClass } aria-label="Close viewer">
						@icons.Icon(icons.Close, "h-5 w-5")
					</button>
				</div>
			</div>
		</dialog>
	</div>
	@utils.ScriptComponent(props.Nonce, lightboxJS(), "lightbox script")
}

}

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// ListNoteVariant selects which count semantics ListNote renders.
type ListNoteVariant string

const (
	// ListNoteTruncated renders "Showing N of M. Narrow your search to see
	// more." — and only when Total > Shown (a truncated result set). This is
	// the default; the zero value behaves identically.
	ListNoteTruncated ListNoteVariant = "truncated"
	// ListNoteCount renders "Showing N items." (pluralized) — count-only,
	// unconditionally, with no total and no advice. For list semantics where
	// "N items in range" is the whole message (e.g. an event log between two
	// timestamps): the consumer already knows why the list is shaped this
	// way, so count-only is the honest hint — including "Showing 0 items."
	// for an empty-but-loaded window.
	ListNoteCount ListNoteVariant = "count"
	// ListNoteRange renders "Showing X–Y of Z." — cursor-paginated position
	// semantics: X–Y is the 1-based span of items on the current page (from
	// RangeFrom/RangeTo), Z is the match count (Total). Unlike the truncated
	// variant it always renders — a cursor journal has no "everything fits"
	// signal, and "Showing 193–216 of 237." on the last page is the honest
	// you-have-seen-it-all hint. An empty or unpositioned range (non-positive
	// RangeFrom/RangeTo) degrades to the count message.
	ListNoteRange ListNoteVariant = "range"
)

// ListNoteProps configures a "Showing N of M" truncation notice.
type ListNoteProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Shown is the number of items currently rendered.
	Shown int
	// Total is the unfiltered/cap-exceeding match count. Read by the
	// truncated variant ("N of M") and by ListNoteRange (the Z in
	// "X–Y of Z"); ignored by ListNoteCount.
	Total int
	// RangeFrom is the 1-based index of the first item on the current page
	// (ListNoteRange only). Non-positive values degrade to the count message.
	RangeFrom int
	// RangeTo is the 1-based index of the last item on the current page
	// (ListNoteRange only). Non-positive values degrade to the count message.
	RangeTo int
	// Variant selects count semantics. Defaults to ListNoteTruncated.
	Variant ListNoteVariant
	// Message, when non-empty, replaces the synthesized sentence while
	// keeping the shared shell (classes, role="status", id, attrs). Use it
	// when the honest sentence is not a count shape — e.g. "Showing the
	// latest 5 of 12 status changes." for a rolling window, where the
	// truncated variant's "Narrow your search" is false advice. A custom
	// message always renders; to hide the note, don't render the component
	// (the count variants keep their own visibility rules).
	Message string
}

// listNoteMessage returns the notice text and whether it renders at all.
// Unknown Variant values degrade to truncated semantics (graceful fallback),
// and a caller-supplied Message wins over every synthesized sentence.
func listNoteMessage(props ListNoteProps) (string, bool) {
	if props.Message != "" {
		return props.Message, true
	}

	if props.Variant == ListNoteRange {
		if props.RangeFrom <= 0 || props.RangeTo <= 0 {
			return countMessage(props.Shown), true
		}

		return fmt.Sprintf("Showing %d–%d of %d.", props.RangeFrom, props.RangeTo, props.Total), true
	}

	if props.Variant == ListNoteCount {
		return countMessage(props.Shown), true
	}

	if props.Total <= props.Shown {
		return "", false
	}

	return fmt.Sprintf("Showing %d of %d. Narrow your search to see more.", props.Shown, props.Total), true
}

// countMessage renders the pluralized count-only phrasing shared by
// ListNoteCount and the ListNoteRange empty fallback.
func countMessage(shown int) string {
	item := "items"
	if shown == 1 {
		item = "item"
	}

	return fmt.Sprintf("Showing %d %s.", shown, item)
}

// listNoteShell renders the shared status div so both variants keep one
// class/ARIA source of truth.
templ listNoteShell(props ListNoteProps, message string) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 px-4 py-2.5 text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		role="status"
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ message }
	</div>
}

// ListNote renders a "Showing N of M" hint when a list is truncated
// (ListNoteTruncated, the default: renders nothing when all rows fit), a
// count-only "Showing N items." hint (ListNoteCount: always renders —
// including zero — for list semantics), or a cursor-paginated position hint
// (ListNoteRange: "Showing X–Y of Z.", always renders).
//
//	@display.ListNote(display.ListNoteProps{Shown: 50, Total: 127})
//	@display.ListNote(display.ListNoteProps{Shown: 42, Variant: display.ListNoteCount})
//	@display.ListNote(display.ListNoteProps{RangeFrom: 193, RangeTo: 216, Total: 237, Variant: display.ListNoteRange})
//	@display.ListNote(display.ListNoteProps{Message: "Showing the latest 5 of 12 status changes."})
templ ListNote(props ListNoteProps) {
	{{ message, visible := listNoteMessage(props) }}
	if visible {
		@listNoteShell(props, message)
	}
}

// LoadingDialogProps configures a modal loading dialog.
type LoadingDialogProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Title names the dialog for assistive technology (aria-label fallback
	// after AriaLabel and Message). It is not rendered as a visible header —
	// a blocking loading state has nothing to close, so the dialog ships no
	// header bar and no close button.
	Title string
	// Message is the visible loading text (also the aria-label fallback).
	Message string
	// ShowProgress swaps the "Please wait..." hint for a determinate bar.
	ShowProgress bool
	// Progress is clamped to [0, 100] before rendering.
	Progress int
	// Open auto-shows the dialog on load (native showModal via the shared
	// overlay script). Toggle at runtime with tcOpenModal(id)/tcCloseModal(id)
	// or the dialog element's native showModal()/close().
	Open bool
}

// DefaultLoadingDialogProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultLoadingDialogProps() LoadingDialogProps {
	return LoadingDialogProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct // zero value IS the default
}

// LoadingDialog renders a BLOCKING loading state as a native <dialog> modal:
// focus is trapped, the page behind it is inert, and Escape or a backdrop
// click dismisses it. This is the modal twin of the static
// feedback.LoadingOverlay — use the static overlay when the page must stay
// reachable, and this dialog when the operation genuinely blocks the page.
//
//	@display.LoadingDialog(display.LoadingDialogProps{ID: "save-dialog", Message: "Saving...", Open: true})
templ LoadingDialog(props LoadingDialogProps) {
	{{ id := utils.EnsureID("loading-dialog", props.ID) }}
	@overlayShell(overlayShellProps{
		id:          id,
		open:        props.Open,
		ariaLabel:   utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, props.Message, props.Title, "Loading"),
		kind:        OverlayModal,
		nonce:       props.Nonce,
		dialogClass: utils.Class("tc-modal bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 rounded-lg shadow-xl dark:shadow-black/20 max-w-sm w-full mx-4 overflow-hidden print:hidden", props.Class),
		attrs:       props.Attrs,
	}) {
		<div class="py-6 text-center" aria-busy="true">
			<div class="mx-auto flex items-center justify-center h-12 w-12 rounded-full bg-accent-100 dark:bg-accent-900/30 mb-4">
				<svg
					class="animate-spin motion-reduce:animate-none h-6 w-6 text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400"
					xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
					fill="none"
					viewBox="0 0 24 24"
					aria-hidden="true"
				>
					@svg.SpinnerSVG()
				</svg>
			</div>
			if props.Message != "" {
				<p class="text-lg font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white mb-2">{ props.Message }</p>
			}
			@feedback.LoadingProgress(props.ShowProgress, props.Progress)
		</div>
	}
}

		attrs:       props.Attrs,
	}) {
		{ children... }
	}
}

// PageHeaderProps configures a page-level header with title, optional subtitle,
// and optional breadcrumb/action slots.
type PageHeaderProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Title string
	// TitleComponent, when set, renders inside the <h1> instead of the Title
	// string — for code elements, badges, or copy buttons inside the header
	// title. Takes precedence over Title.
	TitleComponent templ.Component
	// Subtitle renders below the title in muted text.
	Subtitle string
	// SubtitleComponent, when set, renders inside the subtitle <p> instead
	// of the Subtitle string. Takes precedence over Subtitle.
	SubtitleComponent templ.Component
	// Breadcrumb renders above the title (optional). Pass a navigation.Breadcrumbs
	// component or any custom breadcrumb markup.
	Breadcrumb templ.Component
	// Action renders on the right side of the title row (optional). Use for
	// primary buttons, back links, or status badges.
	Action templ.Component
}

// DefaultPageHeaderProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultPageHeaderProps() PageHeaderProps {
	return PageHeaderProps{}
}

// PageHeader renders a page-level header with title, optional subtitle, optional
// breadcrumb above, and an optional action slot on the right. Title and
// subtitle accept plain strings or templ components (TitleComponent /
// SubtitleComponent) for rich content inside the heading.
//
//	@display.PageHeader(display.PageHeaderProps{
//	   Title: "Users",
//	   Subtitle: "Manage user accounts",
//	   Action: display.Button(display.ButtonProps{Text: "New user", Href: "/users/new"}),
//	})
templ PageHeader(props PageHeaderProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("mb-6", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Breadcrumb != nil {
			<div class="mb-3">
				@props.Breadcrumb
			</div>
		}
		<div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 flex-wrap">
			<div class="min-w-0">
				<h1 class="text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight text-gray-900 dark:text-white break-after-avoid">
					if props.TitleComponent != nil {
						@props.TitleComponent
					} else {
						{ props.Title }
					}
				</h1>
				if props.SubtitleComponent != nil || props.Subtitle != "" {
					<p class={ utils.Class(mutedTextClass, "mt-1") }>
						if props.SubtitleComponent != nil {
							@props.SubtitleComponent
						} else {
							{ props.Subtitle }
						}
					</p>
				}
			</div>
			if props.Action != nil {
				<div class="flex-shrink-0">
					@props.Action
				</div>
			}
		</div>
	</div>
}
package display

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// PieChart renders a pure-SVG pie or donut chart. Zero JavaScript — all
// rendering is server-side using SVG arc paths. Supports external labels,
// a legend, and a center label for donut charts. Dark-mode aware.
//
//	@display.PieChart(display.PieChartProps{
//	    Slices: []display.PieChartSlice{
//	        {Label: "Direct", Value: 45},
//	        {Label: "Organic", Value: 30},
//	        {Label: "Referral", Value: 25},
//	    },
//	})
templ PieChart(props PieChartProps) {
	{{
		width := props.Width
		if width == 0 {
			width = pieChartDefaultWidth
		}
		height := props.Height
		if height == 0 {
			height = pieChartDefaultHeight
		}
		emptyMsg := props.EmptyMessage
		if emptyMsg == "" {
			emptyMsg = pieChartDefaultEmpty
		}

		cx := float64(width) / 2
		cy := float64(height) / 2

		// Reserve space for labels and legend.
		chartRadius := math.Min(float64(width), float64(height)) / 2

		// An unset LabelMode means the documented default (external): the
		// zero value "" failed the equality check and silently suppressed
		// every label for ShowLabels: true struct literals.
		labelMode := props.LabelMode
		if !PieChartLabelModeIsValid(labelMode) {
			labelMode = PieChartLabelExternal
		}

		showLabels := props.ShowLabels && labelMode == PieChartLabelExternal
		labelPad := chartRadius * 0.25
		if !showLabels {
			labelPad = chartRadius * 0.1
		}

		legendHeight := 0.0
		if props.ShowLegend && len(props.Slices) > 0 {
			legendHeight = float64(len(props.Slices))*pieChartLegendYGap + pieChartLegendYGap
		}

		radius := math.Min(chartRadius-labelPad, float64(height)/2-legendHeight/2)
		if radius < 10 {
			radius = 10
		}

		innerR := 0.0
		if props.Donut {
			innerR = radius * SanitizeInnerRadius(props.InnerRadius)
		}

		hasData := pieChartHasData(props.Slices)
		angles := computeSliceAngles(props.Slices)

		type legendEntry struct {
			Label string
			Color string
			Y     float64
		}
		var legend []legendEntry
		if props.ShowLegend && len(props.Slices) > 0 {
			ly := float64(height) - legendHeight + pieChartLegendYGap
			for i, s := range props.Slices {
				if s.Value <= 0 {
					continue
				}
				legend = append(legend, legendEntry{
					Label: s.Label,
					Color: pieChartColor(i, s.Color),
					Y:     ly,
				})
				ly += pieChartLegendYGap
			}
		}
	}}
	<svg
		viewBox={ fmt.Sprintf("0 0 %d %d", width, height) }
		class={ utils.Class("w-full h-auto", props.Class) }
		role="img"
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-hidden="true"
		}
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if hasData {
			for _, sa := range angles {
				{{
					color := pieChartColor(sa.sliceIdx, props.Slices[sa.sliceIdx].Color)
					arcPath := computeArcPath(cx, cy, radius, innerR, sa.startAngle, sa.endAngle)
				}}
				<g class={ color }>
					<path
						d={ arcPath }
						fill="currentColor"
						stroke="white"
						stroke-width="2"
						class="dark:stroke-gray-800"
					></path>
				</g>
				if showLabels && sa.sliceIdx < len(props.Slices) && props.Slices[sa.sliceIdx].Label != "" {
					{{
						labelX, labelY := polarToCartesian(cx, cy, radius*pieChartLabelOffset, sa.midAngle)
						anchor := "start"
						if sa.midAngle > 90 && sa.midAngle < 270 {
							anchor = "end"
						}
					}}
					<text
						x={ labelX }
						y={ labelY }
						text-anchor={ anchor }
						dominant-baseline="middle"
						class="fill-gray-600 dark:fill-gray-300"
						font-size={ pieChartFontSize }
					>{ props.Slices[sa.sliceIdx].Label } ({ pieChartFormatPercent(sa.percent) })</text>
				}
			}
			if props.Donut && props.CenterLabel != "" {
				<text
					x={ cx }
					y={ cy }
					text-anchor="middle"
					dominant-baseline="middle"
					class="fill-gray-700 dark:fill-gray-200 font-semibold"
					font-size={ pieChartCenterFontSize }
				>{ props.CenterLabel }</text>
			}
			if len(legend) > 0 {
				for _, le := range legend {
					{{
						labelText := le.Label
						if labelText == "" {
							labelText = "—"
						}
					}}
					<g transform={ fmt.Sprintf("translate(%d,%g)", pieChartLeftPad, le.Y) }>
						<rect
							width={ pieChartLegendSwatch }
							height={ pieChartLegendSwatch }
							rx="2"
							class={ le.Color }
							fill="currentColor"
						></rect>
						<text
							x={ pieChartLegendSwatch + pieChartLegendGap }
							y={ pieChartLegendSwatch - 1 }
							class="fill-gray-600 dark:fill-gray-300"
							font-size={ pieChartFontSize }
						>{ labelText }</text>
					</g>
				}
			}
		} else {
			<text
				x={ cx }
				y={ cy }
				text-anchor="middle"
				dominant-baseline="middle"
				class="fill-gray-400 dark:fill-gray-500"
				font-size={ pieChartCenterFontSize }
			>{ emptyMsg }</text>
		}
	</svg>
}

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
)

// PopoverProps configures a popover component.
//
// A popover is a floating panel triggered by a button click. It displays
// arbitrary content (unlike Dropdown which renders menu items) and dismisses
// on Escape, click-outside, or when the trigger is toggled again.
type PopoverProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	TriggerText string
	Position    PopoverPosition
}

// DefaultPopoverProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultPopoverProps() PopoverProps {
	return PopoverProps{
		Position: PopoverPositionBottom,
	}
}

// Popover renders a button-triggered floating panel with arbitrary content.
// Uses the native Popover API (popover="auto") for click-toggle via
// popovertarget, light-dismiss, Escape-to-close, and top-layer rendering.
//
// Positioning: the Popover API promotes the panel to the top layer with
// position:fixed (UA stylesheet), detaching it from the trigger's DOM
// subtree. CSS classes therefore cannot anchor to the trigger. A thin
// singleton script (popoverPositionScriptComponent) reads the trigger's
// getBoundingClientRect() on open and sets style.left/top with viewport
// clamping. See ADR-0017.
//
//	@display.Popover(display.PopoverProps{TriggerText: "Details"}) {
//	   <p class="text-sm">Popover content goes here.</p>
//	}
templ Popover(props PopoverProps) {
	{{ id := utils.EnsureID("popover", props.ID) }}
	{{ pos := props.Position }}
	{{ if pos == "" || !PopoverPositionIsValid(pos) {
	pos = PopoverPositionBottom
} }}
	<div
		id={ id }
		class={ utils.Class("relative inline-block text-start", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<button
			type="button"
			id={ id + "-trigger" }
			popovertarget={ id + "-content" }
			class="inline-flex w-full justify-center gap-x-1.5 rounded-md bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-3 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white shadow-xs ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700"
			aria-haspopup="dialog"
			aria-controls={ id + "-content" }
		>
			{ props.TriggerText }
			@svg.FillIcon("-me-1 h-5 w-5 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500", svg.PathChevronSmall, false)
		</button>
		<div
			id={ id + "-content" }
			popover="auto"
			data-tc-anchor={ id + "-trigger" }
			data-tc-position={ string(pos) }
			class="w-72 rounded-md bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 shadow-lg dark:shadow-black/20 ring-1 ring-black/5 p-4 text-sm text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
			role="dialog"
			aria-labelledby={ id + "-trigger" }
		>
			{ children... }
		</div>
	</div>
	@popoverPositionScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
}

// Prose renders a longform-content container (rendered markdown, articles,
// documentation bodies). The .tc-prose family in templates/custom.css styles
// the content's descendants — headings, lists, blockquotes, code, tables,

		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Children != nil {
			@props.Children
		} else {
			{ children... }
		}
	</div>
}
package display

import (
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// RelativeTimeProps configures a human-readable relative timestamp.
// The server renders the initial relative string ("2 hours ago"); the
// machine-readable datetime attribute is always present for screen readers
// and search engines.
type RelativeTimeProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Time is the timestamp to display relative to now.
	Time time.Time
	// Now, when non-zero, pins the reference instant the relative string is
	// computed against (defaults to time.Now at render time). Tests use it to
	// pin boundary behavior ("59s vs 60s") deterministically; production
	// callers leave it zero.
	Now time.Time
	// Title, when non-empty, overrides the default title (absolute time shown
	// on hover). Set to "" to use the formatted absolute timestamp.
	Title string
	// EmptyText, when non-empty and Time is the zero value, renders this text
	// instead of a relative string: zero timestamps mean "never" (never
	// rotated, never used), and date noise like "Jan 1, 0001" is the opposite
	// of the information the reader needs. The empty render stays inside the
	// <time> shell but omits the meaningless zero datetime, the default
	// zero-date title, and data-tc-relative (the auto-refresh script would
	// re-format the placeholder into date noise). Unset, or a non-zero Time,
	// keeps the exact prior behavior.
	EmptyText string
	// AutoRefresh defaults to true — the component injects a singleton script
	// that uses the native Intl.RelativeTimeFormat API to live-update the text
	// every 30 seconds. Also listens to htmx:afterSettle so newly-swapped
	// <time> elements are formatted immediately. This is progressive enhancement:
	// the server-rendered text is correct without JS; the script just keeps it
	// fresh. Set to false for static contexts (PDF, email, SEO-only).
	AutoRefresh bool
}

// DefaultRelativeTimeProps returns sensible defaults. Time defaults to now,
// AutoRefresh defaults to true (live-updating via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat).
func DefaultRelativeTimeProps() RelativeTimeProps {
	return RelativeTimeProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Time:        time.Now(),
		AutoRefresh: true,
	}
}

// RelativeTime renders a <time> element with a human-readable relative
// timestamp (e.g. "2 hours ago", "just now", "3 days ago"). The datetime
// attribute carries the RFC 3339 timestamp for accessibility and SEO.
//
//	@display.RelativeTime(display.RelativeTimeProps{Time: createdAt})
//	@display.RelativeTime(display.RelativeTimeProps{Time: createdAt, AutoRefresh: false}) // static
templ RelativeTime(props RelativeTimeProps) {
	{{
		empty := props.Time.IsZero() && props.EmptyText != ""
		now := props.Now
		if now.IsZero() {
			now = time.Now()
		}
		text := formatRelativeTime(props.Time, now)
		title := props.Title
		if title == "" && !empty {
			title = props.Time.Format("Jan 2, 2006 3:04 PM MST")
		}
		if empty {
			text = props.EmptyText
		}
	}}
	<time
		if !empty {
			datetime={ props.Time.Format(time.RFC3339) }
		}
		if title != "" {
			title={ title }
		}
		if props.AutoRefresh && !empty {
			data-tc-relative
		}
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ text }
	</time>
	if props.AutoRefresh && !empty {
		@relativeTimeScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
	}
}

// formatRelativeTime returns a human-readable string describing how far ago
// (or how far from now) t is relative to now. Examples: "just now",
// "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago", "2 days ago", "1 week ago", "Jan 5, 2025".
func formatRelativeTime(t, now time.Time) string {
	d := now.Sub(t)
	if d < 0 {
		d = -d
	}

	switch {
	case d < time.Minute:
		return "just now"
	case d < time.Hour:
		mins := int(d / time.Minute)
		if mins == 1 {
			return "1 minute ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(mins, "minutes")
	case d < 24*time.Hour:
		hours := int(d / time.Hour)
		if hours == 1 {
			return "1 hour ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(hours, "hours")
	case d < 7*24*time.Hour:
		days := int(d / (24 * time.Hour))
		if days == 1 {
			return "1 day ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(days, "days")
	case d < 30*24*time.Hour:
		weeks := int(d / (7 * 24 * time.Hour))
		if weeks == 1 {
			return "1 week ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(weeks, "weeks")
	default:
		return t.Format("Jan 2, 2006")
	}
}

// formatRelativeAgo returns "<n> <unit> ago".
func formatRelativeAgo(n int, unit string) string {
	return strconv.Itoa(n) + " " + unit + " ago"
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// ScrollbackTone colors a scrollback line's tag column.
type ScrollbackTone string

const (
	ScrollbackToneNeutral ScrollbackTone = "neutral"
	ScrollbackToneInfo    ScrollbackTone = "info"
	ScrollbackToneSuccess ScrollbackTone = "success"
	ScrollbackToneWarning ScrollbackTone = "warning"
	ScrollbackToneDanger  ScrollbackTone = "danger"
)

// ScrollbackToneIsValid reports whether tone is a known scrollback tone.
func ScrollbackToneIsValid(tone ScrollbackTone) bool {
	_, ok := scrollbackToneLookup[tone]
	return ok
}

// ScrollbackLine is one entry in a Scrollback. Timestamp is preformatted by
// the caller (e.g. "12:47:03.184"); Tag is a short column label (e.g.
// "query", "match"); Text is the line body.
type ScrollbackLine struct {
	Timestamp string
	Tag       string
	Text      string
	Tone      ScrollbackTone
	// ID sets the line element's id, so a URL fragment can scroll to it
	// (deep links into a transcript) and scripts can address it. Uniqueness is
	// the caller's responsibility — the component renders whatever it is
	// given. Leave empty for anonymous lines.
	ID string
	// Class is merged onto the line element after the built-in classes, so a
	// consumer can highlight a matched line or attach a test hook without
	// re-rolling the loop. tailwind-merge resolves conflicts; the Stagger
	// nth-child delays keep working (they are keyed on position, not class).
	Class string
}

// ScrollbackProps configures a terminal-style log block.
type ScrollbackProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Lines renders top-down in the given order. Empty slice renders nothing.
	Lines []ScrollbackLine
	// Stagger animates lines in sequentially (pure CSS, reduced-motion safe).
	// DefaultScrollbackProps enables it; the zero value renders instantly.
	Stagger bool
}

// DefaultScrollbackProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultScrollbackProps() ScrollbackProps {
	return ScrollbackProps{
		Stagger: true,
	}
}

// Scrollback renders a server-rendered, terminal-style log block: monospace
// lines with a timestamp column and a tone-colored tag column. With Stagger
// enabled, lines fade in sequentially via CSS nth-child delays — zero
// JavaScript, and prefers-reduced-motion users see all lines immediately.
//
// The block is decorative by default (aria-hidden). Pass AriaLabel when the
// lines carry real information screen readers should read.
//
//	@display.Scrollback(display.ScrollbackProps{
//	   Stagger: true,
//	   Lines: []display.ScrollbackLine{
//	       {Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "query", Text: "ads.example.com A", Tone: display.ScrollbackToneInfo},
//	       {Timestamp: "12:47:03.185", Tag: "action", Text: "NXDOMAIN", Tone: display.ScrollbackToneDanger},
//	   },
//	})
templ Scrollback(props ScrollbackProps) {
	if len(props.Lines) > 0 {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("tc-log text-start border-y border-gray-200 py-3 font-mono text-[0.8125rem] leading-relaxed text-gray-600 dark:border-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel == "" {
				aria-hidden="true"
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				role="log"
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			for _, line := range props.Lines {
				<div
					if line.ID != "" {
						id={ line.ID }
					}
					class={ utils.Class(utils.Ternary(props.Stagger, "tc-log-line", "tc-log-line tc-log-line-still"), line.Class) }
				>
					if line.Timestamp != "" {
						<span class="me-3 text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">{ line.Timestamp }</span>
					}
					if line.Tag != "" {
						<span class={ utils.Class("me-2 inline-block min-w-12 font-medium", scrollbackToneClass(line.Tone)) }>{ line.Tag }</span>
					}
					{ line.Text }
				</div>
			}
		</div>
	}
}

// Lookup maps live in this .templ file (not a separate .go file) so
// Tailwind's content scanner detects the class strings.

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for scrollback tones
var scrollbackToneLookup = map[ScrollbackTone]string{
	ScrollbackToneNeutral: "text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
	ScrollbackToneInfo:    "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400",
	ScrollbackToneSuccess: "text-green-700 dark:text-green-400",
	ScrollbackToneWarning: "text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400",
	ScrollbackToneDanger:  "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400",
}

// scrollbackToneClass maps a tone to its tag color classes, falling back to
// neutral for unknown values.
func scrollbackToneClass(tone ScrollbackTone) string {
	return utils.Lookup(scrollbackToneLookup, tone, scrollbackToneLookup[ScrollbackToneNeutral])
}
