import (
	"net/url"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// LoadMoreProps configures a "Load more" button for cursor-based pagination.
// The button issues an HTMX request to Endpoint with the current Cursor value.
// The server responds with the next batch of items plus a new LoadMore button
// (with the updated cursor) that replaces this one via hx-swap="outerHTML".
type LoadMoreProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Endpoint is the URL the button requests via hx-get. The cursor is
	// appended as a query parameter (?cursor=...).
	Endpoint string
	// Cursor is the opaque cursor value for the next page of results.
	Cursor string
	// Label is the button text. Defaults to "Load more".
	Label string
	// InfiniteScroll, when true, adds a reveal trigger so the button
	// auto-fires when scrolled into view (infinite scroll pattern). Without
	// Wire this renders htmx's hx-trigger="revealed"; with Wire the typed
	// trigger language renders it in BOTH dialects (ADR-0043): htmx
	// "revealed", Datastar data-on-intersect__once — both fire once on first
	// viewport entry.
	InfiniteScroll bool
	// Wire, when set, re-renders the request wiring in the configured
	// transport (see the utils/wire package, ADR-0036). Wire.URL replaces
	// Endpoint (the cursor is appended to it exactly the same way); swap
	// semantics stay self-replacement via the typed trigger language:
	// under htmx the action renders hx-swap="outerHTML" next to the kept
	// hx-target="this"; under Datastar the fragment replaces this region by
	// id-matching — set ID explicitly so the server can echo the wrapper id
	// back (wire.Handler-style). Wire.Target is ignored (pagination is a GET
	// that replaces itself); Wire.Swap is overridden to outer; an explicit
	// Wire.Event merges with the reveal trigger per ADR-0043.
	Wire *wire.Action
	// FocusOnSwap renders autofocus on the button so the replacement button
	// receives focus after the outerHTML self-swap — verified against the
	// embedded htmx 2.0.10 runtime, which focuses swapped-in [autofocus]
	// elements. Without it the clicked button is REMOVED from the DOM and
	// focus silently drops to <body>, stranding keyboard and screen-reader
	// users mid-list. Set it ONLY on swap-RESPONSE renders (the replacement
	// button); an initial-page button with autofocus would steal focus at
	// document parse. Datastar patching ignores the attribute (dialect note
	// in docs/transport-wiring.md — the Datastar focus story is the LiveRegion).
	FocusOnSwap bool
}

// DefaultLoadMoreProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultLoadMoreProps() LoadMoreProps {
	return LoadMoreProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Label: "Load more",
	}
}

// LoadMore renders a centered "Load more" button for cursor-based pagination.
// The button uses hx-get to fetch the next batch and hx-swap="outerHTML" so the
// server's response (next items + updated LoadMore) replaces this button in
// place. The cursor is appended as a ?cursor= query parameter to the hx-get URL.
//
//	@navigation.LoadMore(navigation.LoadMoreProps{
//	   Endpoint: "/api/items",
//	   Cursor:   nextCursor,
//	})
//
// Pass Wire to switch the dialect while keeping the semantics identical:
//
//	@navigation.LoadMore(navigation.LoadMoreProps{
//	   ID:        "items-load-more",
//	   Wire:      &wire.Action{Transport: wire.TransportDatastar, URL: "/api/items"},
//	   Cursor:    nextCursor,
//	})
templ LoadMore(props LoadMoreProps) {
	{{
		label := props.Label
		if label == "" {
			label = "Load more"
		}
		href := props.Endpoint
		if props.Wire != nil {
			href = props.Wire.URL
		}
		if props.Cursor != "" {
			parsed, err := url.Parse(href)
			if err == nil {
				q := parsed.Query()
				q.Set("cursor", props.Cursor)
				parsed.RawQuery = q.Encode()
				href = parsed.String()
			} else {
				href = href + "?cursor=" + url.QueryEscape(props.Cursor)
			}
		}
		wired := templ.Attributes{}
		isDatastar := false
		if props.Wire != nil {
			a := *props.Wire
			a.URL = href
			a.Target = ""
			a.Swap = wire.PatchModeOuter
			if props.InfiniteScroll {
				a.Reveal = &wire.Reveal{}
			}
			wired = a.Attributes()
			isDatastar = a.Transport == wire.TransportDatastar
		}
	}}
	<div
		id={ utils.EnsureID("load-more", props.ID) }
		class={ utils.Class("flex justify-center py-6", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<button
			type="button"
			{ wired... }
			if props.FocusOnSwap {
				autofocus
			}
			if props.Wire == nil {
				hx-get={ href }
				hx-swap="outerHTML"
				hx-target="this"
				if props.InfiniteScroll {
					hx-trigger="revealed"
				}
		} else {
			if !isDatastar && href != "" {
				hx-target="this"
			}
		}
			class={ "inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 cursor-pointer " + utils.TransitionColors + " focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 dark:focus-visible:ring-blue-400" }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
		>
			{ label }
		</button>
	</div>
}
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// mobileMenuToggleClass swaps viewport-keyed (sm:hidden) for container-keyed
// (@sm:hidden) when containerAware is true. Both strings are complete Tailwind
// literals so the content scanner picks them up.
func mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "flex items-center @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "flex items-center sm:hidden"
}

// mobileMenuClass swaps the wrapper's hidden/visible breakpoint the same way.
func mobileMenuClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "hidden sm:hidden"
}

// MobileMenuToggle renders the hamburger button for mobile menus.
// menuID uniquely identifies the menu this toggle controls, so multiple Nav
// instances on one page don't collide on a hardcoded ID.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenuToggle(true, "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenuToggle(show bool, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if show {
		<div class={ mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware) }>
			<button
				type="button"
				class={ "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md p-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:bg-gray-100 hover:text-gray-500 focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-inset focus:ring-blue-500 dark:focus:ring-blue-400 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:text-gray-300 " + utils.TransitionColors }
				aria-controls={ menuID }
				aria-expanded="false"
				data-mobile-menu-toggle={ menuID }
			>
				<span class="sr-only">Open main menu</span>
				@icons.Icon(icons.Menu, "tc-menu-open block h-6 w-6")
				@icons.Icon(icons.X, "tc-menu-close hidden h-6 w-6")
			</button>
		</div>
	}
}

// MobileMenu renders the collapsible mobile navigation menu.
// menuID uniquely identifies this menu; the toggle uses the same ID so the
// aria-controls relationship stays valid even with multiple Navs on a page.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenu(links, "/", "", "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenu(links []NavLinkProps, currentPath string, nonce string, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if len(links) > 0 {
		<div class={ mobileMenuClass(containerAware) } id={ menuID } data-mobile-menu-id={ menuID }>
			<div class="space-y-1 pb-3 pt-2 border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800">
				for _, link := range links {
					@MobileNavLink(link, currentPath)
				}
			</div>
		</div>
		<script { utils.ScriptAttrs(nonce)... }>
			if (!window.tcMobileMenuAttached) {
				window.tcMobileMenuAttached = true;
				function tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, open) {
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var openIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-open');
					var closeIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-close');
					if (!openIcon || !closeIcon) return;
					if (open) {
						menu.classList.remove('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
						var first = menu.querySelector('a[href],button:not([disabled]),input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])');
						if (first) first.focus();
					} else {
						menu.classList.add('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
						btn.focus();
					}
				}
				document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
					var btn = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-toggle]');
					if (!btn) return;
					var menuId = btn.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-toggle');
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var menu = nav.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-id="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!menu) return;
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, menu.classList.contains('hidden'));
				});
				document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
					if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
					var menu = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-id]');
					if (!menu) return;
					if (menu.classList.contains('hidden')) return;
					var menuId = menu.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-id');
					var btn = document.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-toggle="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!btn) return;
					e.preventDefault();
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, false);
				});
			}
		</script>
	}
}
package navigation

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// NavProps configures a navigation bar.
//
// BaseProps.ID pins the nav element's id and derives a distinct mobile-menu
// id from it (<id>-mobile-menu). Left empty, the menu id comes from the nav's
// content instead, which is deterministic: the same page renders identical
// bytes, so ETag/CDN revalidation keeps working.
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the bar collapse to its hamburger menu
// based on its parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the
// viewport. Useful when Nav is placed inside a sidebar, drawer, or other
// constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
type NavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Brand       templ.Component
	Links       []NavLinkProps
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
	// ContainerAware, when true, wraps the nav in a @container div and swaps
	// sm:/lg: breakpoint classes for @sm:/@lg: so the nav responds to its
	// container width, not the viewport. Default false (viewport breakpoints).
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultNavProps() NavProps {
	return NavProps{
		Sticky: true,
	}
}

// navDesktopLinksClass returns the responsive class for the desktop links
// container, swapping viewport-keyed (sm:) for container-keyed (@sm:) when
// the nav is container-aware. Both strings are complete Tailwind literals.
func navDesktopLinksClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:ms-6 @sm:flex @sm:flex-wrap @sm:gap-x-8 @sm:gap-y-2"
	}
	return "hidden sm:ms-6 sm:flex sm:flex-wrap sm:gap-x-8 sm:gap-y-2"
}

// Nav renders a responsive navigation bar
//
//	@navigation.Nav(navigation.NavProps{
//	   Brand: @myLogo(),
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	     {Href: "/about", Text: "About"},
//	   },
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ Nav(props NavProps) {
	{{ menuID := navMobileMenuID(props) }}
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@navInner(props, menuID)
		</div>
	} else {
		@navInner(props, menuID)
	}
}

templ navInner(props NavProps, menuID string) {
	<nav
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Main navigation") }
		class={ utils.Class("z-40 border-b border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900", props.Class),
			templ.KV("sticky top-0", props.Sticky) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
			<div class="flex min-h-16 items-center justify-between">
				<div class="flex">
					if props.Brand != nil {
						<div class="flex flex-shrink-0 items-center">
							@props.Brand
						</div>
					}
					<div class={ navDesktopLinksClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
						for _, link := range props.Links {
							@NavLink(link, props.CurrentPath)
						}
					</div>
				</div>
				if props.RightItems != nil {
					<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
						@props.RightItems
					</div>
				}
				@MobileMenuToggle(len(props.Links) > 0, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
			</div>
		</div>
		@MobileMenu(props.Links, props.CurrentPath, props.Nonce, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
	</nav>
}

// SimpleNavProps configures a minimal navigation with a text brand
type SimpleNavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	BrandText string
	BrandHref string
	Links     []NavLinkProps
	// RightItems is rendered on the right side of the bar (e.g. a ThemeToggle,
	// a sign-in button, a user menu). Forwarded to Nav.RightItems. Optional.
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
}

// DefaultSimpleNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSimpleNavProps() SimpleNavProps {
	return SimpleNavProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		BrandHref: "/",
		Sticky:    true,
	}
}

// SimpleNav renders a minimal navigation with text brand
//
//	@navigation.SimpleNav(navigation.SimpleNavProps{
//	   BrandText: "MyApp",
//	   BrandHref: "/",
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	   },
//	   RightItems: @layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", ""),
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ SimpleNav(props SimpleNavProps) {
	@Nav(NavProps{
		BaseProps:   props.GetBaseProps(),
		Brand:       simpleBrand(props.BrandText, props.BrandHref),
		Links:       props.Links,
		RightItems:  props.RightItems,
		CurrentPath: props.CurrentPath,
		Sticky:      props.Sticky,
	})
}

templ simpleBrand(text, href string) {
	<a href={ templ.SafeURL(href) } class="text-xl font-bold text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400">{ text }</a>
}

// FooterLink is one link in a FooterColumn.
type FooterLink struct {
	Text string
	Href string
}

// FooterColumn is a titled group of links in a multi-column footer.
type FooterColumn struct {
	Title string
	Links []FooterLink
}

// FooterProps configures a footer. When Columns is empty, Footer renders the
// legacy single-row brand+copyright layout (backward compatible). When
// Columns has entries, Footer renders a responsive multi-column grid with an
// optional brand column and a bottom bar.
type FooterProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	BrandText string
	// Columns renders titled link groups in a responsive grid. When non-empty,
	// switches to multi-column layout. The first column is preceded by a brand
	// block showing BrandText (if set). Empty = legacy single-row layout.
	Columns []FooterColumn
	// BottomBar renders below the columns (or below the legacy single-row when
	// Columns is empty). Use it for legal links, copyright, or fine print.
	BottomBar templ.Component
}

// DefaultFooterProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultFooterProps() FooterProps {
	return FooterProps{}
}

// Footer renders a site footer. Two layouts:
//
//  1. Legacy single-row (backward compat) — when Columns is empty. Centered
//     "© Year BrandText. All rights reserved." line.
//  2. Multi-column grid — when Columns is non-empty. Responsive grid of
//     titled link columns (`grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-8`) with an
//     optional brand block and a BottomBar slot for legal/copyright.
//
//	@navigation.Footer(navigation.FooterProps{BrandText: "MyApp"})
//	@navigation.Footer(navigation.FooterProps{
//	   BrandText: "Acme",
//	   Columns: []navigation.FooterColumn{
//	     {Title: "Product", Links: []navigation.FooterLink{{"Features", "/features"}}},
//	     {Title: "Company", Links: []navigation.FooterLink{{"About", "/about"}}},
//	   },
//	   BottomBar: templ.Raw(`<p>© 2026 Acme</p>`),
//	})
templ Footer(props FooterProps) {
	<footer
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-label="Footer"
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if len(props.Columns) == 0 {
			<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
				<p class="text-center text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
					&copy; { utils.CurrentYear() } { props.BrandText }. All rights reserved.
				</p>
				if props.BottomBar != nil {
					<div class="mt-4 text-center text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
						@props.BottomBar
					</div>
				}
			</div>
		} else {
			<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-12 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
				<div class="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-8">
					if props.BrandText != "" {
						<div class="col-span-2 md:col-span-1">
							<p class="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ props.BrandText }</p>
						</div>
					}
					for _, col := range props.Columns {
						<div>
							if col.Title != "" {
								<h3 class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ col.Title }</h3>
							}
							<ul class="mt-4 space-y-3">
								for _, link := range col.Links {
									<li>
										<a
											href={ templ.SafeURL(link.Href) }
											class={ "text-sm text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:text-white " + utils.TransitionColors }
										>
											{ link.Text }
										</a>
									</li>
								}
							</ul>
						</div>
					}
				</div>
				if props.BottomBar != nil {
					<div class="mt-8 border-t border-gray-200 pt-6 dark:border-gray-800">
						<div class="text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
							@props.BottomBar
						</div>
					</div>
				}
			</div>
		}
	</footer>
}
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// navLinkBaseClass is the shared class prefix for active and inactive nav links.
// py-1.5 keeps the link box ≥ 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 target size): pt-1 rendered
// a 20px target (M21/F097 audit).
const navLinkBaseClass = "inline-flex items-center border-b-2 px-2 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors

func navLinkClasses(isActive bool) string {
	if isActive {
		return navLinkBaseClass + " border-blue-500 text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
	}
	return navLinkBaseClass + " border-transparent text-gray-500 hover:border-gray-300 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:border-gray-600 dark:hover:text-gray-200"
}

func mobileNavLinkClass(isActive bool) string {
	base := "block border-s-4 py-2 ps-3 pe-4 text-base font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors
	if isActive {
		return base + " border-blue-500 bg-blue-50 text-blue-700 dark:bg-blue-900/20 dark:text-blue-300"
	}
	return base + " border-transparent text-gray-500 hover:border-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:border-gray-600 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:text-gray-200"
}

// IsActive returns true when href matches currentPath exactly. Shared by NavLink
// and SidebarNav so active-state detection stays consistent across the package.
func IsActive(href, currentPath string) bool {
	return href == currentPath
}

// NavLinkProps configures a single navigation link
type NavLinkProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Href     string
	Text     string
	External bool
	// Wire, when set with a non-empty URL, adds transport wiring to the
	// link: the anchor keeps its href (the no-JS fallback) AND carries the
	// action's dialect attributes (htmx: hx-get + hx-target; Datastar:
	// data-on:click). Use it for nav links that patch a page region instead
	// of navigating; the wire attrs also stay on the active link (clicking
	// re-fetches the region). Consumer Attrs spread after the wire
	// attributes, so a consumer-supplied hx-* overrides the action's.
	// Applies to NavLink, MobileNavLink, and therefore Nav, SimpleNav, and
	// MobileMenu.
	Wire *wire.Action
}

// navLinkWireAttrs renders the NavLink Wire action as anchor attributes.
// nil Wire (or an empty-URL action) renders nothing — the link keeps
// plain-href navigation. The action is CLONED with PreventDefault set
// (copy semantics — components never rewrite consumer specs): NavLink is
// always an <a>, and a Datastar-wired anchor with an href would otherwise
// patch AND navigate, because the runtime auto-preventDefaults only
// form+submit (decoded from the pinned v1.0.3 bundle). htmx ignores the
// flag — its engine intercepts wired clicks itself.
func navLinkWireAttrs(w *wire.Action) templ.Attributes {
	if w == nil {
		return nil
	}

	nav := *w
	nav.PreventDefault = true

	return nav.Attributes()
}

// DefaultNavLinkProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultNavLinkProps() NavLinkProps {
	return NavLinkProps{}
}

// activeSpanOrLink renders a span with aria-current when active, or a link when inactive.
// rel, when non-empty, adds a rel attribute to the <a> (e.g. "canonical", "prev", "next").
templ activeSpanOrLink(isActive bool, href string, text string, activeClass string, inactiveClass string, rel string) {
	if isActive {
		<span aria-current="page" class={ activeClass }>{ text }</span>
	} else {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ inactiveClass }
			if rel != "" {
				rel={ rel }
			}
		>{ text }</a>
	}
}

// navLinkAnchor renders the common anchor element shared by NavLink and
// MobileNavLink. The caller supplies the component-specific base class
// (active/inactive variant); consumer overrides from props.Class are merged
// via utils.Class so conflicting Tailwind utilities resolve correctly.
templ navLinkAnchor(props NavLinkProps, isActive bool, baseClass string) {
	<a
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		href={ templ.SafeURL(props.Href) }
		class={ utils.Class(baseClass, props.Class) }
		if isActive {
			aria-current="page"
		}
		if props.External {
			target="_blank"
			rel="noopener noreferrer"
		}
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ navLinkWireAttrs(props.Wire)... }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ props.Text }
	</a>
}

// NavLink renders a single navigation link with active state styling
//
//	@navigation.NavLink(navigation.NavLinkProps{Href: "/", Text: "Home"}, "/")
templ NavLink(props NavLinkProps, currentPath string) {
	{{ isActive := IsActive(props.Href, currentPath) }}
	@navLinkAnchor(props, isActive, navLinkClasses(isActive))
}

// MobileNavLink renders a mobile-friendly navigation link
//
//	@navigation.MobileNavLink(navigation.NavLinkProps{Href: "/", Text: "Home"}, "/")
templ MobileNavLink(props NavLinkProps, currentPath string) {
	{{ isActive := IsActive(props.Href, currentPath) }}
	@navLinkAnchor(props, isActive, mobileNavLinkClass(isActive))
}
package navigation

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
)

// inactivePageLinkClass is the shared class for a non-current pagination page link.
const inactivePageLinkClass = "relative inline-flex items-center px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-200 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus:z-20 focus:outline-offset-0"

// paginationMobileClass returns the class for the mobile-only pagination row,
// swapping sm: for @sm: when container-aware so the row responds to the
// container's width. Both strings are complete Tailwind literals.
func paginationMobileClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "flex flex-1 justify-between @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "flex flex-1 justify-between sm:hidden"
}

// paginationDesktopClass returns the class for the desktop pagination row,
// swapping sm: for @sm: when container-aware. Both strings are complete literals.
func paginationDesktopClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:flex @sm:flex-1 @sm:items-center @sm:justify-between"
	}
	return "hidden sm:flex sm:flex-1 sm:items-center sm:justify-between"
}

// PaginationProps configures a pagination component.
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the mobile/desktop pagination controls
// respond to the parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the
// viewport. Useful when Pagination is placed inside a card footer, drawer,
// sidebar, or other constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
type PaginationProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	CurrentPage uint
	TotalPages  uint
	BaseURL     string
	QueryParam  string
	MaxVisible  uint
	// ContainerAware, when true, adds @container to the nav and swaps sm:
	// breakpoint classes for @sm: so mobile/desktop controls respond to the
	// container width, not the viewport. Default false (viewport breakpoints).
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultPaginationProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultPaginationProps() PaginationProps {
	return PaginationProps{
		QueryParam: "page",
		MaxVisible: 5,
	}
}

func (p *PaginationProps) normalize() {
	if p.CurrentPage == 0 {
		p.CurrentPage = 1
	}
	if p.TotalPages >= 1 && p.CurrentPage > p.TotalPages {
		p.CurrentPage = p.TotalPages
	}
	if p.QueryParam == "" {
		p.QueryParam = "page"
	}
	if p.MaxVisible == 0 {
		p.MaxVisible = 5
	}
}

func (p PaginationProps) pageURL(page uint) string {
	u, err := url.Parse(p.BaseURL)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s?%s=%d", p.BaseURL, p.QueryParam, page)
	}
	q := u.Query()
	q.Set(p.QueryParam, strconv.FormatUint(uint64(page), 10))
	u.RawQuery = q.Encode()
	return u.String()
}

func paginationRange(current, total, maxVisible uint) (start, end uint) {
	if maxVisible == 0 {
		maxVisible = 5
	}
	if total <= maxVisible {
		return 1, total
	}
	half := maxVisible / 2
	if current > half {
		start = current - half
		end = current + half
		if maxVisible%2 == 0 {
			end--
		}
	} else {
		start = 1
		end = maxVisible
	}
	if end > total {
		end = total
		start = total - maxVisible + 1
	}
	return start, end
}

// mobilePageButton renders an enabled link or disabled span for mobile pagination
templ mobilePageButton(enabled bool, href string, marginClass string, text string) {
	if enabled {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ "relative inline-flex items-center rounded-md border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700", marginClass }
		>
			{ text }
		</a>
	} else {
		<span class={ "relative inline-flex items-center rounded-md border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-900 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 cursor-not-allowed", marginClass }>{ text }</span>
	}
}

// paginationArrowIcon renders the shared icon content for pagination arrows
templ paginationArrowIcon(srText string, svgPath string) {
	<span class="sr-only">{ srText }</span>
	@svg.FillIcon("h-5 w-5", svgPath, false)
}

// paginationArrow renders a previous/next arrow button for desktop pagination.
// roundedClass is the complete border-radius utility (e.g. "rounded-s-md") —
// passed as a literal so Tailwind's content scanner can detect it.
templ paginationArrow(enabled bool, href string, roundedClass string, ariaLabel string, srText string, svgPath string, rel string) {
	if enabled {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ "relative inline-flex items-center px-2 py-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus:z-20 focus:outline-offset-0", roundedClass }
			aria-label={ ariaLabel }
			if rel != "" {
				rel={ rel }
			}
		>
			@paginationArrowIcon(srText, svgPath)
		</a>
	} else {
		<span class={ "relative inline-flex items-center px-2 py-2 text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 cursor-not-allowed", roundedClass } aria-disabled="true" tabindex="-1">
			@paginationArrowIcon(srText, svgPath)
		</span>
	}
}

// paginationEllipsis renders a "..." indicator for truncated page ranges
templ paginationEllipsis() {
	<span class="relative inline-flex items-center px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600">
		&hellip;
	</span>
}

// paginationPageItem renders a single page number inside a list item.
// rel, when non-empty, adds a rel attribute to the link (e.g. "canonical" for page 1).
templ paginationPageItem(isActive bool, href string, text string, activeClass string, rel string) {
	<li>
		@activeSpanOrLink(isActive, href, text, activeClass, inactivePageLinkClass, rel)
	</li>
}

// paginationEllipsisItem renders an ellipsis indicator inside a list item.
templ paginationEllipsisItem() {
	<li>
		@paginationEllipsis()
	</li>
}

// Pagination renders a page navigation bar
//
//	@navigation.Pagination(navigation.PaginationProps{
//	   CurrentPage: 3,
//	   TotalPages: 10,
//	   BaseURL: "/users",
//	})
templ Pagination(props PaginationProps) {
	{{ props.normalize() }}
	if props.TotalPages > 1 {
		<nav
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Pagination") }
			class={ utils.Class("flex items-center justify-between", props.Class),
				templ.KV("@container", props.ContainerAware) }
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			<div class={ paginationMobileClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
				@mobilePageButton(props.CurrentPage > 1, props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage-1), "", "Previous")
				@mobilePageButton(props.CurrentPage < props.TotalPages, props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage+1), "ms-3", "Next")
			</div>
			<div class={ paginationDesktopClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
				<div>
					<p class="text-sm text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300">
						Showing page
						<span class="font-medium">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.CurrentPage) }</span>
						of
						<span class="font-medium">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.TotalPages) }</span>
					</p>
				</div>
				<div>
					<ol class="isolate inline-flex -space-x-px rounded-md shadow-xs" aria-label="Pagination">
						<li>
							@paginationArrow(
								props.CurrentPage > 1,
								props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage-1),
								"rounded-s-md",
								"Previous page",
								"Previous",
								svg.PathArrowLeft,
								"prev",
							)
						</li>
						{{ start, end := paginationRange(props.CurrentPage, props.TotalPages, props.MaxVisible) }}
						if start > 1 {
							@paginationPageItem(false, props.pageURL(1), "1", "", "canonical")
							@paginationEllipsisItem()
						}
						for p := start; p <= end; p++ {
							@paginationPageItem(
								p == props.CurrentPage,
								props.pageURL(p),
								fmt.Sprintf("%d", p),
								"relative z-10 inline-flex items-center bg-blue-600 dark:bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white focus:z-20 focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-blue-500",
								"",
							)
						}
						if end < props.TotalPages {
							@paginationEllipsisItem()
							@paginationPageItem(false, props.pageURL(props.TotalPages), fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.TotalPages), "", "")
						}
						<li>
							@paginationArrow(
								props.CurrentPage < props.TotalPages,
								props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage+1),
								"rounded-e-md",
								"Next page",
								"Next",
								svg.PathArrowRight,
								"next",
							)
						</li>
					</ol>
				</div>
			</div>
		</nav>
	}
}
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SidebarNavItem is one link in a vertical sidebar navigation.
type SidebarNavItem struct {
	Label  string
	Href   string
	Icon   icons.Name // optional; renders before the label if set
	Active bool
	// Section groups this item under a collapsible header. Items with
	// the same Section value are grouped together. Empty = ungrouped.
	Section string
}

// SidebarNavProps configures a vertical sidebar navigation panel.
type SidebarNavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Brand renders at the top of the sidebar (optional).
	Brand templ.Component
	// Header renders between Brand and the nav links (optional).
	// Useful for search/filter inputs.
	Header templ.Component
	// Items are the navigation links.
	Items []SidebarNavItem
	// Footer renders at the bottom of the sidebar (optional).
	Footer templ.Component
	// CurrentPath auto-detects the active item when set. An item is active when
	// its Href matches CurrentPath. Explicit Active=true on an item takes priority.
	CurrentPath string
}

// DefaultSidebarNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSidebarNavProps() SidebarNavProps {
	return SidebarNavProps{}
}

// sidebarItemActive returns true when the item should be highlighted.
// Explicit Active=true takes priority; otherwise the item is active when its
// Href exactly matches CurrentPath (unified with NavLink via IsActive).
func sidebarItemActive(item SidebarNavItem, currentPath string) bool {
	if item.Active {
		return true
	}
	if currentPath == "" || item.Href == "" {
		return false
	}
	return IsActive(item.Href, currentPath)
}

// sidebarNavGroup is a run of consecutive items with the same Section value.
type sidebarNavGroup struct {
	Section string // empty for ungrouped items
	Items   []SidebarNavItem
}

// sidebarNavGroups partitions items into groups of consecutive items sharing
// the same Section value. Items with empty Section form standalone groups.
func sidebarNavGroups(items []SidebarNavItem) []sidebarNavGroup {
	if len(items) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	var groups []sidebarNavGroup
	current := sidebarNavGroup{Section: items[0].Section}

	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Section != current.Section {
			groups = append(groups, current)
			current = sidebarNavGroup{Section: item.Section}
		}

		current.Items = append(current.Items, item)
	}

	groups = append(groups, current)

	return groups
}

// sidebarNavHasSections reports whether any item has a non-empty Section,
// which triggers the grouped rendering path.
func sidebarNavHasSections(items []SidebarNavItem) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Section != "" {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// sidebarGroupHasActive reports whether any item in a group is active.
func sidebarGroupHasActive(items []SidebarNavItem, currentPath string) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if sidebarItemActive(item, currentPath) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// SidebarNav renders a vertical sidebar with brand, nav links (each with an
// optional icon), and a footer slot. Designed for admin panels and dashboards.
//
//	@navigation.SidebarNav(navigation.SidebarNavProps{
//	   Brand: templ.Raw(`<span class="font-bold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">MyApp</span>`),
//	   Items: []navigation.SidebarNavItem{
//	     {Label: "Dashboard", Href: "/", Icon: icons.Squares2x2, Active: true},
//	     {Label: "Users", Href: "/users", Icon: icons.Users},
//	   },
//	   CurrentPath: "/users",
//	})
templ SidebarNav(props SidebarNavProps) {
	<aside
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("flex h-full w-64 flex-col border-e border-[var(--tc-sidebar-border)] bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-bg)]", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-label="Sidebar"
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Brand != nil {
			<div class="flex items-center gap-2.5 px-4 py-5">
				@props.Brand
			</div>
		}
		if props.Header != nil {
			<div class="px-3 pb-1">
				@props.Header
			</div>
		}
		<nav class="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto px-3 py-2" aria-label="Sidebar navigation">
			if sidebarNavHasSections(props.Items) {
				for _, group := range sidebarNavGroups(props.Items) {
					if group.Section != "" {
						{{ hasActive := sidebarGroupHasActive(group.Items, props.CurrentPath) }}
						<details
							class="group"
							if hasActive {
								open
							}
						>
							<summary class="flex cursor-pointer list-none items-center justify-between rounded-lg px-3 pt-3 pb-1 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-[var(--tc-sidebar-muted)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-muted-hover)] [&::-webkit-details-marker]:hidden">
								<span>{ group.Section }</span>
								@icons.Icon(icons.ChevronDown, "h-3 w-3 shrink-0 text-gray-600 transition-transform duration-200 motion-reduce:transition-none group-open:rotate-180 dark:text-gray-500")
							</summary>
							<div class="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
								for _, item := range group.Items {
									{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
									<a
										href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
										class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
											templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
											templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
										if active {
											aria-current="page"
										}
									>
										if item.Icon != "" {
											@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
										}
										{ item.Label }
									</a>
								}
							</div>
						</details>
					} else {
						for _, item := range group.Items {
							{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
							<a
								href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
								class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
									templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
									templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
								if active {
									aria-current="page"
								}
							>
								if item.Icon != "" {
									@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
								}
								{ item.Label }
							</a>
						}
					}
				}
			} else {
				for _, item := range props.Items {
					{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
					<a
						href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
						class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
							templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
							templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
						if active {
							aria-current="page"
						}
					>
						if item.Icon != "" {
							@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
						}
						{ item.Label }
					</a>
				}
			}
		</nav>
		if props.Footer != nil {
			<div class="px-4 py-3 text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
				@props.Footer
			</div>
		}
	</aside>
}

// AuthLayout renders a split-screen authentication page: a centered auth card
// on one side and a branding/feature panel on the other. The branding panel
// hides on mobile (lg: breakpoint), leaving the card centered.
//
// Pass a LoginCard (or any Card-wrapped form) as Card. Set PanelTitle,
// PanelText, and PanelFeatures to fill the branding panel. Set Reverse to flip
// the column order.
//
//	@recipes.AuthLayout(recipes.AuthLayoutProps{
//	   Card:          loginCard,
//	   PanelTitle:    "Acme",
//	   PanelText:     "Build better products, faster.",
//	   PanelFeatures: []string{"SOC 2 compliant", "99.9% uptime SLA"},
//	})
templ AuthLayout(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("min-h-dvh grid lg:grid-cols-2", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Reverse {
			@authPanel(props)
			@authCardSide(props)
		} else {
			@authCardSide(props)
			@authPanel(props)
		}
	</div>
}

// authCardSide renders the card column — centered vertically and horizontally.
templ authCardSide(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div class="flex items-center justify-center px-4 py-12">
		<div class="w-full max-w-sm">
			if props.Card != nil {
				@props.Card
			}
		</div>
	</div>
}

// authPanel renders the branding column — hidden on mobile, visible from the
// lg breakpoint. Uses a blue-tinted background that adapts to dark mode.
templ authPanel(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div class="hidden lg:flex lg:flex-col lg:justify-between bg-blue-600 dark:bg-blue-900 px-12 py-12">
		<div class="max-w-md space-y-6">
			if props.PanelTitle != "" {
				<h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-white">{ props.PanelTitle }</h2>
			}
			if props.PanelText != "" {
				<p class="text-lg text-blue-100">{ props.PanelText }</p>
			}
			if len(props.PanelFeatures) > 0 {
				<ul class="space-y-3">
					for _, feature := range props.PanelFeatures {
						<li class="flex items-start gap-3">
							@icons.IconWithStrokeWidth(icons.CheckCircle, "w-6 h-6 flex-shrink-0 text-blue-200", 1.5)
							<span class="text-blue-50">{ feature }</span>
						</li>
					}
				</ul>
			}
		</div>
		if props.PanelFooter != nil {
			<div class="mt-8">
				@props.PanelFooter
			</div>
		}
	</div>
}

import (

// AuthLayoutProps configures a recipes.AuthLayout screen — the canonical
// split-screen authentication layout: a centered auth card on one side and a
// branding/feature panel on the other. On mobile, the branding panel collapses
// to show only the card.
//
// The card content is consumer-supplied (typically a LoginCard, a signup form,
// or a password-reset form). The branding panel shows an optional title,
// description, feature bullets, and footer.
type AuthLayoutProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Card is the main auth content (typically a LoginCard or forms.Form
	// wrapped in a Card). Required.
	Card templ.Component
	// PanelTitle renders as a large heading in the branding panel. Optional.
	PanelTitle string
	// PanelText renders as body text under the PanelTitle. Optional.
	PanelText string
	// PanelFeatures is a list of bullet points rendered with checkmark icons
	// in the branding panel. Optional.
	PanelFeatures []string
	// PanelFooter renders at the bottom of the branding panel (e.g. a
	// testimonial, copyright, or security badge). Optional.
	PanelFooter templ.Component
	// Reverse flips the layout so the card appears on the right and the
	// branding panel on the left. Default: card left, panel right.
	// (On mobile the panel is always hidden.)
	Reverse bool
}

// DefaultAuthLayoutProps returns sensible defaults (empty).
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultAuthLayoutProps() AuthLayoutProps {
	return AuthLayoutProps{}
}

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/display"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/layout"

// Dashboard renders a complete dashboard screen: AppShell with a sidebar,
// sticky header, a page header (title + optional actions), a responsive stat
// card grid, and a charts grid. Every slot is consumer-supplied via
// templ.Component — Dashboard provides the scaffold only.
//
// Pass components for Sidebar (typically navigation.SidebarNav), Header
// (typically navigation.Nav), StatCards (display.StatCard instances), and
// Charts (display.Card-wrapped visualizations). Charts and StatCards slices
// may be empty.
//
//	@recipes.Dashboard(recipes.DashboardProps{
//	   Title:       "Overview",
//	   Subtitle:    "Last 30 days",
//	   Sidebar:     navSidebar,
//	   Header:      navHeader,
//	   StatCards:   []templ.Component{stat1, stat2, stat3, stat4},
//	   Charts:      []templ.Component{chart1, chart2},
//	});
templ Dashboard(props DashboardProps) {
	@layout.AppShell(layout.AppShellProps{
		BaseProps:      props.GetBaseProps(),
		Sidebar:        props.Sidebar,
		MobileNav:      props.MobileNav,
		Header:         props.Header,
		SidebarWidth:   props.SidebarWidth,
		StickyHeader:   true,
		Container:      true,
		ContainerWidth: layout.ContainerWidthDefault,
		Content:        dashboardContent(props),
	})
}

templ dashboardContent(props DashboardProps) {
	<div class="py-6 space-y-6">
		@display.PageHeader(display.PageHeaderProps{
			Title:      props.Title,
			Subtitle:   props.Subtitle,
			Breadcrumb: props.Breadcrumb,
			Action:     props.HeaderActions,
		})
		if len(props.StatCards) > 0 {
			@display.Grid(display.GridProps{
				Cols: display.GridCols4,
				Gap:  display.GridGapMD,
			}) {
				for _, card := range props.StatCards {
					@card
				}
			}
		}
		if len(props.Charts) > 0 {
			@display.Grid(display.GridProps{
				Cols: display.GridCols2,
				Gap:  display.GridGapLG,
			}) {
				for _, chart := range props.Charts {
					@chart
				}
			}
		}
	</div>
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/layout"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// DashboardProps configures a recipes.Dashboard screen. A dashboard is an
// AppShell with a stat-card grid and arbitrary chart/content slots. Every
// slot is a templ.Component so the consumer controls the actual content —
// recipes.Dashboard provides the layout scaffold only.
//
// Pass slots via templ.Component (Card.Body, navigation.Nav, display.Grid, etc.).
// The Sidebar slot is typically navigation.SidebarNav; the Header slot is
// typically navigation.Nav or navigation.SimpleNav. StatCards is a slice of
// display.StatCard components rendered inside a display.Grid. Charts is a
// slice of arbitrary chart components (display.Card-wrapped) rendered below
// the stat grid.
type DashboardProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Title and Subtitle render in a display.PageHeader at the top of the
	// content column.
	Title    string
	Subtitle string
	// Breadcrumb is an optional templ.Component slot (typically
	// navigation.Breadcrumbs) rendered above the title in the PageHeader.
	Breadcrumb templ.Component
	// Sidebar is the desktop sidebar slot (typically navigation.SidebarNav).
	// Required for the dashboard layout; pass nil for a sidebar-less shell.
	Sidebar templ.Component
	// MobileNav is the below-lg mobile navigation slot (typically
	// display.Drawer). Optional.
	MobileNav templ.Component
	// Header is the sticky top header slot (typically navigation.Nav). Optional.
	Header templ.Component
	// HeaderActions is rendered on the right side of the PageHeader (above
	// the stat grid). Use it for "Add" buttons, filters, or time-range
	// pickers. Optional.
	HeaderActions templ.Component
	// StatCards is the slice of display.StatCard components rendered in a
	// responsive 4-up grid at the top of the dashboard body.
	StatCards []templ.Component
	// Charts is the slice of chart/visualization components rendered below
	// the stat grid in a responsive 2-up grid. Each chart should be wrapped
	// in a display.Card by the consumer.
	Charts []templ.Component
	// SidebarWidth controls the AppShell sidebar width. Default
	// layout.SidebarWidthMD (16rem).
	SidebarWidth layout.SidebarWidth
}

// DefaultDashboardProps returns sensible defaults (MD sidebar, no slots).
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultDashboardProps() DashboardProps {
	return DashboardProps{
		SidebarWidth: layout.SidebarWidthDefault,
	}
}

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/display"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// LoginCard renders a centered sign-in card with a header, form body, optional
// OAuth divider + buttons, and a footer. The canonical login screen.
//
// Pass a forms.Form as FormBody (typically with Layout: forms.FormLayoutStack
// for vertical label-above-input layout). Pass display.Button components in
// OAuthButtons for "Continue with X" options.
//
//	@recipes.LoginCard(recipes.LoginCardProps{
//	   Title:    "Sign in to Acme",
//	   Subtitle: "Welcome back",
//	   FormBody: signInForm,
//	   OAuthButtons: templ.Raw(`<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3">…</div>`),
//	   Footer:   templ.Raw(`<p>Need an account? <a href="/signup">Sign up</a></p>`),
//	})
templ LoginCard(props LoginCardProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("min-h-dvh flex items-center justify-center px-4 py-12", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-sm">
			@display.Card(display.CardProps{
				Title:    props.Title,
				Subtitle: props.Subtitle,
				Padding:  display.CardPaddingMD,
				Body:     loginBody(props),
				Footer:   props.Footer,
			})
		</div>
	</div>
}

templ loginBody(props LoginCardProps) {
	<div class="space-y-4">
		if props.FormBody != nil {
			@props.FormBody
		}
		if props.OAuthButtons != nil {
			<div class="relative py-2">
				<div class="absolute inset-0 flex items-center" aria-hidden="true">
					<div class="w-full border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700"></div>
				</div>
				<div class="relative flex justify-center">
					<span class={ "bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-2 text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400" }>OR</span>
				</div>
			</div>
			@props.OAuthButtons
		}
	</div>
}

// SettingsLayoutProps configures a recipes.SettingsLayout screen — the
// canonical "section nav on the left, form content on the right" pattern
// used by almost every settings page in every admin panel.
//
// The aside is a vertical list of section links; the main is a stack of
// Card-wrapped forms (one per section). Both are consumer-supplied
// templ.Component slots.
type SettingsLayoutProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Title and Subtitle render at the top of the page.
	Title    string
	Subtitle string
	// Aside is the section navigation slot (typically a Card-wrapped list
	// of links to #section-id anchors). Required.
	Aside templ.Component
	// Sections is the list of form sections rendered in the main column.
	// Each section is rendered as a Card with Title + a form body. The
	// Section.ID becomes the card's id (for anchor navigation from Aside).
	Sections []SettingsSection
}

// SettingsSection is one titled section of a settings page.
type SettingsSection struct {
	// ID is used as the anchor target (id attribute) so the Aside links
	// can jump to it. Optional but recommended.
	ID string
	// Title renders as the Card header.
	Title string
	// Subtitle renders as muted text under the Title. Optional.
	Subtitle string
	// Body is the form content of the section. Typically a forms.Form
	// or a Card.Body slot. Required.
	Body templ.Component
}

// DefaultSettingsLayoutProps returns sensible defaults (empty).
func DefaultSettingsLayoutProps() SettingsLayoutProps {
	return SettingsLayoutProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal
}

import (

	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"

	"time"

// TestAddSmoke exercises the real `tc add` binary end-to-end in a throwaway
// directory (TODO #283c, 2026-09-23): the unit tests pin the registry, but
// only an exec'd binary proves the os.Args dispatch, the source-embed read,
// and the file writes actually work together. eyebrow is a single-file
// display component; auth_layout is a recipe shipping a *_types.go companion
// — the two shapes `tc add` must handle.
func TestAddSmoke(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	bin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "tc-build")

	buildCtx, cancelBuild := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
	t.Cleanup(cancelBuild)

	build := exec.CommandContext(buildCtx, "go", "build", "-o", bin, ".")
	if out, err := build.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("go build tc: %v\n%s", err, out)
	}

	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		wantFiles []string
	}{
		{name: "eyebrow", wantFiles: []string{"eyebrow.templ"}},
		{name: "auth_layout", wantFiles: []string{"auth_layout.templ", "auth_layout_types.go"}},
	}

	for _, tcase := range cases {
		t.Run(tcase.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			dir := t.TempDir()

			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
			defer cancel()

			add := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, "add", tcase.name)
			add.Dir = dir

			out, err := add.CombinedOutput()
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("tc add %s: %v\n%s", tcase.name, err, out)
			}

			for _, want := range tcase.wantFiles {
				got := filepath.Join(dir, "components", want)

				data, err := os.ReadFile(got)
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("tc add %s did not produce %s: %v", tcase.name, got, err)

					continue
				}

				if len(data) == 0 {
					t.Errorf("scaffolded %s is empty", got)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
package main

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// TestPackageDepsCoverPackageFiles keeps the --list-deps output honest
// (backlog #285, 2026-09-23): every non-test, non-generated .go file in a
// mirrored package must be either listed in packageDeps[pkg] (a sibling
// `tc add` does not copy) or be a *_types.go companion (which `tc add`
// copies automatically next to its .templ). The kanban, chart,
// calendar-nav, and heading-tag helper files all predate this test and were
// silently missing from `tc add <component> --list-deps`.
func TestPackageDepsCoverPackageFiles(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, pkg := range mirroredPackages {
		entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join("..", "..", pkg))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read package dir %s: %v", pkg, err)
		}

		listed := make(map[string]bool)
		for _, dep := range packageDeps[pkg] {
			listed[dep] = true
		}

		for _, entry := range entries {
			name := entry.Name()
			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".go") {
				continue
			}

			switch {
			case strings.HasSuffix(name, "_test.go"),
				strings.HasSuffix(name, "_templ.go"),
				strings.HasSuffix(name, "_types.go"),
				name == "doc.go":
				continue
			}

			if !listed[name] {
				t.Errorf(
					"%s/%s is not listed in packageDeps[%q] — add it (the deps listing must match what a vendored component needs)",
					pkg,
					name,
					pkg,
				)
			}
		}

		// Listed entries must also exist on disk — a stale dep name is as
		// misleading as a missing one.
		for _, dep := range packageDeps[pkg] {
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join("..", "..", pkg, dep)); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("packageDeps[%q] lists %q which does not exist", pkg, dep)
			}
		}
	}
}
// Package main is the `tc` CLI: scaffolding tool for templ-components.
// See README at docs/cli.md for the full usage guide.
package main
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

// cmdDoctor diagnoses the top consumer-integration traps in one command:
// Tailwind source scanning, the jsonv2 build flag, templ version pinning,
// committed generated files, and (inside the library repo) hook adoption.
// Every check prints pass/fail + a fix hint; the exit code is non-zero when
// any check fails so CI can gate on it.
//
// It runs in TWO contexts and adapts:
//   - inside the templ-components repo (checks library-side invariants),
//   - in a consumer project (checks the consumer-side integration traps).
func cmdDoctor(_ *registry, args []string) {
	cssOverride := ""

	for i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {
		if args[i] == "--css" && i+1 < len(args) {
			cssOverride = args[i+1]
			i++
		}
	}

	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "tc doctor — templ-components environment check")
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout)

	failures := 0
	failures += checkTailwindSources(cssOverride)
	failures += checkGOEXPERIMENT()
	failures += checkTemplVersionPinned()
	failures += checkGeneratedCommitted()
	failures += checkHooksAdoption()
	failures += checkNoncelessScripts()

	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout)

	if failures > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "result: %d check(s) FAILED — see the fix hints above.\n", failures)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, "result: all checks passed.")
}

// doctorCheck prints one pass/fail line and returns 1 on failure.
func doctorCheck(name string, ok bool, hint string) int {
	status := "pass"
	if !ok {
		status = "FAIL"
	}

	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  [%s] %s\n", status, name)

	if !ok && hint != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "         fix: %s\n", hint)
	}

	if !ok {
		return 1
	}

	return 0
}

// checkTailwindSources verifies the consumer's CSS entry point scans the
// directory that holds copied .templ components (the #1 integration trap:
// @source path resolved relative to the CSS file, missing every class).
// Discovery is content-based (#35): a cssOverride (--css PATH) is checked
// directly; otherwise the fixed filename candidates run as the fast path
// and a depth-bounded walk for ANY *.css carrying an @source line takes
// over — the filename probe missed working layouts like assets/css/input.css.
func checkTailwindSources(cssOverride string) int {
	if cssOverride != "" {
		return cssEntryCheck(cssOverride)
	}

	if entry := cssFastPathEntry("."); entry != "" {
		return cssEntryCheck(entry)
	}

	// Content discovery: first @source-carrying css that also scans .templ
	// passes. A hit that does NOT scan .templ is kept as the FAIL hint — that
	// per-file trap is exactly what this check exists for (#35).
	entry, found := discoverCSSEntry(".")
	if !found {
		return doctorCheck(
			"Tailwind entry (app.css) found",
			false,
			"no css file with an @source line found (searched "+strconv.Itoa(
				cssDiscoveryMaxDepth+1,
			)+" directory levels, skipping node_modules/vendor/.git) — run `tc init` and compile with tailwindcss, or point `tc doctor --css <path>` at the entry",
		)
	}

	return cssEntryCheck(entry)
}

// cssFastPathEntry returns the first well-known candidate filename that
// exists under root ("" when none do) — cheap and ordered before discovery.
func cssFastPathEntry(root string) string {
	for _, candidate := range cssCandidates {
		path := filepath.Join(root, candidate)
		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
			return path
		}
	}

	return ""
}

// discoverCSSEntry walks root depth-bounded for a CSS file carrying an
// @source line. Returns the first entry that ALSO scans **/*.templ when one
// exists; otherwise the first @source-carrying css (the FAIL hint) and found=true.
func discoverCSSEntry(root string) (string, bool) {
	hintPath := ""
	scanPath := ""

	walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, dirent os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			//nolint:nilerr // unreadable entries are not this check's business
			return nil
		}

		if dirent.IsDir() && cssDirPruned(root, path, dirent.Name()) {
			return filepath.SkipDir
		}

		if !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".css") {
			return nil
		}

		//nolint:gosec // diagnostic tool reading the consumer's own tree; symlink traversal is the point
		content, readErr := os.ReadFile(path)
		if readErr != nil {
			//nolint:nilerr // unreadable entries are not this check's business
			return nil
		}

		text := string(content)
		if !strings.Contains(text, "@source") {
			return nil
		}

		if hintPath == "" {
			hintPath = path
		}

		if strings.Contains(text, "**/*.templ") {
			scanPath = path

			return filepath.SkipAll
		}

		return nil
	})
	if walkErr != nil {
		return "", false
	}

	if scanPath != "" {
		return scanPath, true
	}

	return hintPath, hintPath != ""
}

// cssDirPruned reports whether a directory in the discovery walk must be
// skipped outright: hidden dirs, dependency/vendor trees, and anything past
// the depth bound (measured relative to the walk root).
func cssDirPruned(root, path, name string) bool {
	switch {
	case name == ".git" || name == "node_modules" || name == "dist" || name == "vendor":
		return true
	case strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".":
		return true
	case strings.Count(strings.TrimPrefix(path, root), string(os.PathSeparator)) >= cssDiscoveryMaxDepth:
		return true
	}

	return false
}

// cssEntryCheck renders the pass/fail verdict for one concrete css entry:
// it must carry an @source line AND scan **/*.templ (the class-yielding part).
func cssEntryCheck(path string) int {
	//nolint:gosec // explicit consumer-supplied path via --css; a local doctor has no privilege boundary to guard
	content, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return doctorCheck("Tailwind entry readable ("+path+")", false, "cannot read "+path+": "+err.Error())
	}

	text := string(content)

	return doctorCheck(
		"Tailwind @source scans .templ files ("+path+")",
		strings.Contains(text, "@source") && strings.Contains(text, "**/*.templ"),
		"add `@source \"./**/*.templ\";` (path relative to the CSS FILE, not the CWD — the demo uses @source \"../../**/*.templ\")",
	)
}

// checkGOEXPERIMENT verifies the jsonv2 build flag is set (env, go.mod
// toolchain directive, or Go >= 1.27 where it is stable). Without it the
// build fails with `build constraints exclude all Go files in .../encoding/json/v2`.
func checkGOEXPERIMENT() int {
	if os.Getenv("GOEXPERIMENT") == "jsonv2" {
		return doctorCheck("GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 (env)", true, "")
	}

	if goModDeclaresJSONv2() {
		return doctorCheck("GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 (go.mod toolchain directive)", true, "")
	}

	return doctorCheck(
		"GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 required (errorpage uses encoding/json/v2)",
		false,
		"`export GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` (or use Go 1.27+, or set `toolchain`/`go` accordingly); symptom without it: 'build constraints exclude all Go files in .../encoding/json/v2'",
	)
}

// goModDeclaresJSONv2 reports whether a go.mod in the CWD declares a Go
// version where jsonv2 is stable (1.27+).
func goModDeclaresJSONv2() bool {
	content, err := os.ReadFile("go.mod")
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}

	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(string(content), "\n") {
		fields := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(line))

		if len(fields) == 2 && (fields[0] == "go" || fields[0] == "toolchain") {
			version := strings.TrimPrefix(fields[1], "go")
			major, minor, ok := parseGoVersion(version)

			if ok && (major > 1 || (major == 1 && minor >= jsonv2StableMinor)) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}

	return false
}

// parseGoVersion extracts major.minor from "1.26.7"-style strings.
func parseGoVersion(version string) (int, int, bool) {
	parts := strings.SplitN(version, ".", goVersionParts)
	if len(parts) < 2 {
		return 0, 0, false
	}

	var major, minor int

	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(parts[0]+"."+parts[1], "%d.%d", &major, &minor); err != nil {
		return 0, 0, false
	}

	return major, minor, true
}

// checkTemplVersionPinned warns when a consumer's go.mod pulls a templ
// version older than templGeneratedWith (the generator version this library
// pins — keep the doctor constant in lockstep with utils' pin, guarded by
// TestTemplVersionPin).
func checkTemplVersionPinned() int {
	return checkTemplVersionPinnedAt("go.mod")
}

// checkTemplVersionPinnedAt is the path-injected core of the pin check
// (testable without chdir, paralleltest-clean).
func checkTemplVersionPinnedAt(path string) int {
	content, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return doctorCheck("go.mod readable (templ pin check)", false, "run inside a Go module")
	}

	pinned, found := templRequireVersion(string(content))
	if !found {
		return doctorCheck(
			"templ dependency present",
			false,
			"add github.com/a-h/templ — the generated components need its runtime",
		)
	}

	want := strings.TrimPrefix(templGeneratedWith, "v")

	return doctorCheck(
		"templ "+pinned+" compatible with generated code ("+templGeneratedWith+")",
		compareSemver(pinned, want) >= 0,
		"`go get github.com/a-h/templ@"+templGeneratedWith+"` — older generators emit incompatible *_templ.go runtime calls",
	)
}

// templRequireVersion extracts the github.com/a-h/templ version from go.mod
// content WITHOUT golang.org/x/mod (the dependency budget is closed, #35):
// both the single-line and the block require forms resolve, `// indirect`
// suffixes and trailing comments are stripped, and other directives
// (replace/exclude) are ignored — their lines never carry a require-shaped
// version field for templ.
func templRequireVersion(content string) (string, bool) {
	inRequireBlock := false

	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(content, "\n") {
		line := stripLineComment(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}

		fields := strings.Fields(line)

		blockStart, blockEnd := requireBlockMarkers(fields)

		switch {
		case blockStart:
			inRequireBlock = true
		case blockEnd:
			inRequireBlock = false
		case inRequireBlock && isTemplRequire(fields):
			return strings.TrimPrefix(fields[1], "v"), true
		case isSingleLineTemplRequire(fields):
			return strings.TrimPrefix(fields[2], "v"), true
		}
	}

	return "", false
}

// stripLineComment removes a trailing // comment (go.mod has no other
// comment syntax) and the whitespace it leaves behind.
func stripLineComment(line string) string {
	line, _, _ = strings.Cut(line, "//")

	return strings.TrimSpace(line)
}

// requireBlockMarkers classifies a directive line as opening ("require (",
// written with or without the space) or closing (")") a require block.
func requireBlockMarkers(fields []string) (bool, bool) {
	start := len(fields) >= 1 && (fields[0] == "require(" ||
		(fields[0] == "require" && len(fields) >= 2 && fields[1] == "("))
	end := len(fields) == 1 && fields[0] == ")"

	return start, end
}

// isTemplRequire matches a block-form line naming templ with a version:
// `github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100 [// indirect]`.
func isTemplRequire(fields []string) bool {
	return len(fields) >= 2 && fields[0] == templModulePath && isVersionLiteral(fields[1])
}

// isSingleLineTemplRequire matches the one-line form:
// `require github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100`.
func isSingleLineTemplRequire(fields []string) bool {
	return len(fields) >= 3 && fields[0] == "require" && fields[1] == templModulePath
}

// isVersionLiteral reports whether s looks like a semver literal (v1.2.3) —
// the guard that keeps replace lines (`mod => mod v1.2.3` aside: their
// second field is `=>`) and other directives out of the require parse.
func isVersionLiteral(s string) bool {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "v") || len(s) < 2 {
		return false
	}

	return s[1] >= '0' && s[1] <= '9'
}

const (
	// goVersionParts bounds version parsing to major.minor.patch.
	goVersionParts = 3
	// jsonv2StableMinor is the Go minor where encoding/json/v2 needs no flag.
	jsonv2StableMinor = 27
	// templModulePath is the upstream templ module the generated code needs.
	templModulePath = "github.com/a-h/templ"
	// cssDiscoveryMaxDepth bounds the @source-entry walk (path separator
	// count of a DIRECTORY) so huge trees cannot stall the doctor.
	cssDiscoveryMaxDepth = 5
)

// cssCandidates is the fast-path probe list, checked before content
// discovery (both cover the same check; #35).
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // static probe table, the doctor's only config
var cssCandidates = []string{"app.css", "static/app.css", "assets/app.css", "css/app.css"}

// templGeneratedWith is the generator version the library pins.
const templGeneratedWith = "v0.3.1100"

// compareSemver compares dotted numeric versions; -1, 0, or 1.
func compareSemver(a, b string) int {
	aParts, bParts := strings.Split(a, "."), strings.Split(b, ".")

	for i := range max(len(aParts), len(bParts)) {
		aPart, bPart := 0, 0

		if i < len(aParts) {
			_, _ = fmt.Sscanf(aParts[i], "%d", &aPart)
		}

		if i < len(bParts) {
			_, _ = fmt.Sscanf(bParts[i], "%d", &bPart)
		}

		switch {
		case aPart < bPart:
			return -1
		case aPart > bPart:
			return 1
		}
	}

	return 0
}

// nonceConsumers lists the library components that render an inline
// <script> gated on the consumer-supplied Nonce. A call site that passes an
// empty nonce renders markup that silently dies under a nonce-locked CSP —
// the 2026-10-12 fleet-audit bug class (cqrs-htmx CopyButton ×13, GmbH
// ThemeToggle, KeyHolderAI ToastContainer). docs/nonce-consumers.md is the
// human-readable twin of this table; TestNonceConsumerDocsSync pins them
// together.
var nonceConsumers = []struct{ Qualified, Note string }{ //nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level scan table, the docs twin pins it
	{"display.Accordion", "chevron rotation script"},
	{"display.Carousel", "prev/next/dot navigation script"},
	{"display.ContextMenu", "menu keyboard-nav + positioning script"},
	{"display.CopyButton", "clipboard singleton script"},
	{"display.Dropdown", "menu keyboard-nav + positioning script"},
	{"display.Drawer", "auto-open + backdrop-click script"},
	{"display.KanbanBoard", "drag-and-drop + optimistic move script"},
	{"display.Lightbox", "viewer navigation script"},
	{"display.Modal", "auto-open + backdrop-click script"},
	{"display.Table", "row-click script when any TableRow.Href is set"},
	{"display.Tabs", "client-side tab switching (when not Wire-driven)"},
	{"errorpage.ErrorPage", "go-back singleton script"},
	{"errorpage.NotFound404", "go-back singleton script"},
	{"echarts.EChart", "chart init script"},
	{"feedback.Alert", "dismiss script when Dismissible"},
	{"feedback.Toast", "dismiss + auto-dismiss timer script"},
	{"feedback.ToastContainer", "container for injected toasts"},
	{"forms.Combobox", "filter/selection singleton script"},
	{"forms.DirtyGuard", "unsaved-changes guard script"},
	{"forms.Form", "validity-bridge singleton script"},
	{"forms.Slider", "track-fill value sync script"},
	{"forms.TagsInput", "tag add/remove script"},
	{"htmx.GlobalErrorHandling", "global error→toast pipeline script"},
	{"htmx.PolledRegion", "poll loop script when Eager"},
	{"layout.ThemeScript", "FOUC-prevention head script"},
	{"layout.ThemeToggle", "theme toggle script"},
}

// Note: MobileMenu's toggle script also consumes a nonce; consumers reach it
// through navigation.Nav/SimpleNav (pass the nonce to the nav component).
// It is documented in docs/nonce-consumers.md rather than the table above
// because the consuming constructor is positional-arg based.

// checkNoncelessScripts scans the consumer's .templ sources for call sites
// that pass an empty nonce to a script-emitting component — markup that
// silently dies under a nonce-locked CSP. Findings FAIL when the repo
// declares a Content-Security-Policy anywhere in its .go sources, and stay
// informational otherwise (nothing is broken yet, but the trap is armed).
func checkNoncelessScripts() int {
	workDir, _ := os.Getwd()

	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(workDir, "go.mod")); err != nil {
		return 0 // not a Go module — check does not apply
	}

	if len(walkTemplSources(workDir)) == 0 {
		return 0 // no templ sources — check does not apply
	}

	findings := scanNonceFindings(workDir)

	if len(findings) == 0 {
		return doctorCheck("no nonce-less script call sites in .templ sources", true, "")
	}

	cspDeclared := declaresCSP(workDir)

	hint := strings.Join(findings, "; ") +
		" — see docs/nonce-consumers.md for the full consuming-component table"
	if cspDeclared {
		return doctorCheck(
			fmt.Sprintf("no nonce-less script call sites in .templ sources (%d found, CSP declared)", len(findings)),
			false,
			hint,
		)
	}

	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  info: %d nonce-less script call site(s), but no CSP declared yet — "+
		"the scripts run today and will silently die the day you adopt one\n", len(findings))

	return 0
}

// scanNonceFindings returns file:line findings for nonce-less call sites to
// script-emitting components under root. Kept separate from the check so the
// tests can assert on the raw findings.
func scanNonceFindings(root string) []string {
	propsRe := regexp.MustCompile(`Nonce:\s*""`)
	positionalRe := regexp.MustCompile(
		`(ThemeScript|ThemeToggle|ToastContainer|MobileMenu)\(([^()]|"[^"]*")*?,?\s*(""|"[a-z][a-z0-9-]*")`)

	findings := []string{}

	for _, file := range walkTemplSources(root) {
		data, err := os.ReadFile(file)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}

		lines := strings.Split(string(data), "\n")
		for i, line := range lines {
			code := stripTemplComment(line)
			if propsRe.MatchString(code) {
				findings = append(findings, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d: Nonce: \"\" — thread the request nonce", file, i+1))

				continue
			}

			if positionalRe.MatchString(code) {
				findings = append(findings, fmt.Sprintf(
					"%s:%d: empty/fake literal nonce passed to a nonce-consuming constructor", file, i+1))
			}
		}
	}

	return findings
}

// walkTemplSources returns .templ files under root, skipping generated
// files, vendor/node_modules, and the library's own packages.
func walkTemplSources(root string) []string {
	files := []string{}

	skip := map[string]bool{
		"vendor": true, "node_modules": true, ".git": true,
		"display": true, "feedback": true, "forms": true, "layout": true,
		"navigation": true, "errorpage": true, "htmx": true, "datastar": true,
		"utils": true, "icons": true, "cmd": true, "examples": true,
		"internal": true, "charts": true, "recipes": true, "website": true,
		"integration": true,
	}

	_ = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, dirEntry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable entries; a scan must not abort on one bad path
		}

		if dirEntry.IsDir() {
			if skip[dirEntry.Name()] {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(path, ".templ") && !strings.HasSuffix(path, "_templ.go") {
			files = append(files, path)
		}

		return nil
	})

	return files
}

// stripTemplComment removes an HTML comment tail so prose never trips the
// nonce regexes (same defense as the utils compliance scans).
func stripTemplComment(line string) string {
	if before, _, ok := strings.Cut(line, "<!--"); ok {
		return before
	}

	return line
}

// declaresCSP reports whether any .go file under root (excluding tests,
// vendor, and generated code) mentions a Content-Security-Policy.
func declaresCSP(root string) bool {
	cspRe := regexp.MustCompile(`Content-Security-Policy`)
	found := false

	_ = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, dirEntry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || found {
			return filepath.SkipAll
		}

		if dirEntry.IsDir() {
			switch dirEntry.Name() {
			case "vendor", "node_modules", ".git", "testdata":
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".go") || strings.HasSuffix(path, "_test.go") ||
			strings.HasSuffix(path, "_templ.go") {
			return nil
		}

		data, readErr := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // diagnostic scan over the consumer's own tree
		if readErr == nil && cspRe.Match(data) {
			found = true
		}

		return nil
	})

	return found
}

// checkGeneratedCommitted applies only inside the library repo: a .templ
// source without its committed *_templ.go means the proxy will serve
// uncompilable code.
func checkGeneratedCommitted() int {
	wd, _ := os.Getwd()

	// Heuristic: inside the library repo a component package dir exists.
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wd, "display")); err != nil {
		return 0 // consumer project — check does not apply
	}

	missing := []string{}

	for _, pkg := range []string{"display", "feedback", "forms", "layout", "navigation", "errorpage", "htmx", "datastar"} {
		entries, err := os.ReadDir(pkg)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}

		for _, entry := range entries {
			name := entry.Name()
			if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".templ") || entry.IsDir() {
				continue
			}

			generated := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".templ") + "_templ.go"
			if _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(pkg, generated)); statErr != nil {
				missing = append(missing, filepath.Join(pkg, generated))
			}
		}
	}

	return doctorCheck(
		"every .templ has its *_templ.go (library repo)",
		len(missing) == 0,
		"run `templ generate ./...` and COMMIT the *_templ.go files (proxy serves the tag as-is): "+strings.Join(
			missing,
			", ",
		),
	)
}

// checkHooksAdoption applies only inside the library repo: the tracked
// .githooks/ guards are active only when core.hooksPath points there.
func checkHooksAdoption() int {
	wd, _ := os.Getwd()

	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wd, ".githooks")); err != nil {
		return 0 // consumer project — check does not apply
	}

	hooksPath := gitConfig("core.hooksPath")

	return doctorCheck(
		"core.hooksPath=.githooks (library repo)",
		hooksPath == ".githooks",
		"run `scripts/setup-hooks.sh` — otherwise the tracked pre-commit guards are inactive",
	)
}

// gitConfig reads a git config value via git itself (respects includes,
// scopes, and the `key = value` spacing variants).
func gitConfig(key string) string {
	ctx := context.Background()

	//nolint:gosec // key is a hardcoded literal from this file, never user input
	out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "config", "--get", key).Output()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}
