// TestNonceConsumerIntegrationSync pins the doctor's nonceConsumers table to
// the integration nonce render tables (third leg of the #407 guard triad:
// doctor ⇔ docs is TestNonceConsumerDocsSync, doctor ⇔ integration is this).
//
// Direction 1 — every doctor entry's component name must appear in at least
// one integration render table (TestAllInlineScriptsHaveNonce's with-nonce
// direction or TestNoEmptyNonceAttribute's omit-empty direction), so no
// scannable component escapes the library's own nonce verification.
//
// Direction 2 — every integration table entry must map back to a doctor
// entry or a documented exception, so the render tables never verify a
// component the doctor cannot scan for.
//
// Integration entry names may carry variant suffixes (KanbanBoardWired,
// TableWithRowHref, PolledRegionEager); a doctor entry matches when the
// integration name starts with the doctor's short name.
func TestNonceConsumerIntegrationSync(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	integrationNames := parseIntegrationRenderTableNames(t, filepath.Join("..", "..", "integration"))

	if len(integrationNames) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no integration render-table entries found — the tables moved or were renamed")
	}

	// Direction 1: doctor → integration.
	for _, consumer := range nonceConsumers {
		short := consumer.Qualified[strings.LastIndex(consumer.Qualified, ".")+1:]

		if !slicesContainsPrefix(integrationNames, short) {
			t.Errorf(
				"nonceConsumers entry %q has no integration render-table coverage (expected an entry starting with %q in integration/csp_nonce_test.go or integration/nonce_omit_empty_test.go) — add it to both tables in the same commit",
				consumer.Qualified,
				short,
			)
		}
	}

	// Direction 2: integration → doctor.
	//
	// Documented exceptions: entries that are deliberately not doctor-scan
	// targets — variant renderings of a scanned component, cross-module
	// runtime emitters the doctor reaches through their component wrapper,
	// and positional-arg components covered in docs/nonce-consumers.md prose.
	exceptions := map[string]string{
		"DatastarSDKScript":  "runtime loader; consumers reach it via components/layout.templ (docs prose)",
		"EChartsSDKScript":   "runtime loader twin of the scanned echarts.EChart",
		"ViewTransitions":    "config script without a Nonce prop (htmx global setting)",
		"SSEErrorHandling":   "datastar module twin of the scanned htmx.GlobalErrorHandling",
		"DatastarLiveRegion": "datastar module; documented in docs/nonce-consumers.md prose",
		"MobileMenu":         "positional-arg component; documented prose exception (see nonceConsumers comment)",
		"ErrorAlert":         "renders via the scanned errorpage script path",
		"Script":             "external-script helper; nonce optional by design (src= needs no nonce)",
		"BaseSelfHostedHTMX": "layout.Base whole-page rendering (ThemeScript + self-host htmx inside)",
		"TagsInput":          "",
		"PolledRegionEager":  "",
		"TableWithRowHref":   "",
		"KanbanBoardWired":   "",
	}

	for _, name := range integrationNames {
		if slicesHasDoctorEntry(nonceConsumers, name) {
			continue
		}

		if _, ok := exceptions[name]; !ok {
			t.Errorf(
				"integration render-table entry %q has no nonceConsumers scan entry — add it to cmd/tc/doctor.go's table (and docs/nonce-consumers.md) or to this test's exception list with a reason",
				name,
			)
		}
	}
}

// parseIntegrationRenderTableNames extracts the entry names from the
// `{"Name", ...}` rows of both integration nonce render tables.
func parseIntegrationRenderTableNames(t *testing.T, integrationDir string) []string {
	t.Helper()

	files := []string{"csp_nonce_test.go", "nonce_omit_empty_test.go"}
	entryRe := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\s*\{"([A-Za-z0-9]+)",`)
	seen := map[string]bool{}

	var names []string

	for _, f := range files {
		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(integrationDir, f))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read integration/%s: %v", f, err)
		}

		for _, m := range entryRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(string(data), -1) {
			if !seen[m[1]] {
				seen[m[1]] = true
				names = append(names, m[1])
			}
		}
	}

	return names
}

// slicesHasDoctorEntry reports whether any doctor entry's short name is a
// prefix of name (integration entries may carry variant suffixes).
func slicesHasDoctorEntry(consumers []struct {
	Qualified string
	Note      string
}, name string,
) bool {
	for _, c := range consumers {
		short := c.Qualified[strings.LastIndex(c.Qualified, ".")+1:]
		if strings.HasPrefix(name, short) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// slicesContainsPrefix reports whether any entry starts with prefix.
func slicesContainsPrefix(names []string, prefix string) bool {
	for _, n := range names {
		if strings.HasPrefix(n, prefix) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}
package main

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// writeFile writes content to path, creating parent directories.
func writeFile(t *testing.T, path, content string) {
	t.Helper()

	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("mkdir %s: %v", filepath.Dir(path), err)
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", path, err)
	}
}

// TestNonceConsumerDocsSync pins docs/nonce-consumers.md to the doctor's
// nonceConsumers scan table: every table entry must appear in the docs and
// vice versa. The docs are the human-readable twin of the scan list (F-058,
// issue #407) — the 2026-10-12 fleet audit shipped three repos of dead
// scripts because nobody knew which components consume a nonce.
func TestNonceConsumerDocsSync(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "docs", "nonce-consumers.md"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read docs/nonce-consumers.md: %v", err)
	}

	docs := string(data)

	if len(nonceConsumers) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("nonceConsumers table is empty — the doctor scan would be a no-op")
	}

	for _, consumer := range nonceConsumers {
		name := consumer.Qualified
		if !strings.Contains(docs, "`"+name+"`") {
			t.Errorf(
				"nonceConsumers entry %q missing from docs/nonce-consumers.md — update both in the same commit",
				name,
			)
		}
	}

	// Every backticked table row in the docs must be a scan entry (or the
	// documented prose exception), so the docs never advertise a component
	// the doctor does not scan.
	rowRe := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\| ` + "`" + `([^` + "`" + `]+)` + "`")
	for _, m := range rowRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(docs, -1) {
		name := m[1]
		if name == "Nonce" || name == "tc doctor" || name == "TableRow.Href" ||
			name == "Dismissible" || name == "Eager" || name == "Content-Security-Policy" {
			continue
		}

		found := false

		for _, consumer := range nonceConsumers {
			if consumer.Qualified == name {
				found = true

				break
			}
		}

		if !found {
			t.Errorf("docs row %q is not in the nonceConsumers scan table — update both in the same commit", name)
		}
	}
}

// TestCheckNoncelessScripts exercises the doctor's nonce scan against a
// fixture module: empty-props-literal and fake-positional-literal call sites
// are detected; clean sources pass.
func TestCheckNoncelessScripts(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("detects empty nonce call sites", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		dir := t.TempDir()
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"), "module example.com/app\n\ngo 1.27\n")
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "page.templ"), "package ui\n\n"+`
templ page() {
	@components.TCErrorHandling()
	@feedback.ToastContainer("")
	@layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", "")
	@display.CopyButton(display.CopyButtonProps{ Nonce: "" })
}
`)

		findings := scanNonceFindings(dir)
		if len(findings) < 3 {
			t.Fatalf("expected >=3 findings, got %d: %v", len(findings), findings)
		}

		for _, f := range findings {
			if !strings.Contains(f, "page.templ:") {
				t.Errorf("finding not file-anchored: %q", f)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("clean sources pass", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		dir := t.TempDir()
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"), "module example.com/app\n\ngo 1.27\n")
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "page.templ"), "package ui\n\n"+`
templ page(nonce string) {
	@feedback.ToastContainer(nonce)
	@layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", nonce)
}
`)

		if findings := scanNonceFindings(dir); len(findings) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("expected 0 findings, got %d: %v", len(findings), findings)
		}
	})

	t.Run("library package dirs are skipped", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		dir := t.TempDir()
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"), "module github.com/larsartmann/templ-components\n\ngo 1.27\n")
		writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "display", "x.templ"), "package display\n\nNonce: \"\"\n")

		if findings := scanNonceFindings(dir); len(findings) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("library dirs must be skipped, got %d findings", len(findings))
		}
	})
}
package main

import (

// The doctor's two false-FAIL fixes (#35): the templ pin check must read
// both go.mod require forms (the line-prefix matcher read only the
// single-line form, so every block-form consumer — the gofmt default —
// read as "templ missing"), and the Tailwind entry check must discover the
// entry by content (the fixed filename probe missed layouts like
// assets/css/input.css).

func TestTemplRequireVersion(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		content string
		want    string
		wantOK  bool
	}{
		{
			name: "block require form resolves",
			content: `module example.com/consumer

go 1.27

require (
	github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100
	github.com/larsartmann/templ-components v1.27.0
)

require (
	github.com/Oudwins/tailwind-merge-go v0.2.3 // indirect
)
`,
			want:   "0.3.1100",
			wantOK: true,
		},
		{
			name: "single-line require form resolves",
			content: `module example.com/consumer

go 1.27

require github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1020
`,
			want:   "0.3.1020",
			wantOK: true,
		},
		{
			name:    "single-line indirect resolves",
			content: "require github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100 // indirect\n",
			want:    "0.3.1100",
			wantOK:  true,
		},
		{
			name: "trailing comment stripped",
			content: `require (
	github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100 // pinned to the generator
)
`,
			want:   "0.3.1100",
			wantOK: true,
		},
		{
			name: "replace block does not masquerade",
			content: `require github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100

replace github.com/a-h/templ => github.com/fork/templ v9.9.9
`,
			want:   "0.3.1100",
			wantOK: true,
		},
		{
			name: "closed and reopened require block resolves",
			content: `require (
	github.com/a v1.0.0
)

exclude github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.900

require (
	github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100
)
`,
			want:   "0.3.1100",
			wantOK: true,
		},
		{
			name:    "missing dependency reports not found",
			content: "module example.com/consumer\n\ngo 1.27\n\nrequire github.com/some/other v1.0.0\n",
			want:    "",
			wantOK:  false,
		},
		{
			name:    "empty go.mod reports not found",
			content: "",
			want:    "",
			wantOK:  false,
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got, ok := templRequireVersion(tt.content)
			if ok != tt.wantOK || got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("templRequireVersion() = (%q, %v), want (%q, %v)", got, ok, tt.want, tt.wantOK)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCheckTemplVersionPinnedAtVerdicts(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		goMod    string
		wantPASS bool
	}{
		{
			name:     "block-form current pin passes",
			goMod:    "module c\n\nrequire (\n\tgithub.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1100\n)\n",
			wantPASS: true,
		},
		{
			name:     "block-form old pin fails",
			goMod:    "module c\n\nrequire (\n\tgithub.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1020\n)\n",
			wantPASS: false,
		},
		{name: "missing templ fails", goMod: "module c\n\ngo 1.27\n", wantPASS: false},
		{name: "unreadable path fails", goMod: "", wantPASS: false},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "go.mod")

			if tt.goMod != "" {
				writeFile(t, path, tt.goMod)
			}

			if (checkTemplVersionPinnedAt(path) == 0) != tt.wantPASS {
				t.Fatalf("checkTemplVersionPinnedAt(%q) verdict != pass=%v", path, tt.wantPASS)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDiscoverCSSEntry(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		cssPath    string
		cssContent string
		want       string
	}{
		{
			name:       "nested entry discovered",
			cssPath:    "assets/css/input.css",
			cssContent: "@import \"tailwindcss\";\n@source \"../../../**/*.templ\";\n",
			want:       "assets/css/input.css",
		},
		{
			name:       "templ-less entry returned as hint",
			cssPath:    "assets/css/input.css",
			cssContent: "@import \"tailwindcss\";\n@source \"../src\";\n",
			want:       "assets/css/input.css",
		},
		{
			name:    "no css at all",
			cssPath: "",
			want:    "",
		},
		{
			name:       "css without @source ignored",
			cssPath:    "styles/theme.css",
			cssContent: "body { color: red; }\n",
			want:       "",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			dir := t.TempDir()

			if tt.cssPath != "" {
				writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, tt.cssPath), tt.cssContent)
			}

			got, found := discoverCSSEntry(dir)
			if tt.want == "" {
				if found {
					t.Fatalf("discoverCSSEntry() = (%q, true), want not found", got)
				}

				return
			}

			if !found || got != filepath.Join(dir, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("discoverCSSEntry() = (%q, %v), want (%q, true)", got, found, filepath.Join(dir, tt.want))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDiscoverCSSEntryPrefersScanningEntry(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	// When several @source-carrying css files exist, the one that actually
	// scans .templ wins over an earlier templ-less hit (lexical walk order
	// must not doom a valid entry).
	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "aaa/inert.css"), "@source \"./other\";\n")
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "zzz/input.css"), "@source \"../../**/*.templ\";\n")

	got, found := discoverCSSEntry(dir)
	if !found || got != filepath.Join(dir, "zzz/input.css") {
		t.Errorf("discoverCSSEntry() = (%q, %v), want the scanning entry", got, found)
	}
}

func TestDiscoverCSSEntryDepthBound(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	// The walk must not reach arbitrarily deep trees (huge consumer repos).
	dir := t.TempDir()

	deep := dir + "/level" + strings.Repeat("/level", cssDiscoveryMaxDepth+4)
	writeFile(t, deep+"/late.css", "@source \"**/*.templ\";\n")

	if got, found := discoverCSSEntry(dir); found {
		t.Errorf("walked past the depth bound (found %q)", got)
	}
}

func TestCssFastPathEntry(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "static/app.css"), "@source \"**/*.templ\";\n")

	if got := cssFastPathEntry(dir); got != filepath.Join(dir, "static/app.css") {
		t.Errorf("cssFastPathEntry() = %q, want the static/app.css candidate", got)
	}

	if got := cssFastPathEntry(t.TempDir()); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("cssFastPathEntry() = %q in an empty dir, want \"\"", got)
	}
}

func TestDoctorGeneratedFileNotBroken(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	// The doctor must hand out advice anchored to the same generator version
	// the library pins (kept in lockstep by utils.TestTemplVersionPin on the
	// library side); this asserts the doctor constant is version-shaped.
	if !isVersionLiteral(templGeneratedWith) {
		t.Errorf("templGeneratedWith = %q, not a version literal", templGeneratedWith)
	}
}
//nolint:gochecknoglobals,nonamedreturns // CLI scanner registry + arg parser; mirrors main.go conventions
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// lintScanner is one compliance check selectable via `tc lint --<flag>`.
type lintScanner struct {
	flag string
	help string
	scan func(dir string) ([]utils.Finding, error)
}

// lintScanners lists every `tc lint` scanner in flag order. The CLI stays in
// lockstep with the library's guard tests: each entry's scan function IS the
// engine behind a utils guard test, so a consumer running `tc lint` enforces
// the same rules the library enforces on itself.
var lintScanners = []lintScanner{
	{
		flag: "rtl",
		help: "physical direction classes (ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-/text-left/text-right/border-l-/border-r-) and deprecated start-*/end-* inset aliases in .templ files",
		scan: utils.ScanRTL,
	},
	{
		flag: "dark",
		help: "neutral + semantic color classes missing a same-line dark: variant (.templ/.go sources)",
		scan: utils.ScanDarkMode,
	},
	{
		flag: "motion",
		help: "transition/animate classes without a motion-reduce fallback (.templ files)",
		scan: utils.ScanMotionReduce,
	},
	{
		flag: "icons",
		help: "inlined SVG path d=\"M...\" literals outside the canonical tables (.templ/.go direct children)",
		scan: utils.ScanIconPaths,
	},
}

// cmdLint runs the compliance scanners and exits with 1 when findings exist,
// so CI and pre-commit hooks can gate on it.
func cmdLint(_ *registry, args []string) {
	os.Exit(runLint(args, os.Stdout, os.Stderr))
}

// runLint parses `tc lint` arguments, runs the selected scanners over the
// given directories, prints findings, and returns the process exit code:
// 0 = clean, 1 = findings or scan failure, 2 = usage error.
func runLint(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
	selected, dirs, ok := parseLintArgs(args, stderr)
	if !ok {
		return 2
	}

	flags := make([]string, 0, len(selected))
	for _, s := range selected {
		flags = append(flags, "--"+s.flag)
	}

	findings := 0

	for _, dir := range dirs {
		if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "tc lint: no such directory: %s\n", dir)

			return 1
		}

		for _, s := range selected {
			found, err := s.scan(dir)
			if err != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "tc lint: --%s scan failed on %s: %v\n", s.flag, dir, err)

				return 1
			}

			for _, f := range found {
				findings++

				fmt.Fprintf(stdout, "%s:%d: %s: %s\n    %s\n", f.File, f.Line, f.Rule, f.Message, f.Snippet)
			}
		}
	}

	pluralDirs := "directory"
	if len(dirs) != 1 {
		pluralDirs = "directories"
	}

	if findings > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(
			stdout,
			"tc lint: %d finding(s) (%s) in %d %s\n",
			findings,
			strings.Join(flags, " "),
			len(dirs),
			pluralDirs,
		)

		return 1
	}

	fmt.Fprintf(stdout, "tc lint: clean — 0 findings (%s) in %d %s\n", strings.Join(flags, " "), len(dirs), pluralDirs)

	return 0
}

// selectLintScanner resolves a scanner flag name to its scanner.
func selectLintScanner(name string) (lintScanner, bool) {
	for _, s := range lintScanners {
		if name == s.flag {
			return s, true
		}
	}

	return lintScanner{}, false //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // zero sentinel
}

// lintArgKind classifies one `tc lint` argument.
type lintArgKind int

const (
	lintArgDir     lintArgKind = iota // positional target directory
	lintArgScanner                    // --<scanner>
	lintArgAll                        // --all
	lintArgHelp                       // -h/--help
)

// classifyLintArg sorts one argument into its kind and (for scanners) its
// flag name.
func classifyLintArg(a string) (lintArgKind, string) {
	switch {
	case a == "-h" || a == "--help":
		return lintArgHelp, ""
	case a == "--all":
		return lintArgAll, ""
	case strings.HasPrefix(a, "--"):
		return lintArgScanner, strings.TrimPrefix(a, "--")
	default:
		return lintArgDir, a
	}
}

// parseLintArgs splits `tc lint` arguments into selected scanners and target
// directories. It prints usage to stderr and reports !ok for usage errors.
func parseLintArgs(args []string, stderr io.Writer) (selected []lintScanner, dirs []string, ok bool) {
	chosen := map[string]bool{}
	wantAll := false

	for _, a := range args {
		kind, name := classifyLintArg(a)

		switch kind {
		case lintArgHelp:
			fmt.Fprint(stderr, lintUsage())

			return nil, nil, false
		case lintArgAll:
			wantAll = true
		case lintArgScanner:
			if _, matched := selectLintScanner(name); !matched {
				fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "tc lint: unknown flag %q\n\n%s", a, lintUsage())

				return nil, nil, false
			}

			chosen[name] = true
		case lintArgDir:
			dirs = append(dirs, name)
		}
	}

	for _, s := range lintScanners {
		if wantAll || chosen[s.flag] {
			selected = append(selected, s)
		}
	}

	if len(selected) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "tc lint: select at least one scanner\n\n%s", lintUsage())

		return nil, nil, false
	}

	if len(dirs) == 0 {
		dirs = []string{"."}
	}

	return selected, dirs, true
}

func lintUsage() string {
	var b strings.Builder

	b.WriteString("tc lint [--rtl] [--dark] [--motion] [--icons] [--all] [DIR ...]\n\n")
	b.WriteString("Scans source files for the library's compliance rules. Without DIR,\n")
	b.WriteString("scans the current directory recursively (icons: direct children).\n\nScanners:\n")

	for _, s := range lintScanners {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  --%-8s %s\n", s.flag, s.help)
	}

	b.WriteString("  --all    run every scanner\n")

	b.WriteString("\nExit codes: 0 clean, 1 findings or scan failure, 2 usage error.\n")

	return b.String()
}
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// TestLintAllParityWithGuardTests pins the parity contract between `tc lint`
// and the library's guard tests (master-plan M2/F7): each scanner must return
// CLEAN on exactly the directory set its guard test sweeps, because the
// scanners ARE the guard engines (same exported funcs) and the guards are
// green on this repo. A seeded-violation proof per rule lives in the utils
// scanner tests; together the two directions prove verdict equality on this
// tree: guard-green ⇒ lint-clean, and lint fires where the guard fires.
func TestLintAllParityWithGuardTests(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	// Repo-root-relative, mirroring the guard tests' dir lists (utils tests
	// run with CWD=utils and prefix each dir with "..").
	guardDirs := map[string][]string{
		"--rtl":    {"display", "feedback", "forms", "navigation", "errorpage", "layout", "htmx"},
		"--motion": {"display", "feedback", "forms", "navigation", "errorpage", "layout", "htmx"},
		"--dark":   {"display", "feedback", "forms", "navigation", "errorpage", "layout", "htmx", "examples/demo"},
		"--icons": {
			"display", "forms", "feedback", "layout", "navigation",
			"errorpage", "recipes", "htmx", "datastar", "charts/echarts",
			"icons", "utils",
		},
	}

	for flag, dirs := range guardDirs {
		t.Run(flag, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			args := []string{flag}
			for _, dir := range dirs {
				args = append(args, filepath.Join("..", "..", dir))
			}

			stdout, stderr := &bytes.Buffer{}, &bytes.Buffer{}

			if code := runLint(args, stdout, stderr); code != 0 {
				t.Errorf(
					"tc lint %s over the guard dir set is NOT clean (exit %d) — the CLI and the guard tests disagree:\n%s%s",
					flag,
					code,
					stderr.String(),
					stdout.String(),
				)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestParseLintArgsAll proves --all selects every scanner exactly once and
// that duplicate/repeated flags do not double-run a scanner.
func TestParseLintArgsAll(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	selected, dirs, ok := parseLintArgs([]string{"--all", "--rtl", "."}, &bytes.Buffer{})
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("parseLintArgs(--all --rtl .) reported !ok")
	}

	if len(selected) != len(lintScanners) {
		t.Errorf("--all selected %d scanners, want %d", len(selected), len(lintScanners))
	}

	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, s := range selected {
		if seen[s.flag] {
			t.Errorf("scanner %s selected twice", s.flag)
		}

		seen[s.flag] = true
	}

	if len(dirs) != 1 || dirs[0] != "." {
		t.Errorf("dirs = %v, want [.] with --all consuming no positional", dirs)
	}
}
package main

import (

	"os"
	"path/filepath"

// runLintCase runs `tc lint` arg parsing + scanning and returns the exit code
// plus both output streams.
func runLintCase(args []string) (int, string, string) {
	outBuf, errBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}, &bytes.Buffer{}

	code := runLint(args, outBuf, errBuf)

	return code, outBuf.String(), errBuf.String()
}

func writeLintCLIFixture(t *testing.T, dir, name, content string) {
	t.Helper()

	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write fixture %s: %v", name, err)
	}
}

// TestRunLintClean proves the exit-code contract on a violation-free
// directory: 0, with a summary naming the scanner.
func TestRunLintClean(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeLintCLIFixture(t, dir, "ok.templ", "<div class=\"ms-2 text-start\">\n</div>\n")

	code, stdout, stderr := runLintCase([]string{"--rtl", dir})
	if code != 0 {
		t.Errorf("exit = %d, want 0\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", code, stdout, stderr)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(stdout, "clean") || !strings.Contains(stdout, "--rtl") {
		t.Errorf("summary should name the scanner and report clean:\n%s", stdout)
	}
}

// TestRunLintFindings proves findings exit 1 with file:line attribution and
// a finding-count summary.
func TestRunLintFindings(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	dir := t.TempDir()
	writeLintCLIFixture(t, dir, "bad.templ", "<div class=\"ml-2\">\n<span class=\"start-0\">\n</div>\n")

	code, stdout, stderr := runLintCase([]string{"--rtl", dir})
	if code != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("exit = %d, want 1\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", code, stdout, stderr)
	}

	for _, want := range []string{"bad.templ:1:", "rtl-physical:", "bad.templ:2:", "rtl-inset-alias:", "ml-2", "2 finding(s)"} {
		if !strings.Contains(stdout, want) {
			t.Errorf("stdout missing %q:\n%s", want, stdout)
		}
	}

	if stderr != "" {
		t.Errorf("stderr should be empty on findings:\n%s", stderr)
	}
}

// TestRunLintUsageErrors pins the usage-error contract: exit 2 with a hint on
// stderr for every malformed invocation.
func TestRunLintUsageErrors(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	dir := t.TempDir()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		args    []string
		wantErr string
	}{
		{name: "no scanner flag", args: []string{dir}, wantErr: "select at least one scanner"},
		{name: "unknown flag", args: []string{"--rtl", "--nope", dir}, wantErr: "unknown flag"},
		{name: "help", args: []string{"--help"}, wantErr: "--rtl"},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			code, stdout, stderr := runLintCase(tt.args)
			if code != 2 {
				t.Errorf("exit = %d, want 2\nstderr:\n%s", code, stderr)
			}

			if !strings.Contains(stderr, tt.wantErr) {
				t.Errorf("stderr missing %q:\n%s", tt.wantErr, stderr)
			}

			if stdout != "" {
				t.Errorf("usage errors should not write findings to stdout:\n%s", stdout)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestRunLintMissingDir proves a missing target directory is a hard failure
// (exit 1) that names the directory — a typo'd path must never read as
// "clean".
func TestRunLintMissingDir(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	code, _, stderr := runLintCase([]string{"--rtl", filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "gone")})
	if code != 1 {
		t.Errorf("exit = %d, want 1", code)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "no such directory") {
		t.Errorf("stderr should name the missing directory:\n%s", stderr)
	}
}

// TestRunLintMultipleDirs proves the summary counts every scanned directory.
func TestRunLintMultipleDirs(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	clean := t.TempDir()
	writeLintCLIFixture(t, clean, "ok.templ", "<p class=\"pe-1\">\n</p>\n")

	dirty := t.TempDir()
	writeLintCLIFixture(t, dirty, "bad.templ", "<div class=\"mr-1\">\n</div>\n")

	code, stdout, stderr := runLintCase([]string{"--rtl", clean, dirty})
	if code != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("exit = %d, want 1\nstderr:\n%s", code, stderr)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(stdout, "in 2 directories") {
		t.Errorf("summary should count 2 directories:\n%s", stdout)
	}
}
// Package main is the `tc` CLI: scaffolding tool for templ-components.
// See README at docs/cli.md for the full usage guide.
//
// This file uses CLI-specific conventions intentionally:
//   - path traversal via user-supplied --out (gosec G703 is a false positive)
//   - Print to stdout is the purpose of the tool (forbidigo doesn't apply)
//   - registry globals are normal for embed-driven CLIs
//
//nolint:errcheck,gosec,forbidigo,gochecknoglobals,nonamedreturns,wsl_v5,nlreturn,nolintlint,gocyclo,cyclop,funlen,goprintffuncname,nilerr // CLI tool conventions
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// CLI tool uses different conventions than library code: path traversal is
// intentional (CLI consumes user-supplied paths), Print to stdout is the
// purpose, globals are normal for embed registries.
//
//nolint:all // CLI tool; see package doc
//go:embed all:_sources
var sourcesFS embed.FS

// registry tracks every embedded component source by lower-cased name.
type registry struct {
	files map[string][]string
	pkg   map[string]string
	pkgs  []string
}

func newRegistry() *registry {
	r := &registry{
		files: map[string][]string{},
		pkg:   map[string]string{},
		pkgs: []string{
			pkgDisplay, pkgFeedback, pkgForms, pkgLayout,
			pkgNav, pkgHTMX, pkgDatastar, pkgErrorpage, pkgRecipes,
		},
	}

	fs.WalkDir(sourcesFS, "_sources", func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if d == nil || d.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}

		rel, relErr := filepath.Rel("_sources", path)
		if relErr != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("resolve %s: %w", path, relErr)
		}

		parts := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))
		if len(parts) < 2 {
			return nil
		}

		pkg := parts[0]
		filename := parts[len(parts)-1]
		if !strings.HasSuffix(filename, ".templ") {
			return nil
		}

		base := strings.TrimSuffix(filename, ".templ")
		key := strings.ToLower(base)
		r.files[key] = append(r.files[key], path)

		if _, ok := r.pkg[key]; !ok {
			r.pkg[key] = pkg
		}

		return nil
	})

	return r
}

		"appshell_types.go", "container_types.go",
		"datastar_nonce.go", "embed.go", "sri.go", "split_types.go", "stack_types.go",
	},

	pkgNav: {"nav_menu_id.go"},
	pkgHTMX: {
		enumsGoFile, "polled_region.go",

	},

	pkgDatastar: {
		"cancellation.go", enumsGoFile, "indicator.go",
		"attributes.go", "live_region.go", "loading_button.go", "polled_region.go",
		"retry.go", "sdk_script.go",

		// runtime bundle) + utils/cdn — SDKScript consumers only.
		"version.go",
	},

	pkgErrorpage: {
		"constructors.go", "fromerror.go", "handler.go",
		"notfound404_types.go", "styles.go",
	},
	pkgRecipes: {
		"dashboard_types.go", "login_card_types.go",
		"settings_layout_types.go",
	},
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		usage()

		return
	}

	r := newRegistry()

	switch os.Args[1] {
	case "init":
		cmdInit(r, os.Args[2:])
	case "ls", "list":
		cmdList(r, os.Args[2:])
	case "add":
		cmdAdd(r, os.Args[2:])
	case "doctor":
		cmdDoctor(r, os.Args[2:])
	case "lint":
		cmdLint(r, os.Args[2:])
	case "version", "-v", "--version":
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout, utils.Version)
	case "-h", "--help", "help":
		usage()
	default:
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown command: %s\n\n", os.Args[1])
		usage()
		os.Exit(2)
	}
}

func usage() {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, `tc — templ-components scaffolding

Usage:
  tc init                   Scaffold the four starter CSS files in the current directory.
  tc ls                     Print every component, grouped by package.
  tc add <component>        Copy <component>.templ (and _types.go if present) to ./components/.
  tc add <component> --out DIR   Copy to a custom directory.
  tc add <component> --list-deps List sibling .go files the component depends on.
  tc version                Print the library version.
  tc doctor [--css PATH]    Diagnose consumer-integration traps (Tailwind @source,
                            GOEXPERIMENT, templ pin, committed *_templ.go, hooks);
                            --css checks one concrete css entry.
  tc lint [flags] [DIR ...] Scan sources for compliance violations (--rtl, --dark,
                            --motion, --icons). Exit 1 on findings — CI-gateable.

Examples:
  tc init
  tc add button
  tc add dropdown --out ./src/components
  tc add modal --list-deps

Available components: run 'tc ls' to see them all.`)
}

func cmdInit(_ *registry, _ []string) {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(".", 0o750); err != nil {
		failf("create dir: %v", err)
	}

	for _, name := range []string{"app.css", "custom.css", "templ-components-theme.css", "safelist.css"} {
		content, err := sourcesFS.ReadFile(filepath.Join("_sources", "starter", name))
		if err != nil {
			failf("read starter %s: %v", name, err)
		}

		if _, err := os.Stat(name); err == nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tc: skip %s (already exists)\n", name)

			continue
		}

		if err := os.WriteFile(name, content, 0o600); err != nil {
			failf("write %s: %v", name, err)
		}

		status("wrote", name)
	}
}

func cmdList(r *registry, _ []string) {
	count := 0
	for _, pkg := range r.pkgs {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\n# %s\n", pkg)

		pkgCount := 0
		for name, p := range r.pkg {
			if p != pkg {
				continue
			}

			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %s\n", name)
			pkgCount++
		}
		count += pkgCount
	}

	// Derived, not hand-typed: always matches the embedded mirror because it
	// IS the mirror's size (backlog #294a — docs hand-typing this number is
	// how "58 enums" class drift happened).
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\n%d components addable with 'tc add <name>'\n", count)
}

func cmdAdd(r *registry, args []string) {
	out, listDeps, positional := parseAddArgs(args)
	if len(positional) < 1 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "tc add <component> [--out DIR] [--list-deps]")

		return
	}

	name := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(positional[0]))
	files, ok := r.files[name]
	if !ok {
		failf("unknown component %q. Run 'tc ls' for the list.", name)
	}

	pkg := r.pkg[name]

	if listDeps {
		deps := packageDeps[pkg]
		sort.Strings(deps)
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "# sibling .go files in package '%s' needed by '%s':\n", pkg, name)
		for _, dep := range deps {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %s/%s\n", pkg, dep)
		}
		imports := packageImports[pkg]
		sort.Strings(imports)
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\n# imports the vendored '%s' package pulls into go.mod:\n", pkg)
		for _, imp := range imports {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "  %s\n", imp)
		}
		if pkg == pkgDatastar {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\ntc: datastar vendors an external runtime bundle — the add copies\n")
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "      %s with the re-audit checklist. Follow it on every\n",
				datastarBumpProtocolDoc)
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "      go-datastar/static bump.\n")
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\ntc: %d file(s). These are NOT copied by 'tc add'.\n", len(deps))
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tc: to get a working component, vendor the full package:\n")
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "      go get github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/%s\n", pkg)

		return
	}

	if err := os.MkdirAll(out, 0o750); err != nil {
		failf("create output dir: %v", err)
	}

	for _, src := range files {
		copyFile(src, filepath.Join(out, filepath.Base(src)))
	}

	// datastar components vendor an external runtime integration: always
	// drop the bump/re-audit checklist next to them (post-audit patterns by
	// construction).
	if pkg == pkgDatastar {
		copyFile(filepath.Join("_sources", pkgDatastar, datastarBumpProtocolDoc),
			filepath.Join(out, datastarBumpProtocolDoc))
	}

	for _, src := range files {
		base := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(src), ".templ")
		typesPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(src), base+"_types.go")

		if content, err := sourcesFS.ReadFile(typesPath); err == nil {
			dest := filepath.Join(out, base+"_types.go")

			if err := os.WriteFile(dest, content, 0o600); err != nil {
				failf("write %s: %v", dest, err)
			}

			status("wrote", dest)
		}
	}

	// Warn: a .templ file references package-level helpers (class lookups,
	// enums, utils, sub-templates) defined in sibling .go files that are NOT
	// embedded or copied. The output will not compile standalone.
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr,
		"tc: note: '%s.templ' is part of the '%s' package and references helpers\n"+
			"    (class lookups, enums, sub-templates) defined in sibling .go files\n"+
			"    that were NOT copied. The output will not compile standalone.\n"+
			"    For a working component, vendor the full package:\n"+
			"      go get github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/%s\n",
		name, pkg, pkg)
}

func parseAddArgs(args []string) (out string, listDeps bool, positional []string) {
	out = "./components"

	i := 0

	for i < len(args) {
		a := args[i]

		switch {
		case a == "--out" || a == "-o":
			if i+1 >= len(args) {
				failf("--out requires a value")
			}

			out = args[i+1]
			i += 2
		case strings.HasPrefix(a, "--out="):
			out = strings.TrimPrefix(a, "--out=")
			i++
		case strings.HasPrefix(a, "-o="):
			out = strings.TrimPrefix(a, "-o=")
			i++
		case a == "--list-deps":
			listDeps = true
			i++
		case a == "-h" || a == "--help":
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "tc add <component> [--out DIR] [--list-deps]")

			return out, listDeps, positional
		default:
			positional = append(positional, a)
			i++
		}
	}

	return out, listDeps, positional
}

func copyFile(srcEmbed, dest string) {
	content, err := sourcesFS.ReadFile(srcEmbed)
	if err != nil {
		failf("read embedded %s: %v", srcEmbed, err)
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(dest, content, 0o600); err != nil {
		failf("write %s: %v", dest, err)
	}

	status("wrote", dest)
}

func status(verb, path string) {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "tc: %s %s\n", verb, path)
}

func failf(format string, args ...any) {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "tc: "+format+"\n", args...)
	os.Exit(1)
}

func TestComponentSourcesPopulated(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := newRegistry()
	if len(r.files) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("registry files is empty — embed failed")
	}

	if _, ok := r.files["button"]; !ok {
		t.Error("expected 'button' in registry files")
	}
}

// TestSourcesMirrorExcludesGenerated bans generated `*_templ.go` files from
// the embedded mirror (outside the curated starter/). The mirror ships
// .templ + *_types.go SOURCES only; consumers run `templ generate` after
// `tc add`. Generated copies would be stale duplicates the moment any
// component is regenerated — and BuildFlow's templ-generate step keeps
// recreating them because its ownership walk doesn't skip _-prefixed
// directories (the daemon then commits them; the 2026-10-10 incident added
// 112 of them in one snapshot, breaking every cmd/tc test via the
// FileName-path drift). go:embed all:_sources picks up these strays even
// when .gitignore'd, so this test is the gate that fires regardless of git
// state. scripts/check-tc-sources-sync.sh removes them in --fix mode.
func TestSourcesMirrorExcludesGenerated(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	err := fs.WalkDir(sourcesFS, "_sources", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
		if walkErr != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return walkErr
		}

		rel, _ := filepath.Rel("_sources", p)

		if strings.HasPrefix(rel, "starter"+string(filepath.Separator)) {
			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(rel, "_templ.go") {
			t.Errorf(
				"embedded %s is a GENERATED file — the mirror ships .templ and "+
					"*_types.go sources only. Delete it (scripts/check-tc-sources-sync.sh "+
					"--fix does this). Root cause: BuildFlow templ-generate regenerates "+
					"the mirror's .templ copies in place; see AGENTS.md.",
				rel,
			)
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("walk _sources: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestSourcesMatchPackageFiles is the _sources/ drift guard: every embedded
// source file must be byte-identical to the real package file it was copied
// from. The sources were copied by hand; without this guard the scaffolder
// silently serves stale components after a package edit.
func TestSourcesMatchPackageFiles(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	repoRoot := filepath.Join("..", "..")

	err := fs.WalkDir(sourcesFS, "_sources", func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
		if walkErr != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return walkErr
		}

		rel, _ := filepath.Rel("_sources", path)
		parts := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))

		if parts[0] == "starter" {
			// Starter CSS is a curated template, not a copy of a package file.
			return nil
		}

		if rel == filepath.Join("datastar", datastarBumpProtocolDoc) {
			// Scaffolder-owned checklist — no package-file counterpart.
			return nil
		}

		embedded, err := sourcesFS.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("read embedded %s: %v", rel, err)

			return nil
		}

		original, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(repoRoot, rel))
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("package file for embedded source missing: %s: %v", rel, err)

			return nil
		}

		if string(embedded) != string(original) {
			t.Errorf("embedded %s drifted from the package file — re-copy it (and re-run this test)", rel)
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("walk _sources: %v", err)
	}
}

// mirroredPackages is the scaffolder's shipped package set: every .templ and
// *_types.go under these directories must be embedded so `tc add` can scaffold
// the component. Keep in sync with MIRRORED_PKGS in
// scripts/check-tc-sources-sync.sh (charts/ is a Tier 2 opt-in adapter and
// utils/ is leaf plumbing — intentionally not mirrored).
// TestMirroredPackagesListsMatch pins THIS list to the bash script's list so
// the two can never drift silently again (found 2026-09-23, TODO #283a: the
// hand-sync had two independent lists with only a comment linking them).
var mirroredPackages = []string{
	"datastar",
	"display",
	"errorpage",
	"feedback",
	"forms",
	"htmx",
	"layout",
	"navigation",
	"recipes",
}

// bashArrayRe captures the first element of a bash parenthesized array
// assignment: MIRRORED_PKGS=(a b c).
var bashArrayRe = regexp.MustCompile(`MIRRORED_PKGS=\(([^)]*)\)`)

// TestMirroredPackagesListsMatch keeps the Go mirror list and the bash
// guard's MIRRORED_PKGS array identical. The bash script is the pre-commit
// self-healing guard; the Go list drives `tc add` and the completeness test
// — a package present in one but missing from the other means either the
// scaffolder silently rejects a package's components or the bash guard
// never checks a package the scaffolder ships.
func TestMirroredPackagesListsMatch(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	scriptPath := filepath.Join("..", "..", "scripts", "check-tc-sources-sync.sh")

	script, err := os.ReadFile(scriptPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", scriptPath, err)
	}

	m := bashArrayRe.FindSubmatch(script)
	if m == nil {
		t.Fatalf("MIRRORED_PKGS=(...) not found in %s", scriptPath)
	}

	bashFields := strings.Fields(string(m[1]))
	if len(bashFields) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("MIRRORED_PKGS array in %s is empty", scriptPath)
	}

	goSet := make(map[string]bool, len(mirroredPackages))
	for _, pkg := range mirroredPackages {
		goSet[pkg] = true
	}

	bashSet := make(map[string]bool, len(bashFields))
	for _, pkg := range bashFields {
		bashSet[pkg] = true
	}

	for _, pkg := range bashFields {
		if !goSet[pkg] {
			t.Errorf("package %q is in MIRRORED_PKGS (bash) but missing from mirroredPackages (Go)", pkg)
		}
	}

	for _, pkg := range mirroredPackages {
		if !bashSet[pkg] {
			t.Errorf("package %q is in mirroredPackages (Go) but missing from MIRRORED_PKGS (bash)", pkg)
		}
	}
}

// TestSourcesShipEveryMirrorableFile is direction 2 of the _sources mirror
// guard: every mirrorable library file must be embedded. Without it, a newly
// added component is invisible to `tc add` ("unknown component") until a human
// remembers to copy it — nothing else fires, not even `go test`.
func TestSourcesShipEveryMirrorableFile(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	repoRoot := filepath.Join("..", "..")

	for _, pkg := range mirroredPackages {
		pkgFS := os.DirFS(filepath.Join(repoRoot, pkg))

		walkErr := fs.WalkDir(pkgFS, ".", func(name string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}

			if d.IsDir() {
				return nil
			}

			if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".templ") && !strings.HasSuffix(name, "_types.go") {
				return nil
			}

			if _, statErr := fs.Stat(sourcesFS, path.Join("_sources", pkg, name)); statErr != nil {
				t.Errorf("package file %s/%s is not embedded — run scripts/check-tc-sources-sync.sh --fix", pkg, name)
			}

			return nil
		})
		if walkErr != nil {
			t.Errorf("walk %s: %v", pkg, walkErr)
		}
	}
}

// TestPackageImportsMatchSources guards the packageImports checklist printed
// by 'tc add --list-deps': it must equal the set of module-level imports the
// package's non-test, non-generated sources actually use.
func TestPackageImportsMatchSources(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for pkg := range packageImports {
		got := collectPackageImports(t, pkg)
		want := map[string]bool{}

		for _, imp := range packageImports[pkg] {
			want[imp] = true
		}

		for imp := range want {
			if !got[imp] {
				t.Errorf("packageImports[%q] lists %q but %s does not import it — prune the checklist", pkg, imp, pkg)
			}
		}

		for imp := range got {
			if !want[imp] {
				t.Errorf("%s imports %q but packageImports[%q] misses it — add it", pkg, imp, pkg)
			}
		}
	}
}

// collectPackageImports scans a package's non-test, non-generated .go and
// .templ sources for module-level imports (the go.mod surface a vendoring
// consumer pulls in). Test-only helpers (/golden) and the package's own path
// are excluded.
func collectPackageImports(t *testing.T, pkg string) map[string]bool {
	t.Helper()

	const selfPrefix = "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/"

	got := map[string]bool{}

	for _, pattern := range []string{"*.go", "*.templ"} {
		files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join("..", "..", pkg, pattern))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("glob %s %s: %v", pkg, pattern, err)
		}

		for _, file := range files {
			base := filepath.Base(file)
			if strings.HasSuffix(base, "_test.go") || strings.HasSuffix(base, "_templ.go") {
				continue
			}

			content, err := os.ReadFile(file)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", file, err)
			}

			for _, imp := range importPattern.FindAllString(string(content), -1) {
				imp = strings.Trim(imp, `"`)
				if strings.Contains(imp, "/golden") || imp == selfPrefix+pkg {
					continue
				}

				got[imp] = true
			}
		}
	}

	return got
}

var importPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`"github\.com/[^"]+"`)

	tmp := t.TempDir()

	// Non-datastar adds must NOT get the checklist.

		t.Errorf("%s copied for a non-datastar component", datastarBumpProtocolDoc)
	}
}

package main

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

// TestTypesFilesHaveTemplTwin catches ghost type files: a *_types.go whose
// component's .templ was deleted or renamed. The types file then ships
// dead types in the published module AND — worse — the scaffolder mirror
// keeps embedding it as a companion for a component that no longer exists
// (the 2026-09-22 pass found nine *_types.go copies whose components had
// never been embedded; the inverse ghost had zero coverage until this test,
// backlog item #283b). The reverse direction (a .templ without a *_types.go) is
// legal: small components inline their props next to the component.
func TestTypesFilesHaveTemplTwin(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, pkg := range mirroredPackages {
		entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join("..", "..", pkg))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read package dir %s: %v", pkg, err)
		}

		for _, entry := range entries {
			name := entry.Name()
			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, "_types.go") {
				continue
			}

			twin := strings.TrimSuffix(name, "_types.go") + ".templ"
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join("..", "..", pkg, twin)); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s/%s has no .templ twin (%s missing) — delete or rename the types file", pkg, name, twin)
			}
		}
	}
}

// --- CopyButton Accessibility ---

func TestCopyButtonA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("button has type=button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="button"`)
	})

	t.Run("propagates aria-label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:      "x",
			AriaLabel: "Copy install command",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Copy install command"`)
	})

	t.Run("has focus-visible ring", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "focus-visible:ring-2")
	})

	t.Run("has motion-reduce transition", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "motion-reduce:transition-none")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "motion-reduce:duration-0")
	})
}

// --- CountBadge Accessibility ---

func TestCountBadgeA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("badge is aria-hidden (decorative)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-hidden="true"`)
	})

	t.Run("propagates aria-label to container", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CountBadge(CountBadgeProps{
			Count:     1,
			AriaLabel: "3 unread notifications",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="3 unread notifications"`)
	})
}

// --- Heatmap Accessibility ---

func TestHeatmapA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("uses table semantics", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Heatmap(HeatmapProps{
			Rows: []HeatmapRow{
				{Label: "Mon", Cells: []HeatmapCell{{Value: 5}}},
			},
			ColumnLabels: []string{"00:00"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<table")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<thead")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<tbody")
	})

	t.Run("names the native table instead of an image role", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Heatmap(HeatmapProps{
			Rows: []HeatmapRow{
				{Label: "Mon", Cells: []HeatmapCell{{Value: 5}}},
			},
			AriaLabel: "Activity heatmap",
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `role="img"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output,
			`<table class="min-w-full border-collapse text-xs" aria-label="Activity heatmap"`)
	})

	t.Run("falls back to the default accessible name", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Heatmap(HeatmapProps{
			Rows: []HeatmapRow{
				{Label: "Mon", Cells: []HeatmapCell{{Value: 5}}},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output,
			`<table class="min-w-full border-collapse text-xs" aria-label="Heatmap"`)
	})

	t.Run("cells have title tooltips", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Heatmap(HeatmapProps{
			Rows: []HeatmapRow{
				{Label: "Mon", Cells: []HeatmapCell{
					{Value: 5, Label: "Mon 00:00 — 5 msgs"},
				}},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `title="Mon 00:00 — 5 msgs"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty state has message", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Heatmap(HeatmapProps{
			EmptyMessage: "No activity data",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "No activity data")
	})
}

func TestDefaultPropsConstructors(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("DefaultCardProps returns valid props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultCardProps()
		if props.Padding != CardPaddingMD {
			t.Errorf("Padding = %q, want %q", props.Padding, CardPaddingMD)
		}

		output := utils.Render(t, Card(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<div")
	})

	t.Run("DefaultBadgeProps returns valid props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultBadgeProps()
		if props.Type != BadgeNeutral {
			t.Errorf("Type = %q, want %q", props.Type, BadgeNeutral)
		}

		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<span")
	})

	t.Run("DefaultModalProps returns valid props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultModalProps()
		if props.Size != ModalSizeMD {
			t.Errorf("Size = %q, want %q", props.Size, ModalSizeMD)
		}
	})

	// The M26 coverage batch: these constructors were public API with 0%
	// coverage — the consumer-audit lesson made them the documented-defaults
	// promise, so each gets its default pinned.
	t.Run("DefaultStatusDotProps defaults to neutral", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		if got := DefaultStatusDotProps(); got.Tone != StatusToneNeutral {
			t.Errorf("Tone = %q, want %q", got.Tone, StatusToneNeutral)
		}
	})

	t.Run("DefaultProseProps defaults to MD", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		if got := DefaultProseProps(); got.Size != ProseSizeMD {
			t.Errorf("Size = %q, want %q", got.Size, ProseSizeMD)
		}
	})

	t.Run("DefaultDataStateProps defaults to Content", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		if got := DefaultDataStateProps(); got.State != DataStateContent {
			t.Errorf("State = %q, want %q", got.State, DataStateContent)
		}
	})

	t.Run("remaining constructors construct", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		// Contract: the documented defaults exist; deeper behavior is the
		// component's own test surface.
		_ = DefaultCodeBlockProps()
		_ = DefaultLightboxProps()
		_ = DefaultDonutChartProps()
		_ = DefaultSegmentBarProps()
	})
}

// TestToneAdaptersExhaustive covers the tone Phase 0 adapters (M26 batch):
// every mapped enum value routes to its canonical tone and unknown values
// degrade to neutral — the map+fallback convention applied to the adapter
// layer.
func TestToneAdaptersExhaustive(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	statusCases := map[StatusTone]tone.Tone{
		StatusToneNeutral: tone.ToneNeutral,
		StatusToneSuccess: tone.ToneSuccess,
		StatusToneWarning: tone.ToneWarning,
		StatusToneDanger:  tone.ToneDanger,
		StatusToneInfo:    tone.ToneInfo,
	}
	for in, want := range statusCases {
		if got := in.Tone(); got != want {
			t.Errorf("StatusTone(%q).Tone() = %q, want %q", in, got, want)
		}
	}

	scrollbackCases := map[ScrollbackTone]tone.Tone{
		ScrollbackToneNeutral: tone.ToneNeutral,
		ScrollbackToneInfo:    tone.ToneInfo,
		ScrollbackToneSuccess: tone.ToneSuccess,
		ScrollbackToneWarning: tone.ToneWarning,
		ScrollbackToneDanger:  tone.ToneDanger,
	}
	for in, want := range scrollbackCases {
		if got := in.Tone(); got != want {
			t.Errorf("ScrollbackTone(%q).Tone() = %q, want %q", in, got, want)
		}
	}

	if got := StatusTone("bogus").Tone(); got != tone.ToneNeutral {
		t.Errorf("unknown StatusTone degraded to %q, want neutral", got)
	}
}

package display

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
)

func ensureAccordionItemIDs(items []AccordionItem) []AccordionItem {
	for i := range items {
		if items[i].ID == "" {
			items[i].ID = utils.EnsureID("accordion", "")
		}
	}
	return items
}

// AccordionItem represents a single collapsible panel
type AccordionItem struct {
	ID      string
	Title   string
	Content templ.Component
	Open    bool
}

// AccordionProps configures an accordion component
type AccordionProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Items []AccordionItem
	// Exclusive, when true, renders every <details> with the same name
	// attribute — the platform's native exclusive disclosure group (Modern
	// Web Guidance: search-hidden-content, "mutually exclusive
	// disclosures"): opening one item closes the others, zero JS. The group
	// name derives from ID (or a generated one), so two accordions on the
	// same page never share a group. Engines without named details (older
	// Firefox) degrade to independent items — every item stays operable.
	Exclusive bool
}

// DefaultAccordionProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultAccordionProps() AccordionProps {
	return AccordionProps{}
}

// Accordion renders a collapsible accordion using native <details>/<summary>
// elements for zero-JS toggle, native keyboard support, and built-in
// accessibility (implicit aria-expanded, role=group).
//
//	@display.Accordion(display.AccordionProps{
//	   Items: []display.AccordionItem{
//	     {ID: "faq1", Title: "What is this?", Open: true},
//	     {ID: "faq2", Title: "How does it work?"},
//	   },
//	})
templ Accordion(props AccordionProps) {
	{{ items := ensureAccordionItemIDs(props.Items) }}
	{{ group := "" }}
	{{ if props.Exclusive {
		group = utils.EnsureID("accordion-group", props.ID)
	} }}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("divide-y divide-gray-200 dark:divide-gray-700 border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 rounded-lg overflow-hidden", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		for _, item := range items {
			<details
				data-tc-accordion
				class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-900"
				if group != "" {
					name={ group }
				}
				if item.ID != "" {
					id={ item.ID }
				}
				if item.Open {
					open
				}
			>
				<summary
					class="flex w-full items-center justify-between px-4 py-4 text-start text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 dark:focus:ring-blue-400 focus:ring-inset cursor-pointer list-none"
				>
					<span>{ item.Title }</span>
					<svg
						data-tc-chevron
						class="h-5 w-5 text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"
						viewBox="0 0 20 20"
						fill="currentColor"
						aria-hidden="true"
					>
						<path fill-rule="evenodd" d={ svg.PathChevronDown } clip-rule="evenodd"></path>
					</svg>
				</summary>
				<div class="px-4 pb-4 text-sm text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400">
					if item.Content != nil {
						@item.Content
					}
				</div>
			</details>
		}
	</div>
}

func TestAccordionRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("basic accordion", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{
			Items: []AccordionItem{
				{
					ID:      accordionIDFAQ1,
					Title:   "What is this?",
					Open:    true,
					Content: templ.Raw("\u003cp\u003eAnswer 1\u003c/p\u003e"),
				},
				{
					ID:      "faq2",
					Title:   "How does it work?",
					Content: templ.Raw("\u003cp\u003eAnswer 2\u003c/p\u003e"),
				},
			},
		}))

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "What is this?")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "How does it work?")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Answer 1")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<details")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<summary")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, " open")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="`+accordionIDFAQ1+`"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-chevron`)
	})

	t.Run("closed accordion item", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{
			Items: []AccordionItem{
				{ID: "item1", Title: "Closed", Open: false, Content: templ.Raw("Content")},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<details")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<summary")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<details open")
	})

	t.Run("no script tag - uses native details", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{
			Nonce: testNonce,
			Items: []AccordionItem{
				{ID: "n1", Title: "Q", Content: templ.Raw("A")},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<script")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcAccordionAttached")
	})

	t.Run("custom class and id", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{
			ID: "faq", Class: cssClassMt4,
			Items: []AccordionItem{
				{ID: "n1", Title: "Q", Content: templ.Raw("A")},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="faq"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, cssClassMt4)
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultAccordionProps()
		if props.Items != nil {
			t.Error("DefaultAccordionProps().Items should be nil")
		}
	})
}

// TestAccordionExclusive (Modern Web Guidance: search-hidden-content,
// mutually exclusive disclosures) pins the native exclusive disclosure
// group: every <details> carries the same name attribute when Exclusive is
// set, and none does by default. Opening one item then closes the others
// with zero JavaScript.
func TestAccordionExclusive(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	items := func() []AccordionItem {
		return []AccordionItem{
			{ID: "ex1", Title: "One", Content: templ.Raw("A1")},
			{ID: "ex2", Title: "Two", Content: templ.Raw("A2")},
		}
	}

	exclusive := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{
		ID:        "faq-group",
		Exclusive: true,
		Items:     items(),
	}))
	utils.AssertContainsAll(t, exclusive, `name="faq-group"`, `id="ex1"`, `id="ex2"`)

	if got := strings.Count(exclusive, `name="faq-group"`); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("exclusive accordion should render the group name on every item, got %d", got)
	}

	independent := utils.Render(t, Accordion(AccordionProps{Items: items()}))
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, independent, `name="faq-group"`)

	if strings.Contains(independent, "accordion-group") {
		t.Error("default accordion must not render a details name attribute")
	}
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// AreaChartProps configures a pure-SVG area chart — a line chart with filled
// areas beneath each series. Like LineChart, it supports axes, gridlines,
// multi-series, dots, and a legend. Zero JavaScript.
//
// Each series renders both a line (top edge) and a semi-transparent fill
// from the line down to the X-axis baseline. Uses currentColor for stroke
// and fill so Tailwind text-* classes control per-series coloring.
type AreaChartProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Series is the data to plot.
	Series []LineChartSeries

	// XAxisLabels are category labels along the X-axis.
	XAxisLabels []string

	// Width is the SVG canvas width in pixels. Default: 600.
	Width int

	// Height is the SVG canvas height in pixels. Default: 300.
	Height int

	// Padding controls the inset around the plot area.
	Padding ChartPadding

	// Min overrides the auto-computed Y-axis minimum.
	Min *float64

	// Max overrides the auto-computed Y-axis maximum.
	Max *float64

	// MaxTicks is the tick budget for the Y axis: ComputeNiceTicks aims for
	// at most this many ticks. 0 or negative keeps the default of 8. The
	// final count is approximate — ticks snap to human-readable steps, so
	// the actual count can land slightly above or below the budget.
	MaxTicks int

	// ShowGrid renders dashed horizontal gridlines at each Y tick. Default: true.
	ShowGrid bool

	// ShowDots renders a circle at each data point. Default: false (cleaner area look).
	ShowDots bool

	// ShowLegend renders a color-swatch legend above the chart when 2+ series.
	ShowLegend bool

	// Style controls whether lines are straight (Linear) or curved (Smooth).
	Style LineChartStyle

	// FillOpacity controls the transparency of the area fill (0.0–1.0).
	// Default: 0.2.
	FillOpacity float64

	// ValueFormat formats Y-axis tick labels.
	ValueFormat func(float64) string

	// EmptyMessage is shown when Series is empty.
	EmptyMessage string
}

// AreaChart defaults. Width/height/empty-message defaults are the shared
// chartDefault* constants in chart_geometry.go.
const (
	areaChartDefaultFill = 0.2
)

// DefaultAreaChartProps returns sensible defaults for an area chart.
func DefaultAreaChartProps() AreaChartProps {
	return AreaChartProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
		Width:        chartDefaultWidth,
		Height:       chartDefaultHeight,
		Padding:      DefaultChartPadding(),
		ShowGrid:     true,
		ShowDots:     false,
		ShowLegend:   true,
		Style:        LineChartStyleLinear,
		FillOpacity:  areaChartDefaultFill,
		ValueFormat:  FormatTickValue,
		EmptyMessage: chartDefaultEmptyMsg,
	}
}

// areaChartFillOpacityStr converts a 0–1 float to an SVG fill-opacity attribute string.
func areaChartFillOpacityStr(opacity float64) string {
	if opacity <= 0 || opacity > 1 {
		return "0.2"
	}

	return formatCoord(opacity)
}
package display

// AreaChart renders a pure-SVG area chart with axes, gridlines, multi-series
// filled areas, optional dots, and a legend. Zero JavaScript — all rendering
// is server-side. Each series renders both a stroked line and a semi-transparent
// fill from the line down to the baseline.
//
//	@display.AreaChart(display.AreaChartProps{
//	    Series: []display.LineChartSeries{
//	        {Name: "Active Users", Values: []float64{120, 180, 250, 300, 280, 340}},
//	    },
//	    XAxisLabels: []string{"Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"},
//	})
templ AreaChart(props AreaChartProps) {
	{{
		width, height, style, emptyMsg := resolveLineAreaChartInputs(
			props.Width, props.Height, props.Style, props.EmptyMessage,
		)

		d := computeChartRenderData(
			width, height, props.Padding,
			props.Series, props.XAxisLabels,
			props.Min, props.Max,
			props.ShowGrid, props.ShowLegend,
			props.ValueFormat, emptyMsg,
			props.Class, props.AriaLabel, props.ID, props.Attrs,
			props.MaxTicks,
		)
	}}
	@lineAreaChartSVG(d, props.Series, style, chartSeriesRenderOpts{
		filled:      true,
		fillOpacity: areaChartFillOpacityStr(props.FillOpacity),
		showDots:    props.ShowDots,
	})
}
package display

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
