// AvatarSize defines the size of an avatar
type AvatarSize string

const (
	AvatarSizeXS AvatarSize = "xs"
	AvatarSizeSM AvatarSize = "sm"
	AvatarSizeMD AvatarSize = "md"
	AvatarSizeLG AvatarSize = "lg"
	AvatarSizeXL AvatarSize = "xl"
)

// AvatarShape defines the shape of an avatar
type AvatarShape string

const (
	AvatarShapeCircle AvatarShape = "circle"
	AvatarShapeSquare AvatarShape = "square"
)

// AvatarStatus represents the online status indicator for an avatar
type AvatarStatus string

const (
	AvatarStatusNone    AvatarStatus = ""
	AvatarStatusOnline  AvatarStatus = "online"
	AvatarStatusOffline AvatarStatus = "offline"
)

// AvatarProps configures an avatar component
type AvatarProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Src      string
	Alt      string
	Initials string
	Size     AvatarSize
	Shape    AvatarShape
	Status   AvatarStatus
}

// DefaultAvatarProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultAvatarProps() AvatarProps {
	return AvatarProps{
		Size:   AvatarSizeMD,
		Shape:  AvatarShapeCircle,
		Status: AvatarStatusNone,
	}
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup tables for avatar sizes
var avatarSizeLookup = map[AvatarSize]string{
	AvatarSizeXS: "h-6 w-6 text-xs",
	AvatarSizeSM: "h-8 w-8 text-sm",
	AvatarSizeLG: "h-12 w-12 text-lg",
	AvatarSizeXL: "h-14 w-14 text-xl",
}

var avatarDotSizeLookup = map[AvatarSize]string{
	AvatarSizeXS: "h-1.5 w-1.5",
	AvatarSizeSM: "h-2 w-2",
	AvatarSizeLG: "h-3 w-3",
	AvatarSizeXL: "h-3.5 w-3.5",
}

func avatarSizeClass(size AvatarSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(avatarSizeLookup, size, "h-10 w-10 text-base")
}

func avatarDotSizeClass(size AvatarSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(avatarDotSizeLookup, size, "h-2.5 w-2.5")
}

func avatarShapeClass(shape AvatarShape) string {
	if shape == AvatarShapeSquare {
		return "rounded-lg"
	}
	return "rounded-full"
}

// Avatar renders a user avatar with image, initials, or fallback
//
//	@display.Avatar(display.AvatarProps{Src: "/avatar.jpg", Alt: "Alice"})
templ Avatar(props AvatarProps) {
	if props.Src != "" {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("relative inline-block", props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			<img
				src={ props.Src }
				alt={ props.Alt }
				class={ utils.Class("inline-block object-cover bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-800", avatarSizeClass(props.Size), avatarShapeClass(props.Shape)) }
			/>
			if props.Status == AvatarStatusOnline || props.Status == AvatarStatusOffline {
				<span
					class={ "absolute bottom-0 inset-e-0 block rounded-full ring-2 ring-white dark:ring-gray-900",
						avatarDotSizeClass(props.Size),
						templ.KV("bg-green-400 dark:bg-green-500", props.Status == AvatarStatusOnline),
						templ.KV("bg-gray-400 dark:bg-gray-500", props.Status == AvatarStatusOffline) }
					aria-hidden="true"
				></span>
			}
		</div>
	} else {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("relative inline-flex items-center justify-center bg-accent-600 text-white dark:bg-accent-500 font-medium", avatarSizeClass(props.Size), avatarShapeClass(props.Shape), props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			if props.Initials != "" {
				{ props.Initials }
			} else {
				<svg class="h-1/2 w-1/2 text-accent-200" fill="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
					<path d={ svg.PathAvatarFill }></path>
				</svg>
			}
			if props.Status == AvatarStatusOnline || props.Status == AvatarStatusOffline {
				<span
					class={ "absolute bottom-0 inset-e-0 block rounded-full ring-2 ring-white dark:ring-gray-900",
						avatarDotSizeClass(props.Size),
						templ.KV("bg-green-400 dark:bg-green-500", props.Status == AvatarStatusOnline),
						templ.KV("bg-gray-400 dark:bg-gray-500", props.Status == AvatarStatusOffline) }
					aria-hidden="true"
				></span>
			}
		</div>
	}
}
// Package display provides tests for display components.
package display

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestAvatarRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("with image", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Src:   "/avatar.jpg",
			Alt:   avatarAltAlice,
			Size:  AvatarSizeMD,
			Shape: AvatarShapeCircle,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `src="/avatar.jpg"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `alt="`+avatarAltAlice+`"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-full")
	})

	t.Run("with initials", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Initials: "AB",
			Size:     AvatarSizeLG,
			Shape:    AvatarShapeSquare,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "AB")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-lg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
	})

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		status AvatarStatus
		class  string
	}{
		{"online status", AvatarStatusOnline, "bg-green-400"},
		{"offline status", AvatarStatusOffline, "bg-gray-400"},
	} {
		t.Run("with "+tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
				Src:    "/me.jpg",
				Alt:    "Me",
				Status: tc.status,
			}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, tc.class)
		})
	}

	t.Run("all size variants render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		for _, size := range []AvatarSize{AvatarSizeXS, AvatarSizeSM, AvatarSizeMD, AvatarSizeLG, AvatarSizeXL} {
			output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
				Src:   "/a.jpg",
				Alt:   "A",
				Size:  size,
				Shape: AvatarShapeCircle,
			}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, `src="/a.jpg"`)
		}
	})

	t.Run("with online status dot scales", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Src:    "/b.jpg",
			Alt:    "B",
			Size:   AvatarSizeXL,
			Status: AvatarStatusOnline,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-green-400")
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultAvatarProps()
		if props.Size != AvatarSizeMD {
			t.Errorf("DefaultAvatarProps().Size = %q, want %q", props.Size, AvatarSizeMD)
		}
	})

	t.Run("fallback SVG when no src or initials", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<svg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<img")
	})

	t.Run("all size variants with status dot", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		for _, size := range []AvatarSize{AvatarSizeXS, AvatarSizeSM, AvatarSizeMD, AvatarSizeLG, AvatarSizeXL} {
			output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
				Src:    "/a.jpg",
				Status: AvatarStatusOnline,
				Size:   size,
			}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-green-400")
		}
	})

	t.Run("image with custom ID and class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			ID: "user-avatar", Class: "ring-2",
			Src: "/me.jpg",
			Alt: "Me",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="user-avatar"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "ring-2")
	})

	t.Run("initials with custom ID and class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			ID: "initials-avatar", Class: "shadow-md",
			Initials: "CD",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="initials-avatar"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "shadow-md")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "CD")
	})

	t.Run("fallback SVG with square shape", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Shape: AvatarShapeSquare,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-lg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<svg")
	})

	t.Run("initials with status dot (now renders in all branches)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Initials: "EF",
			Status:   AvatarStatusOffline,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "EF")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-gray-400")
	})
}

func TestAvatarUnknownStatusNoDot(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("unknown status renders no dot", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Src:    "/me.jpg",
			Alt:    "Me",
			Status: AvatarStatus("busy"),
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "bg-green-400")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "bg-gray-400")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-hidden="true"></span>`)
	})

	t.Run("none status renders no dot", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Avatar(AvatarProps{
			Src:    "/me.jpg",
			Alt:    "Me",
			Status: AvatarStatusNone,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "bg-green-400")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "bg-gray-400")
	})
}
package display

import (
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// BadgeType defines the visual style of a badge
type BadgeType string

const (
	BadgePrimary BadgeType = "primary"
	BadgeSuccess BadgeType = "success"
	BadgeWarning BadgeType = "warning"
	BadgeError   BadgeType = "error"
	BadgeInfo    BadgeType = "info"
	BadgeNeutral BadgeType = "neutral"
)

// BadgeSize defines the size of a badge
type BadgeSize string

const (
	BadgeSizeSM BadgeSize = "sm"
	BadgeSizeMD BadgeSize = "md"
	BadgeSizeLG BadgeSize = "lg"
)

// BadgeProps configures a status badge
type BadgeProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Text string
	Type BadgeType
	Size BadgeSize
	Pill bool
	Dot  bool
	Href string
}

// DefaultBadgeProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultBadgeProps() BadgeProps {
	return BadgeProps{
		Type: BadgeNeutral,
		Size: BadgeSizeMD,
	}
}

// Badge renders a compact status label
//
//	@display.Badge(display.BadgeProps{Text: "Active", Type: display.BadgeSuccess, Dot: true})
templ Badge(props BadgeProps) {
	if props.Href != "" {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(props.Href) }
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("inline-flex items-center font-medium", badgeSizeClass(props.Size), badgeShapeClass(props.Pill), badgeColorClass(props.Type), props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			@badgeContent(props)
		</a>
	} else {
		<span
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("inline-flex items-center font-medium", badgeSizeClass(props.Size), badgeShapeClass(props.Pill), badgeColorClass(props.Type), props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			@badgeContent(props)
		</span>
	}
}

// badgeContent renders the optional dot followed by the label. The dot and the
// label share ONE source line on purpose: a newline between them emits a
// literal space into the text content, so copied badge text started with a
// space and the gap no longer came from the me-1.5 utility alone.
templ badgeContent(props BadgeProps) {
	if props.Dot {
		<span class={ "me-1.5 h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full", badgeDotColorClass(props.Type) } aria-hidden="true"></span>{ props.Text }
	} else {
		{ props.Text }
	}
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for badge sizes
var badgeSizeLookup = map[BadgeSize]string{
	BadgeSizeSM: "px-2 py-0.5 text-xs",
	BadgeSizeMD: "px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs",
	BadgeSizeLG: "px-3 py-1 text-sm",
}

func badgeSizeClass(s BadgeSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(badgeSizeLookup, s, badgeSizeLookup[BadgeSizeMD])
}

func badgeShapeClass(pill bool) string {
	if pill {
		return "rounded-full"
	}
	return "rounded-md"
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for badge styles
type badgeStyle struct {
	BG  string
	Dot string
}

var badgeStyleMap = map[BadgeType]badgeStyle{
	BadgePrimary: {"bg-accent-100 text-accent-800 dark:bg-accent-900/30 dark:text-accent-300", "bg-accent-500"},
	BadgeSuccess: {"bg-green-100 text-green-800 dark:bg-green-900/30 dark:text-green-300", "bg-green-500"},
	BadgeWarning: {"bg-amber-100 text-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-300", "bg-amber-500"},
	BadgeError:   {"bg-red-100 text-red-800 dark:bg-red-900/30 dark:text-red-300", "bg-red-500"},
	BadgeInfo:    {"bg-blue-50 text-blue-800 dark:bg-blue-900/30 dark:text-blue-300", "bg-blue-500"},
	BadgeNeutral: {"bg-gray-100 text-gray-800 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:text-gray-300", "bg-gray-500"},
}

func badgeLookupStyle(t BadgeType) badgeStyle {
	return utils.Lookup(badgeStyleMap, t, badgeStyleMap[BadgeNeutral])
}

func badgeColorClass(t BadgeType) string    { return badgeLookupStyle(t).BG }
func badgeDotColorClass(t BadgeType) string { return badgeLookupStyle(t).Dot }

// StatusBadge is a convenience wrapper for common status values
// Maps status strings to badge types automatically
//
//	@display.StatusBadge("active")
templ StatusBadge(status string) {
	{{ mapped := MapStatusToBadgeType(status) }}
	@Badge(BadgeProps{Text: status, Type: mapped, Dot: true})
}

// StatusBadgeMapper maps a consumer status string to a badge type. Return
// the zero value ("" — rendered neutral) for unknown statuses; mappers that
// want the built-in mapping for unhandled values can call
// MapStatusToBadgeType.
type StatusBadgeMapper func(status string) BadgeType

// MapStatusToBadgeType maps a status string to a badge type — the built-in
// mapping behind StatusBadge, exposed for consumer mappers that extend
// rather than replace it (dnsblockd carries four local mappers — the
// extraction demand behind StatusBadgeWith).
func MapStatusToBadgeType(status string) BadgeType {
	return utils.Lookup(statusToBadgeMap, strings.ToLower(status), BadgeNeutral)
}

// resolveStatusBadgeType applies the consumer mapper when set, else the
// built-in mapping.
func resolveStatusBadgeType(mapper StatusBadgeMapper, status string) BadgeType {
	if mapper != nil {
		return mapper(status)
	}

	return MapStatusToBadgeType(status)
}

// StatusBadgeWith renders a StatusBadge through a consumer-supplied mapper —
// inject your domain's status vocabulary (e.g. dnsblockd's allow/block
// states) without forking the component. A nil mapper falls back to the
// built-in mapping (identical to StatusBadge).
//
//	@display.StatusBadgeWith(func(s string) display.BadgeType {
//		if s == "blocked" { return display.BadgeError }
//		return display.MapStatusToBadgeType(s)
//	}, row.Status)
templ StatusBadgeWith(mapper StatusBadgeMapper, status string) {
	{{ badgeType := resolveStatusBadgeType(mapper, status) }}
	@Badge(BadgeProps{Text: status, Type: badgeType, Dot: true})
}

var statusToBadgeMap = map[string]BadgeType{
	"active": BadgeSuccess, "healthy": BadgeSuccess, "success": BadgeSuccess,
	"completed": BadgeSuccess, "done": BadgeSuccess, "passed": BadgeSuccess, "green": BadgeSuccess,
	"pending": BadgeWarning, "warning": BadgeWarning, "degraded": BadgeWarning,
	"yellow": BadgeWarning, "in_progress": BadgeWarning,
	"error": BadgeError, "failed": BadgeError, "critical": BadgeError,
	"unhealthy": BadgeError, "red": BadgeError, "down": BadgeError,
	"info": BadgeInfo, "blue": BadgeInfo, "running": BadgeInfo,
	"primary": BadgePrimary, "default": BadgeNeutral,
}

const (
	badgeTextActive     = activeBadgeText // reuse existing

func testBadgeProps(text string, badgeType BadgeType) BadgeProps {

		BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{},

func TestBadgeRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name        string
		props       BadgeProps
		wantContain []string
	}{
		{
			name:        "basic success badge",
			props:       testBadgeProps(badgeTextActive, BadgeSuccess),
			wantContain: []string{badgeTextActive, "bg-green-100", "text-green-800"},
		},
		{
			name: "error badge with dot",

			props: BadgeProps{
				BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{},
				Text:      badgeTextFailed,
				Type:      BadgeError,
				Size:      BadgeSizeMD,
				Pill:      false,
				Dot:       true,
			},
			wantContain: []string{badgeTextFailed, "bg-red-100", cssClassRoundedFull, "bg-red-500"},
		},
		{
			name: "pill badge",

			props: BadgeProps{
				BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{},
				Text:      badgeTextBeta,
				Type:      BadgeInfo,
				Size:      BadgeSizeMD,
				Pill:      true,
				Dot:       false,
			},
			wantContain: []string{badgeTextBeta, cssClassRoundedFull, "bg-blue-50"},
		},
		{
			name: "with custom id and class",
			props: BadgeProps{
				BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{
					ID:        "status-badge",
					Class:     cssClassMl2,
					Attrs:     nil,
					AriaLabel: "",
				},
				Text: badgeTextRunning,
				Type: BadgePrimary,
				Size: BadgeSizeMD,
				Pill: false,
				Dot:  false,
			},
			wantContain: []string{`id="status-badge"`, cssClassMl2, "bg-accent-100"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			output := utils.Render(t, Badge(tt.props))
			for _, want := range tt.wantContain {
				utils.AssertContains(t, output, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBadgeFeatures(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("pill badge renders rounded-full", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			Text: badgeTextTag,
			Pill: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, cssClassRoundedFull)
	})

	t.Run("badge with dot", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			Text: badgeTextActive,
			Dot:  true,
			Type: BadgeSuccess,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, badgeTextActive)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, cssClassRoundedFull)
	})

	t.Run("all badge types render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		for _, bt := range []BadgeType{BadgePrimary, BadgeSuccess, BadgeWarning, BadgeError, BadgeInfo, BadgeNeutral} {
			output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
				Text: string(bt),
				Type: bt,
			}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, string(bt))
		}
	})

	t.Run("badge with custom class and id", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			ID: "my-badge", Class: cssClassMt2,
			Text: badgeTextCustom,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-badge"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, cssClassMt2)
	})

	t.Run("badge with aria-label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			AriaLabel: "Status indicator",
			Text:      badgeTextOK,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Status indicator"`)
	})

	t.Run("badge with pill and dot", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			Text: badgeTextBeta,
			Type: BadgePrimary,
			Pill: true,
			Dot:  true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, cssClassRoundedFull)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-500")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, badgeTextBeta)
	})
}

// TestBadgeDotHasNoLiteralSpace pins the text-content contract: the dot and
// the label are adjacent in the source, so copying a badge's text yields
// "Active", not " Active". The gap comes from the dot's me-1.5 utility alone.
func TestBadgeDotHasNoLiteralSpace(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("span variant", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{Text: badgeTextActive, Type: BadgeSuccess, Dot: true}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "</span> "+badgeTextActive)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "</span>"+badgeTextActive)
	})

	t.Run("link variant", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{
			Text: badgeTextActive, Type: BadgeSuccess, Dot: true, Href: "/status",
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "</span> "+badgeTextActive)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "</span>"+badgeTextActive)
	})

	t.Run("no dot keeps the bare label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(BadgeProps{Text: badgeTextActive, Type: BadgeSuccess}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, ">"+badgeTextActive+"<")
	})
}
package display

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// BarOrient controls bar chart orientation.
type BarOrient string

const (
	// BarHorizontal renders bars left-to-right (default).
	BarHorizontal BarOrient = "horizontal"
	// BarVertical renders bars bottom-to-top (column chart).
	BarVertical BarOrient = "vertical"
)

// barChartFallbackName names the role="img" wrapper when the consumer provides
// no AriaLabel — role="img" must never render unnamed.
const barChartFallbackName = "Bar chart"

// BarOrientIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined BarOrient constants.
func BarOrientIsValid(v BarOrient) bool {
	return v == BarHorizontal || v == BarVertical
}

// BarChartBar represents a single bar in a bar chart.
type BarChartBar struct {
	// Label is the bar's category name (e.g. "general", "Alice").
	Label string

	// Value is the bar's magnitude.
	Value float64

	// Color overrides the default bar color — a complete light+dark bg-*
	// literal (e.g. "bg-emerald-600 dark:bg-emerald-500"). Empty = use default.
	Color tone.ColorClass

	// Href makes the bar label a clickable link.
	Href string

	// Tooltip sets a per-bar title attribute (native browser tooltip).
	// Useful for dense charts where per-bar labels are hidden.
	Tooltip string

	// ValueLabel overrides the auto-formatted value display. When set,
	// this string is shown instead of ValueFormat(Value). Useful for
	// composite labels like "123 (45%)" or "1.2 GB".
	ValueLabel string
}

// BarChartProps configures a CSS bar chart.
type BarChartProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Bars are the data points to render.
	Bars []BarChartBar

	// Orient is the bar orientation. Default: BarHorizontal.
	Orient BarOrient

	// Max overrides the auto-computed maximum (0 = auto from data).
	Max float64

	// BarColor is the default bg-* literal for bars without a per-bar Color
	// override. Default: "bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500".
	BarColor tone.ColorClass

	// LabelWidth is the label column width for horizontal charts (Tailwind
	// width class, e.g. "w-32"). Default: "w-32".
	LabelWidth string

	// ShowValues renders the numeric value next to each bar.
	ShowValues bool

	// ValueFormat formats the value for display. Default: fmt.Sprintf("%.0f", v).
	ValueFormat func(float64) string

	// EmptyMessage is shown when Bars is empty. Default: "No data".
	EmptyMessage string

	// MinBarWidth sets the minimum width for vertical bars (Tailwind
	// width class, e.g. "min-w-1" for dense time-series). Default: "min-w-12".
	MinBarWidth string

	// Gap controls the spacing between bars (Tailwind gap class,
	// e.g. "gap-px" for dense charts). Default: "gap-2" (vertical),
	// "" (horizontal, uses space-y-2).
	Gap string

	// Height sets the chart container height (CSS value, e.g. "8rem").
	// Vertical bars are percentage heights — they need a definite ancestor
	// height to resolve against, so empty defaults to 12rem (previously the
	// bars silently collapsed to 0px, #48). Tailwind class strings like
	// `h-40` are invalid here; set a CSS value. No effect on horizontal.
	Height string

	// MaxBarWidth caps each vertical bar column (Tailwind max-width class,
	// e.g. "max-w-16") so small-N series do not stretch into giant blocks;
	// the capped track is centered (#59). Empty = uncapped (each column
	// takes an equal share of the full width, the historical behavior). No
	// effect on horizontal.
	MaxBarWidth string

	// ShowBaseline draws a hairline at the zero position of a vertical
	// chart (#59). Signed series (any negative value) always draw it — the
	// zero line is what makes the sign readable — so this only adds the
	// line for all-positive data. No effect on horizontal.
	ShowBaseline bool

	// NegativeBarColor colors vertical bars with negative values — a
	// complete light+dark bg-* literal (e.g. "bg-rose-700 dark:bg-rose-500")
	// so the sign survives the render (#59). Default:
	// "bg-rose-600 dark:bg-rose-500". No effect on horizontal (which clamps
	// negatives to zero-width today).
	NegativeBarColor tone.ColorClass
}

const (
	defaultBarColor    = "bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500"
	defaultEmptyMsg    = "No data"
	defaultLabelWidth  = "w-32"
	defaultMinBarWidth = "min-w-12"
	defaultVerticalGap = "gap-2"
	// defaultVerticalHeight resolves the percentage-height bars when the
	// consumer sets no Height — without a definite height they collapsed
	// to 0px (the #48 bug class).
	defaultVerticalHeight = "12rem"
	// defaultNegativeBarColor keeps signed series readable: negatives take
	// the danger family instead of losing their sign (#59).
	defaultNegativeBarColor = "bg-rose-600 dark:bg-rose-500"
	percentScale            = 100.0
	percentRound            = 10.0
	zeroPercent             = "0.0%"
	// percentScalePct is the full-range percentage as a CSS string.
	percentScalePct = "100.0%"
)

// DefaultBarChartProps returns sensible defaults for a bar chart.
func DefaultBarChartProps() BarChartProps {
	return BarChartProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
		Orient:       BarHorizontal,
		BarColor:     defaultBarColor,
		LabelWidth:   defaultLabelWidth,
		ShowValues:   true,
		EmptyMessage: defaultEmptyMsg,
		ValueFormat:  func(v float64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f", v) },
	}
}

// barChartMax returns the effective max, auto-computing from data when 0.
func barChartMax(bars []BarChartBar, override float64) float64 {
	return chartMaxWithOverride(override, func() float64 {
		var maxVal float64

		for _, b := range bars {
			if b.Value > maxVal {
				maxVal = b.Value
			}
		}

		return maxVal
	})
}

// barChartBounds returns the signed plotting bounds of a vertical series:
// the largest positive value (or the Max override when set) and the most
// negative one (clamped at zero — a series without negatives plots on a
// bottom baseline exactly like the historical unsigned rendering).
func barChartBounds(bars []BarChartBar, maxOverride float64) (float64, float64) {
	maxVal := barChartMax(bars, maxOverride)
	minVal := 0.0

	for _, b := range bars {
		if b.Value < minVal {
			minVal = b.Value
		}
	}

	return maxVal, minVal
}

// barChartSignedPlacement returns the CSS placement of one vertical bar in
// the signed plot area: how far the zero line sits above the bottom (a
// percentage), the top offset a hanging (negative) bar anchors at, the bar
// height (a percentage of the full signed range), and whether the value is
// negative. An all-zero or degenerate range collapses to the bottom baseline.
func barChartSignedPlacement(
	value, maxVal, minVal float64,
) (string, string, string, bool) {
	total := maxVal - minVal

	if total <= 0 {
		return zeroPercent, percentScalePct, zeroPercent, value < 0
	}

	zeroPct := (0 - minVal) / total * percentScale

	return formatPct(zeroPct), formatPct(percentScale - zeroPct),
		formatPct(math.Round(math.Abs(value)/total*percentScale*percentRound) / percentRound),
		value < 0
}

// formatPct renders a percentage with one decimal (the bar chart's shared
// rounding contract).
func formatPct(v float64) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", math.Round(v*percentRound)/percentRound)
}

// barValueLabel returns the display string for a bar's value, preferring
// the per-bar ValueLabel override when set.
func barValueLabel(bar BarChartBar, fallback func(float64) string) string {
	if bar.ValueLabel != "" {
		return bar.ValueLabel
	}

	return fallback(bar.Value)
}

// barPercentWidth returns the CSS width percentage for a bar value.
func barPercentWidth(value, maxVal float64) string {
	if maxVal <= 0 {
		return zeroPercent
	}

	pct := (value / maxVal) * percentScale

	if pct < 0 {
		pct = 0
	}

	if pct > percentScale {
		pct = percentScale
	}

	return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", math.Round(pct*percentRound)/percentRound)
}
package display

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// BarChart renders a CSS-based bar chart — no JavaScript, no SVG.
// Horizontal orientation shows label bars; vertical shows columns.
// The chart is responsive and dark-mode aware.
//
//	@display.BarChart(display.BarChartProps{
//	   Bars: []display.BarChartBar{
//	       {Label: "general", Value: 1200},
//	       {Label: "random", Value: 800},
//	       {Label: "dev", Value: 450},
//	   },
//	})
templ BarChart(props BarChartProps) {
	{{
		bars := props.Bars
		orient := props.Orient
		if !BarOrientIsValid(orient) {
			orient = BarHorizontal
		}
		barColor := string(props.BarColor)
		if barColor == "" {
			barColor = "bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500"
		}
		labelWidth := props.LabelWidth
		if labelWidth == "" {
			labelWidth = "w-32"
		}
		emptyMsg := props.EmptyMessage
		if emptyMsg == "" {
			emptyMsg = "No data"
		}
		valueFmt := props.ValueFormat
		if valueFmt == nil {
			valueFmt = func(v float64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f", v) }
		}
		maxVal, minVal := barChartBounds(bars, props.Max)
		hasNegative := minVal < 0
		minBarW := props.MinBarWidth
		if minBarW == "" {
			minBarW = defaultMinBarWidth
		}
		gapClass := props.Gap
		if gapClass == "" {
			gapClass = defaultVerticalGap
		}
	}}
	if len(bars) == 0 {
		<p
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		>{ emptyMsg }</p>
	} else if orient == BarVertical {
		{{
			heightVal := props.Height
			if heightVal == "" {
				heightVal = defaultVerticalHeight
			}

			negColor := string(props.NegativeBarColor)
			if negColor == "" {
				negColor = defaultNegativeBarColor
			}
		}}
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("flex overflow-x-auto", gapClass, utils.Ternary(props.MaxBarWidth != "", "justify-center", ""), props.Class) }
			style={ "height:" + heightVal }
			role="img"
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, barChartFallbackName) }
		>
			for _, bar := range bars {
				{{ zeroPct, barTopPct, heightPct, negative := barChartSignedPlacement(bar.Value, maxVal, minVal) }}
				<div
					class={ utils.Class("flex h-full w-full flex-col items-center gap-1", minBarW, props.MaxBarWidth) }
					if bar.Tooltip != "" {
						title={ bar.Tooltip }
					}
				>
					<div class="relative w-full flex-1">
						if props.ShowBaseline || hasNegative {
							<div class="absolute inset-x-0 h-px bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700" style={ "bottom:" + zeroPct }></div>
						}
						if negative {
							if props.ShowValues {
								<span class="absolute inset-x-0 text-center text-xs tabular-nums text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400" style={ "top:calc(" + barTopPct + " + " + heightPct + ")" }>{ barValueLabel(bar, valueFmt) }</span>
							}
							<div class={ utils.Class("absolute inset-x-0 rounded-b", negColor, string(bar.Color)) } style={ "top:" + barTopPct + ";height:" + heightPct }></div>
						} else {
							if props.ShowValues {
								<span class="absolute inset-x-0 text-center text-xs tabular-nums text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400" style={ "bottom:calc(" + zeroPct + " + " + heightPct + ")" }>{ barValueLabel(bar, valueFmt) }</span>
							}
							<div class={ utils.Class("absolute inset-x-0 rounded-t", barColor, string(bar.Color)) } style={ "bottom:" + zeroPct + ";height:" + heightPct }></div>
						}
					</div>
					<span class="w-full truncate text-center text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400" title={ bar.Label }>
						{ truncateLabel(bar.Label, 12) }
					</span>
				</div>
			}
		</div>
	} else {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("space-y-2", props.Class) }
			role="img"
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, barChartFallbackName) }
		>
			for _, bar := range bars {
				<div
					class="flex items-center gap-3"
					if bar.Tooltip != "" {
						title={ bar.Tooltip }
					}
				>
					if bar.Href != "" {
						<a
							href={ templ.SafeURL(bar.Href) }
							class={ utils.Class("shrink-0 truncate text-xs font-medium text-gray-700 hover:text-accent-600 dark:text-gray-300 dark:hover:text-accent-400", labelWidth) }
							title={ bar.Label }
						>
							{ truncateLabel(bar.Label, 22) }
						</a>
					} else {
						<span class={ utils.Class("shrink-0 truncate text-xs font-medium text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300", labelWidth) } title={ bar.Label }>
							{ truncateLabel(bar.Label, 22) }
						</span>
					}
					<div class="flex-1 overflow-hidden rounded bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-800">
						<div
							class={ utils.Class("h-5 rounded bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500", barColor, string(bar.Color)) }
							style={ "width:" + barPercentWidth(bar.Value, maxVal) }
						></div>
					</div>
					if props.ShowValues {
						<span class="w-16 shrink-0 text-end text-xs tabular-nums text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400">
							{ barValueLabel(bar, valueFmt) }
						</span>
					}
				</div>
			}
		</div>
	}
}

// truncateLabel truncates a string to maxLen runes with an ellipsis. Trimming
// runes (not bytes) keeps multibyte labels valid UTF-8 — a byte cut split
// characters in half and rendered mojibake for international labels.
func truncateLabel(s string, maxLen int) string {
	runes := []rune(s)
	if len(runes) <= maxLen {
		return s
	}
	return string(runes[:maxLen-1]) + "…"
}

func TestBarChartVertical(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, BarChart(BarChartProps{
		Orient: BarVertical,
		Bars: []BarChartBar{
			{Label: "Mon", Value: 10},
			{Label: "Tue", Value: 20},
		},
	}))
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "height:12rem")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-full")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "relative w-full flex-1")

}

		}

func TestBarChartPercentWidth(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		value float64
		max   float64
		want  string
	}{
		{0, 100, "0.0%"},
		{50, 100, "50.0%"},
		{100, 100, "100.0%"},
		{150, 100, "100.0%"},
		{-10, 100, "0.0%"},
		{10, 0, "0.0%"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		got := barPercentWidth(tt.value, tt.max)
		if got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("barPercentWidth(%f, %f) = %q, want %q", tt.value, tt.max, got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestTruncateLabel(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		input  string
		maxLen int
		want   string
	}{
		{"short", 10, "short"},
		{"exactly 10", 10, "exactly 10"},
		{"this is too long", 10, "this is t…"},
		// Regression: byte-slicing split multibyte runes, emitting invalid
		// UTF-8 (mojibake) for international bar labels. Truncation must be
		// rune-safe and still end with the ellipsis.
		{"aÜÜÜÜÜÜ", 6, "aÜÜÜÜ…"},
		{"Änderungsübersicht", 10, "Änderungs…"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		got := truncateLabel(tt.input, tt.maxLen)
		if got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("truncateLabel(%q, %d) = %q, want %q", tt.input, tt.maxLen, got, tt.want)
		}

		if !utf8.ValidString(got) {
			t.Errorf("truncateLabel(%q, %d) = %q is not valid UTF-8", tt.input, tt.maxLen, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestBarChartSignedPlacement(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name         string
		value        float64
		maxVal       float64
		minVal       float64
		wantZero     string
		wantTop      string
		wantHeight   string
		wantNegative bool
	}{
		{"all-positive pins the zero line to the bottom", 6, 8, 0, "0.0%", "100.0%", "75.0%", false},
		{"mixed series lifts the zero line", 6, 6, -2, "25.0%", "75.0%", "75.0%", false},
		{"negative hangs below the zero line", -1, 6, -2, "25.0%", "75.0%", "12.5%", true},
		{"all-negative pins the zero line to the top", -3, 0, -3, "100.0%", "0.0%", "100.0%", true},
		{"degenerate range collapses to the baseline", 0, 0, 0, "0.0%", "100.0%", "0.0%", false},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			zero, top, height, negative := barChartSignedPlacement(tt.value, tt.maxVal, tt.minVal)
			if zero != tt.wantZero || top != tt.wantTop || height != tt.wantHeight || negative != tt.wantNegative {
				t.Errorf(
					"barChartSignedPlacement(%v, %v, %v) = (%q, %q, %q, %v), want (%q, %q, %q, %v)",
					tt.value,
					tt.maxVal,
					tt.minVal,
					zero,
					top,
					height,
					negative,
					tt.wantZero,
					tt.wantTop,
					tt.wantHeight,
					tt.wantNegative,
				)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBarChartBoundsSigned(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	bars := []BarChartBar{
		{Label: "a", Value: 420},
		{Label: "b", Value: -180},
		{Label: "c", Value: 90},
	}

	maxVal, minVal := barChartBounds(bars, 0)
	if maxVal != 420 || minVal != -180 {
		t.Errorf("barChartBounds() = (%v, %v), want (420, -180)", maxVal, minVal)
	}

	// The Max override replaces the positive bound only; the negative bound
	// always comes from the data.
	maxVal, minVal = barChartBounds(bars, 1000)
	if maxVal != 1000 || minVal != -180 {
		t.Errorf("barChartBounds(override) = (%v, %v), want (1000, -180)", maxVal, minVal)
	}
}

func TestBarChartVerticalSigned(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	output := utils.Render(t, BarChart(BarChartProps{
		Orient: BarVertical,
		Bars: []BarChartBar{
			{Label: "in", Value: 420},
			{Label: "out", Value: -180},
		},
		Height:     "10rem",
		ShowValues: true,
	}))

	// The zero baseline is mandatory for signed series.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-px")
	// Negatives take the danger family and hang below the zero line.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-rose-600 dark:bg-rose-500")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-b")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "style=\"top:70.0%;height:30.0%;\"")
	// Positives still grow upward from the zero line.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "style=\"bottom:30.0%;height:70.0%;\"")
}

// --- CopyButton Behavior ---

func TestCopyButtonBehavior(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders button with copy data attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:  "hello world",
			Label: "Copy",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-copy="hello world"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Copy")
	})

	t.Run("renders with custom copied label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:        "abc",
			CopiedLabel: "Done!",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-copy-label="Done!"`)
	})

	t.Run("includes clipboard icon when enabled", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text: "x",
			Icon: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<svg")
	})

	t.Run("omits icon when disabled", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text: "x",
			Icon: false,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<svg")
	})

	t.Run("includes singleton script with nonce", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:  "x",
			Nonce: "secret123",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `nonce="secret123"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcCopyAttached")
	})

	t.Run("includes execCommand fallback for non-secure contexts", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "execCommand")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcFallbackCopy")
	})

	t.Run("copy announcement lives outside the interactive element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		// The label span carries NO live semantics: live regions must live
		// outside <button>/<a> (achecker aria_descendant_valid — role AND
		// aria-live both trip it). The sibling [data-tc-copy-status] region
		// (role="status") receives the announcement from the copy script.
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-live="polite"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<span data-tc-copy-status role="status" class="sr-only"></span>`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `tcAnnounceCopy`)
		// The status region must be a SIBLING of the button, not a descendant.
		btnClose := strings.Index(output, "</button>")

		statusIdx := strings.Index(output, `data-tc-copy-status`)
		if btnClose < 0 || statusIdx < 0 || statusIdx < btnClose {
			t.Errorf("status region must render after the button element: %q", output)
		}
	})

	t.Run("renders anchor when Href is set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text: "snippet",
			Href: "/snippets/42",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<a`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/snippets/42"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-copy="snippet"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `<button`)
	})

	t.Run("renders button when Href is empty", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<button`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `<a`)
	})

	t.Run("label span carries the explicit default color", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{Text: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `class="text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200"`)
	})

	t.Run("LabelClass replaces the default label color on buttons", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:       "x",
			LabelClass: "text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-300",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `class="text-emerald-700 dark:text-emerald-300"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `class="text-gray-700`)
	})

	t.Run("LabelClass replaces the default label color on anchors", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CopyButton(CopyButtonProps{
			Text:       "x",
			Href:       "https://example.com",
			LabelClass: "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `class="text-red-600 dark:text-red-400"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `class="text-gray-700`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-copy="x"`)
	})
}

// --- RelativeTime Behavior ---

func TestRelativeTimeBehavior(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders time element with datetime attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		ts := time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 10, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{Time: ts}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<time")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `datetime="2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"`)
	})

	t.Run("shows just now for recent time", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		now := time.Now()
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{Time: now}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "just now")
	})

	t.Run("shows absolute title for hover", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		ts := time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 10, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{Time: ts}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `title="Jan 15, 2025`)
	})

	t.Run("auto-refresh is on by default (progressive enhancement)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultRelativeTimeProps()
		props.Time = time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Hour)
		props.Nonce = "n1"
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-relative`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `nonce="n1"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcRelativeTimeAttached")
	})

	t.Run("auto-refresh can be disabled for static contexts", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{
			Time:        time.Now(),
			AutoRefresh: false,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-tc-relative")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcRelativeTimeAttached")
	})

	t.Run("EmptyText replaces zero-time date noise (issue #52)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{
			Time:      time.Time{},
			EmptyText: "never",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<time")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, ">never<")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "0001")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "datetime=")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "title=")
		// The refresh script must not adopt the placeholder — it would
		// re-format "never" into date noise after the first tick.
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-tc-relative")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcRelativeTimeAttached")
	})

	t.Run("EmptyText with zero time honors an explicit Title", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{
			Time:      time.Time{},
			EmptyText: "never",
			Title:     "no successful probe yet",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `title="no successful probe yet"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, ">never<")
	})

	t.Run("EmptyText is ignored for non-zero Time", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		ts := time.Date(2025, 1, 15, 10, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{
			Time:      ts,
			EmptyText: "never",
			Now:       ts.Add(90 * time.Second),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `datetime="2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "1 minute ago")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "never")
	})

	t.Run("unset EmptyText keeps the legacy zero-time output", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(RelativeTimeProps{
			Time:        time.Time{},
			AutoRefresh: false,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `datetime="0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`)
	})
}

// --- Image Behavior ---

func TestImageBehavior(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders img with src and alt", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{
			Src: "/photo.jpg",
			Alt: "A photo",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `src="/photo.jpg"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `alt="A photo"`)
	})

	t.Run("lazy by default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultImageProps()
		props.Src = "/x.jpg"
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `loading="lazy"`)
	})

	t.Run("eager when lazy is false", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{Src: "/x.jpg", Lazy: false}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `loading="eager"`)
	})

	t.Run("includes width and height when set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{
			Src:    "/x.jpg",
			Width:  200,
			Height: 100,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `width="200"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `height="100"`)
	})

	t.Run("adds fallback data attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{
			Src:         "/x.jpg",
			FallbackSrc: "/fallback.jpg",
			Nonce:       "n1",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-img-fallback="/fallback.jpg"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcImageFallbackAttached")
	})

	t.Run("rounded-full when Rounded is true", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{Src: "/avatar.jpg", Rounded: true}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-full")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "rounded-md")
	})

	t.Run("rounded-md by default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Image(ImageProps{Src: "/x.jpg"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-md")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "rounded-full")
	})
}

package display

import (

const (

// --- Badge Behavior ---

func TestBadgeUserSeesCorrectVisualFeedback(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("user sees success badge with green styling", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Badge(DefaultBadgeProps()))

// benchRender times one component rendering into a fresh buffer.
func benchRender(b *testing.B, component templ.Component) {
	b.Helper()

	b.ResetTimer()

	for b.Loop() {
		var buf bytes.Buffer

		_ = component.Render(context.Background(), &buf)
	}
}

func BenchmarkHotPaths(b *testing.B) {
	b.Run("Class merge", func(b *testing.B) {
		for b.Loop() {
			utils.Class("px-4 py-2", "px-6", "bg-red-500", "bg-blue-500")
		}
	})

	b.Run("Badge render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultBadgeProps()
		props.Text = activeBadgeText

		benchRender(b, Badge(props))
	})

	b.Run("Card render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultCardProps()
		props.Title = "Users"

		benchRender(b, Card(props))
	})

	b.Run("Table render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name", "Email", "Role"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				SimpleTableRow("Alice", "alice@example.com", "Admin"),
				SimpleTableRow("Bob", "bob@example.com", "User"),
			},
		}

		benchRender(b, Table(props))
	})

	b.Run("Modal render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultModalProps()
		props.ID = "test-modal"
		props.Title = "Confirm"

		benchRender(b, Modal(props))
	})

	b.Run("Dropdown render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DropdownProps{
			ID:    "dd",
			Label: dropdownLabelActions,
			Items: []DropdownItem{
				{Text: dropdownItemEdit, Href: dropdownHrefEdit},
				{Text: "Delete", Href: "/delete"},
			},
		}

		benchRender(b, Dropdown(props))
	})

	b.Run("CopyButton render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultCopyButtonProps()
		props.Text = "pnpm add foo"

		benchRender(b, CopyButton(props))
	})

	b.Run("CountBadge render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := CountBadgeProps{Count: 42}

		benchRender(b, CountBadge(props))
	})

	b.Run("Image render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := ImageProps{Src: "/photo.jpg", Alt: "Photo", Width: 128, Height: 128, FallbackSrc: "/placeholder.jpg"}

		benchRender(b, Image(props))
	})

	b.Run("RelativeTime render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := RelativeTimeProps{Time: mustTime("2025-01-15T10:30:00Z")}

		benchRender(b, RelativeTime(props))
	})

	b.Run("Sparkline render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultSparklineProps()
		props.Values = []float64{1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3, 7, 5, 8}

		benchRender(b, Sparkline(props))
	})

	b.Run("BarChart render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultBarChartProps()
		props.Bars = []BarChartBar{
			{Label: "general", Value: 1200},
			{Label: "random", Value: 800},
			{Label: "dev", Value: 450},
		}

		benchRender(b, BarChart(props))
	})

	b.Run("ExternalLink render", func(b *testing.B) {
		props := DefaultExternalLinkProps()
		props.Href = "https://example.com"
		props.Text = "Open"

		benchRender(b, ExternalLink(props))
	})
}

func mustTime(s string) time.Time {
	t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, s)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	return t
}

// TestToneAdapterDefaults cover the unknown-value fallbacks of every Tone/Hue
// adapter: an out-of-set enum must map to the neutral slot, never panic and
// never return an empty value (consumers pass user data through these).
func TestToneAdapterDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	unknown := "not-a-real-value"

	if got := StatusTone(unknown).Tone(); got == "" {
		t.Error("StatusTone(unknown).Tone() returned empty")
	}

	if got := StatusTone(unknown).DotHue(); got == "" {
		t.Error("StatusTone(unknown).DotHue() returned empty")
	}

	if got := KanbanTone(unknown).Hue(); got == "" {
		t.Error("KanbanTone(unknown).Hue() returned empty")
	}

	if got := StatTone(unknown).Hue(); got == "" {
		t.Error("StatTone(unknown).Hue() returned empty")
	}

	if got := TrendDirection(unknown).Tone(); got == "" {
		t.Error("TrendDirection(unknown).Tone() returned empty")
	}

	if got := ScrollbackTone(unknown).Tone(); got == "" {
		t.Error("ScrollbackTone(unknown).Tone() returned empty")
	}

	if got := BadgeType(unknown).Tone(); got == "" {
		t.Error("BadgeType(unknown).Tone() returned empty")
	}
}

// TestDefaultValueFormatters pins the documented default formatters that no
// golden reaches (goldens always pass their own formatter).
func TestDefaultValueFormatters(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	barFormat := DefaultBarChartProps().ValueFormat
	if barFormat == nil {
		t.Fatal("DefaultBarChartProps().ValueFormat is nil")
	}

	if got := barFormat(42.6); got != "43" {
		t.Errorf("default bar ValueFormat(42.6) = %q, want %q", got, "43")
	}

	heatmapFormat := DefaultHeatmapProps().ValueFormat
	if heatmapFormat == nil {
		t.Fatal("DefaultHeatmapProps().ValueFormat is nil")
	}

	if got := heatmapFormat(3.4); got != "3" {
		t.Errorf("default heatmap ValueFormat(3.4) = %q, want %q", got, "3")
	}
}

// TestBarValueLabelPrecedence: a per-bar ValueLabel wins; otherwise the shared
// formatter is used.
func TestBarValueLabelPrecedence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	fallback := func(float64) string { return "fmt" }

	if got := barValueLabel(BarChartBar{Value: 7}, fallback); got != "fmt" {
		t.Errorf("barValueLabel without ValueLabel = %q, want %q", got, "fmt")
	}

	if got := barValueLabel(BarChartBar{Value: 7, ValueLabel: "custom"}, fallback); got != "custom" {
		t.Errorf("barValueLabel with ValueLabel = %q, want %q", got, "custom")
	}
}

// TestChartLegendSkipsUnnamedSeries: a series without a name is data, not a
// legend row, and must not consume horizontal space.
func TestChartLegendSkipsUnnamedSeries(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	items := buildChartLegend([]LineChartSeries{
		{Name: "", Values: []float64{1, 2}},
		{Name: "Named", Values: []float64{1, 2}},
	}, 12)
	if len(items) != 1 || items[0].Name != "Named" {
		t.Fatalf("legend items = %+v, want exactly the named series", items)
	}

	if items[0].X != 12 {
		t.Errorf("first legend X = %d, want startX 12", items[0].X)
	}
}

// TestNiceStepBuckets pins the human-readable tick ladder, including the 5
// bucket that the default fixtures never reach.
func TestNiceStepBuckets(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := niceStepForNormalized(4); got != niceStepFive {
		t.Errorf("niceStepForNormalized(4) = %v, want %v", got, niceStepFive)
	}

	if got := niceStepForNormalized(42); got != niceStepTen {
		t.Errorf("niceStepForNormalized(42) = %v, want %v", got, niceStepTen)
	}
}

// TestLineChartBoundsEdges: caller overrides win over the data range, and a
// flat series is padded so the renderer never divides by zero.
func TestLineChartBoundsEdges(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	series := []LineChartSeries{{Values: []float64{3, 9}}}
	minOverride, maxOverride := 0.0, 100.0

	minVal, maxVal := lineChartBounds(series, &minOverride, &maxOverride)
	if minVal != minOverride || maxVal != maxOverride {
		t.Errorf("lineChartBounds overrides = (%v, %v), want (0, 100)", minVal, maxVal)
	}

	minVal, maxVal = lineChartBounds([]LineChartSeries{{Values: []float64{5, 5}}}, nil, nil)
	if maxVal <= minVal {
		t.Errorf("flat range = (%v, %v), want max > min", minVal, maxVal)
	}
}

// TestLineChartGeometryEdges: positive stroke widths pass through, and a
// single tick label sits at the plot origin.
func TestLineChartGeometryEdges(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := lineChartStrokeWidth(3.5); got != 3.5 {
		t.Errorf("lineChartStrokeWidth(3.5) = %v, want 3.5", got)
	}

	if got := lineChartStrokeWidth(0); got != lineChartDefaultStroke {
		t.Errorf("lineChartStrokeWidth(0) = %v, want default %v", got, lineChartDefaultStroke)
	}

	if got := lineChartTickLabelX(200, 1, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("lineChartTickLabelX(n=1) = %v, want 0", got)
	}

	if got := lineChartTickLabelX(200, 2, 1); got != 200 {
		t.Errorf("lineChartTickLabelX(n=2, i=1) = %v, want 200", got)
	}
}

// TestPieChartFormattingEdges: a zero total yields no angle, and whole

func TestPieChartFormattingEdges(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := pieChartSliceAngle(4, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pieChartSliceAngle(total=0) = %v, want 0", got)
	}

	if got := pieChartFormatPercent(50); got != "50%" {
		t.Errorf("pieChartFormatPercent(50) = %q, want %q", got, "50%")
	}

	if got := pieChartFormatPercent(12.5); got != "12.5%" {
		t.Errorf("pieChartFormatPercent(12.5) = %q, want %q", got, "12.5%")
	}
}

// TestSparklineDegenerateInputs: fewer than two points render nothing, and a
// flat range is padded so the area path stays finite.
func TestSparklineDegenerateInputs(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := sparklineAreaPath([]float64{1}, 20, 10, 0, 1); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("sparklineAreaPath(single point) = %q, want empty", got)
	}

	span, ok := sparklineGeometry([]float64{2, 2}, 2, 2)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("sparklineGeometry(two points) reported ok=false")
	}

	if span <= 0 {
		t.Errorf("sparklineGeometry(flat range) span = %v, want > 0", span)
	}

	if _, ok := sparklineGeometry([]float64{1}, 0, 1); ok {
		t.Error("sparklineGeometry(single point) reported ok=true")
	}
}

	}

	if got := OverlayModal.componentName(); got != "Modal" {
		t.Errorf("OverlayModal.componentName() = %q, want %q", got, "Modal")
	}
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// buttonContent renders the element's inner markup: the consumer Children
// slot when set, otherwise Icon + Text.
templ buttonContent(props ButtonProps) {
	if props.Children != nil {
		@props.Children
	} else {
		if props.Icon != nil {
			@props.Icon
		}{ props.Text }
	}
}

// Button renders a button or link styled as a button.
// When Href is set, renders as an anchor tag; otherwise renders as a button element.
//
//	@display.Button(display.DefaultButtonProps())
//	@display.Button(display.ButtonProps{Text: "Save", Type: display.ButtonHTMLSubmit})
//	@display.Button(display.ButtonProps{Text: "Docs", Href: "/docs", Variant: display.ButtonSecondary})
templ Button(props ButtonProps) {
	{{
		classes := utils.Class(
			buttonBaseClass,
			buttonVariantClasses(props.Variant),
			buttonSizeClasses(props.Size),
			props.Class,
		)
	}}
	if props.Href != "" {
		<a
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			href={ templ.SafeURL(props.Href) }
			class={ utils.Class(classes, utils.Ternary(props.Disabled, "pointer-events-none opacity-50", "")) }
			if props.Disabled {
				aria-disabled="true"
				tabindex="-1"
			}
			if props.External {
				target="_blank"
				rel="noopener noreferrer"
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			if props.Wire != nil {
				{ props.Wire.Attributes()... }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>@buttonContent(props)</a>
	} else {
		<button
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			type={ buttonHTMLType(props.Type) }
			class={ classes }
			if props.Disabled {
				disabled
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			if props.Wire != nil {
				{ props.Wire.Attributes()... }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>@buttonContent(props)</button>
	}
}
// Button component: variant/size enums, default props, and class lookups.
package display

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// ButtonType defines the visual style of a button.
type ButtonType string

// Button variant constants.
const (
	ButtonPrimary   ButtonType = "primary"
	ButtonSecondary ButtonType = "secondary"
	ButtonDanger    ButtonType = "danger"
	ButtonGhost     ButtonType = "ghost"
	ButtonLink      ButtonType = "link"

	// Outline variants: neutral shell (white/transparent, colored ring and
	// text) for secondary destructive/warning/informative actions such as
	// row-level Undo, Restore, or Report-spam buttons. They pair with the
	// filled Primary/Danger for the main action of a toolbar.
	ButtonOutlineDanger  ButtonType = "outline-danger"
	ButtonOutlineWarning ButtonType = "outline-warning"
	ButtonOutlineSuccess ButtonType = "outline-success"
	ButtonOutlineInfo    ButtonType = "outline-info"
)

// ButtonSize defines the size of a button.
type ButtonSize string

// Button size constants.
const (
	ButtonSizeSM ButtonSize = "sm"
	ButtonSizeMD ButtonSize = "md"
	ButtonSizeLG ButtonSize = "lg"
)

// ButtonHTMLType is the HTML type attribute for a <button> element.
type ButtonHTMLType string

// Button HTML type constants.
const (
	ButtonHTMLButton ButtonHTMLType = "button"
	ButtonHTMLSubmit ButtonHTMLType = "submit"
	ButtonHTMLReset  ButtonHTMLType = "reset"
)

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for button HTML types
var buttonHTMLTypeLookup = map[ButtonHTMLType]string{
	ButtonHTMLButton: string(ButtonHTMLButton),
	ButtonHTMLSubmit: string(ButtonHTMLSubmit),
	ButtonHTMLReset:  string(ButtonHTMLReset),
}

// buttonHTMLType returns the validated HTML type attribute. Unknown or empty
// values fall back to "button" — matching the map+fallback convention used by
// all other enums in the library and the HTML spec default.
func buttonHTMLType(t ButtonHTMLType) string {
	return utils.Lookup(buttonHTMLTypeLookup, t, string(ButtonHTMLButton))
}

// ButtonProps configures a button or link styled as a button.
type ButtonProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	Text     string
	Type     ButtonHTMLType // button, submit, reset (default: button; ignored when Href is set)
	Href     string         // if set, renders as <a> instead of <button>
	Variant  ButtonType     // default: Primary
	Size     ButtonSize     // default: MD
	Disabled bool
	Icon     templ.Component
	// Children, when set, replaces the default content (Icon + Text) inside
	// the element. Use it to compose rich button content — a spinner plus a
	// loading label, an icon-text stack, a badge — while keeping the
	// library's classes, variants, and Wire/HTMX attributes. Consumer-owned:
	// a11y of the inner markup is the consumer's responsibility (the element
	// still carries AriaLabel when set).
	Children templ.Component
	External bool // adds target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer" for links
	// Wire is the optional transport-agnostic wiring (see the wire package).
	// When set, the action's attributes are rendered on the element in the
	// configured transport's dialect (htmx by default, Datastar opt-in) so
	// the same props work under either runtime. Composes with Attrs.
	Wire *wire.Action
}

// DefaultButtonProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultButtonProps() ButtonProps {
	return ButtonProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
		Type:    ButtonHTMLButton,
		Variant: ButtonPrimary,
		Size:    ButtonSizeMD,
	}
}

// buttonVariantClasses returns the color classes for each button variant
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for button variants
var buttonVariantLookup = map[ButtonType]string{
	ButtonPrimary:   "bg-accent-600 text-white hover:bg-accent-500 dark:bg-accent-500 dark:hover:bg-accent-400 focus-visible:outline-accent-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-accent-500",
	ButtonSecondary: "bg-white text-gray-900 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:text-white dark:ring-gray-600 dark:hover:bg-gray-700",
	ButtonDanger:    "bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-500 dark:bg-red-500 dark:hover:bg-red-400 focus-visible:outline-red-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-red-500",
	ButtonGhost:     "bg-transparent text-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:text-gray-200 dark:hover:bg-gray-700",
	ButtonLink:      "bg-transparent text-accent-600 hover:text-accent-500 dark:text-accent-400 dark:hover:text-accent-300 underline-offset-2 hover:underline",

	ButtonOutlineDanger:  "bg-transparent text-red-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-red-300 hover:bg-red-50 dark:text-red-400 dark:ring-red-800 dark:hover:bg-red-900/20 focus-visible:outline-red-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-red-400",
	ButtonOutlineWarning: "bg-transparent text-amber-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-amber-300 hover:bg-amber-50 dark:text-amber-400 dark:ring-amber-800 dark:hover:bg-amber-900/20 focus-visible:outline-amber-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-amber-400",
	ButtonOutlineSuccess: "bg-transparent text-green-700 ring-1 ring-inset ring-green-300 hover:bg-green-50 dark:text-green-400 dark:ring-green-800 dark:hover:bg-green-900/20 focus-visible:outline-green-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-green-400",
	ButtonOutlineInfo:    "bg-transparent text-blue-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-blue-300 hover:bg-blue-50 dark:text-blue-400 dark:ring-blue-800 dark:hover:bg-blue-900/20 focus-visible:outline-blue-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-blue-400",
}

func buttonVariantClasses(v ButtonType) string {
	return utils.Lookup(buttonVariantLookup, v, buttonVariantLookup[ButtonPrimary])
}

// ButtonTypeIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined ButtonType constants.
func ButtonTypeIsValid(v ButtonType) bool {
	_, ok := buttonVariantLookup[v]

	return ok
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for button sizes
var buttonSizeLookup = map[ButtonSize]string{
	ButtonSizeSM: "px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs",
	ButtonSizeMD: "px-3 py-2 text-sm",
	ButtonSizeLG: "px-4 py-2.5 text-base",
}

func buttonSizeClasses(s ButtonSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(buttonSizeLookup, s, buttonSizeLookup[ButtonSizeMD])
}

// buttonBaseClass returns the shared base classes for all buttons.
const buttonBaseClass = "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md font-semibold transition-colors focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed cursor-pointer"

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"strings"
	"testing"

func TestButtonRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("primary button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(DefaultButtonProps()))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<button`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="button"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `bg-accent-600`)
	})

	t.Run("button with text", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{
			ID:   "save-btn",
			Text: "Save",
			Type: ButtonHTMLSubmit,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="save-btn"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Save")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="submit"`)
	})

	t.Run("link button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{
			Text:    "Docs",
			Href:    "/docs",
			Variant: ButtonSecondary,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<a`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/docs"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Docs")
	})

	t.Run("disabled button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{
			Text:     "Delete",
			Variant:  ButtonDanger,
			Disabled: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `disabled`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `bg-red-600`)
	})

	t.Run("external link button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{
			Text:     "GitHub",
			Href:     "https://github.com",
			External: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `target="_blank"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`)
	})
}

func TestButtonHTMLType(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("submit type passes through", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{Text: "Save", Type: ButtonHTMLSubmit}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="submit"`)
	})

	t.Run("reset type passes through", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{Text: "Clear", Type: ButtonHTMLReset}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="reset"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty falls back to button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{Text: "Go"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="button"`)
	})

	t.Run("invalid type falls back to button", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Button(ButtonProps{Text: "Go", Type: ButtonHTMLType("destroy-everything")}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="button"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `destroy-everything`)
	})
}
