package display

// Position defines where a floating element appears relative to its trigger,
// expressed in logical (writing-direction aware) sides: start and end map to
// the inline start/end of the surrounding text direction (left/right in LTR,
// mirrored in RTL). It is the shared placement axis for Tooltip, Popover, and
// HoverCard.
type Position string

const (
	PositionTop    Position = "top"
	PositionBottom Position = "bottom"
	PositionStart  Position = "start"
	PositionEnd    Position = "end"
)

// Legacy physical spellings from before the logical axis existed. They keep
// their original physical behavior (never mirrored in RTL) and stay valid so
// existing consumers keep compiling; prefer PositionStart/PositionEnd, which
// are pixel-identical to them in LTR and mirror correctly in RTL. Removal is
// planned for v2 (ADR-0022).
const (
	PositionLeft  Position = "left"
	PositionRight Position = "right"
)

// PositionIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined Position constants.
func PositionIsValid(v Position) bool {
	switch v {
	case PositionTop, PositionBottom, PositionStart, PositionEnd, PositionLeft, PositionRight:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// Component aliases of [Position]: one type serves all floating components;
// the per-component spellings remain so call sites read naturally and
// pre-unification source keeps compiling.
type (
	// TooltipPosition is an alias of [Position]: where a Tooltip appears
	// relative to its trigger.
	TooltipPosition = Position

	// PopoverPosition is an alias of [Position]: where a Popover panel
	// appears relative to its trigger.
	PopoverPosition = Position

	// HoverCardPosition is an alias of [Position]: where a HoverCard appears
	// relative to its trigger.
	HoverCardPosition = Position
)

// Legacy per-component constants, kept for source compatibility. The
// Left/Right spellings predate the logical axis; prefer Start/End in new
// code (identical placement in LTR, correct mirroring in RTL).
const (
	TooltipPositionTop    = PositionTop
	TooltipPositionBottom = PositionBottom
	TooltipPositionStart  = PositionStart
	TooltipPositionEnd    = PositionEnd
	TooltipPositionLeft   = PositionLeft
	TooltipPositionRight  = PositionRight

	PopoverPositionTop    = PositionTop
	PopoverPositionBottom = PositionBottom
	PopoverPositionStart  = PositionStart
	PopoverPositionEnd    = PositionEnd
	PopoverPositionLeft   = PositionLeft
	PopoverPositionRight  = PositionRight

	HoverCardPositionTop    = PositionTop
	HoverCardPositionBottom = PositionBottom
	HoverCardPositionStart  = PositionStart
	HoverCardPositionEnd    = PositionEnd
)

// TooltipPositionIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined Position constants.
func TooltipPositionIsValid(v TooltipPosition) bool {
	return PositionIsValid(v)
}

// PopoverPositionIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined Position constants.
func PopoverPositionIsValid(v PopoverPosition) bool {
	return PositionIsValid(v)
}

// HoverCardPositionIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined Position constants.
func HoverCardPositionIsValid(v HoverCardPosition) bool {
	return PositionIsValid(v)
}
package display

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestPositionIsValid(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	valid := []Position{
		PositionTop, PositionBottom, PositionStart, PositionEnd,
		PositionLeft, PositionRight,
	}
	for _, pos := range valid {
		if !PositionIsValid(pos) {
			t.Errorf("PositionIsValid(%q) = false, want true", pos)
		}
	}

	if PositionIsValid(Position("diagonal")) {
		t.Error(`PositionIsValid("diagonal") = true, want false`)
	}

	if PositionIsValid(Position("")) {
		t.Error(`PositionIsValid("") = true, want false`)
	}
}

// TestPositionAliasesAreOneType pins the unification contract: the
// per-component position types are aliases of Position, and every legacy
// constant is the same value as its canonical spelling, so pre-unification
// consumer source keeps compiling and behaving identically.
func TestPositionAliasesAreOneType(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	typeIdentity := map[string]Position{
		"TooltipPositionTop":      TooltipPositionTop,
		"TooltipPositionBottom":   TooltipPositionBottom,
		"TooltipPositionStart":    TooltipPositionStart,
		"TooltipPositionEnd":      TooltipPositionEnd,
		"TooltipPositionLeft":     TooltipPositionLeft,
		"TooltipPositionRight":    TooltipPositionRight,
		"PopoverPositionTop":      PopoverPositionTop,
		"PopoverPositionBottom":   PopoverPositionBottom,
		"PopoverPositionStart":    PopoverPositionStart,
		"PopoverPositionEnd":      PopoverPositionEnd,
		"PopoverPositionLeft":     PopoverPositionLeft,
		"PopoverPositionRight":    PopoverPositionRight,
		"HoverCardPositionTop":    HoverCardPositionTop,
		"HoverCardPositionBottom": HoverCardPositionBottom,
		"HoverCardPositionStart":  HoverCardPositionStart,
		"HoverCardPositionEnd":    HoverCardPositionEnd,
	}

	canonical := map[string]Position{
		"TooltipPositionTop":      PositionTop,
		"TooltipPositionBottom":   PositionBottom,
		"TooltipPositionStart":    PositionStart,
		"TooltipPositionEnd":      PositionEnd,
		"TooltipPositionLeft":     PositionLeft,
		"TooltipPositionRight":    PositionRight,
		"PopoverPositionTop":      PositionTop,
		"PopoverPositionBottom":   PositionBottom,
		"PopoverPositionStart":    PositionStart,
		"PopoverPositionEnd":      PositionEnd,
		"PopoverPositionLeft":     PositionLeft,
		"PopoverPositionRight":    PositionRight,
		"HoverCardPositionTop":    PositionTop,
		"HoverCardPositionBottom": PositionBottom,
		"HoverCardPositionStart":  PositionStart,
		"HoverCardPositionEnd":    PositionEnd,
	}

	for name, legacy := range typeIdentity {
		if legacy != canonical[name] {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want canonical %q", name, legacy, canonical[name])
		}
	}

	// The wrapper IsValid functions are pure delegates of PositionIsValid.
	for _, pos := range []Position{"top", "bottom", "start", "end", "left", "right", "bogus"} {
		if TooltipPositionIsValid(pos) != PositionIsValid(pos) ||
			PopoverPositionIsValid(pos) != PositionIsValid(pos) ||
			HoverCardPositionIsValid(pos) != PositionIsValid(pos) {
			t.Errorf("wrapper IsValid disagreement at %q", pos)
		}
	}
}

// TestTooltipLogicalPositionsMatchLegacyInLTR pins the design promise: the
// logical start/end entries are pixel-identical to the legacy physical
// left/right entries in LTR, expressed with logical utilities so they mirror
// correctly in RTL.
func TestTooltipLogicalPositionsMatchLegacyInLTR(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	start := tooltipLookupPosition(PositionStart)
	left := tooltipLookupPosition(PositionLeft)

	if start.Tooltip != "inset-e-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 me-2" {
		t.Errorf("start tooltip classes = %q, want logical inset-e-full form", start.Tooltip)
	}

	if left.Tooltip != "right-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 me-2" {
		t.Errorf("legacy left tooltip classes = %q, want unchanged physical form", left.Tooltip)
	}

	if start.Arrow != "inset-s-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-s-gray-900 dark:border-s-gray-700" {
		t.Errorf("start arrow classes = %q, want logical inset-s-full form", start.Arrow)
	}

	if left.Arrow != "left-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-s-gray-900 dark:border-s-gray-700" {
		t.Errorf("legacy left arrow classes = %q, want unchanged physical form", left.Arrow)
	}

	end := tooltipLookupPosition(PositionEnd)
	right := tooltipLookupPosition(PositionRight)

	if end.Tooltip != "inset-s-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 ms-2" {
		t.Errorf("end tooltip classes = %q, want logical inset-s-full form", end.Tooltip)
	}

	if right.Tooltip != "left-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 ms-2" {
		t.Errorf("legacy right tooltip classes = %q, want unchanged physical form", right.Tooltip)
	}

	if end.Arrow != "inset-e-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-e-gray-900 dark:border-e-gray-700" {
		t.Errorf("end arrow classes = %q, want logical inset-e-full form", end.Arrow)
	}

	if right.Arrow != "right-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-e-gray-900 dark:border-e-gray-700" {
		t.Errorf("legacy right arrow classes = %q, want unchanged physical form", right.Arrow)
	}
}

// TestPopoverPositionJSResolvesLogicalSides pins the shared positioner script
// contract: start/end placements are resolved to physical left/right via the
// anchor's computed direction BEFORE the placement math, so the existing
// clamping and flip logic covers them unchanged.
func TestPopoverPositionJSResolvesLogicalSides(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	js := popoverPositionJS()
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `if(pos==="start"||pos==="end")`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `var rtl=getComputedStyle(t).direction==="rtl"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `pos=(pos==="start")?(rtl?"right":"left"):(rtl?"left":"right")`)
	// The physical branches the resolution feeds into are still present.
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `if(pos==="top")`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `else if(pos==="left")`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, `else if(pos==="right")`)
}
// Prose component: a longform-content container for rendered markdown and
// article HTML. One wrapper class (.tc-prose, templates/custom.css) styles
// headings, lists, blockquotes, code, tables, and images via descendant
// selectors — the consumer renders raw content HTML inside and gets the
// library's typographic contract (theme-token colors, dark-mode overrides,
// logical/RTL-safe spacing) without per-element classes.
package display

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// ProseSize controls the container's font scale. Utilities beat the
// .tc-prose descendant rules, so the size classes override the base font.
type ProseSize string

const (
	// ProseSizeSM renders compact longform text (0.875rem).
	ProseSizeSM ProseSize = "sm"
	// ProseSizeMD is the default reading scale (1rem, the .tc-prose base).
	ProseSizeMD ProseSize = "md"
	// ProseSizeLG renders large text (1.125rem) for lead articles.
	ProseSizeLG ProseSize = "lg"
)

// ProseSizeDefault is the zero-value-compatible default size.
const ProseSizeDefault = ProseSizeMD

// ProseSizeIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined ProseSize constants.
func ProseSizeIsValid(v ProseSize) bool {
	switch v {
	case ProseSizeSM, ProseSizeMD, ProseSizeLG:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// proseSizeLookup maps each size to the classes layered over .tc-prose.
// MD is intentionally empty: the .tc-prose base IS the medium scale.
var proseSizeLookup = map[ProseSize]string{ //nolint:gochecknoglobals // typed-key style lookup (repo convention)
	ProseSizeSM: "text-sm leading-relaxed",
	ProseSizeMD: "",
	ProseSizeLG: "text-lg leading-relaxed",
}

// proseSizeClass resolves the size classes with the zero value = default.
func proseSizeClass(size ProseSize) string {
	if size == "" {
		return proseSizeLookup[ProseSizeMD]
	}

	return utils.Lookup(proseSizeLookup, size, "")
}

// ProseProps configures a longform-content container.
type ProseProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Children is the longform content (typically rendered markdown HTML).
	// When nil, Prose renders its templ trailing block instead — both call
	// styles work (the doc example uses the trailing block; programmatic Go
	// consumers set this field). Before the fallback shipped (2026-10-30),
	// trailing-block callers got an EMPTY container — the demo's own Prose
	// section shipped empty for weeks.
	Children templ.Component
	// Size sets the font scale. Zero value falls back to ProseSizeMD.
	Size ProseSize
}

// DefaultProseProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultProseProps() ProseProps {
	return ProseProps{Size: ProseSizeMD} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // Children/BaseProps stay zero by design
}
package display

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// Prose renders a longform-content container (rendered markdown, articles,
// documentation bodies). The .tc-prose family in templates/custom.css styles
// the content's descendants — headings, lists, blockquotes, code, tables,
// images — so callers drop raw content HTML inside without per-element
// classes:
//
//	@display.Prose(display.ProseProps{Size: display.ProseSizeMD}) {
//		<h2>Release notes</h2>
//		<p>Plain markup is styled by the container.</p>
//	}
//
// The wrapper carries BaseProps (ID, Class, Attrs, AriaLabel, Nonce);
// utilities still win over the descendant rules, so per-element Tailwind
// classes and the tc-fluid-* sizes compose on top.
templ Prose(props ProseProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("tc-prose", proseSizeClass(props.Size), props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Children != nil {
			@props.Children
		} else {
			{ children... }
		}
	</div>
}

func proseSample() templ.Component {
	return templ.ComponentFunc(func(_ context.Context, w io.Writer) error {
		_, err := io.WriteString(w, "<p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>")

		return err
	})
}

// TestProseSizeIsValid pins the ProseSize closed set (repo rule: every enum
// ships IsValid + a test in the SAME commit).
func TestProseSizeIsValid(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, valid := range []ProseSize{ProseSizeSM, ProseSizeMD, ProseSizeLG} {
		if !ProseSizeIsValid(valid) {
			t.Errorf("ProseSizeIsValid(%q) = false, want true", valid)
		}
	}

	for _, invalid := range []ProseSize{"", "xl", "small", "SM"} {
		if ProseSizeIsValid(invalid) {
			t.Errorf("ProseSizeIsValid(%q) = true, want false", invalid)
		}
	}
}

// TestProseSizeClassZeroValueEqualsDefault pins the struct-literal rule: the
// zero value resolves to the same classes as the documented default.
func TestProseSizeClassZeroValueEqualsDefault(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if proseSizeClass("") != proseSizeClass(ProseSizeMD) {
		t.Errorf("zero value class %q != default class %q", proseSizeClass(""), proseSizeClass(ProseSizeMD))
	}

	if proseSizeClass(ProseSizeSM) == "" {
		t.Error("ProseSizeSM must carry size classes")
	}
}

// TestProseRender pins the wrapper markup: the tc-prose hook class, the
// size class merge, BaseProps propagation, and children rendering.
func TestProseRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	content := proseSample()

	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		props    ProseProps
		contains []string
		absent   []string
	}{
		{
			name:     "default size renders hook class without size class",
			props:    ProseProps{Children: content},
			contains: []string{`class="tc-prose"`, "<p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>"},
		},
		{
			name:     "small size class merges",
			props:    ProseProps{Children: content, Size: ProseSizeSM},
			contains: []string{"tc-prose", "text-sm", "leading-relaxed"},
		},
		{
			name:     "large size class merges",
			props:    ProseProps{Children: content, Size: ProseSizeLG},
			contains: []string{"tc-prose", "text-lg", "leading-relaxed"},
		},
		{
			name: "id, class, and attrs propagate",
			props: ProseProps{
				Children: content,
				BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{
					ID:    "article-body",
					Class: "max-w-3xl",
					Attrs: templ.Attributes{"data-article": "true"},
				},
			},
			contains: []string{`id="article-body"`, `max-w-3xl`, `data-article="true"`},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			html := utils.Render(t, Prose(tt.props))
			utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html, tt.contains...)

			for _, unwanted := range tt.absent {
				if strings.Contains(html, unwanted) {
					t.Errorf("rendered HTML must not contain %q:\n%s", unwanted, html)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
package display

import (
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// RelativeTimeProps configures a human-readable relative timestamp.
// The server renders the initial relative string ("2 hours ago"); the
// machine-readable datetime attribute is always present for screen readers
// and search engines.
type RelativeTimeProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Time is the timestamp to display relative to now.
	Time time.Time
	// Now, when non-zero, pins the reference instant the relative string is
	// computed against (defaults to time.Now at render time). Tests use it to
	// pin boundary behavior ("59s vs 60s") deterministically; production
	// callers leave it zero.
	Now time.Time
	// Title, when non-empty, overrides the default title (absolute time shown
	// on hover). Set to "" to use the formatted absolute timestamp.
	Title string
	// EmptyText, when non-empty and Time is the zero value, renders this text
	// instead of a relative string: zero timestamps mean "never" (never
	// rotated, never used), and date noise like "Jan 1, 0001" is the opposite
	// of the information the reader needs. The empty render stays inside the
	// <time> shell but omits the meaningless zero datetime, the default
	// zero-date title, and data-tc-relative (the auto-refresh script would
	// re-format the placeholder into date noise). Unset, or a non-zero Time,
	// keeps the exact prior behavior.
	EmptyText string
	// AutoRefresh defaults to true — the component injects a singleton script
	// that uses the native Intl.RelativeTimeFormat API to live-update the text
	// every 30 seconds. Also listens to htmx:afterSettle so newly-swapped
	// <time> elements are formatted immediately. This is progressive enhancement:
	// the server-rendered text is correct without JS; the script just keeps it
	// fresh. Set to false for static contexts (PDF, email, SEO-only).
	AutoRefresh bool
}

// DefaultRelativeTimeProps returns sensible defaults. Time defaults to now,
// AutoRefresh defaults to true (live-updating via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat).
func DefaultRelativeTimeProps() RelativeTimeProps {
	return RelativeTimeProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Time:        time.Now(),
		AutoRefresh: true,
	}
}

// RelativeTime renders a <time> element with a human-readable relative
// timestamp (e.g. "2 hours ago", "just now", "3 days ago"). The datetime
// attribute carries the RFC 3339 timestamp for accessibility and SEO.
//
//	@display.RelativeTime(display.RelativeTimeProps{Time: createdAt})
//	@display.RelativeTime(display.RelativeTimeProps{Time: createdAt, AutoRefresh: false}) // static
templ RelativeTime(props RelativeTimeProps) {
	{{
		empty := props.Time.IsZero() && props.EmptyText != ""
		now := props.Now
		if now.IsZero() {
			now = time.Now()
		}
		text := formatRelativeTime(props.Time, now)
		title := props.Title
		if title == "" && !empty {
			title = props.Time.Format("Jan 2, 2006 3:04 PM MST")
		}
		if empty {
			text = props.EmptyText
		}
	}}
	<time
		if !empty {
			datetime={ props.Time.Format(time.RFC3339) }
		}
		if title != "" {
			title={ title }
		}
		if props.AutoRefresh && !empty {
			data-tc-relative
		}
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ text }
	</time>
	if props.AutoRefresh && !empty {
		@relativeTimeScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
	}
}

// formatRelativeTime returns a human-readable string describing how far ago
// (or how far from now) t is relative to now. Examples: "just now",
// "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago", "2 days ago", "1 week ago", "Jan 5, 2025".
func formatRelativeTime(t, now time.Time) string {
	d := now.Sub(t)
	if d < 0 {
		d = -d
	}

	switch {
	case d < time.Minute:
		return "just now"
	case d < time.Hour:
		mins := int(d / time.Minute)
		if mins == 1 {
			return "1 minute ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(mins, "minutes")
	case d < 24*time.Hour:
		hours := int(d / time.Hour)
		if hours == 1 {
			return "1 hour ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(hours, "hours")
	case d < 7*24*time.Hour:
		days := int(d / (24 * time.Hour))
		if days == 1 {
			return "1 day ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(days, "days")
	case d < 30*24*time.Hour:
		weeks := int(d / (7 * 24 * time.Hour))
		if weeks == 1 {
			return "1 week ago"
		}
		return formatRelativeAgo(weeks, "weeks")
	default:
		return t.Format("Jan 2, 2006")
	}
}

// formatRelativeAgo returns "<n> <unit> ago".
func formatRelativeAgo(n int, unit string) string {
	return strconv.Itoa(n) + " " + unit + " ago"
}
package display

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// TestFormatRelativeTimeBoundaries pins the formatRelativeTime bucket
// boundaries with an injected clock (M20/F089): every fencepost — 59s/60s,
// 59m/1h, 23h/24h, 6d/7d, 29d/30d — plus future timestamps (symmetric
// absolute distance) and the 30-day fallback to an absolute date.
func TestFormatRelativeTimeBoundaries(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	now := time.Date(2026, time.September, 13, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		delta time.Duration
		want  string
	}{
		{"zero distance", 0, "just now"},
		{"one second", 1 * time.Second, "just now"},
		{"59 seconds", 59 * time.Second, "just now"},
		{"60 seconds", 60 * time.Second, "1 minute ago"},
		{"61 seconds", 61 * time.Second, "1 minute ago"},
		{"90 seconds", 90 * time.Second, "1 minute ago"},
		{"119 seconds", 119 * time.Second, "1 minute ago"},
		{"2 minutes", 120 * time.Second, "2 minutes ago"},
		{"59 minutes", 59 * time.Minute, "59 minutes ago"},
		{"1 hour", 1 * time.Hour, "1 hour ago"},
		{"90 minutes", 90 * time.Minute, "1 hour ago"},
		{"2 hours", 2 * time.Hour, "2 hours ago"},
		{"23 hours", 23 * time.Hour, "23 hours ago"},
		{"24 hours", 24 * time.Hour, "1 day ago"},
		{"25 hours", 25 * time.Hour, "1 day ago"},
		{"47 hours", 47 * time.Hour, "1 day ago"},
		{"2 days", 48 * time.Hour, "2 days ago"},
		{"6 days", 6 * 24 * time.Hour, "6 days ago"},
		{"7 days", 7 * 24 * time.Hour, "1 week ago"},
		{"8 days", 8 * 24 * time.Hour, "1 week ago"},
		{"13 days", 13 * 24 * time.Hour, "1 week ago"},
		{"14 days", 14 * 24 * time.Hour, "2 weeks ago"},
		{"29 days", 29 * 24 * time.Hour, "4 weeks ago"},
		{"30 days", 30 * 24 * time.Hour, "Aug 14, 2026"}, // absolute fallback
		{"60 days", 60 * 24 * time.Hour, "Jul 15, 2026"},
	}

	// Only the absolute-date fallback differs between directions: a future
	// date prints itself, not the mirrored past date.
	futureOverrides := map[string]string{
		"30 days": "Oct 13, 2026",
		"60 days": "Nov 12, 2026",
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name+" ago", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := formatRelativeTime(now.Add(-tt.delta), now)
			if got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("formatRelativeTime(now-%s) = %q, want %q", tt.delta, got, tt.want)
			}
		})

		// Future timestamps mirror: distance is absolute, wording stays
		// "... ago" by design (the title attribute carries the absolute time).
		t.Run(tt.name+" future", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			want := tt.want
			if override, ok := futureOverrides[tt.name]; ok {
				want = override
			}

			got := formatRelativeTime(now.Add(tt.delta), now)
			if got != want {
				t.Errorf("formatRelativeTime(now+%s) = %q, want %q (symmetric distance)", tt.delta, got, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestRelativeTimeNowInjection pins the render-time clock injection: a
// pinned Now produces a deterministic relative string AND datetime attribute
// regardless of wall-clock time (the M20 determinism-injection preference).
func TestRelativeTimeNowInjection(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	pinned := time.Date(2026, time.March, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

	props := DefaultRelativeTimeProps()
	props.Time = pinned.Add(-2 * time.Hour)
	props.Now = pinned
	props.AutoRefresh = false // keep the script out of the assertion surface

	html := utils.Render(t, RelativeTime(props))

	utils.AssertContains(t, html, `datetime="2026-02-28T22:00:00Z"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, html, ">2 hours ago<")
}

// TestRelativeTimeJSLocaleContract pins the CLIENT-side locale handling
// (T5.7, #493): the auto-refresh script must format through
// Intl.RelativeTimeFormat using the DOCUMENT language (documentElement.lang)
// with an 'en' fallback — never a hardcoded locale — so server-rendered text
// and client-refreshed text agree in the user's language. Breaking this
// silently flips refreshed timestamps to English on localized pages.
func TestRelativeTimeJSLocaleContract(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	js := relativeTimeJS()

	utils.AssertContains(t, js, "new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(document.documentElement.lang||'en'")
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, "{numeric:'auto'}")
	utils.AssertContains(t, js, "toLocaleDateString()")
}

import (
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// TestRTLDirectionReadsAreSubtreeScoped pins every RTL-aware JS handler
// (menu keyboard nav in shared.go, Tabs, Carousel) to resolve direction from
// the nearest [dir] ancestor, falling back to <html> — so RTL widgets inside
// LTR pages (and vice versa) map ArrowLeft/ArrowRight correctly. A bare
// documentElement read regresses mixed-direction subtrees and must fail here.
func TestRTLDirectionReadsAreSubtreeScoped(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sources := []string{"shared.go", "tabs.templ", "carousel_go.go"}

	for _, name := range sources {
		content, err := os.ReadFile(name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", name, err)
		}

		src := string(content)

		if !strings.Contains(src, "closest('[dir]')") {
			t.Errorf("%s: no subtree-scoped direction read found (missing closest('[dir]'))", name)

			continue
		}

		scoped := strings.ReplaceAll(src, "||document.documentElement", "")
		scoped = strings.ReplaceAll(scoped, "|| document.documentElement", "")

		if strings.Contains(scoped, "documentElement.getAttribute('dir')") {
			t.Errorf(
				"%s: page-scoped direction read found; use (el.closest('[dir]')||document.documentElement).getAttribute('dir')",
				name,
			)
		}
	}
}
package display

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// TestRTLRendering verifies that components render correctly with dir="rtl"
// — logical CSS properties (ms-/me-/start-0/end-0) resolve identically
// regardless of direction, so we assert the logical properties are present.
func TestRTLRendering(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("drawer uses logical positioning via data-side", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Drawer(DrawerProps{
			ID:   "rtl-drawer",
			Open: true,
			Side: DrawerLeft,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-side="left"`)
	})

	t.Run("statcard renders without physical margins", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StatCard(StatCardProps{
			Value:  "42",
			Label:  "Active",
			Change: "+5%",
			Trend:  TrendUp,
		}))
		// ml-2 should have been converted to ms-2 by logical property migration
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "ms-2")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "ml-2")
	})

	t.Run("table uses logical text alignment, not physical", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:     []string{"Name"},
			Rows:        []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("Alice")},
			CellPadding: TableCellPaddingCompact,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-start")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "text-left")
	})
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// ScrollbackTone colors a scrollback line's tag column.
type ScrollbackTone string

const (
	ScrollbackToneNeutral ScrollbackTone = "neutral"
	ScrollbackToneInfo    ScrollbackTone = "info"
	ScrollbackToneSuccess ScrollbackTone = "success"
	ScrollbackToneWarning ScrollbackTone = "warning"
	ScrollbackToneDanger  ScrollbackTone = "danger"
)

// ScrollbackToneIsValid reports whether tone is a known scrollback tone.
func ScrollbackToneIsValid(tone ScrollbackTone) bool {
	_, ok := scrollbackToneLookup[tone]
	return ok
}

// ScrollbackLine is one entry in a Scrollback. Timestamp is preformatted by
// the caller (e.g. "12:47:03.184"); Tag is a short column label (e.g.
// "query", "match"); Text is the line body.
type ScrollbackLine struct {
	Timestamp string
	Tag       string
	Text      string
	Tone      ScrollbackTone
	// ID sets the line element's id, so a URL fragment can scroll to it
	// (deep links into a transcript) and scripts can address it. Uniqueness is
	// the caller's responsibility — the component renders whatever it is
	// given. Leave empty for anonymous lines.
	ID string
	// Class is merged onto the line element after the built-in classes, so a
	// consumer can highlight a matched line or attach a test hook without
	// re-rolling the loop. tailwind-merge resolves conflicts; the Stagger
	// nth-child delays keep working (they are keyed on position, not class).
	Class string
}

// ScrollbackProps configures a terminal-style log block.
type ScrollbackProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Lines renders top-down in the given order. Empty slice renders nothing.
	Lines []ScrollbackLine
	// Stagger animates lines in sequentially (pure CSS, reduced-motion safe).
	// DefaultScrollbackProps enables it; the zero value renders instantly.
	Stagger bool
}

// DefaultScrollbackProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultScrollbackProps() ScrollbackProps {
	return ScrollbackProps{
		Stagger: true,
	}
}

// Scrollback renders a server-rendered, terminal-style log block: monospace
// lines with a timestamp column and a tone-colored tag column. With Stagger
// enabled, lines fade in sequentially via CSS nth-child delays — zero
// JavaScript, and prefers-reduced-motion users see all lines immediately.
//
// The block is decorative by default (aria-hidden). Pass AriaLabel when the
// lines carry real information screen readers should read.
//
//	@display.Scrollback(display.ScrollbackProps{
//	   Stagger: true,
//	   Lines: []display.ScrollbackLine{
//	       {Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "query", Text: "ads.example.com A", Tone: display.ScrollbackToneInfo},
//	       {Timestamp: "12:47:03.185", Tag: "action", Text: "NXDOMAIN", Tone: display.ScrollbackToneDanger},
//	   },
//	})
templ Scrollback(props ScrollbackProps) {
	if len(props.Lines) > 0 {
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("tc-log text-start border-y border-gray-200 py-3 font-mono text-[0.8125rem] leading-relaxed text-gray-600 dark:border-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400", props.Class) }
			if props.AriaLabel == "" {
				aria-hidden="true"
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				role="log"
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			for _, line := range props.Lines {
				<div
					if line.ID != "" {
						id={ line.ID }
					}
					class={ utils.Class(utils.Ternary(props.Stagger, "tc-log-line", "tc-log-line tc-log-line-still"), line.Class) }
				>
					if line.Timestamp != "" {
						<span class="me-3 text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">{ line.Timestamp }</span>
					}
					if line.Tag != "" {
						<span class={ utils.Class("me-2 inline-block min-w-12 font-medium", scrollbackToneClass(line.Tone)) }>{ line.Tag }</span>
					}
					{ line.Text }
				</div>
			}
		</div>
	}
}

// Lookup maps live in this .templ file (not a separate .go file) so
// Tailwind's content scanner detects the class strings.

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for scrollback tones
var scrollbackToneLookup = map[ScrollbackTone]string{
	ScrollbackToneNeutral: "text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
	ScrollbackToneInfo:    "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400",
	ScrollbackToneSuccess: "text-green-700 dark:text-green-400",
	ScrollbackToneWarning: "text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400",
	ScrollbackToneDanger:  "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400",
}

// scrollbackToneClass maps a tone to its tag color classes, falling back to
// neutral for unknown values.
func scrollbackToneClass(tone ScrollbackTone) string {
	return utils.Lookup(scrollbackToneLookup, tone, scrollbackToneLookup[ScrollbackToneNeutral])
}

func scrollbackFixtureLines() []ScrollbackLine {
	return []ScrollbackLine{
		{Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "query", Text: "ads.example.com A", Tone: ScrollbackToneInfo},
		{Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "match", Text: "blocklist: StevenBlack/hosts", Tone: ScrollbackToneDanger},
		{Timestamp: "12:47:03.185", Tag: "action", Text: "NXDOMAIN", Tone: ScrollbackToneWarning},
		{Timestamp: "12:47:03.185", Tag: "ttl", Text: "86400s", Tone: ScrollbackToneSuccess},
	}
}

func TestScrollbackBehavior(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("user sees every log line with timestamp and tag", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output,
			"12:47:03.184", "query", "ads.example.com A",
			"match", "blocklist: StevenBlack/hosts",
			"action", "NXDOMAIN", "ttl", "86400s",
		)
	})

	t.Run("lines render in a monospace terminal voice", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "font-mono")
	})

	t.Run("stagger opt-in emits the animated line class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Stagger: true,
			Lines:   scrollbackFixtureLines(),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tc-log-line")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tc-log-line-still")
	})

	t.Run("zero value renders instantly via the still modifier", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tc-log-line-still")
	})

	t.Run("tone colors the tag column per line", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output,
			"text-blue-600", "dark:text-blue-400",
			"text-red-600", "dark:text-red-400",
			"text-amber-700", "dark:text-amber-400",
			"text-green-700", "dark:text-green-400",
		)
	})
}

func TestScrollbackA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("decorative by default: aria-hidden hides the trace from screen readers", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-hidden="true"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "aria-label=")
	})

	t.Run("aria-label exposes real log content to screen readers", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Lines:     scrollbackFixtureLines(),
			AriaLabel: "DNS resolution trace",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="DNS resolution trace"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-hidden="true"`)
	})

	t.Run("reduced-motion users see all lines immediately (CSS guard)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		css, err := os.ReadFile("../templates/custom.css")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read custom.css: %v", err)
		}

		styles := string(css)
		for _, want := range []string{
			".tc-log-line",
			".tc-log-line.tc-log-line-still",
			"prefers-reduced-motion: reduce",
			"@keyframes tc-log-in",
		} {
			if !strings.Contains(styles, want) {
				t.Errorf("custom.css missing %q — the scrollback animation depends on it", want)
			}
		}
	})
}

func TestScrollbackEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("empty lines render nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(DefaultScrollbackProps()))
		if output != "" {
			t.Errorf("expected empty output, got %q", output)
		}
	})

	t.Run("unknown tone falls back to neutral", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Lines: []ScrollbackLine{{Tag: "x", Text: "y", Tone: ScrollbackTone("bogus")}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "text-gray-500", "dark:text-gray-400")
	})

	t.Run("lines without timestamp or tag omit the empty columns", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Lines: []ScrollbackLine{{Text: "bare line"}},
		}))
		if strings.Contains(output, "min-w-12") {
			t.Error("expected no tag column for a line without a tag")
		}
	})

	t.Run("more than 8 lines still render (stagger cap is CSS-only)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		lines := make([]ScrollbackLine, 12)
		for i := range lines {
			lines[i] = ScrollbackLine{Tag: "l", Text: strings.Repeat("x", i+1)}
		}

		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Stagger: true, Lines: lines}))
		if got := strings.Count(output, "tc-log-line"); got != 12 {
			t.Errorf("expected 12 line divs, got %d", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("no physical RTL properties are emitted", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: scrollbackFixtureLines()}))
		for _, physical := range []string{" ml-", " mr-", " pl-", " pr-", "text-left", "text-right"} {
			if strings.Contains(output, physical) {
				t.Errorf("physical property %q emitted — use logical (ms-/me-/text-start)", physical)
			}
		}
	})
}

func TestScrollbackToneLookup(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for tone, classes := range scrollbackToneLookup {
		if !strings.Contains(classes, "dark:") {
			t.Errorf("tone %s lacks a dark: variant: %q", tone, classes)
		}
	}

	if _, ok := scrollbackToneLookup[ScrollbackTone("bogus")]; ok {
		t.Error("unknown tone must not resolve")
	}
}

// Per-line hooks let a consumer anchor a line (deep link into a transcript)
// or highlight a matched one without re-rolling the loop (#51).
func TestScrollbackLineHooks(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	lines := []ScrollbackLine{
		{Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "query", Text: "one"},
		{
			Timestamp: "12:47:03.185", Tag: "match", Text: "two",
			ID: "turn-2", Class: "bg-amber-100 dark:bg-amber-900/40",
		},
	}

	t.Run("id and class land on the line element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{Lines: lines}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="turn-2"`)
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "bg-amber-100", "dark:bg-amber-900/40")
	})

	t.Run("anonymous lines stay byte-identical to the default render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		plain := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Lines: []ScrollbackLine{{Timestamp: "12:47:03.184", Tag: "query", Text: "one"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, plain, `id=`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, plain, "tc-log-line")
	})

	t.Run("consumer class merges after the stagger class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Scrollback(ScrollbackProps{
			Stagger: false,
			Lines:   []ScrollbackLine{{Text: "x", Class: "rounded"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "tc-log-line-still", "rounded")
	})
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// HeadingLevel defines the HTML heading element used by SectionHeading.
type HeadingLevel string

const (
	HeadingLevelH1 HeadingLevel = "h1"
	HeadingLevelH2 HeadingLevel = "h2"
	HeadingLevelH3 HeadingLevel = "h3"
	HeadingLevelH4 HeadingLevel = "h4"
	HeadingLevelH5 HeadingLevel = "h5"
	HeadingLevelH6 HeadingLevel = "h6"
)

// headingLevelClass returns the Tailwind text size class for a heading level.
func headingLevelClass(level HeadingLevel) string {
	switch level {
	case HeadingLevelH1:
		return "text-3xl font-bold"
	case HeadingLevelH2:
		return "text-2xl font-bold"
	case HeadingLevelH3:
		return "text-xl font-semibold"
	case HeadingLevelH4:
		return "text-lg font-semibold"
	case HeadingLevelH5:
		return "text-base font-semibold"
	case HeadingLevelH6:
		return "text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide"
	default:
		return "text-2xl font-bold"
	}
}

// TextAlign defines the horizontal alignment of a SectionHeading.
type TextAlign string

const (
	TextAlignLeft   TextAlign = "left"
	TextAlignCenter TextAlign = "center"
	TextAlignRight  TextAlign = "right"
)

// textAlignClass returns the Tailwind text alignment class.
func textAlignClass(align TextAlign) string {
	switch align {
	case TextAlignCenter:
		return "text-center"
	case TextAlignRight:
		return "text-end"
	default:
		return "text-start"
	}
}

// sectionHeadingTitleClass combines the heading level, base title classes,
// and optional override into a single class string.
func sectionHeadingTitleClass(level HeadingLevel, override string) string {
	return utils.Class(headingLevelClass(level), "text-gray-900 dark:text-white break-after-avoid", override)
}

// SectionHeadingProps configures a section-level heading with typed
// heading level and alignment.
type SectionHeadingProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Title    string
	Level    HeadingLevel
	Align    TextAlign
	SubTitle string
}

// SectionHeading renders a section-level heading with configurable heading
// element (h1-h6), alignment, and optional subtitle. Headings include
// break-after-avoid for print pagination. Use this for section titles within
// page content (not the page title itself — use PageHeader for that).
//
//	@display.SectionHeading(display.SectionHeadingProps{
//	   Title: "Experience",
//	   Level: display.HeadingLevelH2,
//	   Align: display.TextAlignCenter,
//	})
templ SectionHeading(props SectionHeadingProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class(textAlignClass(props.Align), props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		switch props.Level {
			case HeadingLevelH1:
				<h1 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h1>
			case HeadingLevelH3:
				<h3 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h3>
			case HeadingLevelH4:
				<h4 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h4>
			case HeadingLevelH5:
				<h5 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h5>
			case HeadingLevelH6:
				<h6 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h6>
			default:
				<h2 class={ sectionHeadingTitleClass(props.Level, "") }>{ props.Title }</h2>
		}
		if props.SubTitle != "" {
			<p class={ utils.Class(mutedTextClass, "mt-1") }>{ props.SubTitle }</p>
		}
	</div>
}

// SegmentBar component: a stacked proportion bar with a legend — language
// shares, evidence breakdowns, storage composition. Extracted from
// mr-sync's language bars and nsfw-classifier's evidence proportions
// (2026-10-10 analysis, TODO_LIST #395).
package display

import (
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// SegmentBarSegment is one proportion of the bar.
type SegmentBarSegment struct {
	// Label names the segment in the legend and the accessible summary.
	Label string
	// Value is the segment's magnitude (relative to the sum of all values).
	// Negative values clamp to zero.
	Value float64
	// Color optionally overrides the deterministic palette — a complete
	// light+dark literal pair such as "bg-emerald-600 dark:bg-emerald-400".
	Color tone.ColorClass
}

// SegmentBarProps configures a stacked proportion bar.
type SegmentBarProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Segments stack in the given order. A bar with no positive-value
	// segments renders nothing (an empty proportion bar is no bar).
	Segments []SegmentBarSegment
	// NoLegend hides the dot+label+percent legend. The zero value shows it.
	NoLegend bool
}

// DefaultSegmentBarProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultSegmentBarProps() SegmentBarProps {
	return SegmentBarProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // no non-zero defaults
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table: the shared chart palette as background class pairs
var segmentBarPalette = []tone.ColorClass{
	"bg-blue-600 dark:bg-blue-400",
	"bg-emerald-600 dark:bg-emerald-400",
	"bg-amber-600 dark:bg-amber-400",
	"bg-rose-600 dark:bg-rose-400",
	"bg-violet-600 dark:bg-violet-400",
	"bg-cyan-600 dark:bg-cyan-400",
	"bg-orange-600 dark:bg-orange-400",
	"bg-pink-600 dark:bg-pink-400",
}

// segmentBarColor resolves a segment's background class: explicit override
// first, then the deterministic palette keyed by label (stable across
// renders and filter orders — the same label always gets the same color).
func segmentBarColor(seg SegmentBarSegment) string {
	if seg.Color != "" {
		return string(seg.Color)
	}

	hash := 0

	for _, r := range seg.Label {
		hash = (hash*31 + int(r)) % len(segmentBarPalette)
	}

	return string(segmentBarPalette[hash])
}

// segmentBarTotal sums the clamped segment values.
func segmentBarTotal(segments []SegmentBarSegment) float64 {
	total := 0.0

	for _, seg := range segments {
		if seg.Value > 0 {
			total += seg.Value
		}
	}

	return total
}

// segmentBarPercent formats one segment's share of total with one decimal.
func segmentBarPercent(value, total float64) string {
	if total <= 0 {
		return "0.0%"
	}

	return strconv.FormatFloat(max(value, 0)/total*100, 'f', 1, 64) + "%"
}

// segmentBarAriaLabel composes the accessible summary ("Go 62.3%, TS 37.7%").
func segmentBarAriaLabel(segments []SegmentBarSegment, total float64) string {
	var parts []string

	for _, seg := range segments {
		if seg.Value > 0 && seg.Label != "" {
			parts = append(parts, seg.Label+" "+segmentBarPercent(seg.Value, total))
		}
	}

	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}
package display

import (
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SegmentBar renders a stacked proportion bar with an optional legend.
//
//	@display.SegmentBar(display.SegmentBarProps{
//		Segments: []display.SegmentBarSegment{
//			{Label: "Go", Value: 62.3},
//			{Label: "TypeScript", Value: 37.7},
//		},
//	})
//
// Proportions use flex-grow (not percentage widths), so rounding never opens
// gaps between segments. The runtime flex-grow values are the component's
// documented inline-style exemption (same class as BarChart's bar widths —
// see utils.TestInlineStyleCompliance).
//
// The role="img" wraps ONLY the bar graphic (img is a leaf role — visible
// descendants under it are invalid ARIA, achecker aria_descendant_valid);
// the legend renders as a real list sibling, readable as ordinary content.
templ SegmentBar(props SegmentBarProps) {
	{{ total := segmentBarTotal(props.Segments) }}
	if total > 0 {
		{{
			label := props.AriaLabel
			if label == "" {
				label = segmentBarAriaLabel(props.Segments, total)
			}
		}}
		<div
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class("flex flex-col gap-2", props.Class) }
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			<div class="flex h-2.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full" role="img" aria-label={ label }>
				for _, seg := range props.Segments {
					if seg.Value > 0 {
						<div
							class={ segmentBarColor(seg) }
							style={ "flex-grow:" + strconv.FormatFloat(seg.Value, 'f', -1, 64) }
						></div>
					}
				}
			</div>
			if !props.NoLegend {
				<ul class="flex flex-wrap gap-x-4 gap-y-1">
					for _, seg := range props.Segments {
						if seg.Value > 0 {
							<li class="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400">
								<span class={ "h-2 w-2 rounded-full " + segmentBarColor(seg) } aria-hidden="true"></span>
								{ seg.Label }
								<span class="text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">{ segmentBarPercent(seg.Value, total) }</span>
							</li>
						}
					}
				</ul>
			}
		</div>
	}
}
package display

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/golden"
)

func TestSegmentBarRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	segments := []SegmentBarSegment{
		{Label: "Go", Value: 62.3},
		{Label: "TypeScript", Value: 37.7},
	}

	t.Run("renders proportional flex-grow segments", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{Segments: segments}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "flex-grow:62.3")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "flex-grow:37.7")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="img"`)
	})

	t.Run("role=img wraps only the bar, never the legend", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{Segments: segments}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="img" aria-label=`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `<div class="flex flex-col gap-2" role="img"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `overflow-hidden rounded-full" role="img"`)
	})

	t.Run("legend shows labels and percents", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{Segments: segments}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Go")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "62.3%")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "37.7%")
	})

	t.Run("no legend opt-out", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, renderSegmentBarNoLegend(segments))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<li")
	})

	t.Run("aria label composed from segments", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{Segments: segments}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Go 62.3%, TypeScript 37.7%"`)
	})

	t.Run("aria label override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			AriaLabel: "Language shares",
			Segments:  segments,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Language shares"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty or zero-total renders nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		if output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{})); output != "" {
			t.Errorf("empty segments rendered %q", output)
		}

		zero := []SegmentBarSegment{{Label: "A", Value: 0}, {Label: "B", Value: -5}}
		if output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{Segments: zero})); output != "" {
			t.Errorf("zero-total rendered %q", output)
		}
	})

	t.Run("negative values clamp in percents", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			Segments: []SegmentBarSegment{{Label: "A", Value: 10}, {Label: "B", Value: -3}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "100.0%")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "-3")
	})

	t.Run("explicit color override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			Segments: []SegmentBarSegment{{Label: "A", Value: 1, Color: "bg-emerald-600 dark:bg-emerald-400"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-emerald-600")
	})

	t.Run("deterministic palette keyed by label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		first := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			Segments: []SegmentBarSegment{{Label: "Go", Value: 1}},
		}))

		second := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			Segments: []SegmentBarSegment{{Label: "Go", Value: 1}},
		}))
		if first != second {
			t.Error("same label renders different colors across renders")
		}
	})

	t.Run("propagates base props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentBar(SegmentBarProps{
			ID: "bar", Class: "mb-2", Attrs: templ.Attributes{"data-x": "1"},
			Segments: segments,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="bar"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "mb-2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-x="1"`)
	})
}

func TestSegmentBarHelpers(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("percent zero total", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		if got := segmentBarPercent(5, 0); got != "0.0%" {
			t.Errorf("segmentBarPercent(5, 0) = %q", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("color palette cycle is deterministic", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		a := segmentBarColor(SegmentBarSegment{Label: "a"})

		b := segmentBarColor(SegmentBarSegment{Label: "a"})
		if a != b {
			t.Errorf("label 'a' resolved to two colors: %q vs %q", a, b)
		}
	})

	t.Run("total ignores negative values", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := segmentBarTotal([]SegmentBarSegment{{Value: 5}, {Value: -2}, {Value: 5}})
		if got != 10 {
			t.Errorf("segmentBarTotal = %v, want 10", got)
		}
	})
}

// mutedTextClass is the shared Tailwind class string for secondary/muted text
// (Card subtitle, PageHeader subtitle, EmptyState description). Callers combine
// it with a margin utility via utils.Class, e.g. utils.Class(mutedTextClass, "mt-1").
const mutedTextClass = "text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"

// Motion class constants — re-exported from utils for backward compatibility.
// Use utils.TransitionFast, utils.TransitionNormal, etc. directly in new code.
const (
	transitionFast      = utils.TransitionFast
	transitionNormal    = utils.TransitionNormal
	transitionColors    = utils.TransitionColors
	transitionTransform = utils.TransitionTransform
