func TestToggleSortDir(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		input SortDirection
		want  SortDirection
	}{
		{SortAsc, SortDesc},
		{SortDesc, SortAsc},
		{SortNone, SortAsc},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		got := toggleSortDir(tt.input)
		if got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("toggleSortDir(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.input, got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestColumnSortKey(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	// Explicit SortKey
	col := DataTableColumn{Label: "Name", SortKey: "full_name"}
	if got := columnSortKey(col); got != "full_name" {
		t.Errorf("expected full_name, got %s", got)
	}
	// Default to lowercase Label
	col2 := DataTableColumn{Label: "CreatedAt"}
	if got := columnSortKey(col2); got != "createdat" {
		t.Errorf("expected createdat, got %s", got)
	}
}
package display

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestTableRowHref(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("row with href renders clickable attributes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "Alice"}}, Href: "/users/1"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `data-tc-row-href="/users/1"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `tabindex="0"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, "cursor-pointer")
	})

	// ARIA in HTML forbids any role on a <tr> inside a real table, so the
	// clickable row must not carry role="link" — the Nu HTML checker rejected
	// every page that shipped it. The row stays keyboard-operable through
	// tabindex + the row-href script instead.
	t.Run("row with href carries no role", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "Alice"}}, Href: "/users/1"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, html, `role="link"`)

		start := strings.Index(html, "<tr data-tc-row-href")
		if start == -1 {
			t.Fatalf("clickable row not found:\n%s", html)
		}

		tag := html[start:]
		if end := strings.Index(tag, ">"); end != -1 {
			tag = tag[:end]
		}

		if strings.Contains(tag, "role=") {
			t.Errorf("clickable row must not carry a role attribute, got %s", tag)
		}
	})

	// WCAG 2.4.7: browsers draw no default focus ring on a <tr>, so a keyboard
	// user cannot see which row Enter will activate without an explicit style.
	t.Run("row with href has a visible focus indicator", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "Alice"}}, Href: "/users/1"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html,
			"focus-visible:outline-2",
			"focus-visible:outline-accent-600",
			"dark:focus-visible:outline-accent-400",
		)
	})

	t.Run("row without href has no focus indicator", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "Alice"}}}},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, html, "focus-visible:outline-2")
	})

	t.Run("row without href has no clickable attributes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "Bob"}}},
			},
		}))
		if strings.Contains(html, "data-tc-row-href") {
			t.Error("non-clickable row should not have data-tc-row-href")
		}

		if strings.Contains(html, "cursor-pointer") {
			t.Error("non-clickable row should not have cursor-pointer")
		}
	})

	t.Run("clickable rows include nonce-guarded script", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Nonce:   "row-nonce",
			Headers: []string{"X"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "A"}}, Href: "/a"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `<script nonce="row-nonce">`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, "tcTableRowHrefAttached")
	})

	t.Run("non-clickable table omits script", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"X"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "A"}}},
			},
		}))
		if strings.Contains(html, "tcTableRowHref") {
			t.Error("table without href rows should not include the row-href script")
		}
	})

	t.Run("hover enabled automatically when any row has href", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"X"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "A"}}, Href: "/a"},
				{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "B"}}},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, "hover:bg-gray-100")
	})
}

func TestTableHasRowHref(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name string
		rows []TableRow
		want bool
	}{
		{"empty", nil, false},
		{"no href", []TableRow{{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "x"}}}}, false},
		{"with href", []TableRow{{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "x"}}, Href: "/x"}}, true},
		{"mixed", []TableRow{{Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "x"}}}, {Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "y"}}, Href: "/y"}}, true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			if got := tableHasRowHref(tt.rows); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("tableHasRowHref() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

package display

import (

func TestTableRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("basic table", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{tableHeaderName, "Email"},
			Rows: []TableRow{
				SimpleTableRow("Alice", "alice@example.com"),
				SimpleTableRow("Bob", "bob@example.com"),
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, tableHeaderName)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Email")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Alice")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bob@example.com")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "scope=\"col\"")
	})

	t.Run("striped rows", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1"), SimpleTableRow("2")},
			Striped: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-gray-50")
	})

	t.Run("with caption", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Caption: "User list",
			Headers: []string{tableHeaderName},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("Alice")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "User list")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<caption")
	})

	t.Run("with custom id", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			ID:      "users-table",
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("Alice")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="users-table"`)
	})

	t.Run("row with fewer cells than headers is padded", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A", "B", "C"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("only-one")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "only-one")
	})

	t.Run("row with more cells than headers is truncated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1", "2", "3")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "1")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, ">2<")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, ">3<")
	})

	t.Run("no headers renders all cells", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Rows: []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("x", "y", "z")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "x")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "y")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "z")
	})

	t.Run("bordered table", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:  []string{"A"},
			Rows:     []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			Bordered: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border border-gray-200")
	})

	t.Run("hover table", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			Hover:   true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "hover:bg-gray-100")
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultTableProps()
		if props.Striped != true {
			t.Error("DefaultTableProps().Striped should be true")
		}
	})

	t.Run("Body slot overrides Rows", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name", "Status"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("should-not-appear")},
			Body: templ.Raw(
				"<tr><td>Alice</td><td><span class=\"badge\">Admin</span></td></tr><tr><td>Bob</td><td>User</td></tr>",
			),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Alice")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Bob")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<span class=\"badge\">Admin</span>")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "should-not-appear")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<tbody")
	})

	t.Run("Body slot renders headers and tbody wrapper", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Body:    templ.Raw("<tr><td>Custom row</td></tr>"),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Name")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Custom row")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<thead")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<tbody")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "divide-y")
	})

	t.Run("BodyID lands on the tbody element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("Alice")},
			BodyID:  "recent-rows",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<tbody id="recent-rows"`)
	})

	t.Run("tbody carries no id when BodyID is unset", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"Name"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("Alice")},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tbody id=")
	})
}

func TestTableFlush(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("default table has wrapper border", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "overflow-x-auto")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "rounded-lg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700")
	})

	t.Run("flush table suppresses wrapper border", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			Flush:   true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "overflow-x-auto")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "rounded-lg")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "border border-gray-200")
	})

	t.Run("Flush and Bordered interact: the border moves onto the table element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:  []string{"A"},
			Rows:     []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			Flush:    true,
			Bordered: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "overflow-x-auto")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "rounded-lg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border-gray-200")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:border-gray-700")
	})
}

func TestTableCellPaddingOption(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("default uses comfortable padding", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "px-4", "py-3")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "py-2")
	})

	t.Run("compact uses py-2 padding", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:     []string{"A"},
			Rows:        []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			CellPadding: TableCellPaddingCompact,
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "px-4", "py-2")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "py-3")
	})

	t.Run("comfortable explicitly uses py-3", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:     []string{"A"},
			Rows:        []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			CellPadding: TableCellPaddingComfortable,
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "px-4", "py-3")
	})

	t.Run("invalid cell padding falls back to comfortable", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers:     []string{"A"},
			Rows:        []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			CellPadding: TableCellPadding("bogus"),
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "px-4", "py-3")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "py-2")
	})

	t.Run("compact applies to typed headers too", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			TypedHeaders: []TableHeader{{Label: "A"}},
			Rows:         []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1")},
			CellPadding:  TableCellPaddingCompact,
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "px-4", "py-2")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "py-3")
	})
}

func TestTableTypedHeaders(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("sortable headers with aria-sort", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			TypedHeaders: []TableHeader{
				{Label: "Name", Sortable: true, SortDirection: SortAsc, Href: "/sort?col=name&dir=asc"},

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-sort="none"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `/sort?col=name`)

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "↑")

			TypedHeaders: []TableHeader{
				{Label: "Name"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "aria-sort")
	})
}

func TestTableRowClass(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("class lands on the row", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A", "B"},
			Rows: []TableRow{{
				Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "1"}, {Text: "2"}},
				Class: "ds-row-hover",
			}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `ds-row-hover`)
	})

	t.Run("no class renders unchanged", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A", "B"},
			Rows:    []TableRow{SimpleTableRow("1", "2")},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `ds-row-hover`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<tr>`)
	})

	t.Run("consumer hover overrides the library hover via tailwind-merge", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A", "B"},
			Hover:   true,
			Rows: []TableRow{{
				Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "1"}, {Text: "2"}},
				Class: "hover:bg-blue-50 dark:hover:bg-blue-900/20",
			}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hover:bg-blue-50`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `hover:bg-gray-100`)
	})

	t.Run("class without href emits no row-click script", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Table(TableProps{
			Headers: []string{"A", "B"},
			Rows: []TableRow{{
				Cells: []TableCell{{Text: "1"}, {Text: "2"}},
				Class: "ds-row-hover",
			}},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `data-tc-row-href`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `data-tc-table-row-href`)
	})
}
package display

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// Tab represents a single tab panel
type Tab struct {
	ID      string
	Label   string
	Content templ.Component
}

// TabsVariant defines the visual style of tabs
type TabsVariant string

const (
	TabsDefault TabsVariant = "default"
	TabsPills   TabsVariant = "pills"
)

// TabsProps configures a tab component
type TabsProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Tabs        []Tab
	ActiveTabID string
	Variant     TabsVariant
	ClientSide  bool
	// Wire, when set, switches the tabs from client-side toggling to
	// SERVER-side switching: each tab link carries the wired action with the
	// URL's `{tab}` placeholder substituted by that tab's ID (the same
	// URL-template convention as the Calendar MonthNav `{year}`/`{month}`),
	// and the endpoint re-renders the WHOLE Tabs component with the new
	// ActiveTabID. Under htmx the action self-replaces the container with
	// `outerHTML settle:0s` (the Calendar re-bind-window rationale: without
	// settle, rapid tab clicks land in htmx's ~20ms processing window and
	// silently no-op); under Datastar targeting is response-driven
	// (wire.Handler) or id-matched — give the fragment root the Tabs' id.
	// An empty Wire.Target defaults to the component's own `#ID` when ID is
	// set. Wire is nil-safe inert: an empty URL wires nothing. ClientSide is
	// ignored when Wire is set (one switching model at a time); the anchors'
	// hash hrefs remain as the no-JS fallback, so the clone sets
	// PreventDefault (the Datastar runtime auto-prevents only form+submit).
	Wire *wire.Action
}

// DefaultTabsProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultTabsProps() TabsProps {
	return TabsProps{
		Variant: TabsDefault,
	}
}

// isActiveTab returns true if the given tab ID matches the active tab
func isActiveTab(tabID, activeTabID string) bool {
	return tabID == activeTabID && tabID != ""
}

// ensureTabIDs generates stable IDs for tabs that omit them, preventing
// invalid HTML (duplicate id="" attributes) and JS selector crashes in
// client-side mode.
func ensureTabIDs(tabs []Tab) []Tab {
	for i := range tabs {
		if tabs[i].ID == "" {
			tabs[i].ID = utils.EnsureID("tab", "")
		}
	}
	return tabs
}

// resolveActiveTabID returns activeTabID if set, otherwise defaults to the
// first tab so that exactly one tab is keyboard-focusable (tabindex=0) per
// the WAI-ARIA tab pattern.
func resolveActiveTabID(activeTabID string, tabs []Tab) string {
	if activeTabID != "" {
		return activeTabID
	}
	if len(tabs) > 0 {
		return tabs[0].ID
	}
	return ""
}

// tabLink renders a single tab link with the given class based on active state.
// aria-controls is emitted only when the tab owns a panel — referencing a
// non-existent id is an axe aria-valid-attr-value violation. wired carries
// the per-tab transport attributes when TabsProps.Wire is set (nil renders
// nothing — the plain hash-fallback anchor).
templ tabLink(tab Tab, hasPanel bool, isActive bool, activeClass, inactiveClass string, wired templ.Attributes) {
	<a
		id={ tab.ID + "-tab" }
		href={ templ.SafeURL("#" + tab.ID) }
		role="tab"
		aria-selected={ fmt.Sprintf("%t", isActive) }
		if hasPanel {
			aria-controls={ tab.ID }
		}
		tabindex={ utils.Ternary(isActive, 0, -1) }
		class={ utils.Ternary(isActive, activeClass, inactiveClass) }
		{ wired... }
	>
		{ tab.Label }
	</a>
}

// tabsWiredAttrs clones the Wire action for one tab (never mutating the
// consumer's spec — the kanban lesson): the URL's {tab} placeholder becomes
// that tab's ID, the anchor-fallback href forces PreventDefault (the Datastar
// runtime auto-prevents only form+submit; htmx intercepts wired clicks
// itself), an empty Target defaults to the Tabs container's own #ID, and htmx
// gets the settle:0s self-swap composed on top. Nil/empty stays inert.
func tabsWiredAttrs(base *wire.Action, tabID, tabsID string) templ.Attributes {
	if base == nil || base.URL == "" {
		return nil
	}

	nav := *base
	nav.URL = strings.ReplaceAll(base.URL, "{tab}", tabID)
	nav.PreventDefault = true
	if nav.Target == "" && tabsID != "" {
		nav.Target = "#" + tabsID
	}

	attrs := nav.Attributes()
	if attrs != nil && nav.Transport != wire.TransportDatastar {
		attrs["hx-swap"] = tabsSwap
	}

	return attrs
}

// tabsSwap self-replaces the whole Tabs container and settles synchronously —
// htmx processes swapped-in anchors in its settle phase (~20ms by default);
// tab switching is exactly the quick-burst pattern where a click inside that
// window would silently no-op (Calendar MonthNav lesson, e2e-verified there).
const tabsSwap = "outerHTML settle:0s"

// Tabs renders a tabbed interface with accessible markup
//
//	@display.Tabs(display.TabsProps{
//	   ActiveTabID: "users",
//	   Tabs: []display.Tab{
//	     {ID: "users", Label: "Users"},
//	     {ID: "settings", Label: "Settings"},
//	   },
//	})
templ Tabs(props TabsProps) {
	{{ tabs := ensureTabIDs(props.Tabs) }}
	{{ activeID := resolveActiveTabID(props.ActiveTabID, tabs) }}
	{{ clientSide := props.ClientSide && props.Wire == nil }}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("w-full", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		if clientSide {
			data-tc-tabs=""
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div role="tablist" aria-label="Tabs" class="border-b border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700">
			<div
				class={ "-mb-px flex space-x-8", templ.KV("space-x-2", props.Variant == TabsPills) }
			>
				for _, tab := range tabs {
					{{ active := isActiveTab(tab.ID, activeID) }}
					{{ wired := tabsWiredAttrs(props.Wire, tab.ID, props.ID) }}
					if props.Variant == TabsPills {
						@tabLink(tab, tab.Content != nil, active,
							"rounded-md bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500 px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-white",
							"rounded-md px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:text-gray-200",
							wired,
						)
					} else {
						@tabLink(tab, tab.Content != nil, active,
							"whitespace-nowrap border-b-2 border-accent-500 px-1 py-4 text-sm font-medium text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400",
							"whitespace-nowrap border-b-2 border-transparent px-1 py-4 text-sm font-medium text-gray-500 hover:border-gray-300 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:border-gray-600 dark:hover:text-gray-200",
							wired,
						)
					}
				}
			</div>
		</div>
		for _, tab := range tabs {
			if tab.Content != nil {
				<div
					id={ tab.ID }
					role="tabpanel"
					aria-labelledby={ tab.ID + "-tab" }
					if !isActiveTab(tab.ID, activeID) {
						hidden
					}
					class="mt-4"
				>
					@tab.Content
				</div>
			}
		}
		if clientSide {
			<script { utils.ScriptAttrs(props.Nonce)... }>
				if (!window.tcTabsAttached) {
					window.tcTabsAttached = true;
					document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
						var link = e.target.closest('[data-tc-tabs] [role="tab"]');
						if (!link) return;
						e.preventDefault();
						activateTab(link);
					});
					document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
						var tab = e.target.closest('[data-tc-tabs] [role="tab"]');
						if (!tab) return;
						var tabs = Array.from(tab.closest('[role="tablist"]').querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]'));
						var idx = tabs.indexOf(tab);
						var next = -1;
						var rtl = (tab.closest('[dir]') || document.documentElement).getAttribute('dir') === 'rtl';
						var nextKey = rtl ? 'ArrowLeft' : 'ArrowRight';
						var prevKey = rtl ? 'ArrowRight' : 'ArrowLeft';
						if (e.key === nextKey || e.key === 'ArrowDown') { next = (idx + 1) % tabs.length; }
						else if (e.key === prevKey || e.key === 'ArrowUp') { next = (idx - 1 + tabs.length) % tabs.length; }
						else if (e.key === 'Home') { next = 0; }
						else if (e.key === 'End') { next = tabs.length - 1; }
						if (next >= 0) { e.preventDefault(); tabs[next].focus(); activateTab(tabs[next]); }
					});
				}
				function activateTab(link) {
					var container = link.closest('[data-tc-tabs]');
					container.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]').forEach(function(t) {
						t.setAttribute('aria-selected','false');
						t.setAttribute('tabindex','-1');
					});
					link.setAttribute('aria-selected','true');
					link.setAttribute('tabindex','0');
					container.querySelectorAll('[role="tabpanel"]').forEach(function(p) { p.hidden = true; });
					var panel = container.querySelector('#' + link.getAttribute('aria-controls'));
					if (panel) panel.hidden = false;
				}
			</script>
		}
	</div>
}
package display

import (
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

func TestTabsRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("basic tabs", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "tab1",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "tab1", Label: "First"},
				{ID: "tab2", Label: "Second"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "First")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Second")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="tablist"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-selected="true"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-selected="false"`)
	})

	t.Run("tab with content", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "panel1",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{
					ID:      "panel1",
					Label:   "Panel",
					Content: templ.Raw("<p>Hello</p>"),
				},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="tabpanel"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Hello")
	})

	t.Run("pills style", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Variant:     TabsPills,
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "A"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
	})

	t.Run("no active tab defaults to first", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "x", Label: "X"},
				{ID: "y", Label: "Y"},
			},
		}))
		// WAI-ARIA tab pattern: exactly one tab must be keyboard-focusable
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `tabindex="0"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-selected="true"`)
	})

	t.Run("tabs without IDs get auto-generated IDs", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{Label: "No ID"},
				{Label: "Also No ID"},
			},
		}))
		// Auto-generated IDs prevent invalid HTML (id="-tab") and JS crashes
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="tc-tab-`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `id="-tab"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-controls=""`)
	})

	t.Run("default props has TabsDefault variant", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultTabsProps()
		if props.Variant != TabsDefault {
			t.Errorf("DefaultTabsProps().Variant = %q, want %q", props.Variant, TabsDefault)
		}
	})

	t.Run("tabs with empty tabs list", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="tablist"`)
	})

	t.Run("default underline variant", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Variant:     TabsDefault,
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "A"},
				{ID: "b", Label: "B"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border-accent-500")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border-transparent")
	})

	t.Run("tab without content", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "A"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `role="tabpanel"`)
	})

	t.Run("pills variant with content", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "p1",
			Variant:     TabsPills,
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "p1", Label: "One", Content: templ.Raw("<p>Pill content</p>")},
				{ID: "p2", Label: "Two"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Pill content")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `space-x-2`)
	})

	t.Run("custom ID and class propagated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID: "my-tabs", Class: "max-w-2xl",
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Tabs:        []Tab{{ID: "a", Label: "A"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-tabs"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "max-w-2xl")
	})

	t.Run("inactive tab panel has hidden attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "Active", Content: templ.Raw("<p>Visible</p>")},
				{ID: "b", Label: "Hidden", Content: templ.Raw("<p>Hidden content</p>")},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Hidden content")
	})

	t.Run("client-side tabs renders data-tc-tabs and script", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			ClientSide:  true,
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "A"},
				{ID: "b", Label: "B"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-tabs`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcTabsAttached")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "activateTab")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "ArrowRight")
	})

	t.Run("non-client-side tabs omit script", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ActiveTabID: "a",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "a", Label: "A"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `data-tc-tabs`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcTabsAttached")
	})
}

// TestTabsWire pins the server-side tab switching contract (ADR-0036): each
// tab link carries the wired action with the {tab} URL placeholder
// substituted, the anchor fallback forces PreventDefault, an empty Target
// defaults to the container's own #ID, htmx gets the settle:0s self-swap,
// and the consumer's *Action is never mutated.
func TestTabsWire(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("htmx renders per-tab hx-get with substituted URLs and the settle swap", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID:          "prefs-tabs",
			ActiveTabID: "general",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
				{ID: "advanced", Label: "Advanced"},
			},
			Wire: &wire.Action{URL: "/api/tabs/{tab}", Target: "#prefs-tabs"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-get="/api/tabs/general"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-get="/api/tabs/advanced"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-target="#prefs-tabs"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-swap="outerHTML settle:0s"`)
	})

	t.Run("datastar renders per-tab data-on:click with prevent", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID:          "prefs-tabs",
			ActiveTabID: "general",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
				{ID: "advanced", Label: "Advanced"},
			},
			Wire: &wire.Action{Transport: wire.TransportDatastar, URL: "/api/tabs/{tab}"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-on:click__prevent="@get(&#39;/api/tabs/general&#39;)"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-on:click__prevent="@get(&#39;/api/tabs/advanced&#39;)"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-")
	})

	t.Run("empty Target defaults to the container's own #ID (htmx)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID: "prefs-tabs",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
			},
			Wire: &wire.Action{URL: "/api/tabs/{tab}"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-target="#prefs-tabs"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty URL wires nothing (inert anchors)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID: "prefs-tabs",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
			},
			Wire: &wire.Action{},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-get")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-on:")
	})

	t.Run("consumer action is never mutated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		original := &wire.Action{URL: "/api/tabs/{tab}"}
		snapshot := *original

		_ = utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID: "prefs-tabs",
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
				{ID: "advanced", Label: "Advanced"},
			},
			Wire: original,
		}))

		if !reflect.DeepEqual(*original, snapshot) {
			t.Errorf("Tabs mutated the consumer's action: %+v", *original)
		}

		if original.Target != "" {
			t.Errorf("Target = %q, want empty (the clone carries the default, not the original)", original.Target)
		}
	})

	t.Run("ClientSide is ignored when Wire is set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Tabs(TabsProps{
			ID:         "prefs-tabs",
			ClientSide: true,
			Tabs: []Tab{
				{ID: "general", Label: "General"},
			},
			Wire: &wire.Action{URL: "/api/tabs/{tab}", Target: "#prefs-tabs"},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-tc-tabs")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcTabsAttached")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-get="/api/tabs/general"`)
	})
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"

// Tone/Hue adapters (utils/tone Phase 0, TODO #425): every color-bearing
// enum in display gains a mapping onto the canonical color language. The
// existing lookup maps keep rendering (zero visual change); equivalence
// tests in tone_adapters_test.go prove the adapters describe the shipped
// strings byte-for-byte. The maps collapse into the tone tables at v2
// (ADR-0039/0044, TODO #431).

// Tone maps StatusTone onto the canonical semantic axis.
func (t StatusTone) Tone() tone.Tone {
	switch t {
	case StatusToneNeutral:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	case StatusToneSuccess:
		return tone.ToneSuccess
	case StatusToneWarning:
		return tone.ToneWarning
	case StatusToneDanger:
		return tone.ToneDanger
	case StatusToneInfo:
		return tone.ToneInfo
	default:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	}
}

// DotHue is the hue StatusDot actually renders for t. Warning deliberately
// diverges from the tone table (amber here, yellow in the tone table's
// majority dialect) — the documented warning split brain, unified by the
// #428 decision.
func (t StatusTone) DotHue() tone.Hue {
	switch t {
	case StatusToneNeutral:
		return tone.HueGray
	case StatusToneSuccess:
		return tone.HueGreen
	case StatusToneWarning:
		return tone.HueAmber
	case StatusToneDanger:
		return tone.HueRed
	case StatusToneInfo:
		return tone.HueBlue
	default:
		return tone.HueGray
	}
}

// Hue maps KanbanTone onto the categorical hue axis. Kanban lanes are
// categorical, not semantic — there is deliberately no Tone() here.
func (t KanbanTone) Hue() tone.Hue {
	switch t {
	case KanbanToneGray:
		return tone.HueGray
	case KanbanToneBlue:
		return tone.HueBlue
	case KanbanToneGreen:
		return tone.HueGreen
	case KanbanToneYellow:
		return tone.HueYellow
	case KanbanToneRed:
		return tone.HueRed
	case KanbanTonePurple:
		return tone.HuePurple
	default:
		return tone.HueGray
	}
}

// Hue maps StatTone onto the categorical hue axis (stat tiles are
// decorative emphasis, not semantics).
func (t StatTone) Hue() tone.Hue {
	switch t {
	case StatToneBlue:
		return tone.HueBlue
	case StatToneGreen:
		return tone.HueGreen
	case StatToneYellow:
		return tone.HueYellow
	case StatToneRed:
		return tone.HueRed
	case StatTonePurple:
		return tone.HuePurple
	default:
		return tone.HueGray
	}
}

// Tone maps TrendDirection onto the canonical semantic axis.
func (t TrendDirection) Tone() tone.Tone {
	switch t {
	case TrendUp:
		return tone.ToneSuccess
	case TrendDown:
		return tone.ToneDanger
	case TrendWarn:
		return tone.ToneWarning
	case TrendNone:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	default:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	}
}

// Tone maps ScrollbackTone onto the canonical semantic axis.
func (t ScrollbackTone) Tone() tone.Tone {
	switch t {
	case ScrollbackToneNeutral:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	case ScrollbackToneInfo:
		return tone.ToneInfo
	case ScrollbackToneSuccess:
		return tone.ToneSuccess
	case ScrollbackToneWarning:
		return tone.ToneWarning
	case ScrollbackToneDanger:
		return tone.ToneDanger
	default:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	}
}

// Tone maps BadgeType onto the canonical semantic axis. Primary maps to
// Accent (the ADR-0044 accent slot); the FeedbackError-style "error"
// spelling maps to Danger.
func (t BadgeType) Tone() tone.Tone {
	switch t {
	case BadgeNeutral:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	case BadgeSuccess:
		return tone.ToneSuccess
	case BadgeWarning:
		return tone.ToneWarning
	case BadgeError:
		return tone.ToneDanger
	case BadgeInfo:
		return tone.ToneInfo
	case BadgePrimary:
		return tone.ToneAccent
	default:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	}
}

// TestStatusToneAdapterEquivalence: the tone adapter + DotHue must derive
// exactly what statusToneBgMap ships today — zero visual change, proven.
func TestStatusToneAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, st := range []StatusTone{
		StatusToneNeutral, StatusToneSuccess, StatusToneWarning,
		StatusToneDanger, StatusToneInfo,
	} {
		derived := tone.UtilitiesFor(st.DotHue()).BGSolid.Classes()
		shipped := statusToneBgMap[st]

		if derived != shipped {
			t.Errorf(
				"StatusTone %s: DotHue().BGSolid = %q, statusToneBgMap ships %q — adapter drifted from pixels",
				st, derived, shipped,
			)
		}
	}

	wantTones := map[StatusTone]tone.Tone{
		StatusToneNeutral: tone.ToneNeutral,
		StatusToneSuccess: tone.ToneSuccess,
		StatusToneWarning: tone.ToneWarning, // amber hue — the #428 decision (one warning hue)
		StatusToneDanger:  tone.ToneDanger,
		StatusToneInfo:    tone.ToneInfo,
	}

	for st, want := range wantTones {
		if got := st.Tone(); got != want {
			t.Errorf("StatusTone %s.Tone() = %s, want %s", st, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestKanbanToneAdapterEquivalence: KanbanTone.Hue() must derive exactly
// what kanbanToneLookup ships today.
func TestKanbanToneAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for kt, shipped := range kanbanToneLookup {
		derived := tone.UtilitiesFor(kt.Hue()).BGSolid.Classes()

		if derived != shipped {
			t.Errorf(
				"KanbanTone %s: Hue().BGSolid = %q, kanbanToneLookup ships %q",
				kt, derived, shipped,
			)
		}
	}
}

// TestStatToneAdapterEquivalence: StatTone.Hue() must derive exactly the
// tint/icon strings statTileLookup ships (tile + icon halves of the
// "tile|icon" value).
func TestStatToneAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for st, shipped := range statTileLookup {
		u := tone.UtilitiesFor(st.Hue())

		if tint, _, ok := cutStatTile(shipped); ok && tint != u.BGTint.Classes() {
			t.Errorf(
				"StatTone %s: Hue().BGTint = %q, statTileLookup tile = %q",
				st, u.BGTint.Classes(), tint,
			)
		}
	}
}

// cutStatTile splits a statTileLookup "tile|icon" value.
func cutStatTile(v string) (string, string, bool) {
	for i := len(v) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if v[i] == '|' {
			return v[:i], v[i+1:], true
		}
	}

	return "", "", false
}

// TestTrendDirectionAdapterEquivalence: the trend text classes must be
// derivable from the adapter tone/hue grammar (green/amber use the Strong
// slot, red uses the Text slot — pinned as shipped).
func TestTrendDirectionAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	derived := map[TrendDirection]string{
		TrendUp:   tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGreen).TextStrong.Classes(),
		TrendDown: tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueRed).Text.Classes(),
		TrendWarn: tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueAmber).TextStrong.Classes(),
	}

	for td, want := range map[TrendDirection]string{
		TrendUp:   "text-green-700 dark:text-green-400",
		TrendDown: "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400",
		TrendWarn: "text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400",
	} {
		if derived[td] != want {
			t.Errorf("TrendDirection %s derived %q, want shipped %q", td, derived[td], want)
		}

		if got := td.Tone(); got == "" {
			t.Errorf("TrendDirection %s.Tone() empty", td)
		}
	}
}

// TestBadgeTypeAdapterEquivalence: BadgeType's dot is a single light-mode
// class (no dark half — deliberate). Semantic rows derive from the hue
// grammar; the gray neutral dot is bg-gray-500 (one step darker than the
// uniform grammar's 400 — the same gray-dot convention as statusToneBgMap);
// BadgePrimary is the ADR-0049 accent emission (brand axis, pinned literal —
// the accent row ships no BGSolid pair yet, S11).
func TestBadgeTypeAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	wantDots := map[BadgeType]string{
		BadgePrimary: "bg-accent-500",
		BadgeSuccess: tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGreen).BGSolid.Light,
		BadgeWarning: tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueAmber).BGSolid.Light,
		BadgeError:   tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueRed).BGSolid.Light,
		BadgeInfo:    tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueBlue).BGSolid.Light,
		BadgeNeutral: "bg-gray-500",
	}

	for bt, style := range badgeStyleMap {
		want, ok := wantDots[bt]
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("BadgeType %s missing from the wantDots map", bt)

			continue
		}

		if style.Dot != want {
			t.Errorf(
				"BadgeType %s: dot %q != expected %q",
				bt, style.Dot, want,
			)
		}
	}

	wantTones := map[BadgeType]tone.Tone{
		BadgePrimary: tone.ToneAccent,
		BadgeSuccess: tone.ToneSuccess,
		BadgeWarning: tone.ToneWarning,
		BadgeError:   tone.ToneDanger,
		BadgeInfo:    tone.ToneInfo,
		BadgeNeutral: tone.ToneNeutral,
	}

	for bt, want := range wantTones {
		if got := bt.Tone(); got != want {
			t.Errorf("BadgeType %s.Tone() = %s, want %s", bt, got, want)
		}
	}
}
package display

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// TooltipProps configures a tooltip component.
//
// The tooltip shows on :hover and :focus-within via pure CSS. A tiny
// singleton script (tooltipAriaScriptComponent) propagates aria-describedby
// from the non-focusable wrapper <div> to the first focusable child so
// screen readers announce the tooltip text on focus.
type TooltipProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Text     string
	Position TooltipPosition
}

// DefaultTooltipProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultTooltipProps() TooltipProps {
	return TooltipProps{
		Position: TooltipPositionTop,
	}
}

type tooltipPositionStyles struct {
	Tooltip string
	Arrow   string
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for tooltip position styles
var tooltipPositionMap = map[Position]tooltipPositionStyles{
	PositionTop: {
		Tooltip: "bottom-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 mb-2",
		Arrow:   "top-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 border-t-gray-900 dark:border-t-gray-700",
	},
	PositionBottom: {
		Tooltip: "top-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 mt-2",
		Arrow:   "bottom-full left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 border-b-gray-900 dark:border-b-gray-700",
	},
	PositionStart: {
		Tooltip: "inset-e-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 me-2",
		Arrow:   "inset-s-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-s-gray-900 dark:border-s-gray-700",
	},
	PositionEnd: {
		Tooltip: "inset-s-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 ms-2",
		Arrow:   "inset-e-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-e-gray-900 dark:border-e-gray-700",
	},
	PositionLeft: {
		Tooltip: "right-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 me-2",
		Arrow:   "left-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-s-gray-900 dark:border-s-gray-700",
	},
	PositionRight: {
		Tooltip: "left-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 ms-2",
		Arrow:   "right-full top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 border-e-gray-900 dark:border-e-gray-700",
	},
}

func tooltipLookupPosition(pos TooltipPosition) tooltipPositionStyles {
	return utils.Lookup(tooltipPositionMap, pos, tooltipPositionMap[PositionTop])
}

// Tooltip wraps content in a hover/focus-activated tooltip. Pure CSS for
// show/hide (group-hover/group-focus-within); a singleton script propagates
// aria-describedby to the focusable trigger for screen-reader support.
//
//	@display.Tooltip(display.TooltipProps{Text: "More info"}) {
//	   <button>Hover me</button>
//	}
templ Tooltip(props TooltipProps) {
	{{ id := utils.EnsureID("tooltip", props.ID) }}
	{{ pos := tooltipLookupPosition(props.Position) }}
	<div
		id={ id }
		data-tc-tooltip
		data-tc-position={ string(props.Position) }
		class={ utils.Class("group relative inline-flex", props.Class) }
		aria-describedby={ id + "-tooltip" }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ children... }
		<div
			id={ id + "-tooltip" }
			class={ "absolute z-20 hidden group-hover:block group-focus-within:block whitespace-nowrap rounded-md bg-gray-900 dark:bg-gray-700 px-2 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-white shadow-xs",
				pos.Tooltip }
			role="tooltip"
		>
			{ props.Text }
			<div class={ "absolute h-0 w-0 border-4 border-transparent", pos.Arrow }></div>
		</div>
	</div>
	@tooltipAriaScriptComponent(props.Nonce)
}

package display

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestTooltipRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name     string
		text     string
		position TooltipPosition
		wantAll  []string
		wantAny  []string
		wantNone []string
	}{
		{
			name:     "top tooltip",
			text:     "More info",
			position: TooltipPositionTop,
			wantAll:  []string{"More info", `role="tooltip"`, "group-hover:block", "bottom-full"},
		},
		{
			name:     "bottom tooltip",
			text:     "Help",
			position: TooltipPositionBottom,
			wantAll:  []string{"Help", "top-full"},
		},
		{
			name:     "right tooltip",
			text:     "Details",
			position: TooltipPositionRight,
			wantAll:  []string{"left-full"},
		},
		{
			name:     "left tooltip",
			text:     "Sidebar",
			position: TooltipPositionLeft,
			wantAll:  []string{"right-full"},
		},
		{
			name:     "start tooltip",
			text:     "Logical start",
			position: TooltipPositionStart,
			wantAll:  []string{"inset-e-full", "me-2"},
			wantNone: []string{"right-full", "left-full"},
		},
		{
			name:     "end tooltip",
			text:     "Logical end",
			position: TooltipPositionEnd,
			wantAll:  []string{"inset-s-full", "ms-2"},
			wantNone: []string{"right-full", "left-full"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			output := utils.Render(t, Tooltip(TooltipProps{
				Text:     tt.text,
				Position: tt.position,
			}))
			for _, want := range tt.wantAll {
				utils.AssertContains(t, output, want)
			}

			for _, banned := range tt.wantNone {
				utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, banned)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDefaultTooltipProps(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := DefaultTooltipProps()
	if props.Position != TooltipPositionTop {
		t.Errorf("DefaultTooltipProps().Position = %q, want %q", props.Position, TooltipPositionTop)
	}
}

func TestTooltipA11yLinkage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("tooltip has role=tooltip", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tooltip(TooltipProps{
			Text:     "Help text",
			Position: TooltipPositionTop,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="tooltip"`)
	})

	t.Run("tooltip with custom class and ID", func(t *testing.T) {

			ID: "tip-1", Class: "ml-2",
			Text:     "Hint",
			Position: TooltipPositionTop,

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "ml-2")
	})
}

func TestTooltipPositionEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("tooltip without ID auto-generates id and aria-describedby", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tooltip(TooltipProps{
			Text:     "Tip",
			Position: TooltipPositionTop,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "aria-describedby=")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="tooltip"`)
	})
	t.Run("tooltip with ID sets aria-describedby linkage", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Tooltip(TooltipProps{
			ID:       "my-tip",
			Text:     "Tip",
			Position: TooltipPositionTop,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-describedby="my-tip-tooltip"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-tip-tooltip"`)
	})
}

func TestTooltipEscapeDismiss(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	output := utils.Render(t, Tooltip(TooltipProps{
		Nonce:    "n",
		Text:     "Dismissible",
		Position: TooltipPositionTop,
	}))

	// Escape on the focusable trigger sets the dismissed state.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `e.key!=="Escape"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-tooltip-dismissed`)

	// Re-entering/focusing the trigger clears the dismissed state.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `"mouseenter"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `"focusin"`)

	// The companion CSS hides the tooltip when the dismissed state is active.
	cssPath := filepath.Join("..", "templates", "custom.css")
	if css, err := os.ReadFile(cssPath); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read custom.css: %v", err)
	} else {
		utils.AssertContains(t, string(css), `[data-tc-tooltip][data-tc-tooltip-dismissed] [role="tooltip"]`)
	}
}

// T5.5 (#493): the tooltip trigger is ARBITRARY children — buttons, links,
// and inputs are all legitimate triggers. These tests pin the wrapper
// contract those custom triggers rely on: the trigger markup renders inside
// the data-tc-tooltip wrapper (before the panel), and the singleton script
// targets every interactive element kind when propagating aria-describedby.
func TestTooltipCustomTriggerElements(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	renderTooltipWithChild := func(t *testing.T, props TooltipProps, child templ.Component) string {
		t.Helper()

		var buf bytes.Buffer

		ctx := templ.WithChildren(context.Background(), child)
		if err := Tooltip(props).Render(ctx, &buf); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("render tooltip: %v", err)
		}

		return strings.TrimSpace(buf.String())
	}

	t.Run("button trigger renders inside the wrapper", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := renderTooltipWithChild(t, TooltipProps{
			ID:   "tip-btn",
			Text: "Button hint",
		}, templ.Raw(`<button type="button" id="trigger-btn">Save</button>`))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-tc-tooltip`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<button type="button" id="trigger-btn">Save</button>`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="tip-btn-tooltip"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-describedby="tip-btn-tooltip"`)
	})

	t.Run("link trigger renders inside the wrapper", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := renderTooltipWithChild(t, TooltipProps{
			ID:   "tip-link",
			Text: "Link hint",
		}, templ.Raw(`<a href="/docs">Docs</a>`))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<a href="/docs">Docs</a>`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="tip-link-tooltip"`)
	})

	t.Run("script propagates describedby to every interactive trigger kind", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := renderTooltipWithChild(t, TooltipProps{
			ID:       "tip-aria",
			Text:     "A11y hint",
			Nonce:    "test-nonce",
			Position: TooltipPositionBottom,
		}, templ.Raw(`<input type="text" id="trigger-input">`))
		// The focusable-selector list names each trigger kind the
		// propagation covers — a new interactive element kind must be
		// added here or screen readers lose the describedby association.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `button,a[href],input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`)
	})
}
package main

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
)

// demoBasePath is the canonical mount prefix for every demo page, asset, and
// endpoint. The Firebase Hosting site (templcomponents.lars.software) rewrites
// /demo/** to the Cloud Run service, and Cloud Run passes the ORIGINAL path
// through — so the demo must serve its routes under /demo to be reachable at
// https://templcomponents.lars.software/demo/**. withBasePath additionally
// keeps the bare paths (/health, /wire, /api/...) working so the raw run.app
// URL, the visualtest harness, and orchestrator probes keep working unchanged.
const demoBasePath = "/demo"

// demoDocsURL is the documentation site the demo links back to; the same
// site proxies this demo under /demo/**.
const demoDocsURL = "https://templcomponents.lars.software"

// demoGitHubURL is the repository link shown in the shell chrome.
const demoGitHubURL = "https://github.com/larsartmann/templ-components"

// demoURL prefixes a root-relative path with the demo base path. Every URL
// EMITTED by the demo templates (links, CSS, favicons, wire endpoints) goes
// through this so pages work identically on both origins:
//
//	https://templcomponents.lars.software/demo/display
//	https://templcomponents-demo-<hash>.us-central1.run.app/demo/display
func demoURL(path string) string {
	if path == "" {
		return demoBasePath
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(path, demoBasePath+"/") || path == demoBasePath {
		return path
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "/") {
		return demoBasePath + "/" + path
	}

	return demoBasePath + path
}

// withBasePath dual-mounts the mux under /demo: requests to /demo/<path> are
// served by the same handler as /<path>. Bare /demo serves the home page
// directly (no redirect): Firebase Hosting's trailingSlash normalization may
// bounce /demo/ and /demo in either direction, so BOTH must render the home
// page — a redirect here could loop with the edge's own redirect.
func withBasePath(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path == demoBasePath {
			r.URL.Path = "/"

			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)

			return
		}
		if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.URL.Path, demoBasePath+"/"); ok {
			r.URL.Path = "/" + rest
		}

		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

// demoCSP is the demo's Content-Security-Policy. It must stay in sync with
// the /demo/** header override in website/firebase.json (if Firebase Hosting
// applies its own CSP to proxied responses, the browser INTERSECTS both —
// equal values make that a no-op). Allowances beyond 'self':
//   - cdn.jsdelivr.net: the ECharts and Datastar SDK scripts (SDKScript
//     components load their runtimes from the jsDelivr CDN)
//   - 'unsafe-eval' in script-src: the pinned Datastar runtime compiles
//     action expressions by evaluating strings (GenerateExpression → eval);
//     without it every data-on:* action dies with EvalError — the documented
//     runtime requirement (docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md). The nonce still
//     gates script LOADING; unsafe-eval only widens runtime-internal
//     expression compilation.
//   - fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com: demoFonts() web fonts
//   - ui-avatars.com / picsum.photos: the Avatar/Image/Lightbox demo
//     placeholder images
//   - 'unsafe-inline' in style-src: library components emit style=""
//     attributes (heatmap cells, progress bars); inline scripts stay
//     nonce-gated ('nonce-demo-nonce')
const demoCSP = "default-src 'self'; " +
	"script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net 'unsafe-eval' 'nonce-demo-nonce'; " +
	"style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; " +
	"font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; " +
	"img-src 'self' data: https://ui-avatars.com https://picsum.photos https://fastly.picsum.photos; " +
	"connect-src 'self'; " +
	"object-src 'none'; " +
	"base-uri 'self'; " +
	"form-action 'self'; " +
	"frame-ancestors 'none'"

// withSecurityHeaders stamps the demo's baseline security headers on every
// response, making the demo's CSP guarantee real on BOTH serving origins
// (the raw run.app URL has no Firebase in front of it).
func withSecurityHeaders(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		h := w.Header()
		h.Set("Content-Security-Policy", demoCSP)
		h.Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
		h.Set("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}
package main

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"net/http"
)

// Session-scoped CSRF for the demo's mutating endpoints (backlog #229,
// 2026-09-23). A real app issues one token per session and validates it
// server-side on every mutating request; the demo used to mint ONE random
// token per process, which protected nothing beyond the process boundary.
// Now every visitor gets a random token in a SameSite=Lax cookie on their
// first response, and mutating endpoints compare the submitted csrf_token
// against that cookie — a token scraped from yesterday's page render no
// longer validates.
//
// Still demo-grade by design: no HMAC binding to the session, no expiry, in
// a public demo holding no real data. The shape matches what a real app
// should grow into.

const demoSessionCookie = "tc_demo_csrf"

type demoSessionCtxKey struct{}

// withDemoSession middleware: mint the CSRF cookie on first response and
// expose the token to handlers via the request context.
func withDemoSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if c, err := r.Cookie(demoSessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(context.WithValue(r.Context(), demoSessionCtxKey{}, c.Value)))

			return
		}

		token := newDemoSessionToken()
		http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
			Name:     demoSessionCookie,
			Value:    token,
			Path:     "/",
			MaxAge:   86400,
			HttpOnly: true,
			SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
			Secure:   true,
		})
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(context.WithValue(r.Context(), demoSessionCtxKey{}, token)))
	})
}

// demoSessionCSRF returns the visitor's session token (empty when the
// middleware has not run or the visitor sent no cookie yet — a mutating
// endpoint must treat empty as a failed validation, since the form could not
// have legitimately carried a token).
func demoSessionCSRF(r *http.Request) string {
	token, _ := r.Context().Value(demoSessionCtxKey{}).(string)

	return token
}

// demoSessionTokenValid reports whether the submitted form token matches the
// visitor's session cookie token.
func demoSessionTokenValid(r *http.Request) bool {
	session := demoSessionCSRF(r)

	return session != "" && r.FormValue(kanbanCSRFFieldName) == session
}

// newDemoSessionToken mints one random session token.
func newDemoSessionToken() string {
	var b [16]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
		panic("demo session: generate csrf token: " + err.Error())
	}

	return hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
}
package main

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// postWithSession builds a mutating request carrying a session cookie and a
// csrf_token form field, the way the kanban endpoints receive them.
func postWithSession(t *testing.T, cookie, formToken string) *http.Request {
	t.Helper()

	form := url.Values{}
	if formToken != "" {
		form.Set(kanbanCSRFFieldName, formToken)
	}

	r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/kanban/htmx", strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
	r.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")

	if cookie != "" {
		r.Header.Set("Cookie", demoSessionCookie+"="+cookie)
	}

	return r
}

// TestDemoSessionCSRF pins the session-scoped CSRF contract (#229): a first
// visit mints the SameSite=Lax cookie and exposes the token to handlers;
// the submitted form token validates only against THAT session's value — a
// token from another session, or no cookie at all, fails closed.
func TestDemoSessionCSRF(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	var handlerToken string
	firstVisit := withDemoSession(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		handlerToken = demoSessionCSRF(r)
	}))

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	firstVisit.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))

	if handlerToken == "" {
		t.Fatal("first visit exposed an empty token to the handler")
	}

	for _, c := range rec.Result().Cookies() {
		if c.Name != demoSessionCookie {
			continue
		}

		if c.Value != handlerToken {
			t.Errorf("cookie value %q != handler token %q", c.Value, handlerToken)
		}

		if c.SameSite != http.SameSiteLaxMode {
			t.Errorf("cookie SameSite = %v, want Lax", c.SameSite)
		}
	}

	t.Run("matching session token validates", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		var valid bool
		withDemoSession(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			valid = demoSessionTokenValid(r)
		})).ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), postWithSession(t, handlerToken, handlerToken))

		if !valid {
			t.Error("the session's own token must validate")
		}
	})

	t.Run("foreign session cookie fails closed", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		var valid bool
		withDemoSession(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			valid = demoSessionTokenValid(r)
		})).ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), postWithSession(t, "some-other-session", handlerToken))

		if valid {
			t.Error("a foreign session must not validate another session's token")
		}
	})

	t.Run("no cookie fails closed", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		var valid bool
		withDemoSession(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			valid = demoSessionTokenValid(r)
		})).ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), postWithSession(t, "", handlerToken))

		if valid {
			t.Error("no session cookie must fail validation even with a token in the form")
		}
	})
}

// datastarPolledStatsRegion is the datastar.PolledRegion demo for both the
// initial render and the /api/datastar/tick response. The region self-patches
// (response fragment root id = region id), so the response re-renders the
// whole component to re-arm the interval — until the final tick, which
// renders the settled static shell without the interval attributes.
templ datastarPolledStatsRegion(tick int) {
	@datastar.PolledRegion(datastar.PolledRegionProps{
		BaseProps:     datastarPolledStatsBaseProps(),
		URL:           demoURL("/api/datastar/tick") + "?tick=" + strconv.Itoa(tick),
		Every:         "5s",
		ShowTimestamp: true,
		TimeFormat:    "15:04:05 MST",
		Now: func() time.Time {
			return time.Now().UTC()
		},
	}) {
		@datastarPolledStatsContent(tick, true)
	}
}

// datastarPolledStatsSettled is the final tick's fragment: the same region
// shell WITHOUT the interval attributes, so the runtime's outer patch
// replaces the polling region with static content and the demo settles.
templ datastarPolledStatsSettled(tick int) {
	{{ now := time.Now().UTC() }}
	<div id="datastar-polled-stats" role="region" aria-label="Live demo statistics" aria-live="polite">
		@datastarPolledStatsContent(tick, false)
		<div class="mt-3 flex justify-end">
			<time
				class="text-xs tabular-nums text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"
				datetime={ now.Format(time.RFC3339) }
			>
				Updated { now.Format("15:04:05") } UTC
			</time>
		</div>
	</div>
}

import (

// TestDecodeFormEndpoints pins the DecodeForm-migrated demo endpoints: GET
// query decoding, POST body decoding, and the malformed-value paths. Every
// handler in main.go now decodes via wire.DecodeForm — these tests keep that
// migration honest (behavior parity with the old ParseForm chains).
func TestDecodeFormEndpoints(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		method     string
		path       string
		form       url.Values
		wantStatus int
		wantIn     string
	}{
		{
			name:       "load-more decodes cursor query",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/items?cursor=1",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "/api/items?cursor=2",
		},
		{
			name:       "load-more without cursor defaults to first page",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/items",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "Item",
		},
		{
			name:       "demo-stats decodes tick and advances",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/demo-stats?tick=1",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "tick=2",
		},
		{
			name:       "demo-stats with garbage tick restarts at 1",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/demo-stats?tick=not-a-number",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "tick=1",
		},
		{
			name:       "users decodes status and sort",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/users?status=active&sort=name",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "Alice",
		},
		{
			name:       "wire wizard advances step 0 with valid email",
			method:     http.MethodPost,
			path:       "/api/wire/wizard",
			form:       url.Values{"step": {"0"}, "email": {"ada@example.com"}},
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "step",
		},
		{
			name:       "wire wizard restarts on malformed step",
			method:     http.MethodPost,
			path:       "/api/wire/wizard",
			form:       url.Values{"step": {"garbage"}},
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     wireWizardInvalid,
		},
		{
			name:       "wire form decodes name and email",
			method:     http.MethodPost,
			path:       "/api/wire/form",
			form:       url.Values{"name": {"Ada"}, "email": {"ada@example.com"}},
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "Ada",
		},
		{
			name:       "wire form flags missing name",
			method:     http.MethodPost,
			path:       "/api/wire/form",
			form:       url.Values{"email": {"ada@example.com"}},
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     wireFormNameMissing,
		},
		{
			name:       "wire filter decodes q query",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/wire/filter?q=go",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "go",
		},
		{
			name:       "calendar htmx endpoint decodes year and month",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/wire/calendar/htmx?year=2026&month=7",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "July 2026",
		},
		{
			name:       "calendar htmx endpoint renders self-swap attributes",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/wire/calendar/htmx?year=2026&month=7",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     `hx-swap="outerHTML settle:0s"`,
		},
		{
			name:       "calendar datastar endpoint decodes year and month",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/wire/calendar/datastar?year=2026&month=12",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "December 2026",
		},
		{
			name:       "calendar endpoint with garbage query falls back to current month",
			method:     http.MethodGet,
			path:       "/api/wire/calendar/htmx?year=abc&month=zzz",
			wantStatus: http.StatusOK,
			wantIn:     "aria-label=\"Next month\"",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			server := httptest.NewServer(newMux())
			t.Cleanup(server.Close)

			var body io.Reader
			if tt.form != nil {
				body = strings.NewReader(tt.form.Encode())
			}

			req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(t.Context(), tt.method, server.URL+tt.path, body)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if tt.form != nil {
				req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
			}

			resp, err := server.Client().Do(req)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			t.Cleanup(func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() })

			if resp.StatusCode != tt.wantStatus {
				t.Errorf("status = %d, want %d", resp.StatusCode, tt.wantStatus)
			}

			got, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if tt.wantIn != "" && !strings.Contains(string(got), tt.wantIn) {
				t.Errorf("response missing %q\nbody:\n%s", tt.wantIn, got)
			}
		})
	}
}

// demoCardFilterScript wires the home filter input to the page cards: a
// case-insensitive substring match over each card's text, hiding non-matches.
templ demoCardFilterScript() {
	<script nonce={ demoNonceConst }>
		document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
			var input = document.getElementById('demo-search');
			if (!input) return;
			var cards = document.querySelectorAll('.demo-card');
			input.addEventListener('input', function() {
				var term = input.value.trim().toLowerCase();
				cards.forEach(function(card) {
					var match = !term || card.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(term) !== -1;
					card.style.display = match ? '' : 'none';
				});
			});
		});
	</script>
}

package main

import (
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// The demo-content guard (#C13): every demoSection anchor on the registry
// pages must be followed by non-whitespace CONTENT — not just its heading.
// A broken composition (a component renamed out from under the demo, a
// conditional that silently renders nothing) otherwise ships as a
// visible-but-empty section that only a human eyeballing the page would
// catch.
//
// Shipped-structure note (TODO row 485): the demo calls @demoSection(...)
// WITHOUT a children block, so each section renders its heading only and the
// section's content lands as SIBLING markup after </section> — visually
// identical in block flow, which is why this shipped unnoticed. This guard
// therefore asserts content over the span [section start, next section
// start), heading excluded — the contract the pages actually ship.

var (
	sectionAnchorRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`<section class="demo-section[^"]*" id="([^"]+)"`)
	sectionHeadingRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^<div class="flex items-center justify-between mb-6">.*?</div>`)
	// snippetMarker opens a demoCodeSnippet block; everything from here on
	// belongs to the code listing, not the live specimen, so the guard cuts
	// the span there — otherwise a section whose specimen died still passes
	// on its snippet's text (mutation-proven 2026-10-30).
	snippetMarker = `<div class="mt-4 rounded-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-gray-900`
	tagRe         = regexp.MustCompile(`<[^>]+>`)
)

// contentSkipList exempts sections whose content is legitimately textless
// (pure icon/SVG specimens) from the non-whitespace-text assertion.
var contentSkipList = map[string]string{
	"feedback-spinners":  "spinner specimens are pure SVG — textless by design",
	"feedback-skeletons": "skeleton grid is pure shimmer boxes — textless by design",
	"display-avatars":    "avatar specimens are image-only (see TODO 486: external ui-avatars.com CDN)",
}

// noSectionPages are registry routes that intentionally compose no
// demoSection blocks (appshell/card pages); the guard must not demand
// sections from them.
var noSectionPages = map[string]string{
	"/":        "home page — hero + cards, no demoSection blocks",
	"/recipes": "appshell recipe screens, no demoSection blocks",
	"/users":   "appshell table screen, no demoSection blocks",
}

func stripTags(s string) string { return strings.TrimSpace(tagRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "")) }

func TestDemoSectionsRenderContent(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(newDemoHandler())
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)

	client := srv.Client()

	for _, page := range demoPages() {
		t.Run(page.Path, func(t *testing.T) {
			resp, err := client.Get(srv.URL + page.Path) //nolint:noctx // test-local server, bounded response
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("fetch %s: %v", page.Path, err)
			}
			defer resp.Body.Close()

			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
				t.Fatalf("fetch %s: status %d", page.Path, resp.StatusCode)
			}

			html, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", page.Path, err)
			}

			pageHTML := string(html)

			matches := sectionAnchorRe.FindAllStringSubmatchIndex(pageHTML, -1)
			if len(matches) == 0 {
				if reason, known := noSectionPages[page.Path]; known {
					t.Logf("no demo sections: %s", reason)

					return
				}

				t.Fatalf("page %s renders NO demo sections — did the page composition change?", page.Path)
			}

			for i, m := range matches {
				anchor := pageHTML[m[2]:m[3]]

				if reason, skip := contentSkipList[anchor]; skip {
					t.Logf("skip %s: %s", anchor, reason)

					continue
				}

				end := len(pageHTML)
				if i+1 < len(matches) {
					end = matches[i+1][0]
				}

				chunk := pageHTML[m[0]:end]

				// Cut past the section's own open tag, then drop the heading
				// wrapper (one div, no nested div inside) so only the
				// section's and siblings' CONTENT text remains.
				if openEnd := strings.IndexByte(chunk, '>'); openEnd >= 0 {
					chunk = chunk[openEnd+1:]
				}

				chunk = sectionHeadingRe.ReplaceAllString(chunk, "")

				if cut := strings.Index(chunk, snippetMarker); cut >= 0 {
					chunk = chunk[:cut]
				}

				if text := stripTags(chunk); text == "" {
					t.Errorf(
						"section #%s on %s renders NO content (heading only) — a demo composition broke",
						anchor, page.Path,
					)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
package main

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// TestHeroCountsMatchFeatures guards the demo hero stat cards against drift:
// the hardcoded component/package counts must equal the canonical totals in
// FEATURES.md (which itself is drift-guard verified). The icon count is
// computed dynamically from icons.AllIconNames() and is asserted against
// FEATURES.md so both stay honest.
func TestHeroCountsMatchFeatures(t *testing.T) {
	features, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "FEATURES.md"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("FEATURES.md not readable: %v", err)
	}

	totals := regexp.MustCompile(`\*\*Totals:\*\* (\d+) templ components.*?, (\d+) icon names`).
		FindStringSubmatch(string(features))
	if totals == nil {
		t.Fatal("could not parse FEATURES.md Totals line")
	}

	if componentCount != totals[1] {
		t.Errorf("demo componentCount = %s, FEATURES.md totals = %s (update the const in demo.templ)",
			componentCount, totals[1])
	}

	// packageCount must equal the README Packages row (live-computed by
	// utils.TestDocsCountDrift) so the demo hero sells the same number as the
	// README and the site — one number everywhere.
	readme, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "README.md"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("README.md not readable: %v", err)
	}

	packages := regexp.MustCompile(`\|\s*Packages\s*\|\s*(\d+) `).FindStringSubmatch(string(readme))
	if packages == nil {
		t.Fatal("could not parse README.md Packages row")
	}

	if packageCount != packages[1] {
		t.Errorf("demo packageCount = %s, README.md Packages row = %s (update the const in demo.templ)",
			packageCount, packages[1])
	}

	wantIcons, err := strconv.Atoi(totals[2])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse icon count: %v", err)
	}
	if got := len(icons.AllIconNames()); got != wantIcons {
		t.Errorf("icons.AllIconNames() = %d icons, FEATURES.md = %d", got, wantIcons)
	}

	// The rendered hero must carry the real library version, not a stale one.
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := demoHero().Render(context.Background(), &buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("render demoHero: %v", err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(buf.String(), "v"+utils.Version) {
		t.Errorf("hero does not render current utils.Version (%s)", utils.Version)
	}
}
package main

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/display"

// demoStatusBadgeMapper is the StatusBadgeWith demo mapper: it extends the
// built-in status mapping with a demo-only provisioning state and delegates
// everything else to the built-in map (unknown statuses render neutral).
func demoStatusBadgeMapper(status string) display.BadgeType {
	if status == "provisioning" {
		return display.BadgeInfo
	}

	return display.MapStatusToBadgeType(status)
}

func demoDate(year int, month time.Month, day int) *time.Time {
	t := time.Date(year, month, day, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	return &t
}

// demo — a badge + action layout the built-in Title/Subtitle fields can't
// express (demo code, exempt from the ADR-0010 sub-template extraction rule).

	</div>
}

// Hand-authored equivalents of go-echarts RenderSnippet() output — the
// ECharts adapter accepts Element + Script strings, so the demo needs no
// go-echarts dependency.
const (
	echartsDemoElement = `<div id="demo-echarts" style="width:100%;height:280px;"></div>`
	echartsDemoScript  = `var demoChart = echarts.init(document.getElementById('demo-echarts'));
demoChart.setOption({
  tooltip: {trigger: 'axis'},
  xAxis: {type: 'category', data: ['Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu','Fri','Sat','Sun']},
  yAxis: {type: 'value'},
  series: [{type: 'bar', data: [120, 200, 150, 80, 70, 110, 130]}]
});
window.addEventListener('resize', function() { demoChart.resize(); });`
)
