// TestWireWizardEndpoint pins the server-owned step machine: each request
// validates the CURRENT step, errors re-render the same step as 200 OK,
// and valid input advances.
func TestWireWizardEndpoint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name         string
		form         url.Values
		wantContains []string
	}{
		{
			name:         "invalid email stays on step 0 with the inline error",
			form:         url.Values{"step": {"0"}, "email": {"ada@example"}},
			wantContains: []string{`CurrentStep="1"`},
		},
	}

	_ = tests
	server := httptest.NewServer(newMux())
	t.Cleanup(server.Close)

	post := func(form url.Values) string {
		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(
			context.Background(),
			http.MethodPost,
			server.URL+"/api/wire/wizard",
			strings.NewReader(form.Encode()),
		)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")

		resp, err := server.Client().Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		t.Cleanup(func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() })

		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
			t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 200", resp.StatusCode)
		}

		body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}

		return string(body)
	}

	// Step 0 with an invalid email: same step, inline error.
	body := post(url.Values{"step": {"0"}, "email": {"ada@example"}})
	if !strings.Contains(body, wireFormEmailBad) {
		t.Error("invalid email must re-render step 0 with the error")
	}
	if strings.Contains(body, `value="1"`) && strings.Contains(body, `name="Full name"`) {
		t.Error("wizard must not advance past an invalid step")
	}

	// Step 0 valid: advances to the profile step.
	body = post(url.Values{"step": {"0"}, "email": {"ada@example.com"}})
	if !strings.Contains(body, `name="name"`) || !strings.Contains(body, `Full name`) {
		t.Error("valid email must advance to the profile step")
	}

	// Step 1 without a name: stays with an error.
	body = post(url.Values{"step": {"1"}, "name": {" "}})
	if !strings.Contains(body, "Enter your name.") {
		t.Error("missing name must keep the wizard on the profile step")
	}

	// Step 1 complete: done.
	body = post(url.Values{"step": {"1"}, "name": {"Ada Lovelace"}})
	if !strings.Contains(body, "Wizard complete") {
		t.Error("valid profile must complete the wizard")
	}

	// Unknown step: restarts at 0 (server owns the machine).
	body = post(url.Values{"step": {"9"}, "email": {"x@y.zz"}})
	if !strings.Contains(body, `value="0"`) {
		t.Error("unknown step must restart the wizard at step 0")
	}
}

// TestWireDemoSingleOptionsObject pins the ONE-options-object rule at the
// demo-render level: every data-on action expression on the rendered wire
// page carries at most one `{` — the pinned runtime reads exactly one options
// argument, so a second object is silently ignored (the 2026-10-02 regression
// class: `{selector: …}, {contentType: 'form'}` dropped form encoding).
func TestWireDemoSingleOptionsObject(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	html := fetchDemoHTML(t)

	re := regexp.MustCompile(`data-on:[a-zA-Z:_-]+="([^"]*)"`)
	for _, m := range re.FindAllStringSubmatch(html, -1) {
		expr := m[1]
		if strings.Count(expr, "{") > 1 {
			t.Errorf("action expression emits more than one options object: %q", expr)
		}
	}
}

package feedback

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// AlertProps configures an alert banner
type AlertProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Title       string
	Message     string
	Type        FeedbackType
	Dismissible bool
}

// DefaultAlertProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultAlertProps() AlertProps {
	return AlertProps{
		Type: FeedbackInfo,
	}
}

// Alert renders a full-width alert banner
//
//	@feedback.Alert(feedback.AlertProps{Title: "Error", Message: "Something went wrong", Type: feedback.FeedbackError})
//
// The ARIA role derives from Type: errors announce assertively
// (role="alert"); every other type reports politely (role="status") so a
// success banner is never read as an error by screen readers.
//
// The dismiss control markup is shared via utils.DismissButton; only the style
// classes differ from errorpage.ErrorAlert. JS behaviour is shared via
// utils.DismissScript().
templ Alert(props AlertProps) {
	{{ s := feedbackStyle(props.Type) }}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("rounded-md border p-4", s.Border, s.BG, props.Class) }
		role={ feedbackRole(props.Type) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="flex">
			<div class="flex-shrink-0">
				@icons.Icon(feedbackIcon(props.Type), utils.Class("h-5 w-5", s.Icon))
			</div>
			<div class="ms-3 flex-1">
				if props.Title != "" {
					<h3 class={ "text-sm font-medium", s.Text }>{ props.Title }</h3>
				}
				<div class={ "text-sm", s.Text }>
					<p>{ props.Message }</p>
					{ children... }
				</div>
			</div>
			if props.Dismissible {
				@utils.DismissButton(s.BG, s.Text)
			}
		</div>
		if props.Dismissible {
			@utils.ScriptComponent(props.Nonce, utils.DismissScript(), "alert dismiss script")
		}
	</div>
}

// inlineMessage renders a compact inline status message with icon
templ inlineMessage(message string, colorClass string, role string, icon templ.Component) {
	<div class={ "mt-2 flex items-center gap-1.5 text-sm", colorClass } role={ role } aria-live="polite">
		@icon
		<span>{ message }</span>
	</div>
}

// InlineError renders a compact inline error message for forms
//
//	@feedback.InlineError("This field is required")
templ InlineError(message string) {
	@inlineMessage(message, "text-red-600 dark:text-red-400", "alert", icons.Icon(icons.ExclamationTriangle, "h-4 w-4 flex-shrink-0"))
}

// InlineSuccess renders a compact inline success message
//
//	@feedback.InlineSuccess("Saved successfully")
templ InlineSuccess(message string) {
	@inlineMessage(message, "text-green-700 dark:text-green-400", "status", icons.Icon(icons.Check, "h-4 w-4 flex-shrink-0"))
}
package feedback

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

// Alert's dismiss script must never emit an EMPTY nonce attribute: under a
// strict CSP, `nonce=""` matches no source, so the browser blocks the script
// and the dismiss button silently dies. When the caller omits Nonce the
// component falls back to templ.GetNonce(ctx); when neither is set the
// attribute is omitted entirely (no-CSP sites keep the same behavior minus
// the useless empty attribute). Consumer evidence: crush-daily's
// collectErrorBanner forgot the nonce and its alert dismiss script was
// blocked by the site's script-src 'nonce-…' policy.
func TestAlertNonceFallback(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		ctxNonce  string
		propNonce string
		want      string
		notWant   string
	}{
		{
			name:      "prop nonce wins",
			ctxNonce:  "ctx-nonce",
			propNonce: "prop-nonce",
			want:      `nonce="prop-nonce"`,
			notWant:   `nonce=""`,
		},
		{
			name:      "falls back to context nonce",
			ctxNonce:  "ctx-nonce",
			propNonce: "",
			want:      `nonce="ctx-nonce"`,
			notWant:   `nonce=""`,
		},
		{
			name:      "no nonce anywhere omits the attribute",
			ctxNonce:  "",
			propNonce: "",
			want:      "<script>",
			notWant:   `nonce=`,
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			ctx := context.Background()
			if tt.ctxNonce != "" {
				ctx = templ.WithNonce(ctx, tt.ctxNonce)
			}

			var buf strings.Builder

			err := Alert(AlertProps{
				Message:     "nonce probe",
				Dismissible: true,
				Nonce:       tt.propNonce,
			}).Render(ctx, &buf)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("render: %v", err)
			}

			out := buf.String()

			if tt.want != "" && !strings.Contains(out, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("output missing %q:\n%s", tt.want, out)
			}

			if tt.notWant != "" && strings.Contains(out, tt.notWant) {
				t.Errorf("output contains %q:\n%s", tt.notWant, out)
			}
		})
	}
}

package feedback

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// CircularProgressSize controls the diameter of the ring.
type CircularProgressSize string

const (
	CircularProgressSizeSM CircularProgressSize = "sm"
	CircularProgressSizeMD CircularProgressSize = "md"
	CircularProgressSizeLG CircularProgressSize = "lg"
)

// CircularProgressProps configures a circular SVG progress indicator.
type CircularProgressProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Value is the percentage (0–100). Values outside the range are clamped.
	Value int
	// Size controls the rendered diameter. Defaults to md.
	Size CircularProgressSize
	// ShowLabel renders the numeric percentage in the centre.
	ShowLabel bool
	// Color overrides the progress arc colour (Tailwind stroke utility).
	// Defaults to text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-500 (the ADR-0044/0049
	// accent token family).
	Color tone.ColorClass
	// TrackColor overrides the background track colour.
	// Defaults to text-gray-200 dark:text-gray-700.
	TrackColor tone.ColorClass
}

// DefaultCircularProgressProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultCircularProgressProps() CircularProgressProps {
	return CircularProgressProps{
		Size:       CircularProgressSizeMD,
		Color:      "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-500",
		TrackColor: "text-gray-200 dark:text-gray-700",
	}
}

// circularProgressSizeLookup maps size enums to Tailwind dimension classes.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for circular progress sizes
var circularProgressSizeLookup = map[CircularProgressSize]string{
	CircularProgressSizeSM: "w-8 h-8",
	CircularProgressSizeMD: "w-12 h-12",
	CircularProgressSizeLG: "w-16 h-16",
}

// circularProgressStrokeLookup maps size enums to SVG stroke widths.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for stroke widths
var circularProgressStrokeLookup = map[CircularProgressSize]float64{
	CircularProgressSizeSM: 8,
	CircularProgressSizeMD: 7,
	CircularProgressSizeLG: 6,
}

// CircularProgress renders a circular SVG progress indicator with an optional
// percentage label. The value is clamped to [0, 100].
//
//	@feedback.CircularProgress(feedback.CircularProgressProps{Value: 75, ShowLabel: true})
templ CircularProgress(props CircularProgressProps) {
	{{
		value := max(0, min(100, props.Value))
		strokeWidth := utils.Lookup(circularProgressStrokeLookup, props.Size, 7)
		radius := 50.0 - strokeWidth/2
		circumference := 2 * math.Pi * radius
		dashOffset := circumference * (1 - float64(value)/100)
		sizeClass := utils.Lookup(circularProgressSizeLookup, props.Size, "w-12 h-12")
		color := string(props.Color)
		if color == "" {
			color = "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-500"
		}
		trackColor := string(props.TrackColor)
		if trackColor == "" {
			trackColor = "text-gray-200 dark:text-gray-700"
		}
	}}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("relative inline-flex items-center justify-center", sizeClass, props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
		role="progressbar"
		aria-valuenow={ fmt.Sprintf("%d", value) }
		aria-valuemin="0"
		aria-valuemax="100"
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-label={ fmt.Sprintf("%d%% complete", value) }
		}
	>
		<svg class={ utils.Class("w-full h-full -rotate-90", color) } viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none">
			<circle
				cx="50"
				cy="50"
				r={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", radius) }
				stroke="currentColor"
				stroke-width={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", strokeWidth) }
				class={ trackColor }
			></circle>
			<circle
				cx="50"
				cy="50"
				r={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", radius) }
				stroke="currentColor"
				stroke-width={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", strokeWidth) }
				stroke-linecap="round"
				stroke-dasharray={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", circumference) }
				stroke-dashoffset={ fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", dashOffset) }
				class="transition-all duration-500 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none"
			></circle>
		</svg>
		if props.ShowLabel {
			<span class="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center text-xs font-semibold text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300">
				{ fmt.Sprintf("%d%%", value) }
			</span>
		}
	</div>
}
package feedback

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestCircularProgress_A11Y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name        string
		props       CircularProgressProps
		checkHidden bool
	}{
		{
			name:  "role progressbar",
			props: CircularProgressProps{Value: 50},
		},
		{
			name:  "aria-valuenow reflects clamped value",
			props: CircularProgressProps{Value: 75},
		},
		{
			name:  "aria-valuemin is 0",
			props: CircularProgressProps{Value: 50},
		},
		{
			name:  "aria-valuemax is 100",
			props: CircularProgressProps{Value: 50},
		},
		{
			name:  "custom aria-label",
			props: CircularProgressProps{Value: 50, BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{AriaLabel: "Upload progress"}},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(tt.props))

			if !strings.Contains(html, `role="progressbar"`) {
				t.Error("expected role='progressbar'")
			}

			if !strings.Contains(html, `aria-valuenow=`) {
				t.Error("expected aria-valuenow attribute")
			}

			if !strings.Contains(html, `aria-valuemin="0"`) {
				t.Error("expected aria-valuemin='0'")
			}

			if !strings.Contains(html, `aria-valuemax="100"`) {
				t.Error("expected aria-valuemax='100'")
			}

			if tt.props.AriaLabel != "" {
				if !strings.Contains(html, fmt.Sprintf(`aria-label="%s"`, tt.props.AriaLabel)) {
					t.Errorf("expected aria-label=%q", tt.props.AriaLabel)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCircularProgress_EdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		props   CircularProgressProps
		wantVal int
	}{
		{"zero value", CircularProgressProps{Value: 0}, 0},
		{"exactly 100", CircularProgressProps{Value: 100}, 100},
		{"negative clamps to 0", CircularProgressProps{Value: -50}, 0},
		{"over 100 clamps to 100", CircularProgressProps{Value: 150}, 100},
		{"default zero value", CircularProgressProps{}, 0},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(tt.props))
			expected := fmt.Sprintf(`aria-valuenow="%d"`, tt.wantVal)

			if !strings.Contains(html, expected) {
				t.Errorf("expected %s in HTML", expected)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCircularProgress_BDD(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders with default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{}))
		if !strings.Contains(html, `role="progressbar"`) {
			t.Error("should render as a progressbar")
		}
	})

	t.Run("shows label when ShowLabel is true", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value:     42,
			ShowLabel: true,
		}))
		if !strings.Contains(html, "42%") {
			t.Error("should render '42%' label")
		}
	})

	t.Run("hides label when ShowLabel is false", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value:     42,
			ShowLabel: false,
		}))
		// aria-label always contains the percentage, but the visible label span should not be present
		if strings.Contains(html, `<span class="absolute inset-0`) {
			t.Error("should not render visible label span when ShowLabel is false")
		}
	})

	t.Run("applies custom color class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value: 50,
			Color: "text-green-600",
		}))
		if !strings.Contains(html, "text-green-600") {
			t.Error("should apply custom color class")
		}
	})

	t.Run("applies custom track color class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value:      50,
			TrackColor: "text-red-200",
		}))
		if !strings.Contains(html, "text-red-200") {
			t.Error("should apply custom track color class")
		}
	})
}

func TestCircularProgress_Coverage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("DefaultCircularProgressProps returns md size", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultCircularProgressProps()
		if props.Size != CircularProgressSizeMD {
			t.Errorf("expected md, got %s", props.Size)
		}

		if props.Color == "" {
			t.Error("default color should not be empty")
		}

		if props.TrackColor == "" {
			t.Error("default track color should not be empty")
		}
	})

	t.Run("all sizes produce valid dimension classes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		sizes := []CircularProgressSize{
			CircularProgressSizeSM,
			CircularProgressSizeMD,
			CircularProgressSizeLG,
		}

		for _, size := range sizes {
			html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
				Value: 50,
				Size:  size,
			}))
			if html == "" {
				t.Errorf("size %s produced empty output", size)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("unknown size falls back gracefully", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value: 50,
			Size:  "xl",
		}))
		// Should still render as a progressbar with valid value
		if !strings.Contains(html, `role="progressbar"`) {
			t.Error("unknown size should still render as progressbar")
		}

		if !strings.Contains(html, `aria-valuenow="50"`) {
			t.Error("unknown size should still show correct value")
		}
	})

	t.Run("custom ID is rendered", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value: 50,
			ID:    "my-progress",
		}))
		if !strings.Contains(html, `id="my-progress"`) {
			t.Error("should render custom ID")
		}
	})
}

func TestGoldenCircularProgress(t *testing.T) {

		name  string
		props CircularProgressProps
	}{
		{
			name: "md_75_with_label",

				Size:      CircularProgressSizeMD,

				Size:  CircularProgressSizeSM,
			},
		},
		{
			name: "lg_100_clamped",
			props: CircularProgressProps{
				Value: 150,
				Size:  CircularProgressSizeLG,
			},
		},

			name:  "default_zero",
			props: CircularProgressProps{},

			t.Parallel()

		})

func TestSkeletonCardGridContainerAware(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("viewport breakpoints by default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SkeletonCardGrid(SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 3}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "@container")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "sm:grid-cols-2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "lg:grid-cols-3")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "@sm:")
	})

	t.Run("container breakpoints when flag set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SkeletonCardGrid(SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 3, ContainerAware: true}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "@container")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "@sm:grid-cols-2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "@lg:grid-cols-3")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, " sm:")
	})
}

	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// Coverage: exercise low-coverage branches in feedback package.
// StepIndicator (71.8%), ProgressBar (72.8%), LoadingOverlay (72.6%), Spinner (73.8%).

func TestStepIndicatorCoverageGaps(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("vertical orientation", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			Orientation: StepVertical,
			Steps:       []string{"Step 1", "Step 2", "Step 3"},
			CurrentStep: 1,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Step 1")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Step 2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Step 3")
	})

	t.Run("horizontal orientation", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			Orientation: StepHorizontal,
			Steps:       []string{"Create", "Review", "Deploy"},
			CurrentStep: 1,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Create")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Deploy")
	})

	t.Run("propagates aria-label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			AriaLabel:   "Checkout progress",
			Steps:       []string{"Cart"},
			CurrentStep: 0,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Checkout progress"`)
	})

	t.Run("propagates custom class", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			Class:       "my-steps",
			Steps:       []string{"X"},
			CurrentStep: 0,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "my-steps")
	})
}

package feedback

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestAlertFullCoverage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, ft := range []FeedbackType{FeedbackSuccess, FeedbackError, FeedbackWarning, FeedbackInfo} {
		t.Run(string(ft)+" dismissible with BaseProps", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
				ID:          "alert-" + string(ft),
				Class:       "mt-2",
				AriaLabel:   string(ft) + " alert",
				Title:       string(ft) + " title",
				Message:     string(ft) + " message",
				Type:        ft,
				Dismissible: true,
			}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, string(ft)+" title")

		})
	}
}

func TestProgressBarCoverage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("current exceeds total caps at 100%", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Current: 150, Total: 100, ShowLabel: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "100%")
	})

	t.Run("with label shows percentage", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Current: 45, Total: 100, Label: "Uploading", ShowLabel: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Uploading")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "45%")
	})

	t.Run("label without showLabel still renders", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Current: 30, Total: 100, Label: "Processing",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Processing")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "30%")
	})

	t.Run("indeterminate with label hides percentage", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Indeterminate: true, Label: "Loading", ShowLabel: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Loading")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "%")
	})

	t.Run("size SM", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Size: ProgressBarSizeSM,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-1.5")
	})

	t.Run("size LG", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Size: ProgressBarSizeLG,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-4")
	})

	t.Run("with ID and AriaLabel", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			ID: "pb1", AriaLabel: "Upload progress",
			Current: 50, Total: 100,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="pb1"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Upload progress"`)
	})

	t.Run("with custom color", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(ProgressBarProps{
			Current: 50, Total: 100, Color: "bg-green-600 dark:bg-green-500",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-green-600")
	})

	t.Run("default props renders", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, ProgressBar(DefaultProgressBarProps()))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-accent-600")
	})
}

func TestAlertEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("empty title renders without h3", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
			Message: "Just a message",
			Type:    FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Just a message")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty message renders empty paragraph", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
			Title: "Title Only",
			Type:  FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Title Only")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)
	})

	t.Run("unknown type falls back to info styling", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
			Message: "Fallback",
			Type:    FeedbackType("unknown"),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Fallback")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border-gray-200")
	})

	t.Run("alert with ID propagates to root element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
			ID:      "my-alert",
			Message: "Test",
			Type:    FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-alert"`)
	})
}

func TestToastEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("empty message renders", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Toast(ToastProps{
			Title: "No Body",
			Type:  FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "No Body")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)
	})

	t.Run("unknown type falls back to info styling", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Toast(ToastProps{
			Message: "Fallback",
			Type:    FeedbackType("unknown"),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Fallback")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "border-gray-200")
	})

	t.Run("toast with ID propagates to root element", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Toast(ToastProps{
			ID:      "my-toast",
			Message: "Test",
			Type:    FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-toast"`)
	})

	t.Run("auto-dismiss fires even without ID", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		// DefaultToastProps sets Duration: 5000 but no ID. Before the fix,
		// the absence of an ID silently disabled auto-dismiss.
		output := utils.Render(t, Toast(DefaultToastProps()))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="tc-toast-`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "setTimeout")
	})

	t.Run("duration zero omits setTimeout", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Toast(ToastProps{
			ID:      "manual-toast",
			Message: "Manual",
			Type:    FeedbackInfo,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "setTimeout")
	})
}

func TestProgressBarEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {

		}))

		}))

		}))

	})
}

func TestStepIndicatorVertical(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("vertical layout uses flex-col", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			Steps:       []string{"Details", "Review", "Confirm"},
			CurrentStep: 1,
			Orientation: StepVertical,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "flex-col")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Details")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="step"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "flex-1 flex items-center")
	})

	t.Run("horizontal is default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, StepIndicator(StepIndicatorProps{
			Steps: []string{"A", "B"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "flex-1")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "space-y-4")
	})
}

func TestDefaultLoadingOverlayProps(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := DefaultLoadingOverlayProps()
	if props.ShowProgress {
		t.Error("DefaultLoadingOverlayProps ShowProgress should be false")
	}

	if props.Message != "" {
		t.Error("DefaultLoadingOverlayProps Message should be empty")
	}

	output := utils.Render(t, LoadingOverlay(props))
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "fixed")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-busy="true"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `role="dialog"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-modal="true"`)
}
package feedback

// SpinnerSizeIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined SpinnerSize constants.
func SpinnerSizeIsValid(v SpinnerSize) bool {
	_, ok := spinnerSizeLookup[v]

	return ok
}

// ProgressBarSizeIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined ProgressBarSize constants.
func ProgressBarSizeIsValid(v ProgressBarSize) bool {
	_, ok := progressHeightLookup[v]

	return ok
}

// SkeletonVariantIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined SkeletonVariant constants.
func SkeletonVariantIsValid(v SkeletonVariant) bool {
	switch v {
	case SkeletonText, SkeletonTextShort, SkeletonTitle, SkeletonAvatar, SkeletonImage, SkeletonCard, SkeletonTableRow:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// StepIndicatorOrientationIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined StepIndicatorOrientation constants.
func StepIndicatorOrientationIsValid(v StepIndicatorOrientation) bool {
	switch v {
	case StepHorizontal, StepVertical:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// StepStateIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined StepState constants.
func StepStateIsValid(v StepState) bool {
	switch v {
	case StepStateComplete, StepStateCurrent, StepStatePending:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}
package feedback

import "testing"

func TestIsValidEnums(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name string
		fn   func() bool
		want bool
	}{
		{"SpinnerSize SM", func() bool { return SpinnerSizeIsValid(SpinnerSM) }, true},
		{"SpinnerSize invalid", func() bool { return SpinnerSizeIsValid(SpinnerSize("bogus")) }, false},
		{"ProgressBarSize MD", func() bool { return ProgressBarSizeIsValid(ProgressBarSizeMD) }, true},
		{"ProgressBarSize invalid", func() bool { return ProgressBarSizeIsValid(ProgressBarSize("bogus")) }, false},
		{"SkeletonVariant Text", func() bool { return SkeletonVariantIsValid(SkeletonText) }, true},
		{"SkeletonVariant invalid", func() bool { return SkeletonVariantIsValid(SkeletonVariant("bogus")) }, false},
		{"FeedbackType Success", func() bool { return FeedbackTypeIsValid(FeedbackSuccess) }, true},
		{"FeedbackType invalid", func() bool { return FeedbackTypeIsValid(FeedbackType("bogus")) }, false},
		{"StepOrientation Horizontal", func() bool {
			return StepIndicatorOrientationIsValid(StepHorizontal)
		}, true},
		{"StepOrientation invalid", func() bool {
			return StepIndicatorOrientationIsValid(StepIndicatorOrientation("bogus"))
		}, false},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			if got := tt.fn(); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("got %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

package feedback

import (
	"strconv"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// T5.8 (#493): boolean-flag components are usually tested one flag at a
// time, so flag INTERACTIONS go unproven. These tables walk meaningful flag
// combinations and assert the invariant that must hold for EVERY
// combination: rendered in one pass, no panic, and each combination's
// contract markers present (or absent) together.

// TestAlertFlagCombinations walks Dismissible × every feedback type: role
// and (when dismissible) the dismiss affordance + script must co-render for
// each type — a type whose style lookup regresses must not silently drop
// the script or the role.
func TestAlertFlagCombinations(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, tt := range []FeedbackType{
		FeedbackSuccess, FeedbackError, FeedbackWarning, FeedbackInfo,
	} {
		for _, dismissible := range []bool{false, true} {
			t.Run(string(tt)+"/dismissible="+b2s(dismissible), func(t *testing.T) {
				t.Parallel()

				output := utils.Render(t, Alert(AlertProps{
					Message:     "combo",
					Type:        tt,
					Dismissible: dismissible,
				}))

				utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="`+feedbackRole(tt)+`"`)

				if dismissible {
					utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-dismiss="alert"`)
					utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<script")
				} else {
					utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-dismiss")
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

// TestToastFlagCombinations walks Duration × Title: the auto-dismiss timer
// script renders only for duration > 0 and the title markup only when set —
// no combination may leak the other's markup.
func TestToastFlagCombinations(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, duration := range []int{0, ToastDurationMedium} {
		for _, withTitle := range []bool{false, true} {
			name := "duration=" + strconv.Itoa(duration) + "/title=" + b2s(withTitle)
			t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
				t.Parallel()

				props := ToastProps{
					Message:  "combo",
					Duration: duration,
				}
				if withTitle {
					props.Title = "Head"
				}

				output := utils.Render(t, Toast(props))
				utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)

				if duration > 0 {
					utils.AssertContains(t, output, "setTimeout")
				}

				if withTitle {
					utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Head")
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

func b2s(b bool) string {
	if b {
		return "t"
	}

	return "f"
}

func assertStyleFunc4(
	t *testing.T,
	funcName, border, bg, text, icon, wantBorder, wantIconColor string,
) {
	t.Helper()

	if border == "" || bg == "" || text == "" || icon == "" {
		t.Errorf(
			"%s returned empty value: border=%q bg=%q text=%q icon=%q",
			funcName,
			border,
			bg,
			text,
			icon,
		)
	}

	if wantBorder != "" && border != wantBorder {
		t.Errorf("%s border = %q, want %q", funcName, border, wantBorder)
	}

	if wantIconColor != "" && icon != wantIconColor {
		t.Errorf("%s icon = %q, want %q", funcName, icon, wantIconColor)
	}
}

				s.Border,

		})
	}
}

func TestStepState(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		step, current int
		want          StepState
	}{
		{0, 2, StepStateComplete},
		{2, 2, StepStateCurrent},
		{3, 2, StepStatePending},
		{0, 0, StepStateCurrent},
		{0, -1, StepStatePending},
		{4, 9, StepStateComplete},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		if have := stepState(tt.step, tt.current); have != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("stepState(%d, %d) = %q, want %q", tt.step, tt.current, have, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestStepStateIsValid(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, state := range []StepState{StepStateComplete, StepStateCurrent, StepStatePending} {
		if !StepStateIsValid(state) {
			t.Errorf("StepStateIsValid(%q) = false, want true", state)
		}
	}

	if StepStateIsValid(StepState("invalid")) {
		t.Error("StepStateIsValid(\"invalid\") = true, want false")
	}
}
package feedback

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// SpinnerSize defines the size of a loading spinner
type SpinnerSize string

const (
	SpinnerSM SpinnerSize = "sm"
	SpinnerMD SpinnerSize = "md"
	SpinnerLG SpinnerSize = "lg"
)

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for spinner sizes
var spinnerSizeLookup = map[SpinnerSize]string{
	SpinnerSM: "h-4 w-4",
	SpinnerMD: "h-6 w-6",
	SpinnerLG: "h-8 w-8",
}

func spinnerSizeClass(s SpinnerSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(spinnerSizeLookup, s, "h-6 w-6")
}

// SkeletonVariant defines the shape of a skeleton placeholder
type SkeletonVariant string

const (
	SkeletonText      SkeletonVariant = "text"
	SkeletonTextShort SkeletonVariant = "text-short"
	SkeletonTitle     SkeletonVariant = "title"
	SkeletonAvatar    SkeletonVariant = "avatar"
	SkeletonImage     SkeletonVariant = "image"
	SkeletonCard      SkeletonVariant = "card"
	SkeletonTableRow  SkeletonVariant = "table-row"
)

// SpinnerProps configures a loading spinner component
type SpinnerProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Size  SpinnerSize
	Color tone.ColorClass
}

// DefaultSpinnerProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSpinnerProps() SpinnerProps {
	return SpinnerProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		Size: SpinnerMD,
	}
}

// Spinner renders a simple animated loading spinner
//
//	@feedback.Spinner(feedback.SpinnerProps{Size: feedback.SpinnerMD, Color: "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400"})
templ Spinner(props SpinnerProps) {
	<svg
		class={ utils.Class("animate-spin motion-reduce:animate-none", spinnerSizeClass(props.Size), string(props.Color), props.Class) }
		xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
		fill="none"
		viewBox="0 0 24 24"
		if props.AriaLabel == "" {
			aria-hidden="true"
		} else {
			role="img"
		}
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		@svg.SpinnerSVG()
	</svg>
}

// LoadingOverlayProps configures a static loading overlay
// (see LoadingOverlay for the semantics split).
type LoadingOverlayProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Message      string
	ShowProgress bool
	Progress     int
}

// DefaultLoadingOverlayProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultLoadingOverlayProps() LoadingOverlayProps {
	return LoadingOverlayProps{}
}

// LoadingOverlay renders a STATIC loading overlay: a positioned region
// (full-screen by default; scope it to a container with `Class: "absolute"`
// inside a `relative` frame) that announces its loading state politely.
//
// It deliberately carries NO dialog semantics — a div with role="dialog"
// aria-modal="true" promises focus containment and an inert page it never
// delivered. Use the status semantics here when the page behind the overlay
// must stay reachable, and @display.LoadingDialog when you need a real
// blocking modal (native <dialog>: focus trap, inert page, Escape).
//
//	@feedback.LoadingOverlay(feedback.LoadingOverlayProps{Message: "Loading...", ShowProgress: true, Progress: 45})
templ LoadingOverlay(props LoadingOverlayProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 z-50 flex items-center justify-center", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
		aria-busy="true"
	>
		<div
			class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 rounded-lg shadow-xl dark:shadow-black/20 p-8 max-w-sm w-full mx-4"
			role="status"
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, props.Message) }
		>
			<div class="text-center">
				<div class="mx-auto flex items-center justify-center h-12 w-12 rounded-full bg-accent-100 dark:bg-accent-900/30 mb-4">
					@Spinner(SpinnerProps{Size: SpinnerMD, Color: "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400"})
				</div>
				<h3 class="text-lg font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white mb-2">{ props.Message }</h3>
				@LoadingProgress(props.ShowProgress, props.Progress)
			</div>
		</div>
	</div>
}

// LoadingProgress renders the determinate progress bar with its percentage
// caption, or the indeterminate "Please wait..." hint when showProgress is
// false. Shared by LoadingOverlay and display.LoadingDialog so the bar markup,
// the [0, 100] clamp, and the motion-reduce contract live in one place.
templ LoadingProgress(showProgress bool, progress int) {
	if showProgress {
		{{ clamped := max(0, min(100, progress)) }}
		<div class="w-full bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-full h-2 mb-2">
			<div
				class="bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500 h-2 rounded-full transition-all duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0"
				style={ fmt.Sprintf("width: %d%%", clamped) }
			></div>
		</div>
		<p class="text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d%%", clamped) }</p>
	} else {
		<p class="text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">Please wait...</p>
	}
}

// InlineLoading renders a compact inline loading indicator
//
//	@feedback.InlineLoading("Saving...")
templ InlineLoading(message string) {
	<div class="inline-flex items-center gap-2" aria-live="polite">
		@Spinner(SpinnerProps{Size: SpinnerSM, Color: "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400"})
		<span class="text-sm text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400">{ message }</span>
	</div>
}

// Skeleton renders a pulsing placeholder for loading content
//
//	@feedback.Skeleton("text")
templ Skeleton(variant SkeletonVariant) {
	<div aria-busy="true" role="status" aria-label="Loading" class="contents">
		@skeletonBody(variant)
	</div>
}

// skeletonBody renders the visual placeholder without aria annotations, so
// SkeletonGroup can compose many variants under a single role="status"
// announcement instead of N+1 redundant "Loading" reads.
templ skeletonBody(variant SkeletonVariant) {
	switch variant {
		case SkeletonText:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-4 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-3/4"></div>
		case SkeletonTextShort:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-4 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-1/2"></div>
		case SkeletonTitle:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-6 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-1/2"></div>
		case SkeletonAvatar:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-10 w-10 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-full"></div>
		case SkeletonImage:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-48 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-lg w-full"></div>
		case SkeletonCard:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none space-y-4">
				<div class="h-48 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-lg"></div>
				<div class="space-y-3">
					<div class="h-4 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-3/4"></div>
					<div class="h-3 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-1/2"></div>
				</div>
			</div>
		case SkeletonTableRow:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none grid grid-cols-4 gap-4 mb-3">
				for range 4 {
					<div class="h-3 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded"></div>
				}
			</div>
		default:
			<div class="animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none h-4 bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded w-full"></div>
	}
}

// skeletonContainer renders the shared aria shell for skeleton groups:
// a single `role="status"` + `aria-busy="true"` wrapper with pulse animation.
// Both SkeletonGroup and SkeletonCardGrid compose through it to avoid
// duplicating the accessibility annotations.
templ skeletonContainer(layoutClass string, label string) {
	<div class={ layoutClass, "animate-pulse motion-reduce:animate-none" } aria-busy="true" role="status" aria-label={ label }>
		{ children... }
	</div>
}

// SkeletonGroup renders multiple skeleton placeholders under a single
// role="status" announcement to avoid redundant screen-reader reads.
//
//	@feedback.SkeletonGroup([]string{"title", "text", "text", "text"})
templ SkeletonGroup(variants []SkeletonVariant) {
	@skeletonContainer("space-y-3", "Loading content") {
		for _, v := range variants {
			@skeletonBody(v)
		}
	}
}

// SkeletonCardGridProps configures a responsive grid of skeleton cards —
// the common "loading state" for a dashboard card list.
type SkeletonCardGridProps struct {
	// Count is the number of skeleton cards to render. Negative or zero
	// renders a single placeholder so consumers never see an empty container.
	Count int
	// ContainerAware, when true, wraps the grid in a @container div and uses
	// container-query variants (@sm:, @lg:) so the skeleton grid matches the
	// behavior of display.Grid with ContainerAware: true. Useful when
	// the skeleton grid is placed inside a sidebar, card, or other constrained
	// layout. Default false (viewport breakpoints). See ADR-0018.
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultSkeletonCardGridProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultSkeletonCardGridProps() SkeletonCardGridProps {
	return SkeletonCardGridProps{}
}

// skeletonCardGridClassViewport is the viewport-keyed grid class for the
// skeleton card grid (matches GridCols3 in gridColsLookup).
const skeletonCardGridClassViewport = "grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-4"

// skeletonCardGridClassContainer mirrors skeletonCardGridClassViewport with
// @container-keyed breakpoints (matches GridCols3 in gridColsContainerLookup).
const skeletonCardGridClassContainer = "grid grid-cols-1 @sm:grid-cols-2 @lg:grid-cols-3 gap-4"

// SkeletonCardGrid renders a responsive grid of N skeleton cards — the common
// "loading state" for a dashboard card list. It wraps SkeletonGroup so the
// whole grid shares one `role="status"` announcement, and uses the same
// responsive grid classes as display.Grid. Negative or zero counts render a
// single placeholder card so consumers never see an empty container.
//
//	@feedback.SkeletonCardGrid(feedback.SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 6})
//	@feedback.SkeletonCardGrid(feedback.SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 12, ContainerAware: true})
templ SkeletonCardGrid(props SkeletonCardGridProps) {
	{{
		n := props.Count
		if n <= 0 {
			n = 1
		}
		gridClass := skeletonCardGridClassViewport
		if props.ContainerAware {
			gridClass = skeletonCardGridClassContainer
		}
	}}
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@skeletonContainer(gridClass, "Loading cards") {
				for range n {
					@skeletonBody(SkeletonCard)
				}
			}
		</div>
	} else {
		@skeletonContainer(gridClass, "Loading cards") {
			for range n {
				@skeletonBody(SkeletonCard)
			}
		}
	}
}
package feedback

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// ProgressBarSize defines the height of a progress bar
type ProgressBarSize string

const (
	ProgressBarSizeSM ProgressBarSize = "sm"
	ProgressBarSizeMD ProgressBarSize = "md"
	ProgressBarSizeLG ProgressBarSize = "lg"
)

// ProgressBarProps configures a progress bar
type ProgressBarProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Current       int
	Total         int
	Label         string
	Size          ProgressBarSize
	Color         tone.ColorClass
	ShowLabel     bool
	Indeterminate bool
}

// DefaultProgressBarProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultProgressBarProps() ProgressBarProps {
	return ProgressBarProps{
		Size:  ProgressBarSizeMD,
		Color: "bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500",
	}
}

// ProgressBar renders a progress indicator
//
//	@feedback.ProgressBar(feedback.ProgressBarProps{Current: 45, Total: 100, Label: "Uploading"})
templ ProgressBar(props ProgressBarProps) {
	{{
		percent := 0.0
		if props.Total > 0 {
			percent = float64(props.Current) * 100.0 / float64(props.Total)
		}
		percent = max(0, min(100, percent))
		clamped := max(0, props.Current)
		if props.Total > 0 && clamped > props.Total {
			clamped = props.Total
		}
		// The native <progress> element needs a positive max; a zero or
		// negative Total falls back to a 100-part scale so the bar still
		// renders meaningfully.
		progressMax := props.Total
		if progressMax <= 0 {
			progressMax = 100
		}
		progressValue := clamped
		if progressValue > progressMax || props.Total <= 0 {
			progressValue = 0
		}
		// role="progressbar" requires an accessible name (axe aria-progressbar-name).
		// Fall back to the visible label, then a generic name, so the bare
		// progress bar never renders unnamed.
		progressName := props.AriaLabel
		if progressName == "" {
			progressName = props.Label
		}
		if progressName == "" {
			progressName = progressbarFallbackName
		}
	}}
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("w-full", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.ShowLabel || props.Label != "" {
			<div class="flex justify-between text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 mb-1">
				<span>{ props.Label }</span>
				if !props.Indeterminate {
					<span>{ fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%%", percent) }</span>
				}
			</div>
		}
		<div class={ progressTrackClass(props.Size) }>
			if props.Indeterminate {
				<div
					class={ "rounded-full animate-indeterminate-progress motion-reduce:animate-none", progressHeightClass(props.Size), string(props.Color) }
					role="progressbar"
					aria-busy="true"
					aria-label={ progressName }
				></div>
			} else {
				<progress
					class={ utils.Class("tc-progress appearance-none block w-full rounded-full transition-all duration-300 ease-out motion-reduce:transition-none", progressHeightClass(props.Size), string(props.Color)) }
					value={ fmt.Sprintf("%d", progressValue) }
					max={ fmt.Sprintf("%d", progressMax) }
					aria-label={ progressName }
				></progress>
			}
		</div>
	</div>
}

// progressbarFallbackName is the accessible name for progress bars rendered
// without an explicit AriaLabel or visible Label — role="progressbar" must
// never render unnamed (axe aria-progressbar-name).
const progressbarFallbackName = "Progress"

func progressTrackClass(size ProgressBarSize) string {
	return "w-full bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700 rounded-full " + progressHeightClass(size)
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for progress bar heights
var progressHeightLookup = map[ProgressBarSize]string{
	ProgressBarSizeSM: "h-1.5",
	ProgressBarSizeMD: "h-2.5",
	ProgressBarSizeLG: "h-4",
}

func progressHeightClass(size ProgressBarSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(progressHeightLookup, size, "h-2.5")
}

func TestAlertRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("error alert", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := AlertProps{
			Title:   "Error",
			Message: "Something failed",
			Type:    FeedbackError,
		}
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Error")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Something failed")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-red-50")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="alert"`)
	})

	t.Run("dismissible alert", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := AlertProps{
			Title:       "Warning",
			Type:        FeedbackWarning,
			Dismissible: true,
		}
		output := utils.Render(t, Alert(props))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Dismiss"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-dismiss="alert"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `onclick=`)
	})
}

func TestSkeletonCardGridRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders N cards in a responsive grid", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SkeletonCardGrid(SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 6}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "grid")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "sm:grid-cols-2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "lg:grid-cols-3")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-busy="true"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="status"`)
		// Each SkeletonCard body emits a `h-48` image placeholder; 6 cards → 6 occurrences.
		if got := strings.Count(output, "h-48"); got != 6 {
			t.Errorf("expected 6 skeleton cards (h-48), got %d", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("non-positive count renders a single placeholder", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		for _, n := range []int{0, -1, -10} {
			output := utils.Render(t, SkeletonCardGrid(SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: n}))
			if got := strings.Count(output, "h-48"); got != 1 {
				t.Errorf("count=%d: expected 1 fallback card, got %d", n, got)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("preserves motion-reduce variant", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SkeletonCardGrid(SkeletonCardGridProps{Count: 3}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "motion-reduce:animate-none")
	})
}

func TestDefaultPropsConstructors(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("DefaultAlertProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultAlertProps()
		if props.Type != FeedbackInfo {
			t.Errorf("DefaultAlertProps().Type = %q, want %q", props.Type, FeedbackInfo)
		}
	})
	t.Run("DefaultToastProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultToastProps()
		if props.Type != FeedbackInfo {
			t.Errorf("DefaultToastProps().Type = %q, want %q", props.Type, FeedbackInfo)
		}
	})
	t.Run("DefaultStepIndicatorProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultStepIndicatorProps()
		if props.Steps != nil {
			t.Error("DefaultStepIndicatorProps().Steps should be nil")
		}
	})
	t.Run("DefaultLoadingOverlayProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultLoadingOverlayProps()
		if props.Message != "" {
			t.Errorf("DefaultLoadingOverlayProps().Message = %q, want empty", props.Message)
		}

		if props.ShowProgress {
			t.Error("DefaultLoadingOverlayProps().ShowProgress = true, want false")
		}
	})
	t.Run("DefaultProgressBarProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := DefaultProgressBarProps()
		if props.Current != 0 || props.Total != 0 {
			t.Errorf(
				"DefaultProgressBarProps() = {Current: %d, Total: %d}, want zeros",
				props.Current,
				props.Total,
			)
		}
	})
}

	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-4")

func TestCircularProgressRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders SVG with viewBox and rotation", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<svg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "-rotate-90")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "fill=\"none\"")
	})

	t.Run("track and progress circles", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 60}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "<circle", "<circle")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `cx="50"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `cy="50"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `stroke="currentColor"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "stroke-linecap=\"round\"")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "stroke-dasharray=")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "stroke-dashoffset=")
	})

	t.Run("size variants produce dimension classes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		t.Run("sm", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50, Size: CircularProgressSizeSM}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "w-8")
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-8")
		})
		t.Run("md", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50, Size: CircularProgressSizeMD}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "w-12")
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-12")
		})
		t.Run("lg", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()
			output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50, Size: CircularProgressSizeLG}))
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "w-16")
			utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-16")
		})
	})

	t.Run("label span when ShowLabel true", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 42, ShowLabel: true}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<span")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "42%")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "absolute inset-0")
	})

	t.Run("no label span when ShowLabel false", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 42, ShowLabel: false}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "absolute inset-0")
	})

	t.Run("default colors applied", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-accent-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:text-accent-500")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-gray-200")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:text-gray-700")
	})

	t.Run("custom color overrides default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{
			Value:      50,
			Color:      "text-emerald-600",
			TrackColor: "text-emerald-100",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-emerald-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-emerald-100")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "text-accent-600")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "text-gray-200")
	})

	t.Run("motion-reduce on transition", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 50}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "transition-all")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "motion-reduce:transition-none")
	})

	t.Run("zero value has full dashoffset", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 0}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-valuenow="0"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="0% complete"`)
	})

	t.Run("full value has zero dashoffset", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, CircularProgress(CircularProgressProps{Value: 100}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-valuenow="100"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="100% complete"`)
	})
}
package feedback

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// StepIndicatorOrientation defines the layout direction of a step indicator
type StepIndicatorOrientation string

const (
	StepHorizontal StepIndicatorOrientation = "horizontal"
	StepVertical   StepIndicatorOrientation = "vertical"
)

// StepState is the lifecycle state of a single step relative to CurrentStep:
// steps before it are Complete, the step at it is Current, later steps are
// Pending.
type StepState string

const (
	StepStateComplete StepState = "complete"
	StepStateCurrent  StepState = "current"
	StepStatePending  StepState = "pending"
)

// stepState derives the StepState of step stepIndex from the current step
// index. Out-of-range CurrentStep values follow the same ordering: every step
// before it is complete, the step at it (if any) is current, the rest pending.
func stepState(stepIndex, currentStep int) StepState {
	if stepIndex < currentStep {
		return StepStateComplete
	}
	if stepIndex == currentStep {
		return StepStateCurrent
	}
	return StepStatePending
}

// StepIndicatorProps configures a step/progress indicator
type StepIndicatorProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Steps       []string
	CurrentStep int
	Orientation StepIndicatorOrientation
}

// DefaultStepIndicatorProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultStepIndicatorProps() StepIndicatorProps {
	return StepIndicatorProps{}
}

// StepIndicator renders a step indicator (horizontal or vertical)
//
//	@feedback.StepIndicator(feedback.StepIndicatorProps{Steps: []string{"Details", "Review", "Confirm"}, CurrentStep: 1})
templ StepIndicator(props StepIndicatorProps) {
	<nav
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Progress") }
		class={ utils.Class("", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Orientation == StepVertical {
			<ol class="flex flex-col space-y-4">
				for i, step := range props.Steps {
					<li class="flex items-start">
						<div class="flex flex-col items-center">
							@stepCircle(i, stepState(i, props.CurrentStep))
							if i < len(props.Steps)-1 {
								<div class={ "w-0.5 h-8", stepLineClass(stepState(i+1, props.CurrentStep)) }></div>
							}
						</div>
						<span class={ "ms-3 text-sm font-medium mt-1", stepLabelClass(stepState(i, props.CurrentStep)) }>{ step }</span>
					</li>
				}
			</ol>
		} else {
			<ol class="flex items-center w-full">
				for i, step := range props.Steps {
					<li class={ "flex-1 flex items-center", templ.KV("", i == len(props.Steps)-1) }>
						if i > 0 {
							<div class={ "flex-1 h-0.5 mx-2", stepLineClass(stepState(i, props.CurrentStep)) }></div>
						}
						<div class="flex flex-col items-center">
							@stepCircle(i, stepState(i, props.CurrentStep))
							<span class={ "mt-2 text-xs font-medium", stepLabelClass(stepState(i, props.CurrentStep)) }>{ step }</span>
						</div>
					</li>
				}
			</ol>
		}
	</nav>
}

// stepCircle renders the numbered circle (or check icon when complete) shared by
// both the vertical and horizontal step layouts.
templ stepCircle(stepIndex int, state StepState) {
	<div
		class={ "w-8 h-8 rounded-full flex items-center justify-center text-sm font-semibold " + utils.TransitionColors, stepCircleClass(state) }
		if state == StepStateCurrent {
			aria-current="step"
		}
	>
		if state == StepStateComplete {
			@icons.Icon(icons.Check, "w-4 h-4")
		} else {
			{ fmt.Sprintf("%d", stepIndex+1) }
		}
	</div>
}

func stepLineClass(state StepState) string {
	if state != StepStatePending {
		return "bg-accent-600 dark:bg-accent-500"
	}
	return "bg-gray-200 dark:bg-gray-700"
}

func stepCircleClass(state StepState) string {
	if state == StepStateComplete {
		return "bg-accent-600 text-white dark:bg-accent-500"
	}
	if state == StepStateCurrent {
		return "bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 border-2 border-accent-600 text-accent-600 dark:border-accent-400 dark:text-accent-400"
	}
	return "bg-gray-100 text-gray-500 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:text-gray-400"
}

func stepLabelClass(state StepState) string {
	if state != StepStatePending {
		return "text-accent-600 dark:text-accent-400"
	}
	return "text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"
}
// Feedback style lookups: shared style sets, icon mapping, and generic enum lookup.
package feedback

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// FeedbackType represents the severity/visual style of a feedback component.
// Shared by Alert and Toast components.
type FeedbackType string

// Feedback severity levels shared by Alert and Toast components.
const (
	FeedbackSuccess FeedbackType = "success"
	FeedbackError   FeedbackType = "error"
	FeedbackWarning FeedbackType = "warning"
	FeedbackInfo    FeedbackType = "info"
)

// feedbackStyleSet holds the CSS classes for a feedback component variant.
type feedbackStyleSet struct {
	Border, BG, Text, Icon string
}

// feedbackStyle derives the style set for t from the canonical tone table
// (utils/tone) — the ADR-0049 collapse: the former feedbackStyleMap was
// the tone table's anchor dialect, and TestToneAdapterEquivalence keeps
// those byte-for-byte expectations as literals, so the derived classes
// still ship exactly the strings feedback has always rendered. Semantic
// severities stay palette classes (ADR-0044 decision 3); only the brand
// axis emits token families.
func feedbackStyle(t FeedbackType) feedbackStyleSet {
	s := tone.For(t.Tone())

	return feedbackStyleSet{
		Border: s.Border.Classes(),
		BG:     s.BGTint.Classes(),
		Text:   s.Text.Classes(),
		Icon:   s.Icon.Classes(),
	}
}

// feedbackIconMap is the single source of truth for feedback icons.
// Uses circle-style icons for clear completion/failure semantics.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table for shared feedback icons
var feedbackIconMap = map[FeedbackType]icons.Name{
	FeedbackSuccess: icons.CheckCircle,
	FeedbackError:   icons.XCircle,
	FeedbackWarning: icons.ExclamationTriangle,
	FeedbackInfo:    icons.Information,
}

// feedbackRole maps the feedback type onto the ARIA role: errors announce
// assertively (role="alert"); every other severity reports politely
// (role="status") so success and info banners are not read as errors by
// screen readers. Mirrors the inlineMessage twins' split (InlineError
// "alert" vs InlineSuccess "status").
func feedbackRole(t FeedbackType) string {
	if t == FeedbackError {
		return "alert"
	}

	return "status"
}

func feedbackIcon(t FeedbackType) icons.Name {
	return utils.Lookup(feedbackIconMap, t, icons.Information)
}

// FeedbackTypeIsValid reports whether the FeedbackType value is one of the
// four defined constants (Success, Error, Warning, Info).
func FeedbackTypeIsValid(t FeedbackType) bool {
	switch t {
	case FeedbackSuccess, FeedbackError, FeedbackWarning, FeedbackInfo:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

package feedback

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// ToastProps configures a toast notification
type ToastProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Message  string
	Title    string
	Type     FeedbackType
	Duration int // milliseconds, 0 for no auto-dismiss
}

// Default toast durations
const (
	ToastDurationShort  = 3000
	ToastDurationMedium = 5000
	ToastDurationLong   = 8000
)

// toastJSStyles generates the JS color map string from the Go style definitions
func toastJSStyles() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("var tcToastColors = {")
	for _, t := range []FeedbackType{FeedbackSuccess, FeedbackError, FeedbackWarning, FeedbackInfo} {
		s := feedbackStyle(t)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "'%s': {border:'%s',bg:'%s',text:'%s',icon:'%s'},", t, s.Border, s.BG, s.Text, s.Icon)
	}
	b.WriteString("};")
	return b.String()
}

func toastJSIconPaths() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("var tcToastIcons = {")
	for _, t := range []FeedbackType{FeedbackSuccess, FeedbackError, FeedbackWarning, FeedbackInfo} {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "'%s':'%s',", t, icons.IconPathJS(feedbackIconMap[t]))
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "dismiss:'%s'", icons.IconPathJS(icons.X))
	b.WriteString("};")
	return b.String()
}

// toastContainerScript builds the tcShowToast bootstrap script. The JS is
// composed from the Go style tables so classes and icon paths cannot drift
// from the server-rendered toast markup; templ would JSON-marshal a raw JS
// literal inside {{ }} expressions, so the tag renders through
// utils.ScriptComponent, which also owns the omit-empty nonce rule (an
// empty nonce renders NO nonce attribute — nonce="" is rejected by
// strict-CSP pages) and the ADR-0047 context-nonce precedence.
func toastContainerScript(nonce string) templ.Component {
	script := fmt.Sprintf(`%s\n%s\nfunction tcShowToast(message, type, title, duration) {\nvar container = document.getElementById('tc-toast-container');\nif (!container) return;\nvar toast = document.createElement('div');\ntcToastSeq = (window.tcToastSeq || 0) + 1;\nvar toastId = 'tcToast-' + Date.now() + '-' + tcToastSeq;\ntoast.id = toastId;\ntoast.setAttribute('popover', 'manual');\nvar typeKey = type || 'info';\nvar style = tcToastColors[typeKey] || tcToastColors.info;\ntoast.className = 'pointer-events-auto max-w-sm w-full rounded-lg border shadow-lg dark:shadow-black/20 px-4 py-3 transform transition-all duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0 translate-x-full ' + style.border + ' ' + style.bg + ' ' + style.text;\nvar inner = document.createElement('div');\ninner.className = 'flex items-start gap-3';\nvar svgEl = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg');\nsvgEl.setAttribute('class', 'h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0 mt-0.5 ' + style.icon);\nsvgEl.setAttribute('fill', 'none');\nsvgEl.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 24 24');\nsvgEl.setAttribute('stroke', 'currentColor');\nsvgEl.innerHTML = (tcToastIcons[typeKey] || tcToastIcons.info);\ninner.appendChild(svgEl);\nvar content = document.createElement('div');\ncontent.className = 'flex-1 min-w-0';\nif (title) {\nvar titleEl = document.createElement('div');\ntitleEl.className = 'text-sm font-semibold';\ntitleEl.textContent = title;\ncontent.appendChild(titleEl);\n}\nvar msgEl = document.createElement('div');\nmsgEl.className = 'text-sm';\nmsgEl.textContent = message;\ncontent.appendChild(msgEl);\ninner.appendChild(content);\nvar btn = document.createElement('button');\nbtn.className = 'flex-shrink-0 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-600 dark:hover:text-gray-200 transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0';\nbtn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Dismiss');\nbtn.setAttribute('popovertarget', toastId);\nbtn.setAttribute('popovertargetaction', 'hide');\ntoast.addEventListener('hide', function() { toast.remove(); });\nbtn.addEventListener('click', function() { this.closest('.pointer-events-auto').remove(); });\nbtn.innerHTML = '<svg class="h-4 w-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor">' + (tcToastIcons.dismiss || '') + '</svg>';\ninner.appendChild(btn);\ntoast.appendChild(inner);\ncontainer.appendChild(toast);\nif (typeof toast.showPopover === 'function') { try { toast.showPopover(); } catch (err) {} }\nrequestAnimationFrame(function() { toast.classList.remove('translate-x-full'); });\nif (duration && duration > 0) {\nsetTimeout(function() {\ntoast.classList.add('translate-x-full');\nsetTimeout(function() { if (typeof toast.hidePopover === 'function') { try { toast.hidePopover(); } catch (err) {} } toast.remove(); }, 300);\n}, duration);\n}\n}`, toastJSStyles(), toastJSIconPaths())
	script = strings.ReplaceAll(script, `\n`, "\n")
	return utils.ScriptComponent(nonce, script, "toast container script")
}

// toastDismissScript attaches the shared [data-dismiss] handling plus the
// per-toast auto-dismiss timer (duration > 0), through
// utils.ScriptComponent for the nonce contract.
func toastDismissScript(nonce, toastID string, duration int) templ.Component {
	js := utils.DismissScript()
	if duration > 0 {
		js += fmt.Sprintf("setTimeout(function(){var t=document.getElementById('%s');if(t)t.remove();},%d);", toastID, duration)
	}
	return utils.ScriptComponent(nonce, js, "toast dismiss script")
}

// DefaultToastProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultToastProps() ToastProps {
	return ToastProps{
		Type:     FeedbackInfo,
		Duration: ToastDurationMedium,
	}
}

// ToastContainer renders the fixed-position container for toasts
// Place this once near the top of your body
//
//	@feedback.ToastContainer()
templ ToastContainer(nonce string) {
	<div id="tc-toast-container" class="fixed bottom-4 inset-e-4 z-50 flex flex-col gap-2 pointer-events-none" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
		<!-- Toasts are injected here -->
	</div>
	@toastContainerScript(nonce)
}

// Toast renders a single toast notification (server-side rendered)
// For HTMX responses, use ToastContainer + the tcShowToast() JS function
//
//	@feedback.Toast(feedback.ToastProps{Message: "Saved!", Type: feedback.FeedbackSuccess})
templ Toast(props ToastProps) {
	{{ toastID := utils.EnsureID("toast", props.ID) }}
	{{ s := feedbackStyle(props.Type) }}
	<div
		id={ toastID }
		class={ utils.Class("max-w-sm w-full rounded-lg border shadow-lg dark:shadow-black/20 px-4 py-3 transform transition-all duration-300 motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0", s.Border, s.BG, props.Class) }
		role="status"
		aria-live="polite"
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="flex items-start gap-3">
			@icons.Icon(feedbackIcon(props.Type), utils.Class("h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0 mt-0.5", s.Icon))
			<div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
				if props.Title != "" {
					<div class={ "text-sm font-semibold", s.Text }>{ props.Title }</div>
				}
				<div class={ "text-sm", s.Text }>{ props.Message }</div>
			</div>
			<button
				data-dismiss="toast"
				class={ "flex-shrink-0 p-1.5 -m-1.5 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-600 dark:hover:text-gray-200 " + utils.TransitionColors }
				aria-label="Dismiss"
			>
				@icons.Icon(icons.X, "h-4 w-4")
			</button>
		</div>
	</div>
	if props.Duration > 0 {
		@toastDismissScript(props.Nonce, toastID, props.Duration)
	} else {
		@toastDismissScript(props.Nonce, toastID, 0)
	}
}

package feedback

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"

// Tone maps FeedbackType onto the canonical semantic axis (utils/tone
// Phase 0, TODO #425). The "error" spelling maps to Danger — the canonical
// spelling this library converges on at v2 (ADR-0022 removes the alias;
// the value rename rides the #431 batch).
func (t FeedbackType) Tone() tone.Tone {
	switch t {
	case FeedbackSuccess:
		return tone.ToneSuccess
	case FeedbackError:
		return tone.ToneDanger
	case FeedbackWarning:
		return tone.ToneWarning
	case FeedbackInfo:
		return tone.ToneInfo
	default:
		return tone.ToneNeutral
	}
}
package feedback

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// TestToneAdapterEquivalence is the flagship Phase-0 proof, carried through
// the ADR-0049 collapse: for every FeedbackType, the canonical tone table
// must reproduce the classes feedback SHIPPED BYTE-FOR-BYTE — border,
// background, text, and icon. The shipped literals below were the
// feedbackStyleMap anchor dialect before styles.go began deriving from
// tone.For; if this test fails, pixels changed. Semantic severities stay
// palette classes (ADR-0044 decision 3) — the accent family swap only ever
// touched brand-axis sites, never these.
func TestToneAdapterEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	wantByType := map[FeedbackType][4]string{
		FeedbackSuccess: {
			"border-green-200 dark:border-green-800",
			"bg-green-50 dark:bg-green-900/20",
			"text-green-800 dark:text-green-200",
			"text-green-600 dark:text-green-400",
		},
		FeedbackError: {
			"border-red-200 dark:border-red-800",
			"bg-red-50 dark:bg-red-900/20",
			"text-red-800 dark:text-red-200",
			"text-red-600 dark:text-red-400",
		},
		FeedbackWarning: {
			"border-amber-200 dark:border-amber-800",
			"bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-900/20",
			"text-amber-800 dark:text-amber-200",
			"text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400",
		},
		FeedbackInfo: {
			"border-blue-200 dark:border-blue-800",
			"bg-blue-50 dark:bg-blue-900/20",
			"text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-200",
			"text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400",
		},
	}

	for ft, want := range wantByType {
		surfaces := tone.For(ft.Tone())

		checks := []struct {
			name    string
			derived string
			shipped string
		}{
			{"Border", surfaces.Border.Classes(), want[0]},
			{"BG", surfaces.BGTint.Classes(), want[1]},
			{"Text", surfaces.Text.Classes(), want[2]},
			{"Icon", surfaces.Icon.Classes(), want[3]},
		}

		for _, c := range checks {
			if c.derived != c.shipped {
				t.Errorf(
					"FeedbackType %s: tone table %s = %q, feedback ships %q",
					ft, c.name, c.derived, c.shipped,
				)
			}
		}
	}

	// The neutral fallback dialect must equal the Neutral tone's surfaces —
	// same byte-for-byte proof for the default.
	neutral := tone.For(tone.ToneNeutral)

	for _, c := range []struct {
		name    string
		derived string
		shipped string
	}{
		{"Border", neutral.Border.Classes(), "border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700"},
		{"BG", neutral.BGTint.Classes(), "bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-800/50"},
		{"Text", neutral.Text.Classes(), "text-gray-800 dark:text-gray-200"},
		{"Icon", neutral.Icon.Classes(), "text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400"},
	} {
		if c.derived != c.shipped {
			t.Errorf(
				"neutral fallback: tone table %s = %q, feedback ships %q",
				c.name, c.derived, c.shipped,
			)
		}
	}
}

// ARIA attribute helpers for form field accessibility.
package forms

import "github.com/a-h/templ"

const (
	ariaDescribedBy = "aria-describedby"
	ariaInvalid     = "aria-invalid"
	ariaTrue        = "true"
	errorIDSuffix   = "-error"
)

// ErrorAttrs returns templ attributes for aria-invalid and aria-describedby
// when an error message or help text is present. Returns nil only when both
// errorMessage and helpTextID are empty. When helpTextID is non-empty it is always
// emitted via aria-describedby (independent of id), so id-less fields with help
// text remain accessible to assistive technology.
func ErrorAttrs(id, errorMessage, helpTextID string) templ.Attributes {
	if errorMessage == "" {
		if helpTextID != "" {
			return templ.Attributes{ariaDescribedBy: helpTextID}
		}

		return nil
	}

	attrs := templ.Attributes{
		ariaInvalid: ariaTrue,
	}

	switch {
	case id != "" && helpTextID != "":
		attrs[ariaDescribedBy] = id + errorIDSuffix + " " + helpTextID
	case id != "":
		attrs[ariaDescribedBy] = id + errorIDSuffix
	case helpTextID != "":
		attrs[ariaDescribedBy] = helpTextID
	}

	return attrs
}
package forms

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// TestInputAutocomplete covers the autocomplete attribute contract: recognized
// tokens reach the DOM, an unset field renders no attribute at all (an empty
// autocomplete="" would tell browsers "no idea", not "unspecified"), and an
// unrecognized token is dropped rather than emitted, because browsers silently
// ignore it and the form would look autofill-ready while never autofilling.
func TestInputAutocomplete(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("valid sign-in tokens render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{
			ID:           "ac-user",
			Name:         "username",
			Type:         InputText,
			Autocomplete: AutocompleteUsername,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocomplete="username"`)

		output = utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{
			ID:           "ac-pass",
			Name:         "password",
			Type:         InputPassword,
			Autocomplete: AutocompleteCurrentPassword,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocomplete="current-password"`)
	})

	t.Run("payment and address tokens render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{
			ID:           "ac-cc",
			Name:         "card",
			Type:         InputText,
			Autocomplete: AutocompleteCardNumber,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocomplete="cc-number"`)

		output = utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{
			ID:           "ac-zip",
			Name:         "postal",
			Type:         InputText,
			Autocomplete: AutocompletePostalCode,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocomplete="postal-code"`)
	})

	t.Run("unset omits the attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{ID: "ac-none", Name: "q", Type: InputText}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "autocomplete=")
	})

	t.Run("unknown token is dropped instead of emitted", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{
			ID:           "ac-bogus",
			Name:         "q",
			Type:         InputText,
			Autocomplete: AutocompleteType("not-a-real-token"),
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "autocomplete=")
	})
}

package forms

const (

	inputLabelEmail     = "Email"
	inputNameUsername   = "username"
	inputLabelUsername  = "Username"
	selectFieldCountry  = "country"
	selectLabelCountry  = "Country"
	selectOptionGermany = "Germany"
	selectOptionRed     = "Red"
	selectOptionBlue    = "Blue"
