// Package forms provides tests for form components like Input, Select, Textarea, and helpers.
package forms

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

const emailErrorSuffix = "email-error"

func TestSanitizeID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		want  string
	}{
		{name: "simple text", input: "This field is required", want: "This-field-is-required"},
		{name: "already clean", input: emailErrorSuffix, want: emailErrorSuffix},
		{name: "special chars", input: "foo@bar.baz!", want: "foo-bar-baz-"},
		{name: "empty", input: "", want: ""},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := SanitizeID(tt.input)
			if got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("SanitizeID(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.input, got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func assertErrorAttrsMatch(t *testing.T, got, want templ.Attributes) {
	t.Helper()

	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("ErrorAttrs returned %d attrs, want %d", len(got), len(want))
	}

	for k, v := range want {
		if got[k] != v {
			t.Errorf("attrs[%q] = %v, want %v", k, got[k], v)
		}
	}
}

func TestErrorAttrs_NoErrorNoHelpText(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := ErrorAttrs("email", "", "")
	if got != nil {
		t.Errorf("ErrorAttrs(%q, %q, %q) = %v, want nil", "email", "", "", got)
	}
}

func TestErrorAttrs_AriaAttrsWithID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := ErrorAttrs("email", "required", "")
	assertErrorAttrsMatch(t, got, templ.Attributes{
		ariaInvalid:     "true",
		ariaDescribedBy: "email-error",
	})
}

func TestErrorAttrs_AriaAttrsWithoutID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := ErrorAttrs("", "required", "")
	if _, ok := got[ariaDescribedBy]; ok {
		t.Error("should not have aria-describedby when id is empty")
	}

	if got[ariaInvalid] != ariaTrue {
		t.Error("should have aria-invalid=true")
	}
}

func TestErrorAttrs_HelpTextIDIncluded(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := ErrorAttrs("email", "required", "email-help")
	assertErrorAttrsMatch(t, got, templ.Attributes{
		ariaInvalid:     "true",
		ariaDescribedBy: "email-error email-help",
	})
}

func TestErrorAttrs_HelpTextOnlyNoError(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := ErrorAttrs("email", "", "email-help")
	if got == nil {
		t.Fatal("ErrorAttrs with helpTextID should not return nil")
	}

	if got[ariaDescribedBy] != "email-help" {
		t.Errorf("aria-describedby = %v, want %q", got[ariaDescribedBy], "email-help")
	}

	if _, ok := got[ariaInvalid]; ok {
		t.Error("should not have aria-invalid when there is no error")
	}
}
// ID sanitization for form field elements.
package forms

import "regexp"

var nonAlphaNum = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9-]`)

// SanitizeID returns a safe HTML ID from arbitrary text.
func SanitizeID(s string) string {
	return nonAlphaNum.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
}

// HelpTextID returns the HTML ID for a help text element, or "" if id is empty.
func HelpTextID(id string) string {
	if id == "" {
		return ""
	}

	return id + "-help"
}
package forms

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// InputType defines HTML input types
type InputType string

const (
	InputText     InputType = "text"
	InputEmail    InputType = "email"
	InputPassword InputType = "password"
	InputNumber   InputType = "number"
	InputTel      InputType = "tel"
	InputURL      InputType = "url"
	InputDate     InputType = "date"
	InputTime     InputType = "time"
	InputDatetime InputType = "datetime-local"
	InputSearch   InputType = "search"
	InputHidden   InputType = "hidden"
)

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level validation set for input types
var validInputTypes = map[InputType]bool{
	InputText: true, InputEmail: true, InputPassword: true,
	InputNumber: true, InputTel: true, InputURL: true,
	InputDate: true, InputTime: true, InputDatetime: true,
	InputSearch: true, InputHidden: true,
}

// inputType returns the HTML input type string. Unknown values fall back
// to "text" — matching the HTML spec behavior where unknown types default
// to text. This aligns with the map+fallback convention used by all other
// enums in the library.
func inputType(t InputType) string {
	if t == "" {
		return string(InputText)
	}
	if !validInputTypes[t] {
		return string(InputText)
	}
	return string(t)
}

// enterKeyHintForType maps InputType to the optimal mobile keyboard Enter
// key label. Returns "" when no hint applies (text, password, hidden, date/time).
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Mobile UX lookup table
var enterKeyHintForType = map[InputType]string{
	InputEmail:  "next",
	InputNumber: "next",
	InputTel:    "next",
	InputURL:    "next",
	InputSearch: "search",
}

// inputModeForType maps InputType to the optimal mobile keyboard layout.
// Returns "" when the native type attribute already provides the correct
// keyboard (text, password, date, time, datetime-local, hidden).
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Mobile UX lookup table
var inputModeForType = map[InputType]string{
	InputEmail:  "email",
	InputNumber: "decimal",
	InputTel:    "tel",
	InputURL:    "url",
	InputSearch: "search",
}

// enterKeyHintValue returns the explicit EnterKeyHint if set and valid,
// otherwise falls back to the auto-derived value from InputType. This
// unifies the EnterKeyHint API: Input uses the same EnterKeyHintType enum
// as Textarea, with auto-derivation as a smart default.
func enterKeyHintValue(props InputProps) string {
	if props.EnterKeyHint != "" && EnterKeyHintTypeIsValid(props.EnterKeyHint) {
		return string(props.EnterKeyHint)
	}
	return utils.Lookup(enterKeyHintForType, props.Type, "")
}

// AutocompleteType is a token from the HTML autofill vocabulary, emitted as
// the autocomplete attribute. Not an arbitrary string: unknown tokens are
// silently ignored by browsers, so a typo looks like a working form that never
// autofills. Only the tokens that matter for the forms this library ships are
// enumerated here — the spec's list is larger (address-level1/2, tel-national,
// transaction-currency, nickname, …); add a constant rather than passing a raw
// string.
//
// Modern Web Guidance: autofill-sign-in-form, autofill-sign-up-form,
// autofill-payment-form, autofill-address-form.
type AutocompleteType string

const (
	AutocompleteOff          AutocompleteType = "off"
	AutocompleteOn           AutocompleteType = "on"
	AutocompleteName         AutocompleteType = "name"
	AutocompleteGivenName    AutocompleteType = "given-name"
	AutocompleteFamilyName   AutocompleteType = "family-name"
	AutocompleteUsername     AutocompleteType = "username"
	AutocompleteEmail        AutocompleteType = "email"
	AutocompleteTel          AutocompleteType = "tel"
	AutocompleteURL          AutocompleteType = "url"
	AutocompleteOrganization AutocompleteType = "organization"

	// Credential fields. NewPassword MUST be used for sign-up and password
	// change forms — reusing CurrentPassword there makes the browser offer the
	// OLD password, and it never offers to save the new one.
	AutocompleteCurrentPassword AutocompleteType = "current-password"
	AutocompleteNewPassword     AutocompleteType = "new-password"
	AutocompleteOneTimeCode     AutocompleteType = "one-time-code"

	// Address fields.
	AutocompleteStreetAddress AutocompleteType = "street-address"
	AutocompleteAddressLine1  AutocompleteType = "address-line1"
	AutocompleteAddressLine2  AutocompleteType = "address-line2"
	AutocompletePostalCode    AutocompleteType = "postal-code"
	AutocompleteCountry       AutocompleteType = "country"
	AutocompleteCountryName   AutocompleteType = "country-name"

	// Payment fields.
	AutocompleteCardName         AutocompleteType = "cc-name"
	AutocompleteCardNumber       AutocompleteType = "cc-number"
	AutocompleteCardExpiry       AutocompleteType = "cc-exp"
	AutocompleteCardSecurityCode AutocompleteType = "cc-csc"
)

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level validation set for autocomplete
var validAutocompletes = map[AutocompleteType]bool{
	AutocompleteOff: true, AutocompleteOn: true, AutocompleteName: true,
	AutocompleteGivenName: true, AutocompleteFamilyName: true, AutocompleteUsername: true,
	AutocompleteEmail: true, AutocompleteTel: true, AutocompleteURL: true,
	AutocompleteOrganization: true, AutocompleteCurrentPassword: true,
	AutocompleteNewPassword: true, AutocompleteOneTimeCode: true,
	AutocompleteStreetAddress: true, AutocompleteAddressLine1: true,
	AutocompleteAddressLine2: true, AutocompletePostalCode: true,
	AutocompleteCountry: true, AutocompleteCountryName: true,
	AutocompleteCardName: true, AutocompleteCardNumber: true,
	AutocompleteCardExpiry: true, AutocompleteCardSecurityCode: true,
}

// AutocompleteTypeIsValid reports whether v is a known autocomplete token.
func AutocompleteTypeIsValid(v AutocompleteType) bool { return validAutocompletes[v] }

// autocompleteValue returns the token to emit, or "" when Autocomplete is unset
// or not a recognized token. Unknown tokens are ignored by browsers anyway, so
// emitting one would look like a working form that silently never autofills.
func autocompleteValue(props InputProps) string {
	if props.Autocomplete == "" || !AutocompleteTypeIsValid(props.Autocomplete) {
		return ""
	}
	return string(props.Autocomplete)
}

// identifierInputTypes lists the input types that hold identifiers or codes
// rather than prose. Text correction (autocorrect, autocapitalize,
// spellcheck) fights the keyboard on these — the OS rewrites "user@exampl…"
// mid-typing and flags a username as misspelled — so all three are turned
// off (Modern Web Guidance: forms §3, "turn off text correction on fields
// that hold identifiers rather than prose"). Plain text and password keep
// the defaults; text inputs opted into an identifier autocomplete token
// (username, one-time-code) join this set at render time.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Mobile UX lookup table
var identifierInputTypes = map[InputType]bool{
	InputEmail:  true,
	InputNumber: true,
	InputTel:    true,
	InputURL:    true,
	InputSearch: true,
}

// identifierAutocompleteTokens are autocomplete tokens that mark even a
// type=text field as an identifier field (so text correction goes off).
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Mobile UX lookup table
var identifierAutocompleteTokens = map[AutocompleteType]bool{
	AutocompleteUsername:    true,
	AutocompleteOneTimeCode: true,
}

// isIdentifierInput reports whether this input should disable text
// correction: an identifier TYPE, or a text input whose autocomplete token
// is an identifier token.
func isIdentifierInput(props InputProps) bool {
	if identifierInputTypes[props.Type] {
		return true
	}
	return props.Type == InputText && identifierAutocompleteTokens[props.Autocomplete]
}

// InputProps configures a text input. EnterKeyHint, when set, overrides the
// auto-derived mobile keyboard hint. Uses the same EnterKeyHintType enum as
// Textarea for a unified API across form components. Autocomplete, when valid,
// is emitted as the autocomplete attribute so password managers and browsers
// can fill the field.
type InputProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Type         InputType
	Name         string
	Value        string
	Placeholder  string
	Label        string
	Required     bool
	Disabled     bool
	ReadOnly     bool
	AutoFocus    bool
	MaxLength    int
	EnterKeyHint EnterKeyHintType
	Autocomplete AutocompleteType
	Error        string
	HelpText     string
	Stacked      bool
}

// DefaultInputProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultInputProps() InputProps {
	return InputProps{
		Type: InputText,
	}
}

// Input renders a labeled text input with optional error and help text
//
//	@forms.Input(forms.InputProps{
//	   Name: "email",
//	   Type: forms.InputEmail,
//	   Label: "Email address",
//	   Required: true,
//	})
templ Input(props InputProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	if props.Type == InputHidden {
		<input
			type="hidden"
			name={ props.Name }
			id={ props.ID }
			value={ props.Value }
			{ props.Attrs... }
		/>
	} else {
		@FormFieldWrapper(FormFieldProps{ID: props.ID, Label: props.Label, Required: props.Required, Error: props.Error, HelpText: props.HelpText, Stacked: props.Stacked}) {
			if props.Type == InputSearch {
				<search class="relative">
					@inputElement(props)
				</search>
			} else {
				<div class="relative">
					@inputElement(props)
				</div>
			}
		}
	}
}

// inputElement renders the visible <input> element with all shared attributes.
// Extracted per ADR 0010 (2 callers, 30+ lines, clear domain name) to eliminate
// the duplication between the <search> and <div> wrapper branches.
templ inputElement(props InputProps) {
	<input
		type={ inputType(props.Type) }
		name={ props.Name }
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		value={ props.Value }
		if props.Placeholder != "" {
			placeholder={ props.Placeholder }
		}
		if eh := enterKeyHintValue(props); eh != "" {
			enterkeyhint={ eh }
		}
		if ac := autocompleteValue(props); ac != "" {
			autocomplete={ ac }
		}
		if im, ok := inputModeForType[props.Type]; ok {
			inputmode={ im }
		}
		if isIdentifierInput(props) {
			autocorrect="off"
			autocapitalize="off"
			spellcheck="false"
		}
		class={ utils.Class(baseInputClass(props.Error != ""), props.Class) }
		if props.Required {
			required
			aria-required="true"
		}
		if props.Disabled {
			disabled
		}
		if props.ReadOnly {
			readonly
		}
		if props.AutoFocus {
			autofocus
		}
		if props.MaxLength > 0 {
			maxlength={ fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.MaxLength) }
		}
		{ ErrorAttrs(props.ID, props.Error, utils.Ternary(props.HelpText != "", HelpTextID(props.ID), ""))... }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	/>
}

// CheckboxProps configures a checkbox input
type CheckboxProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Name     string
	Value    string
	Label    string
	Checked  bool
	Required bool
	Disabled bool
	Error    string
	HelpText string
}

// DefaultCheckboxProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultCheckboxProps() CheckboxProps {
	return CheckboxProps{}
}

// checkboxLabel renders the label and optional help text for a checkbox
templ checkboxLabel(id, label, helpMsg string) {
	<div class="ms-3 text-sm leading-6">
		if label != "" {
			if id != "" {
				<label for={ id } class="font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ label }</label>
			} else {
				<span class="font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ label }</span>
			}
		}
		@helpText(id, helpMsg)
	</div>
}

// Checkbox renders a checkbox with label
//
//	@forms.Checkbox(forms.CheckboxProps{Name: "terms", ID: "terms", Label: "I agree to the terms"})
templ Checkbox(props CheckboxProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	<div class="flex items-start">
		<div class="flex h-6 items-center">
			<input
				if props.ID != "" {
					id={ props.ID }
				}
				name={ props.Name }
				if props.Value != "" {
					value={ props.Value }
				}
				type="checkbox"
				class={ utils.Class("h-4 w-4 rounded border-gray-300 text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400 focus:ring-blue-600 dark:focus:ring-blue-500 dark:border-gray-600 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:checked:bg-blue-600", props.Class) }
				if props.Checked {
					checked
				}
				if props.Required {
					required
					aria-required="true"
				}
				if props.Disabled {
					disabled
				}
				{ ErrorAttrs(props.ID, props.Error, utils.Ternary(props.HelpText != "", HelpTextID(props.ID), ""))... }
				if props.AriaLabel != "" {
					aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
				}
				{ props.Attrs... }
			/>
		</div>
		@checkboxLabel(props.ID, props.Label, props.HelpText)
	</div>
	@FieldError(props.ID, props.Error)
}
// Shared Tailwind class strings for form input elements.
package forms

// baseInputClass returns the shared Tailwind classes for text inputs, selects, and textareas.
func baseInputClass(hasError bool) string {
	base := "block w-full rounded-md border-0 px-3 py-1.5 text-gray-900 dark:text-white shadow-xs ring-1 ring-inset placeholder:text-gray-400 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-inset sm:text-sm sm:leading-6 transition-colors caret-blue-600 dark:caret-blue-400 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:ring-gray-700 dark:placeholder:text-gray-500"
	if hasError {
		return base + " ring-red-300 focus:ring-red-500 dark:ring-red-700 dark:focus:ring-red-500"
	}

	return base + " ring-gray-300 focus:ring-blue-600 dark:focus:ring-blue-500"
}
package forms

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// InputGroupProps configures an input group with optional left/right addons
//
// Use with Input, Select, or Textarea. When using an addon, add padding
// to the input so the content doesn't overlap:
//   - Left addon  → add "ps-10" to input Class
//   - Right addon → add "pe-10" to input Class
//   - Both        → add "ps-10 pe-10"
type InputGroupProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	LeftAddon  templ.Component
	RightAddon templ.Component
}

// DefaultInputGroupProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultInputGroupProps() InputGroupProps {
	return InputGroupProps{}
}

// InputGroupPaddingClass returns the appropriate padding class for an input
// that lives inside an InputGroup with the given addons. Call this from your
// input's Class field to avoid manual padding:
//
//	@forms.InputGroup(forms.InputGroupProps{LeftAddon: icon}) {
//	   @forms.Input(forms.InputProps{Class: forms.InputGroupPaddingClass(true, false)})
//	}
func InputGroupPaddingClass(left, right bool) string {
	switch {
	case left && right:
		return "ps-10 pe-10"
	case left:
		return "ps-10"
	case right:
		return "pe-10"
	default:
		return ""
	}
}

// InputGroup renders a form control with optional left/right addons.
// Addons are absolutely positioned inside the input area.
//
//	@forms.InputGroup(forms.InputGroupProps{
//	   LeftAddon: icons.Icon(icons.Search, "h-5 w-5 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500"),
//	}) {
//	   @forms.Input(forms.InputProps{Class: "ps-10"})
//	}
templ InputGroup(props InputGroupProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("relative flex items-center", props.Class) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.LeftAddon != nil {
			<div class="pointer-events-none absolute inset-y-0 inset-s-0 flex items-center ps-3">
				@props.LeftAddon
			</div>
		}
		<div class="w-full">
			{ children... }
		</div>
		if props.RightAddon != nil {
			<div class="pointer-events-none absolute inset-y-0 inset-e-0 flex items-center pe-3">
				@props.RightAddon
			</div>
		}
	</div>
}
package forms

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// TestInputIdentifierTextCorrection (Modern Web Guidance: forms §3) pins
// the autocorrect/autocapitalize/spellcheck trio on identifier fields:
// identifier TYPES always, identifier AUTOCOMPLETE tokens on text inputs,
// and never on plain prose-capable text inputs.
func TestInputIdentifierTextCorrection(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	identifierTypes := []InputType{InputEmail, InputURL, InputTel, InputSearch, InputNumber}
	for _, typ := range identifierTypes {
		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{Type: typ, Name: "f"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocorrect="off"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `autocapitalize="off"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `spellcheck="false"`)
	}

	for _, token := range []AutocompleteType{AutocompleteUsername, AutocompleteOneTimeCode} {
		output := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{Type: InputText, Name: "f", Autocomplete: token}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `spellcheck="false"`)
	}

	prose := utils.Render(t, Input(InputProps{Type: InputText, Name: "f", Autocomplete: AutocompleteOff}))
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, prose, `autocorrect="off"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, prose, `spellcheck="false"`)
}
package forms

// Label renders a form label with optional required indicator
//
//	@forms.Label("email", "Email address", true)
templ Label(forID, text string, required bool) {
	<label
		if forID != "" {
			for={ forID }
		}
		class="block text-sm font-medium leading-6 text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
	>
		{ text }
		if required {
			<span class="text-red-500 dark:text-red-400 ms-0.5" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
		}
	</label>
}

// helpText renders the shared help text paragraph for form fields
templ helpText(id, text string) {
	if text != "" {
		<p
			if HelpTextID(id) != "" {
				id={ HelpTextID(id) }
			}
			class="mt-1 text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"
		>{ text }</p>
	}
}

// FieldError renders a field-level validation error
//
//	@forms.FieldError("email", "This field is required")
templ FieldError(fieldID, message string) {
	if message != "" {
		<p
			class="mt-2 text-sm text-red-600 dark:text-red-400"
			role="alert"
			if fieldID != "" {
				id={ fieldID + errorIDSuffix }
			}
		>{ message }</p>
	}
}

// FormFieldProps configures the standard form field wrapper structure.
// Used by FormFieldWrapper to DRY up all form control components.
type FormFieldProps struct {
	ID       string
	Label    string
	Required bool
	Error    string
	HelpText string
	// Stacked wraps the field parts in a single <div> so the component is
	// ONE child in flex/grid parents; default renders unwrapped siblings.
	Stacked  bool
}

// FormFieldWrapper renders the standard form field structure:
// optional Label, children (input/select/textarea), optional Error, optional HelpText.
// Use this to DRY up all form control components.
// With Stacked, all parts share one <div> for flex/grid parents (one child);
// the default keeps the parts as unwrapped siblings for free-form parents.
//
//	@forms.FormFieldWrapper(forms.FormFieldProps{ID: "email", Label: "Email", Required: true, Error: "Invalid", HelpText: "Use work email"}) {
//	   <input type="email" name="email" />
//	}
templ FormFieldWrapper(props FormFieldProps) {
	if props.Stacked {
		<div>
			@fieldContents(props) {
				{ children... }
			}
		</div>
	} else {
		@fieldContents(props) {
			{ children... }
		}
	}
}

// fieldContents renders the shared field parts; FormFieldWrapper picks the
// bare-sibling or single-container shape around them.
templ fieldContents(props FormFieldProps) {
	if props.Label != "" {
		@Label(props.ID, props.Label, props.Required)
	}
	{ children... }
	@FieldError(props.ID, props.Error)
	if props.HelpText != "" {
		@helpText(props.ID, props.HelpText)
	}
}

	}

	t.Parallel()

	props := DefaultTextareaProps()
	props.ID = "bio"
	props.Name = "bio"

			t.Errorf("AutoGrow=true should add %s class", want)
		}
	}

func TestSelectStylableEmitsSelectedContent(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	html := utils.Render(t, Select(SelectProps{
		ID:       "country",

		Stylable: true,
		Options: []SelectOption{
			{Value: "de", Label: "Germany"},
		},
	}))
	if !strings.Contains(html, "tc-select") {
		t.Error("Stylable=true should add tc-select class")
	}

	if !strings.Contains(html, "<selectedcontent>") {
		t.Error("Stylable=true should emit <selectedcontent> element")
	}

	if !strings.Contains(html, "<button>") {
		t.Error("Stylable=true should emit <button> wrapper")
	}
}

	}

		t.Error("Stylable=false should not emit <selectedcontent>")
	}
}

// --- FilterDropdown Accessibility ---

func TestFilterDropdownA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("select has correct name attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			Name:     "status",
			Options:  []SelectOption{{Value: "all", Label: "All"}},
			HxGet:    "/api",
			HxTarget: "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `name="status"`)
	})

	t.Run("propagates aria-label from BaseProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			AriaLabel: "Filter by status",
			Name:      "status",
			Options:   []SelectOption{{Value: "all", Label: "All"}},
			HxGet:     "/api",
			HxTarget:  "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Filter by status"`)
	})

	t.Run("label is associated with select when ID is set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			ID:       "status-filter",
			Name:     "status",
			Label:    "Status",
			Options:  []SelectOption{{Value: "all", Label: "All"}},
			HxGet:    "/api",
			HxTarget: "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="status-filter"`)
	})

	t.Run("dark mode classes present on select", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			Name:     "status",
			Options:  []SelectOption{{Value: "all", Label: "All"}},
			HxGet:    "/api",
			HxTarget: "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:bg-gray-800")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:text-white")
	})
}

// --- Rating Accessibility ---

func TestRatingA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("interactive rating has radiogroup role", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "quality",
			Value: 3,
			Max:   5,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="radiogroup"`)
	})

	t.Run("readonly rating has img role", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    4,
			Max:      5,
			ReadOnly: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="img"`)
	})

	t.Run("interactive rating has aria-required when required", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:     "quality",
			Value:    3,
			Max:      5,
			Required: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-required="true"`)
	})

	t.Run("readonly rating does NOT have aria-required even when required", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    3,
			Max:      5,
			ReadOnly: true,
			Required: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `aria-required`)
	})

	t.Run("screen reader text shows value out of max", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    3,
			Max:      5,
			ReadOnly: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "3 out of 5")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "sr-only")
	})

	t.Run("each radio has sr-only label with star text", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "quality",
			Value: 3,
			Max:   5,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "1 star")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "2 stars")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "3 stars")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "4 stars")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "5 stars")
	})

	t.Run("aria-label defaults to Label when set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "quality",
			Value: 3,
			Max:   5,
			Label: "Product Quality",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Product Quality"`)
	})

	t.Run("aria-label defaults to 'Rating' when no label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "quality",
			Value: 3,
			Max:   5,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Rating"`)
	})

	t.Run("aria-label overrides Label when both set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			AriaLabel: "Custom Rating",
			Name:      "quality",
			Value:     3,
			Max:       5,
			Label:     "Product Quality",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Custom Rating"`)
	})

	t.Run("only first radio has required boolean attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			ID:       "rate",
			Name:     "quality",
			Value:    3,
			Max:      5,
			Required: true,
		}))
		// Count only the boolean required attribute on inputs (not aria-required on div)
		requiredAttrCount := strings.Count(output, " required>")
		if requiredAttrCount != 1 {
			t.Errorf("expected 1 required boolean attribute, got %d", requiredAttrCount)
		}
	})
}

// --- Edge Cases: FilterDropdown ---

func TestFilterDropdownEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("preselect does not mutate caller slice", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		opts := []SelectOption{
			{Value: "a", Label: "A"},
			{Value: "b", Label: "B", Selected: true},
		}
		_ = filterDropdownPreselect(opts, "a")
		// Caller's slice must be unchanged
		if !opts[1].Selected {
			t.Error("preselect mutated caller slice: B.Selected should still be true")
		}

		if opts[0].Selected {
			t.Error("preselect mutated caller slice: A.Selected should still be false")
		}
	})

	t.Run("preselect with no matching value clears all selections", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		opts := []SelectOption{
			{Value: "a", Label: "A"},
			{Value: "b", Label: "B", Selected: true},
		}

		result := filterDropdownPreselect(opts, "nonexistent")
		if result[0].Selected {
			t.Error("A should not be selected")
		}

		if result[1].Selected {
			t.Error("B should not be selected after non-matching preselect")
		}
	})

	t.Run("empty value returns same slice identity", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		opts := []SelectOption{
			{Value: "a", Label: "A"},
		}
		result := filterDropdownPreselect(opts, "")
		// When value is empty, the same slice is returned (not a copy)
		if len(result) != len(opts) {
			t.Errorf("expected same length, got result=%d opts=%d", len(result), len(opts))
		}

		if result[0].Selected != opts[0].Selected {
			t.Error("values should match when value is empty")
		}
	})

	t.Run("no options renders empty select", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			Name:     "empty",
			HxGet:    "/api",
			HxTarget: "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<select")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "</select>")
	})

	t.Run("all optional HTMX attrs omitted when empty", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			Name:     "status",
			Options:  []SelectOption{{Value: "all", Label: "All"}},
			HxGet:    "/api",
			HxTarget: "#results",
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-swap")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-include")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-indicator")
	})
}

// --- Edge Cases: Slider ---

func TestSliderEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("negative min and max range", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{
			Name:  "temp",
			Min:   -50,
			Max:   50,
			Value: 0,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `min="-50"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `max="50"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `value="0"`)
	})

	t.Run("decimal step", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{
			Name:  "price",
			Min:   0,
			Max:   10,
			Value: 5.5,
			Step:  0.5,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `step="0.5"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `value="5.5"`)
	})

	t.Run("zero step defaults to 1", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{
			Name:  "x",
			Value: 50,
			Step:  0,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `step="1"`)
	})

	t.Run("no label renders bare input", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{
			Name:  "vol",
			Value: 50,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<label")
	})

	t.Run("custom class propagated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{
			Class: "my-slider",
			Name:  "vol",
			Value: 50,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "my-slider")
	})
}

// --- Edge Cases: Rating ---

func TestRatingEdgeCases(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("value exceeds max clips display", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    10,
			Max:      5,
			ReadOnly: true,
		}))
		// Value > Max: "10 out of 5" in sr-only text, but only 5 stars rendered
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "10 out of 5")
	})

	t.Run("zero value in interactive mode renders no checked", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "score",
			Value: 0,
			Max:   5,
		}))
		// "checked" also appears in CSS class names (peer-checked:),
		// so check for the boolean attribute pattern specifically
		checkedAttrCount := strings.Count(output, `" checked>`)
		if checkedAttrCount != 0 {
			t.Errorf("expected 0 checked boolean attributes, got %d", checkedAttrCount)
		}
	})

	t.Run("negative value in readonly mode", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    -1,
			Max:      5,
			ReadOnly: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "-1 out of 5")
	})

	t.Run("max stars of 1", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:  "binary",
			Value: 1,
			Max:   1,
		}))

		count := substringCount(output, `type="radio"`)
		if count != 1 {
			t.Errorf("expected 1 radio input, got %d", count)
		}
	})

	t.Run("invalid size falls back to MD", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Value:    3,
			Max:      5,
			Size:     RatingSize("invalid"),
			ReadOnly: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "h-5 w-5")
	})

	t.Run("custom class propagated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Class: "my-rating",
			Value: 3,
			Max:   5,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "my-rating")
	})

	t.Run("help text rendered", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
			Name:     "q",
			Value:    3,
			HelpText: "Click a star to rate",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Click a star to rate")
	})
}

// --- Rating Coverage (private helpers) ---

func TestRatingSizeClass(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, tt := range []struct {
		size RatingSize
		want string
	}{
		{RatingSizeSM, "h-4 w-4"},
		{RatingSizeMD, "h-5 w-5"},
		{RatingSizeLG, "h-6 w-6"},
		{RatingSize("invalid"), "h-5 w-5"},
	} {
		got := ratingSizeClass(tt.size)
		if got != tt.want {
			t.Errorf("ratingSizeClass(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.size, got, tt.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestPluralStars(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := pluralStars(1); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("pluralStars(1) = %q, want empty", got)
	}

	if got := pluralStars(2); got != "s" {
		t.Errorf("pluralStars(2) = %q, want %q", got, "s")
	}
}

// --- FilterInput Behavior (BDD-style) ---

func TestFilterInputUserCanSearchAsTheyType(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("user sees a labeled search box with a hint", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterInput(FilterInputProps{
			Name:        "q",
			Label:       "Search users",
			Placeholder: "Type to filter…",
			HelpText:    "Matches name or email",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Search users")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Type to filter…")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Matches name or email")
	})

	t.Run("user's typed query stays visible after server re-render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterInput(FilterInputProps{
			Name:  "q",
			Label: "Search users",
			Value: "ada",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `value="ada"`)
	})

	t.Run("typing pauses long enough fire one request targeting the results region", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterInput(FilterInputProps{
			Name:       "q",
			Label:      "Search users",
			DebounceMS: 300,
			Wire: &wire.Action{
				URL:    "/api/users/search",
				Target: "#user-list",
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-target="#user-list"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-trigger="input changed delay:300ms"`)
	})

	t.Run("without javascript the form still submits natively", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterInput(FilterInputProps{
			Name:   "q",
			Label:  "Search users",
			Action: "/users",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `action="/users"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `method="GET"`)
	})
}

func TestFilterDropdownUserCanFilterUnderEitherTransport(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("selecting an option refreshes the results region without a page load", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, FilterDropdown(FilterDropdownProps{
			Name:  "status",
			Label: "Status",
			Options: []SelectOption{

				Target: "#user-list",

			Options: []SelectOption{
				{Value: "active", Label: "Active"},

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Apply")
	})
}

// --- Form Wire Behavior (BDD-style) ---

func TestFormUserCanSubmitWithoutPageReload(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("the wired form posts to the API and targets the results region", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Form(FormProps{
			Method:    FormPost,
			CSRFToken: "session-token",
			Wire: &wire.Action{
				Method: wire.MethodPost,
				URL:    "/api/save",
				Target: "#save-region",
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-post="/api/save"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-trigger="submit"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `hx-target="#save-region"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `value="session-token"`)
	})

	t.Run("without javascript the form still submits natively to the action", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Form(FormProps{
			Action: "/api/save",
			Method: FormPost,
			Wire: &wire.Action{
				Method: wire.MethodPost,
				URL:    "/api/save",
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `action="/api/save"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `method="POST"`)
	})

	t.Run("an empty wire URL leaves the form as a plain HTML form", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Form(FormProps{
			Action: "/api/save",
			Method: FormPost,
			Wire:   &wire.Action{URL: ""},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-on:")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "hx-post")
	})
}

// Radio and RadioGroup component types and helpers.
package forms

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// RadioProps configures a single radio button input.
type RadioProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	Name     string
	Value    string
	Label    string
	Checked  bool
	Required bool
	Disabled bool
}

// DefaultRadioProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultRadioProps() RadioProps {
	return RadioProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
}

// RadioOption represents a single option in a radio group.
type RadioOption struct {
	Value    string
	Label    string
	Checked  bool
	Disabled bool
}

// RadioGroupProps configures a group of radio buttons.
type RadioGroupProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	Name     string
	Label    string // renders as <legend>
	Options  []RadioOption
	Inline   bool   // horizontal layout
	Error    string // group-level error
	HelpText string
	Required bool
}

// DefaultRadioGroupProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultRadioGroupProps() RadioGroupProps {
	return RadioGroupProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal defaults
}

// radioItemProps builds a RadioProps for an option within a group.
// Auto-generates the ID from the group ID and option value.
func radioItemProps(groupID, name string, opt RadioOption, required bool, ariaAttrs templ.Attributes) RadioProps {
	p := RadioProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // BaseProps.ID set conditionally below
		Name:     name,
		Value:    opt.Value,
		Label:    opt.Label,
		Checked:  opt.Checked,
		Required: required,
		Disabled: opt.Disabled,
	}
	if groupID == "" {
		groupID = name
	}

	p.ID = groupID + "-" + SanitizeID(opt.Value)

	if len(ariaAttrs) > 0 {
		p.Attrs = ariaAttrs
	}

	return p
}
package forms

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// fieldID derives the DOM id used for label/control association: the explicit
// ID, falling back to the field Name. A labeled control without an id can
// never be associated with its label (invalid for="" or no association at
// all) — an axe `label`/`select-name` critical violation and a WCAG 1.3.1 /
// 4.1.2 failure. Name is the natural fallback: it is required for form
// submission anyway, so the derived id stays deterministic across re-renders.
func fieldID(id, name string) string {
	if id != "" {
		return id
	}

	return name
}

// radioInputClass returns the shared Tailwind classes for radio inputs
func radioInputClass() string {
	return "h-4 w-4 border-gray-300 text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400 focus:ring-blue-600 dark:focus:ring-blue-500 dark:border-gray-600 dark:bg-gray-800 dark:checked:bg-blue-600"
}

// Radio renders a single radio button with label
//
//	@forms.Radio(forms.RadioProps{
//	   ID: "plan-pro",
//	   Name: "plan",
//	   Value: "pro",
//	   Label: "Pro Plan",
//	   Checked: true,
//	})
templ Radio(props RadioProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	<div class={ utils.Class("flex items-center", props.Class) }>
		<input
			type="radio"
			name={ props.Name }
			value={ props.Value }
			id={ props.ID }
			class={ radioInputClass() }
			if props.Checked {
				checked
			}
			if props.Required {
				required
			}
			if props.Disabled {
				disabled
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		/>
		if props.Label != "" {
			<label
				for={ props.ID }
				class="ms-3 text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
			>
				{ props.Label }
			</label>
		}
	</div>
}

// RadioGroup renders a fieldset of radio buttons with legend, error, and help text
//
//	@forms.RadioGroup(forms.RadioGroupProps{
//	   Name: "plan",
//	   Label: "Select a plan",
//	   Options: []forms.RadioOption{
//	     {Value: "free", Label: "Free"},
//	     {Value: "pro", Label: "Pro"},
//	   },
//	})
templ RadioGroup(props RadioGroupProps) {
	{{ errorAttrs := ErrorAttrs(props.ID, props.Error, utils.Ternary(props.HelpText != "", HelpTextID(props.ID), "")) }}
	<fieldset
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		if props.Required {
			aria-required="true"
		}
		{ errorAttrs... }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Label != "" {
			<legend class="block text-sm font-medium leading-6 text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
				{ props.Label }
				if props.Required {
					<span class="text-red-500 dark:text-red-400 ms-0.5" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
				}
			</legend>
		}
		<div class={ utils.Ternary(props.Inline, "mt-2 flex space-x-6", "mt-2 space-y-2") }>
			for _, opt := range props.Options {
				@Radio(radioItemProps(props.ID, props.Name, opt, props.Required, errorAttrs))
			}
		</div>
		if props.Error != "" {
			@FieldError(props.ID, props.Error)
		}
		if props.HelpText != "" {
			@helpText(props.ID, props.HelpText)
		}
	</fieldset>
}

import (

	"github.com/a-h/templ"

func TestRadioGroupRequiredPropagatesToInputs(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := RadioGroupProps{
		Name:     "plan",
		Label:    "Select a plan",
		Required: true,
		Options: []RadioOption{
			{Value: "free", Label: "Free"},
			{Value: "pro", Label: "Pro"},
		},
	}

	var buf strings.Builder

	_ = RadioGroup(props).Render(t.Context(), &buf)
	html := buf.String()

	if !strings.Contains(html, "required") {
		t.Error("RadioGroup with Required=true should render 'required' on radio inputs")
	}
}

func TestRadioOptionCheckedPreSelects(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := RadioGroupProps{

			{Value: "free", Label: "Free"},

		},

	var buf strings.Builder

	_ = RadioGroup(props).Render(t.Context(), &buf)
	html := buf.String()

	if !strings.Contains(html, "checked") {
		t.Error("RadioOption with Checked=true should render 'checked' on the input")
	}
}

}

// TestRadioGroupErrorPropagatesAriaToInputs verifies that aria-invalid and
// aria-describedby are propagated to individual radio <input> elements, not
// just the <fieldset>. Screen readers need these attributes on the focusable
// form controls to announce the error state.
func TestRadioGroupErrorPropagatesAriaToInputs(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := RadioGroupProps{
		Name:  "plan",
		Label: "Select a plan",
		ID:    "plan-group",
		Error: "Please select a plan",
		Options: []RadioOption{
			{Value: "free", Label: "Free"},
			{Value: "pro", Label: "Pro"},
		},
	}

	var buf strings.Builder

	_ = RadioGroup(props).Render(t.Context(), &buf)
	html := buf.String()

	// Count aria-invalid occurrences — should be on each input
	ariaInvalidCount := strings.Count(html, `aria-invalid="true"`)
	if ariaInvalidCount < 2 {
		t.Errorf("expected aria-invalid on each radio input (at least 2), got %d", ariaInvalidCount)
	}

	// Each input should also have aria-describedby
	ariaDescribedByCount := strings.Count(html, `aria-describedby`)
	if ariaDescribedByCount < 2 {
		t.Errorf("expected aria-describedby on each radio input (at least 2), got %d", ariaDescribedByCount)
	}
}

// TestRadioGroupHelpTextPropagatesAriaToInputs verifies that aria-describedby
// for help text is also propagated to individual inputs.
func TestRadioGroupHelpTextPropagatesAriaToInputs(t *testing.T) {

package forms

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// RatingSize controls the visual size of rating stars.
type RatingSize string

const (
	RatingSizeSM RatingSize = "sm"
	RatingSizeMD RatingSize = "md" // default
	RatingSizeLG RatingSize = "lg"
)

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level lookup table
var ratingSizeLookup = map[RatingSize]string{
	RatingSizeSM: "h-4 w-4",
	RatingSizeMD: "h-5 w-5",
	RatingSizeLG: "h-6 w-6",
}

// RatingSizeIsValid reports whether v is one of the defined RatingSize constants.
func RatingSizeIsValid(v RatingSize) bool {
	_, ok := ratingSizeLookup[v]
	return ok
}

func ratingSizeClass(s RatingSize) string {
	return utils.Lookup(ratingSizeLookup, s, ratingSizeLookup[RatingSizeMD])
}

// RatingProps configures an interactive star rating component.
// Uses radio inputs under the hood for full keyboard accessibility.
type RatingProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Name     string
	Value    int // current rating (0 = unrated)
	Max      int // maximum stars (default: 5)
	Size     RatingSize
	ReadOnly bool // display-only mode (no inputs)
	Required bool
	Label    string
	HelpText string
}

// DefaultRatingProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultRatingProps() RatingProps {
	return RatingProps{
		Max:  5,
		Size: RatingSizeMD,
	}
}

// Rating renders an accessible star rating using radio inputs.
// Each star is a labeled radio button with keyboard navigation.
// In ReadOnly mode, renders a static display with aria-label.
//
//	@forms.Rating(forms.RatingProps{
//	   Name:  "quality",
//	   Value: 4,
//	   Max:   5,
//	})
templ Rating(props RatingProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	{{
		maxStars := props.Max
		if maxStars <= 0 {
			maxStars = 5
		}
	}}
	<div class={ utils.Class("space-y-1", props.Class) } { props.Attrs... }>
		if props.Label != "" {
			<span class="block text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
				{ props.Label }
				if props.Required {
					<span class="text-red-500 dark:text-red-400 ms-0.5" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
				}
			</span>
		}
		<div
			class={ utils.Ternary(props.ReadOnly, "inline-flex items-center gap-0.5", "inline-flex flex-row-reverse items-center gap-0.5") }
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			role={ utils.Ternary(props.ReadOnly, "img", "radiogroup") }
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, props.Label, "Rating") }
			if props.Required && !props.ReadOnly {
				aria-required="true"
			}
		>
			if props.ReadOnly {
				for i := 1; i <= maxStars; i++ {
					if i <= props.Value {
						@icons.Icon(icons.Star, ratingSizeClass(props.Size)+" text-amber-400 dark:text-amber-400")
					} else {
						@icons.Icon(icons.Star, ratingSizeClass(props.Size)+" text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-600")
					}
				}
				<span class="sr-only">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d out of %d", props.Value, maxStars) }</span>
			} else {
				for i := 1; i <= maxStars; i++ {
					<input
						type="radio"
						name={ props.Name }
						value={ fmt.Sprintf("%d", i) }
						id={ fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d", props.ID, i) }
						class="sr-only peer"
						if i == props.Value {
							checked
						}
						if props.Required && i == 1 {
							required
						}
					/>
					<label
						for={ fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d", props.ID, i) }
						class={ ratingStarLabelClass() }
					>
						<span class="sr-only">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d star%s", i, pluralStars(i)) }</span>
						@icons.Icon(icons.Star, ratingSizeClass(props.Size))
					</label>
				}
			}
		</div>
		if props.HelpText != "" {
			@helpText(props.ID, props.HelpText)
		}
	</div>
}

// ratingStarLabelClass returns the interactive star label classes. Color,
// hover, checked-fill, and focus-ring utilities live on the <label> (a sibling
// of the hidden radio .peer) rather than the nested <svg> so that Tailwind's
// peer-checked combinator (~) resolves: the checked radio fills itself and
// every label after it in DOM order, which flex-row-reverse maps to the
// correct left-to-right ★★★☆☆ visual. The SVG inherits color via
// currentColor. Forward DOM order (1..N) keeps radiogroup arrow-key direction
// increasing in value per the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern.
func ratingStarLabelClass() string {
	return "inline-flex cursor-pointer rounded text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-600 peer-checked:text-amber-400 dark:peer-checked:text-amber-400 hover:text-amber-300 dark:hover:text-amber-300 peer-focus-visible:text-amber-400 dark:peer-focus-visible:text-amber-400 peer-focus-visible:ring-2 peer-focus-visible:ring-amber-400 dark:peer-focus-visible:ring-amber-400 " + utils.TransitionColors
}

func pluralStars(n int) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return ""
	}
	return "s"
}

func TestRatingKeyboardOrder(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, Rating(RatingProps{
		Name:  "quality",
		Value: 3,
		Max:   5,
	}))

	// Forward DOM order: radio value=1 must precede value=2 so radiogroup arrow
	// keys (ArrowDown/ArrowRight) move toward increasing value per WAI-ARIA.
	// The old reversed order (5..1) made arrows decrease the value.
	idx1 := strings.Index(output, `value="1"`)
	idx2 := strings.Index(output, `value="2"`)

	if idx1 < 0 || idx2 < 0 {
		t.Fatalf("expected value=1 and value=2 radios; got indices %d, %d", idx1, idx2)
	}

	if idx1 >= idx2 {
		t.Errorf("expected value=1 before value=2 (forward DOM order); got 1@%d, 2@%d", idx1, idx2)
	}

	// flex-row-reverse maps the forward DOM back to a correct visual so the
	// peer-checked ~ fill still lights the leftmost N stars.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "flex-row-reverse")

	// Fill classes live on the <label> (sibling of the .peer radio), not the
	// nested <svg>, so peer-checked resolves and cumulatively fills the checked
	// star and every lower-value star.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "peer-checked:text-amber-400")
}

//nolint:unparam // substr is always type="radio" but kept for flexibility
func substringCount(s, substr string) int {
	count := 0

	for {
		idx := indexOf(s, substr)
		if idx == -1 {
			break
		}

		count++
		s = s[idx+len(substr):]
	}

	return count
}

func indexOf(s, substr string) int {
	for i := 0; i <= len(s)-len(substr); i++ {
		if s[i:i+len(substr)] == substr {
			return i
		}
	}

	return -1
}
// SegmentedControl component: a single-select segmented button group in two
// zero-JS modes — link mode (server-round-trip filtering, the FilterChips
// sibling with segmented visuals) and radio mode (a native radiogroup that
// submits with its enclosing form, e.g. FilterBar). Extracted from
// dnsblockd's duration/preset button groups and nsfw-classifier's threshold
// presets (2026-10-10 analysis, TODO_LIST #394).
package forms

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SegmentedControlItem is one option.
type SegmentedControlItem struct {
	// Label is the visible text.
	Label string
	// Value is the option's submitted value (radio mode).
	Value string
	// Href, when set on ANY item, switches the whole control to link mode —
	// every item should carry one (a mixed control is a consumer bug;
	// items without an Href render inert links in link mode).
	Href string
}

// SegmentedControlProps configures a segmented single-select group.
type SegmentedControlProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Name is the radio group's field name (radio mode). Ignored in link
	// mode.
	Name string
	// Items render in FORWARD DOM order (first item first) so radiogroup
	// arrow keys move down the value order (the Rating rule).
	Items []SegmentedControlItem
	// ActiveValue marks the selected item: the checked radio (radio mode)
	// or aria-current link (link mode).
	ActiveValue string
}

// DefaultSegmentedControlProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultSegmentedControlProps() SegmentedControlProps {
	return SegmentedControlProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // no non-zero defaults
		Name: "segment",
	}
}

// segmentedControlIsLinkMode reports whether any item carries an Href.
func segmentedControlIsLinkMode(items []SegmentedControlItem) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Href != "" {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}
package forms

import (
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// segmentedControlFallbackLabel names a control whose consumer set neither
// AriaLabel nor a visible heading — a radiogroup must never render unnamed.
const segmentedControlFallbackLabel = "Options"

// segmentedControlItemClass is the shared segment style: the label (radio
// mode) or link (link mode) carries the checked/current styling via
// peer-checked (the label is the radio's sibling — the Rating rule).
const segmentedControlItemClass = "cursor-pointer rounded-sm px-3 py-1 text-sm text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0 hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-700 peer-checked:bg-blue-600 peer-checked:text-white peer-focus-visible:ring-2 peer-focus-visible:ring-blue-500 peer-focus-visible:outline-none dark:peer-checked:bg-blue-500 dark:peer-focus-visible:ring-blue-400"

// segmentedControlLinkActiveClass is the active link's override in link mode.
const segmentedControlLinkActiveClass = "bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700 dark:bg-blue-500 dark:text-white dark:hover:bg-blue-400"

// SegmentedControl renders a single-select segmented group.
//
// Link mode (server-round-trip, zero JS):
//
//	@forms.SegmentedControl(forms.SegmentedControlProps{
//		Items: []forms.SegmentedControlItem{
//			{Label: "Strict", Value: "30", Href: "/settings?threshold=30"},
//			{Label: "Balanced", Value: "50", Href: "/settings?threshold=50"},
//		},
//		ActiveValue: "50",
//	})
//
// Radio mode (submits with the enclosing form — e.g. inside FilterBar):
//
//	@forms.SegmentedControl(forms.SegmentedControlProps{
//		Name: "duration",
//		Items: []forms.SegmentedControlItem{
//			{Label: "15m", Value: "15m"},
//			{Label: "1h", Value: "60m"},
//		},
//		ActiveValue: "15m",
//	})
templ SegmentedControl(props SegmentedControlProps) {
	{{
		label := props.AriaLabel
		if label == "" {
			label = segmentedControlFallbackLabel
		}
		groupID := utils.EnsureID("seg", props.ID)
		linkMode := segmentedControlIsLinkMode(props.Items)
	}}
	<div
		id={ groupID }
		class={ utils.Class("inline-flex items-center gap-0.5 rounded-md border border-gray-300 bg-white p-0.5 dark:border-gray-600 dark:bg-gray-800", props.Class) }
		if linkMode {
			role="group"
		} else {
			role="radiogroup"
		}
		aria-label={ label }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		for i, item := range props.Items {
			if linkMode {
				<a
					href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
					class={ utils.Class(segmentedControlItemClass, utils.Ternary(item.Value == props.ActiveValue, segmentedControlLinkActiveClass, ""), "no-underline") }
					if item.Value == props.ActiveValue {
						aria-current="true"
					}
				>
					{ item.Label }
				</a>
			} else {
				<input
					type="radio"
					name={ props.Name }
					value={ item.Value }
					id={ groupID + "-" + strconv.Itoa(i) }
					if item.Value == props.ActiveValue {
						checked
					}
					class="peer sr-only"
				/>
				<label for={ groupID + "-" + strconv.Itoa(i) } class={ segmentedControlItemClass }>{ item.Label }</label>
			}
		}
	</div>
}
package forms

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/golden"
)

func TestSegmentedControlRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	radioItems := []SegmentedControlItem{
		{Label: "15m", Value: "15m"},
		{Label: "1h", Value: "60m"},
		{Label: "1d", Value: "1440m"},
	}

	linkItems := []SegmentedControlItem{
		{Label: "Strict", Value: "30", Href: "/settings?threshold=30"},
		{Label: "Balanced", Value: "50", Href: "/settings?threshold=50"},
		{Label: "Lenient", Value: "70", Href: "/settings?threshold=70"},
	}

	t.Run("radio mode renders radiogroup with forward order", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Name:        "duration",
			Items:       radioItems,
			ActiveValue: "15m",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="radiogroup"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `type="radio"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `name="duration"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `value="15m"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "peer-checked:bg-blue-600")
		// Forward DOM order: the first radio in the HTML is the first item.
		first := strings.Index(output, `value="15m"`)

		second := strings.Index(output, `value="60m"`)
		if first > second || first < 0 {
			t.Errorf("radios not in forward DOM order (15m at %d, 60m at %d)", first, second)
		}
	})

	t.Run("checked radio matches active value exactly once", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Name:        "duration",
			Items:       radioItems,
			ActiveValue: "60m",
		}))
		if got, want := strings.Count(output, ` checked`), 1; got != want {
			t.Errorf("checked count = %d, want %d", got, want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("link mode renders aria-current links without radios", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Items:       linkItems,
			ActiveValue: "50",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="group"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/settings?threshold=50"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="true"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `type="radio"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<script")
	})

	t.Run("radiogroup fallback label", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Name:  "duration",
			Items: radioItems,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Options"`)
	})

	t.Run("aria label override", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			AriaLabel:   "Threshold presets",
			Name:        "threshold",
			Items:       radioItems,
			ActiveValue: "15m",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Threshold presets"`)
	})

	t.Run("propagates class and attrs", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Class: "mb-2", Attrs: templ.Attributes{"data-x": "1"},
			Name:  "duration",
			Items: radioItems,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "mb-2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-x="1"`)
	})

	t.Run("empty items render empty group", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{Name: "x"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `role="radiogroup"`)
	})

	t.Run("logical properties only (RTL safe)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SegmentedControl(SegmentedControlProps{
			Name:  "duration",
			Items: radioItems,
		}))
		for _, banned := range []string{"rounded-l-", "rounded-r-", " ml-", " mr-", " pl-", " pr-", "border-l-", "border-r-", " translate-x"} {
			if strings.Contains(output, banned) {
				t.Errorf("physical property %q present — use logical utilities", banned)
			}
		}
	})
}

func TestDefaultSegmentedControlProps(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := DefaultSegmentedControlProps()
	if props.Name != "segment" {
		t.Errorf("DefaultSegmentedControlProps().Name = %q, want %q", props.Name, "segment")
	}

	if len(props.Items) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DefaultSegmentedControlProps().Items = %v, want empty slice", props.Items)
	}
}

func TestSegmentedControlIsLinkMode(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		items []SegmentedControlItem
		want  bool
	}{
		{"no items", nil, false},
		{"no hrefs", []SegmentedControlItem{{Label: "A", Value: "a"}}, false},
		{"one href switches", []SegmentedControlItem{{Label: "A", Value: "a", Href: "/x"}}, true},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			if got := segmentedControlIsLinkMode(tt.items); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("segmentedControlIsLinkMode() = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

package forms

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// SelectOption represents a single option in a select.
// If both Disabled and Selected are true, Selected is cleared because a
// disabled option cannot be meaningfully pre-selected by the user.
type SelectOption struct {
	Value    string
	Label    string
	Disabled bool
	Selected bool
}

// SelectGroup represents an <optgroup> with a label and its options.
// When SelectProps.Groups is non-empty, options are rendered as optgroups
// instead of a flat list. Use this for logically grouping options (e.g.
// channels by category, cities by country).
type SelectGroup struct {
	Label   string
	Options []SelectOption
}

// normalizeSelectOptions returns a defensive copy of opts with contradictions
// resolved: Disabled+Selected clears Selected, and only the first Selected option
// is kept (a single-value <select> cannot have multiple pre-selected options —
// browsers resolve the ambiguity inconsistently). The caller's slice is never
// mutated, so reusing the same []SelectOption across renders is safe.
func normalizeSelectOptions(opts []SelectOption) []SelectOption {
	out := make([]SelectOption, len(opts))
	copy(out, opts)
	firstSelected := true
	for i := range out {
		if out[i].Disabled && out[i].Selected {
			out[i].Selected = false
			continue
		}
		if out[i].Selected {
			if !firstSelected {
				out[i].Selected = false
			}
			firstSelected = false
		}
	}
	return out
}

// SelectProps configures a select dropdown.
// Set Groups to render <optgroup> elements; Options is ignored when Groups is non-empty.
type SelectProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Name    string
	Label   string
	Options []SelectOption
	// Groups, when non-empty, renders <optgroup> elements instead of a flat
	// Options list. Each group has its own label. Options is ignored when
	// Groups is set.
	Groups   []SelectGroup
	Required bool
	Disabled bool
	// Stylable, when true, opts into the modern customizable <select> API
	// (appearance: base-select). Emits a <button><selectedcontent> structure
	// inside the select for CSS styling. Non-supporting browsers ignore
	// these elements — progressive enhancement, no breaking changes.
	// Requires the .tc-select CSS from templates/app.css.
	Stylable bool
	Error    string
	HelpText string
	Stacked  bool
}

// DefaultSelectProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSelectProps() SelectProps {
	return SelectProps{}
}

// Select renders a labeled select dropdown
//
//	@forms.Select(forms.SelectProps{
//	   Name: "country",
//	   Label: "Country",
//	   Options: []forms.SelectOption{
//	     {Value: "de", Label: "Germany"},
//	     {Value: "at", Label: "Austria"},
//	   },
//	})
//	// Grouped options (renders <optgroup>):
//	//
//	@forms.Select(forms.SelectProps{
//	   Name: "channel",
//	   Label: "Channel",
//	   Groups: []forms.SelectGroup{
//	     {Label: "Text Channels", Options: []forms.SelectOption{
//	       {Value: "general", Label: "#general"},
//	       {Value: "random", Label: "#random"},
//	     }},
//	     {Label: "Voice Channels", Options: []forms.SelectOption{
//	       {Value: "voice-1", Label: "🔊 Lounge"},
//	     }},
//	   },
//	})
templ Select(props SelectProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	@FormFieldWrapper(FormFieldProps{ID: props.ID, Label: props.Label, Required: props.Required, Error: props.Error, HelpText: props.HelpText, Stacked: props.Stacked}) {
		<select
			name={ props.Name }
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			class={ utils.Class(baseInputClass(props.Error != ""), utils.Ternary(props.Stylable, "tc-select", ""), props.Class) }
			if props.Required {
				required
				aria-required="true"
			}
			if props.Disabled {
				disabled
			}
			{ ErrorAttrs(props.ID, props.Error, utils.Ternary(props.HelpText != "", HelpTextID(props.ID), ""))... }
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			if props.Stylable {
				<button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>
			}
			if len(props.Groups) > 0 {
				for _, grp := range props.Groups {
					{{ opts := normalizeSelectOptions(grp.Options) }}
					<optgroup label={ grp.Label }>
						for _, opt := range opts {
							<option
								value={ opt.Value }
								if opt.Disabled {
									disabled
								}
								if opt.Selected {
									selected
								}
							>
								{ opt.Label }
							</option>
						}
					</optgroup>
				}
			} else {
				{{ options := normalizeSelectOptions(props.Options) }}
				for _, opt := range options {
					<option
						value={ opt.Value }
						if opt.Disabled {
							disabled
						}
						if opt.Selected {
							selected
						}
					>
						{ opt.Label }
					</option>
				}
			}
		</select>
	}
}
package forms

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestSelectGroups(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders optgroups when Groups is set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Select(SelectProps{
			Name: "channel",
			ID:   "ch",
			Groups: []SelectGroup{
				{Label: "Text Channels", Options: []SelectOption{
					{Value: "general", Label: "#general"},
					{Value: "random", Label: "#random"},
				}},
				{Label: "Voice Channels", Options: []SelectOption{
					{Value: "voice-1", Label: "Lounge"},
				}},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `<optgroup label="Text Channels">`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `<optgroup label="Voice Channels">`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `value="general"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `value="voice-1"`)
	})

	t.Run("flat options when Groups is empty", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		html := utils.Render(t, Select(SelectProps{
			Name:    "country",
			ID:      "ctry",
			Options: []SelectOption{{Value: "de", Label: "Germany"}},
		}))
		if strings.Contains(html, "<optgroup") {
			t.Error("flat options should not render optgroup")
		}

		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `value="de"`)
	})

	t.Run("Groups selected option is normalized", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		html := utils.Render(t, Select(SelectProps{
			Name: "x",
			ID:   "x",
			Groups: []SelectGroup{
				{Label: "G1", Options: []SelectOption{
					{Value: "a", Label: "A", Disabled: true, Selected: true},
					{Value: "b", Label: "B", Selected: true},
				}},
			},
		}))
		// Disabled+Selected clears Selected, only the first valid Selected stays
		if strings.Contains(html, `value="a"`) && strings.Contains(html, `value="a" selected`) {
			t.Error("disabled option should not be selected")
		}

		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `value="b" selected`)
	})
}
package forms

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SliderProps configures a range input slider.
type SliderProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Name     string
	Label    string
	Min      float64
	Max      float64
	Value    float64
	Step     float64
	Required bool
	Disabled bool
	HelpText string
	Error    string
	// ShowValue displays the current value next to the label.
	ShowValue bool
}

// DefaultSliderProps returns sensible defaults.
func DefaultSliderProps() SliderProps {
	return SliderProps{
		Min:  0,
		Max:  100,
		Step: 1,
	}
}

// sliderInputClass returns the Tailwind classes for the range input. The
// INPUT box is h-6 so the hit target clears the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum
// (M21/F097 audit caught an 8px target); the visual track stays 8px via the
// engine track pseudo-elements, and the thumb keeps its accent-color
// rendering (Chromium/Firefox both apply accent-color under
// appearance:none — browser-verified by the routes visual goldens).
//
// Track fill (Modern Web Guidance: slider, "style the active track"): a
// styled track loses the native filled portion, so Firefox gets a live
// fill back from ::-moz-range-progress (pure CSS, updates while dragging),
// and WebKit engines get the custom.css progress() gradient on
// ::-webkit-slider-runnable-track (data-tc-slider hook; live values via
// tcSliderSyncJS).
func sliderInputClass() string {
	return "w-full h-6 appearance-none cursor-pointer bg-transparent accent-blue-600 dark:accent-blue-400 " +
		"focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-600 dark:focus-visible:ring-blue-500 " +
		"disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed " +
		"[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:h-2 [&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:rounded-lg " +
		"[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:bg-gray-200 dark:[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:bg-gray-700 " +
		"[&::-moz-range-track]:h-2 [&::-moz-range-track]:rounded-lg " +
		"[&::-moz-range-track]:bg-gray-200 dark:[&::-moz-range-track]:bg-gray-700 " +
		"[&::-moz-range-progress]:h-2 [&::-moz-range-progress]:rounded-lg " +
		"[&::-moz-range-progress]:bg-blue-600 dark:[&::-moz-range-progress]:bg-blue-500"
}

// tcSliderSyncJS keeps the WebKit track fill in step with the thumb while
// dragging: the attr(value)-seeded custom property in custom.css only knows
// the server-rendered value (dragging changes the value PROPERTY, not the
// attribute), so this singleton mirrors the live value via the CSSOM
// (element.style.setProperty — programmatic writes are not blocked by
// strict style-src CSPs, unlike inline style attributes). Document-level
// input listener, one guard per page — the same singleton shape as
// tcCopyAttached/tcGoBackAttached.
const tcSliderSyncJS = "if(!window.tcSliderAttached){window.tcSliderAttached=true;" +
	"document.addEventListener('input',function(e){" +
	"var t=e.target;" +
	"if(t&&t.matches&&t.matches('input[type=\"range\"][data-tc-slider]')){" +
	"t.style.setProperty('--tc-slider-value',t.value);" +
	"}" +
	"});}"

// Slider renders a labeled range input with accessible labeling.
//
//	@forms.Slider(forms.SliderProps{
//	   Name:  "volume",
//	   Label: "Volume",
//	   Min:   0,
//	   Max:   100,
//	   Value: 50,
//	   Step:  5,
//	})
templ Slider(props SliderProps) {
	{{ props.ID = fieldID(props.ID, props.Name) }}
	{{
		step := props.Step
		if step == 0 {
			step = 1
		}
	}}
	// Singleton script renders BEFORE the field: a trailing script would
	// become its parent's last element child, and space-y parents grant the
	// previously-last sibling a fresh margin-block-end (the wire-page +16px
	// golden shift, 2026-11-03). A display:none first child renders no box.
	@utils.ScriptComponent(props.Nonce, tcSliderSyncJS, "slider fill sync")
	<div class={ utils.Class("space-y-1", props.Class) } { props.Attrs... }>
		if props.Label != "" {
			<div class="flex items-center justify-between">
				<label
					if props.ID != "" {
						for={ props.ID }
					}
					class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
				>
					{ props.Label }
					if props.Required {
						<span class="text-red-500 dark:text-red-400 ms-0.5" aria-hidden="true">*</span>
					}
				</label>
				if props.ShowValue {
					<span class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400" data-slider-value>{ fmt.Sprintf("%g", props.Value) }</span>
				}
			</div>
		}
		<input
			type="range"
			name={ props.Name }
			data-tc-slider
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			min={ fmt.Sprintf("%g", props.Min) }
			max={ fmt.Sprintf("%g", props.Max) }
			value={ fmt.Sprintf("%g", props.Value) }
			step={ fmt.Sprintf("%g", step) }
			class={ sliderInputClass() }
			if props.Disabled {
				disabled
			}
			if props.Required {
				required
			}
			if props.AriaLabel != "" {
				aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
			}
			{ ErrorAttrs(props.ID, props.Error, utils.Ternary(props.HelpText != "", HelpTextID(props.ID), ""))... }
			{ props.Attrs... }
		/>
		if props.Error != "" {
			@FieldError(props.ID, props.Error)
		}
		if props.HelpText != "" {
			@helpText(props.ID, props.HelpText)
		}
	</div>
}

// TestSliderTrackFill (Modern Web Guidance: slider, "style the active
// track") pins both halves of the fill: the Firefox pseudo-element classes
// and the WebKit data hook + CSP-safe live-value sync script.
func TestSliderTrackFill(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	output := utils.Render(t, Slider(SliderProps{Name: "vol", Value: 50}))

	t.Run("firefox fill pseudo-element classes", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "[&amp;::-moz-range-progress]:bg-blue-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "dark:[&amp;::-moz-range-progress]:bg-blue-500")
	})

	t.Run("webkit hook attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "data-tc-slider")
	})

	t.Run("live-value sync script present and singleton-guarded", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcSliderAttached")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "--tc-slider-value")
	})
}

func TestRadioGroupInlineRender(t *testing.T) {

		t.Errorf("InputGroupPaddingClass(true,false) = %q, want ps-10", got)
	}

	if got := InputGroupPaddingClass(false, true); got != "pe-10" {
		t.Errorf("InputGroupPaddingClass(false,true) = %q, want pe-10", got)
	}

	if got := InputGroupPaddingClass(true, true); got != "ps-10 pe-10" {
		t.Errorf("InputGroupPaddingClass(true,true) = %q, want ps-10 pe-10", got)
	}

	if got := InputGroupPaddingClass(false, false); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("InputGroupPaddingClass(false,false) = %q, want empty", got)
	}
}
