package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// mobileMenuToggleClass swaps viewport-keyed (sm:hidden) for container-keyed
// (@sm:hidden) when containerAware is true. Both strings are complete Tailwind
// literals so the content scanner picks them up.
func mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "flex items-center @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "flex items-center sm:hidden"
}

// mobileMenuClass swaps the wrapper's hidden/visible breakpoint the same way.
func mobileMenuClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "hidden sm:hidden"
}

// MobileMenuToggle renders the hamburger button for mobile menus.
// menuID uniquely identifies the menu this toggle controls, so multiple Nav
// instances on one page don't collide on a hardcoded ID.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenuToggle(true, "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenuToggle(show bool, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if show {
		<div class={ mobileMenuToggleClass(containerAware) }>
			<button
				type="button"
				class={ "inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md p-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 hover:bg-gray-100 hover:text-gray-500 focus:outline-hidden focus:ring-2 focus:ring-inset focus:ring-blue-500 dark:focus:ring-blue-400 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:text-gray-300 " + utils.TransitionColors }
				aria-controls={ menuID }
				aria-expanded="false"
				data-mobile-menu-toggle={ menuID }
			>
				<span class="sr-only">Open main menu</span>
				@icons.Icon(icons.Menu, "tc-menu-open block h-6 w-6")
				@icons.Icon(icons.X, "tc-menu-close hidden h-6 w-6")
			</button>
		</div>
	}
}

// MobileMenu renders the collapsible mobile navigation menu.
// menuID uniquely identifies this menu; the toggle uses the same ID so the
// aria-controls relationship stays valid even with multiple Navs on a page.
// containerAware swaps the breakpoint from viewport (sm:hidden) to container
// (@sm:hidden); defaults to false (viewport).
//
//	@navigation.MobileMenu(links, "/", "", "abc123", false)
templ MobileMenu(links []NavLinkProps, currentPath string, nonce string, menuID string, containerAware bool) {
	if len(links) > 0 {
		<div class={ mobileMenuClass(containerAware) } id={ menuID } data-mobile-menu-id={ menuID }>
			<div class="space-y-1 pb-3 pt-2 border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800">
				for _, link := range links {
					@MobileNavLink(link, currentPath)
				}
			</div>
		</div>
		<script { utils.ScriptAttrs(nonce)... }>
			if (!window.tcMobileMenuAttached) {
				window.tcMobileMenuAttached = true;
				function tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, open) {
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var openIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-open');
					var closeIcon = nav.querySelector('.tc-menu-close');
					if (!openIcon || !closeIcon) return;
					if (open) {
						menu.classList.remove('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
						var first = menu.querySelector('a[href],button:not([disabled]),input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])');
						if (first) first.focus();
					} else {
						menu.classList.add('hidden');
						openIcon.classList.remove('hidden');
						closeIcon.classList.add('hidden');
						btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
						btn.focus();
					}
				}
				document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
					var btn = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-toggle]');
					if (!btn) return;
					var menuId = btn.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-toggle');
					var nav = btn.closest('nav');
					if (!nav) return;
					var menu = nav.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-id="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!menu) return;
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, menu.classList.contains('hidden'));
				});
				document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
					if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
					var menu = e.target.closest('[data-mobile-menu-id]');
					if (!menu) return;
					if (menu.classList.contains('hidden')) return;
					var menuId = menu.getAttribute('data-mobile-menu-id');
					var btn = document.querySelector('[data-mobile-menu-toggle="' + menuId + '"]');
					if (!btn) return;
					e.preventDefault();
					tcMobileMenuSet(menu, btn, false);
				});
			}
		</script>
	}
}
package navigation

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestMobileMenuKeyboardNavigation(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	links := []NavLinkProps{
		{Text: "Home", Href: "/"},
		{Text: "About", Href: "/about"},
	}
	output := utils.Render(t, MobileMenu(links, "/", "n", "mobile-kbd", false))

	// Escape closes the menu when focus is inside it.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "e.key !== 'Escape'")

	// Opening moves focus to the first focusable menu item.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "first = menu.querySelector")
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "first.focus()")

	// Closing returns focus to the toggle button.
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "btn.focus()")
}

// TestMobileMenuScriptMarkupCoRender pins the script/markup co-rendering
// invariant (#365 decision): the singleton script and the menu markup render
// under the SAME condition (links exist). A script without markup would be
// dead weight; markup without the script is the dead-hamburger trap — a
// toggle whose clicks do nothing (the #402/#403 fleet class). The Nav
// composition gates MobileMenuToggle on the SAME len(links) condition, so
// the composed path can never ship a toggle without its script.
func TestMobileMenuScriptMarkupCoRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	links := []NavLinkProps{{Text: "Home", Href: "/"}}

	t.Run("with links: menu and script co-render", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, MobileMenu(links, "/", "", "mm-x", false))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-mobile-menu-id="mm-x"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "tcMobileMenuAttached")
	})

	t.Run("without links: neither menu nor script renders", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, MobileMenu(nil, "/", "", "mm-y", false))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `data-mobile-menu-id="mm-y"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcMobileMenuAttached")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<script")
	})

	t.Run("Nav with no links renders no dead toggle", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Nav(NavProps{Links: nil, CurrentPath: "/"}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-mobile-menu-toggle")
	})
}
package navigation

import "github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// NavProps configures a navigation bar.
//
// BaseProps.ID pins the nav element's id and derives a distinct mobile-menu
// id from it (<id>-mobile-menu). Left empty, the menu id comes from the nav's
// content instead, which is deterministic: the same page renders identical
// bytes, so ETag/CDN revalidation keeps working.
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the bar collapse to its hamburger menu
// based on its parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the
// viewport. Useful when Nav is placed inside a sidebar, drawer, or other
// constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
type NavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Brand       templ.Component
	Links       []NavLinkProps
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
	// ContainerAware, when true, wraps the nav in a @container div and swaps
	// sm:/lg: breakpoint classes for @sm:/@lg: so the nav responds to its
	// container width, not the viewport. Default false (viewport breakpoints).
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultNavProps() NavProps {
	return NavProps{
		Sticky: true,
	}
}

// navDesktopLinksClass returns the responsive class for the desktop links
// container, swapping viewport-keyed (sm:) for container-keyed (@sm:) when
// the nav is container-aware. Both strings are complete Tailwind literals.
func navDesktopLinksClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:ms-6 @sm:flex @sm:flex-wrap @sm:gap-x-8 @sm:gap-y-2"
	}
	return "hidden sm:ms-6 sm:flex sm:flex-wrap sm:gap-x-8 sm:gap-y-2"
}

// Nav renders a responsive navigation bar
//
//	@navigation.Nav(navigation.NavProps{
//	   Brand: @myLogo(),
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	     {Href: "/about", Text: "About"},
//	   },
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ Nav(props NavProps) {
	{{ menuID := navMobileMenuID(props) }}
	if props.ContainerAware {
		<div class="@container">
			@navInner(props, menuID)
		</div>
	} else {
		@navInner(props, menuID)
	}
}

templ navInner(props NavProps, menuID string) {
	<nav
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Main navigation") }
		class={ utils.Class("z-40 border-b border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900", props.Class),
			templ.KV("sticky top-0", props.Sticky) }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
			<div class="flex min-h-16 items-center justify-between">
				<div class="flex">
					if props.Brand != nil {
						<div class="flex flex-shrink-0 items-center">
							@props.Brand
						</div>
					}
					<div class={ navDesktopLinksClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
						for _, link := range props.Links {
							@NavLink(link, props.CurrentPath)
						}
					</div>
				</div>
				if props.RightItems != nil {
					<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
						@props.RightItems
					</div>
				}
				@MobileMenuToggle(len(props.Links) > 0, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
			</div>
		</div>
		@MobileMenu(props.Links, props.CurrentPath, props.Nonce, menuID, props.ContainerAware)
	</nav>
}

// SimpleNavProps configures a minimal navigation with a text brand
type SimpleNavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	BrandText string
	BrandHref string
	Links     []NavLinkProps
	// RightItems is rendered on the right side of the bar (e.g. a ThemeToggle,
	// a sign-in button, a user menu). Forwarded to Nav.RightItems. Optional.
	RightItems  templ.Component
	CurrentPath string
	Sticky      bool
}

// DefaultSimpleNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSimpleNavProps() SimpleNavProps {
	return SimpleNavProps{ //nolint:exhaustruct // intentionally minimal defaults
		BrandHref: "/",
		Sticky:    true,
	}
}

// SimpleNav renders a minimal navigation with text brand
//
//	@navigation.SimpleNav(navigation.SimpleNavProps{
//	   BrandText: "MyApp",
//	   BrandHref: "/",
//	   Links: []navigation.NavLinkProps{
//	     {Href: "/", Text: "Home"},
//	   },
//	   RightItems: @layout.ThemeToggle("Toggle theme", ""),
//	   CurrentPath: "/",
//	})
templ SimpleNav(props SimpleNavProps) {
	@Nav(NavProps{
		BaseProps:   props.GetBaseProps(),
		Brand:       simpleBrand(props.BrandText, props.BrandHref),
		Links:       props.Links,
		RightItems:  props.RightItems,
		CurrentPath: props.CurrentPath,
		Sticky:      props.Sticky,
	})
}

templ simpleBrand(text, href string) {
	<a href={ templ.SafeURL(href) } class="text-xl font-bold text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400">{ text }</a>
}

// FooterLink is one link in a FooterColumn.
type FooterLink struct {
	Text string
	Href string
}

// FooterColumn is a titled group of links in a multi-column footer.
type FooterColumn struct {
	Title string
	Links []FooterLink
}

// FooterProps configures a footer. When Columns is empty, Footer renders the
// legacy single-row brand+copyright layout (backward compatible). When
// Columns has entries, Footer renders a responsive multi-column grid with an
// optional brand column and a bottom bar.
type FooterProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	BrandText string
	// Columns renders titled link groups in a responsive grid. When non-empty,
	// switches to multi-column layout. The first column is preceded by a brand
	// block showing BrandText (if set). Empty = legacy single-row layout.
	Columns []FooterColumn
	// BottomBar renders below the columns (or below the legacy single-row when
	// Columns is empty). Use it for legal links, copyright, or fine print.
	BottomBar templ.Component
}

// DefaultFooterProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultFooterProps() FooterProps {
	return FooterProps{}
}

// Footer renders a site footer. Two layouts:
//
//  1. Legacy single-row (backward compat) — when Columns is empty. Centered
//     "© Year BrandText. All rights reserved." line.
//  2. Multi-column grid — when Columns is non-empty. Responsive grid of
//     titled link columns (`grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-8`) with an
//     optional brand block and a BottomBar slot for legal/copyright.
//
//	@navigation.Footer(navigation.FooterProps{BrandText: "MyApp"})
//	@navigation.Footer(navigation.FooterProps{
//	   BrandText: "Acme",
//	   Columns: []navigation.FooterColumn{
//	     {Title: "Product", Links: []navigation.FooterLink{{"Features", "/features"}}},
//	     {Title: "Company", Links: []navigation.FooterLink{{"About", "/about"}}},
//	   },
//	   BottomBar: templ.Raw(`<p>© 2026 Acme</p>`),
//	})
templ Footer(props FooterProps) {
	<footer
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-800 bg-white dark:bg-gray-900", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-label="Footer"
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if len(props.Columns) == 0 {
			<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
				<p class="text-center text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
					&copy; { utils.CurrentYear() } { props.BrandText }. All rights reserved.
				</p>
				if props.BottomBar != nil {
					<div class="mt-4 text-center text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
						@props.BottomBar
					</div>
				}
			</div>
		} else {
			<div class="mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-12 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
				<div class="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 gap-8">
					if props.BrandText != "" {
						<div class="col-span-2 md:col-span-1">
							<p class="text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ props.BrandText }</p>
						</div>
					}
					for _, col := range props.Columns {
						<div>
							if col.Title != "" {
								<h3 class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ col.Title }</h3>
							}
							<ul class="mt-4 space-y-3">
								for _, link := range col.Links {
									<li>
										<a
											href={ templ.SafeURL(link.Href) }
											class={ "text-sm text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:text-white " + utils.TransitionColors }
										>
											{ link.Text }
										</a>
									</li>
								}
							</ul>
						</div>
					}
				</div>
				if props.BottomBar != nil {
					<div class="mt-8 border-t border-gray-200 pt-6 dark:border-gray-800">
						<div class="text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
							@props.BottomBar
						</div>
					</div>
				}
			</div>
		}
	</footer>
}
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// navLinkBaseClass is the shared class prefix for active and inactive nav links.
// py-1.5 keeps the link box ≥ 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 target size): pt-1 rendered
// a 20px target (M21/F097 audit).
const navLinkBaseClass = "inline-flex items-center border-b-2 px-2 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors

func navLinkClasses(isActive bool) string {
	if isActive {
		return navLinkBaseClass + " border-blue-500 text-gray-900 dark:text-white"
	}
	return navLinkBaseClass + " border-transparent text-gray-500 hover:border-gray-300 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:border-gray-600 dark:hover:text-gray-200"
}

func mobileNavLinkClass(isActive bool) string {
	base := "block border-s-4 py-2 ps-3 pe-4 text-base font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors
	if isActive {
		return base + " border-blue-500 bg-blue-50 text-blue-700 dark:bg-blue-900/20 dark:text-blue-300"
	}
	return base + " border-transparent text-gray-500 hover:border-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 hover:text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-400 dark:hover:border-gray-600 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 dark:hover:text-gray-200"
}

// IsActive returns true when href matches currentPath exactly. Shared by NavLink
// and SidebarNav so active-state detection stays consistent across the package.
func IsActive(href, currentPath string) bool {
	return href == currentPath
}

// NavLinkProps configures a single navigation link
type NavLinkProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	Href     string
	Text     string
	External bool
	// Wire, when set with a non-empty URL, adds transport wiring to the
	// link: the anchor keeps its href (the no-JS fallback) AND carries the
	// action's dialect attributes (htmx: hx-get + hx-target; Datastar:
	// data-on:click). Use it for nav links that patch a page region instead
	// of navigating; the wire attrs also stay on the active link (clicking
	// re-fetches the region). Consumer Attrs spread after the wire
	// attributes, so a consumer-supplied hx-* overrides the action's.
	// Applies to NavLink, MobileNavLink, and therefore Nav, SimpleNav, and
	// MobileMenu.
	Wire *wire.Action
}

// navLinkWireAttrs renders the NavLink Wire action as anchor attributes.
// nil Wire (or an empty-URL action) renders nothing — the link keeps
// plain-href navigation. The action is CLONED with PreventDefault set
// (copy semantics — components never rewrite consumer specs): NavLink is
// always an <a>, and a Datastar-wired anchor with an href would otherwise
// patch AND navigate, because the runtime auto-preventDefaults only
// form+submit (decoded from the pinned v1.0.3 bundle). htmx ignores the
// flag — its engine intercepts wired clicks itself.
func navLinkWireAttrs(w *wire.Action) templ.Attributes {
	if w == nil {
		return nil
	}

	nav := *w
	nav.PreventDefault = true

	return nav.Attributes()
}

// DefaultNavLinkProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultNavLinkProps() NavLinkProps {
	return NavLinkProps{}
}

// activeSpanOrLink renders a span with aria-current when active, or a link when inactive.
// rel, when non-empty, adds a rel attribute to the <a> (e.g. "canonical", "prev", "next").
templ activeSpanOrLink(isActive bool, href string, text string, activeClass string, inactiveClass string, rel string) {
	if isActive {
		<span aria-current="page" class={ activeClass }>{ text }</span>
	} else {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ inactiveClass }
			if rel != "" {
				rel={ rel }
			}
		>{ text }</a>
	}
}

// navLinkAnchor renders the common anchor element shared by NavLink and
// MobileNavLink. The caller supplies the component-specific base class
// (active/inactive variant); consumer overrides from props.Class are merged
// via utils.Class so conflicting Tailwind utilities resolve correctly.
templ navLinkAnchor(props NavLinkProps, isActive bool, baseClass string) {
	<a
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		href={ templ.SafeURL(props.Href) }
		class={ utils.Class(baseClass, props.Class) }
		if isActive {
			aria-current="page"
		}
		if props.External {
			target="_blank"
			rel="noopener noreferrer"
		}
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ navLinkWireAttrs(props.Wire)... }
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		{ props.Text }
	</a>
}

// NavLink renders a single navigation link with active state styling
//
//	@navigation.NavLink(navigation.NavLinkProps{Href: "/", Text: "Home"}, "/")
templ NavLink(props NavLinkProps, currentPath string) {
	{{ isActive := IsActive(props.Href, currentPath) }}
	@navLinkAnchor(props, isActive, navLinkClasses(isActive))
}

// MobileNavLink renders a mobile-friendly navigation link
//
//	@navigation.MobileNavLink(navigation.NavLinkProps{Href: "/", Text: "Home"}, "/")
templ MobileNavLink(props NavLinkProps, currentPath string) {
	{{ isActive := IsActive(props.Href, currentPath) }}
	@navLinkAnchor(props, isActive, mobileNavLinkClass(isActive))
}

func TestNavLinkClasses(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	active := navLinkClasses(true)
	if active == "" {
		t.Error("navLinkClasses(true) returned empty string")
	}

	inactive := navLinkClasses(false)
	if inactive == "" {
		t.Error("navLinkClasses(false) returned empty string")
	}

	if active == inactive {
		t.Error("navLinkClasses(true) should differ from navLinkClasses(false)")
	}

	if !strings.Contains(active, "border-blue-500") {
		t.Errorf("active link should contain border-blue-500, got %q", active)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(inactive, "border-transparent") {
		t.Errorf("inactive link should contain border-transparent, got %q", inactive)
	}
}

	props := DefaultNavLinkProps()
	if props.Href != "" {
		t.Errorf("DefaultNavLinkProps().Href = %q, want empty", props.Href)
	}

	if props.Text != "" {
		t.Errorf("DefaultNavLinkProps().Text = %q, want empty", props.Text)
	}
}

	t.Parallel()

	props := DefaultBreadcrumbsProps()
	if props.Items != nil {
		t.Error("DefaultBreadcrumbsProps().Items should be nil")
	}
}
package navigation

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/golden"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/wire"
)

// TestNavLinkWire pins the NavLink-level Wire contract (#155): a wired link
// keeps its href (no-JS fallback) and carries the action's dialect
// attributes; nil Wire or an empty URL stays a plain link; the active link
// renders as a span with no wiring at all; the consumer's action is never
// mutated. The field rides NavLinkProps, so Nav, SimpleNav, MobileMenu, and
// MobileNavLink inherit it through the same anchor.
func TestNavLinkWire(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	base := NavLinkProps{Href: "/inbox", Text: "Inbox"}

	t.Run("htmx dialect renders hx attributes alongside href", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		props.Wire = &wire.Action{ //nolint:exhaustruct // URL+Target are the wiring surface
			URL:    "/api/inbox-fragment",
			Target: "#content",
		}

		html := utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html,
			`href="/inbox"`,
			`hx-get="/api/inbox-fragment"`,
			`hx-target="#content"`,
		)
	})

	t.Run("datastar dialect renders click binding alongside href", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		props.Wire = &wire.Action{ //nolint:exhaustruct // URL is the wiring surface
			Transport: wire.TransportDatastar,
			URL:       "/api/inbox-fragment",
		}

		html := utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html,
			`href="/inbox"`,
			`data-on:click__prevent="@get(&#39;/api/inbox-fragment&#39;)"`,
		)
	})

	t.Run("consumer action is cloned, not mutated (PreventDefault set on the copy only)", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		action := &wire.Action{ //nolint:exhaustruct // URL is the wiring surface
			Transport: wire.TransportDatastar,
			URL:       "/api/inbox-fragment",
		}
		props.Wire = action

		_ = utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))

		if action.PreventDefault {
			t.Errorf("Wire action PreventDefault mutated on the consumer's spec — components clone, never rewrite")
		}
	})

	t.Run("nil Wire keeps a plain link", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base

		html := utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `href="/inbox"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, html, "hx-get=")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, html, "data-on:click=")
	})

	t.Run("empty URL Wire is inert", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		props.Wire = &wire.Action{Target: "#content"} //nolint:exhaustruct // empty URL = no wiring

		html := utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))
		utils.AssertContains(t, html, `href="/inbox"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, html, "hx-get=")
	})

	t.Run("active link keeps the anchor with wiring for a region refresh", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		props.Wire = &wire.Action{
			URL:    "/api/inbox-fragment",
			Target: "#content",
		} //nolint:exhaustruct // URL+Target are the wiring surface

		html := utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/inbox"))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html,
			`aria-current="page"`,
			`href="/inbox"`,
			`hx-get="/api/inbox-fragment"`,
		)
	})

	t.Run("MobileNavLink carries the wiring too", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		props.Wire = &wire.Action{
			URL:    "/api/inbox-fragment",
			Target: "#content",
		} //nolint:exhaustruct // URL+Target are the wiring surface

		html := utils.Render(t, MobileNavLink(props, "/"))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, html, `href="/inbox"`, `hx-get="/api/inbox-fragment"`)
	})

	t.Run("consumer action is never mutated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		props := base
		action := &wire.Action{URL: "/api/inbox-fragment"} //nolint:exhaustruct // URL is the wiring surface
		props.Wire = action

		_ = utils.Render(t, NavLink(props, "/"))

		if action.URL != "/api/inbox-fragment" {
			t.Errorf("Wire action URL mutated: %q — components render consumer specs, never rewrite them", action.URL)
		}
	})
}

// TestGoldenSweepNavLinkWire pins the wired NavLink markup for both dialects.
func TestGoldenSweepNavLinkWire(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	golden.AssertSnapshots(t, []golden.Snapshot{
		{Name: "nav_link_wire_htmx", HTML: utils.Render(t, NavLink(NavLinkProps{
			Href: "/inbox",
			Text: "Inbox",
			Wire: &wire.Action{
				URL:    "/api/inbox-fragment",
				Target: "#content",
			}, //nolint:exhaustruct // URL+Target are the wiring surface
		}, "/"))},
		{Name: "nav_link_wire_datastar", HTML: utils.Render(t, NavLink(NavLinkProps{
			Href: "/inbox",
			Text: "Inbox",
			Wire: &wire.Action{
				Transport: wire.TransportDatastar,
				URL:       "/api/inbox-fragment",
			}, //nolint:exhaustruct // URL is the wiring surface
		}, "/"))},
	})
}
package navigation

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"strings"
)

// navMobileMenuID returns the id shared by a Nav's mobile menu and its toggle.
//
// With a caller-supplied BaseProps.ID the menu id is DERIVED from it
// ("<id>-mobile-menu") rather than reusing it: reusing it puts the same id on
// the <nav> element and the menu div, which is invalid HTML and leaves
// getElementById()/aria-controls resolving the wrong element.
//
// Without one the id is derived from the nav's own content, so rendering the
// same page twice produces byte-identical HTML. A random per-render id (what
// utils.EnsureID mints) makes every response body unique, so ETag
// revalidation can never answer 304 and each navigation or htmx poll
// re-downloads a full document. Two Navs with identical links, current path,
// and label in one page share the derived id — give each Nav its own
// BaseProps.ID when that distinction matters.
func navMobileMenuID(p NavProps) string {
	if p.ID != "" {
		return p.ID + "-mobile-menu"
	}

	var seed strings.Builder
	seed.WriteString(p.CurrentPath)
	seed.WriteString("\x00")
	seed.WriteString(p.AriaLabel)

	if p.ContainerAware {
		seed.WriteString("\x01container")
	}

	for _, link := range p.Links {
		seed.WriteString("\x00")
		seed.WriteString(link.Href)
		seed.WriteString("\x00")
		seed.WriteString(link.Text)
	}

	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(seed.String()))

	return "tc-mobile-menu-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:8])
}
package navigation

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/svg"
)

// inactivePageLinkClass is the shared class for a non-current pagination page link.
const inactivePageLinkClass = "relative inline-flex items-center px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900 dark:text-gray-200 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus:z-20 focus:outline-offset-0"

// paginationMobileClass returns the class for the mobile-only pagination row,
// swapping sm: for @sm: when container-aware so the row responds to the
// container's width. Both strings are complete Tailwind literals.
func paginationMobileClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "flex flex-1 justify-between @sm:hidden"
	}
	return "flex flex-1 justify-between sm:hidden"
}

// paginationDesktopClass returns the class for the desktop pagination row,
// swapping sm: for @sm: when container-aware. Both strings are complete literals.
func paginationDesktopClass(containerAware bool) string {
	if containerAware {
		return "hidden @sm:flex @sm:flex-1 @sm:items-center @sm:justify-between"
	}
	return "hidden sm:flex sm:flex-1 sm:items-center sm:justify-between"
}

// PaginationProps configures a pagination component.
//
// Set ContainerAware: true to make the mobile/desktop pagination controls
// respond to the parent container's width (CSS @container) instead of the
// viewport. Useful when Pagination is placed inside a card footer, drawer,
// sidebar, or other constrained layout. See ADR-0018.
type PaginationProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	CurrentPage uint
	TotalPages  uint
	BaseURL     string
	QueryParam  string
	MaxVisible  uint
	// ContainerAware, when true, adds @container to the nav and swaps sm:
	// breakpoint classes for @sm: so mobile/desktop controls respond to the
	// container width, not the viewport. Default false (viewport breakpoints).
	ContainerAware bool
}

// DefaultPaginationProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultPaginationProps() PaginationProps {
	return PaginationProps{
		QueryParam: "page",
		MaxVisible: 5,
	}
}

func (p *PaginationProps) normalize() {
	if p.CurrentPage == 0 {
		p.CurrentPage = 1
	}
	if p.TotalPages >= 1 && p.CurrentPage > p.TotalPages {
		p.CurrentPage = p.TotalPages
	}
	if p.QueryParam == "" {
		p.QueryParam = "page"
	}
	if p.MaxVisible == 0 {
		p.MaxVisible = 5
	}
}

func (p PaginationProps) pageURL(page uint) string {
	u, err := url.Parse(p.BaseURL)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s?%s=%d", p.BaseURL, p.QueryParam, page)
	}
	q := u.Query()
	q.Set(p.QueryParam, strconv.FormatUint(uint64(page), 10))
	u.RawQuery = q.Encode()
	return u.String()
}

func paginationRange(current, total, maxVisible uint) (start, end uint) {
	if maxVisible == 0 {
		maxVisible = 5
	}
	if total <= maxVisible {
		return 1, total
	}
	half := maxVisible / 2
	if current > half {
		start = current - half
		end = current + half
		if maxVisible%2 == 0 {
			end--
		}
	} else {
		start = 1
		end = maxVisible
	}
	if end > total {
		end = total
		start = total - maxVisible + 1
	}
	return start, end
}

// mobilePageButton renders an enabled link or disabled span for mobile pagination
templ mobilePageButton(enabled bool, href string, marginClass string, text string) {
	if enabled {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ "relative inline-flex items-center rounded-md border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-200 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-700", marginClass }
		>
			{ text }
		</a>
	} else {
		<span class={ "relative inline-flex items-center rounded-md border border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 bg-gray-100 dark:bg-gray-900 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 cursor-not-allowed", marginClass }>{ text }</span>
	}
}

// paginationArrowIcon renders the shared icon content for pagination arrows
templ paginationArrowIcon(srText string, svgPath string) {
	<span class="sr-only">{ srText }</span>
	@svg.FillIcon("h-5 w-5", svgPath, false)
}

// paginationArrow renders a previous/next arrow button for desktop pagination.
// roundedClass is the complete border-radius utility (e.g. "rounded-s-md") —
// passed as a literal so Tailwind's content scanner can detect it.
templ paginationArrow(enabled bool, href string, roundedClass string, ariaLabel string, srText string, svgPath string, rel string) {
	if enabled {
		<a
			href={ templ.SafeURL(href) }
			class={ "relative inline-flex items-center px-2 py-2 text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gray-800 focus:z-20 focus:outline-offset-0", roundedClass }
			aria-label={ ariaLabel }
			if rel != "" {
				rel={ rel }
			}
		>
			@paginationArrowIcon(srText, svgPath)
		</a>
	} else {
		<span class={ "relative inline-flex items-center px-2 py-2 text-gray-300 dark:text-gray-600 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600 cursor-not-allowed", roundedClass } aria-disabled="true" tabindex="-1">
			@paginationArrowIcon(srText, svgPath)
		</span>
	}
}

// paginationEllipsis renders a "..." indicator for truncated page ranges
templ paginationEllipsis() {
	<span class="relative inline-flex items-center px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300 ring-1 ring-inset ring-gray-300 dark:ring-gray-600">
		&hellip;
	</span>
}

// paginationPageItem renders a single page number inside a list item.
// rel, when non-empty, adds a rel attribute to the link (e.g. "canonical" for page 1).
templ paginationPageItem(isActive bool, href string, text string, activeClass string, rel string) {
	<li>
		@activeSpanOrLink(isActive, href, text, activeClass, inactivePageLinkClass, rel)
	</li>
}

// paginationEllipsisItem renders an ellipsis indicator inside a list item.
templ paginationEllipsisItem() {
	<li>
		@paginationEllipsis()
	</li>
}

// Pagination renders a page navigation bar
//
//	@navigation.Pagination(navigation.PaginationProps{
//	   CurrentPage: 3,
//	   TotalPages: 10,
//	   BaseURL: "/users",
//	})
templ Pagination(props PaginationProps) {
	{{ props.normalize() }}
	if props.TotalPages > 1 {
		<nav
			if props.ID != "" {
				id={ props.ID }
			}
			aria-label={ utils.Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, "Pagination") }
			class={ utils.Class("flex items-center justify-between", props.Class),
				templ.KV("@container", props.ContainerAware) }
			{ props.Attrs... }
		>
			<div class={ paginationMobileClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
				@mobilePageButton(props.CurrentPage > 1, props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage-1), "", "Previous")
				@mobilePageButton(props.CurrentPage < props.TotalPages, props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage+1), "ms-3", "Next")
			</div>
			<div class={ paginationDesktopClass(props.ContainerAware) }>
				<div>
					<p class="text-sm text-gray-700 dark:text-gray-300">
						Showing page
						<span class="font-medium">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.CurrentPage) }</span>
						of
						<span class="font-medium">{ fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.TotalPages) }</span>
					</p>
				</div>
				<div>
					<ol class="isolate inline-flex -space-x-px rounded-md shadow-xs" aria-label="Pagination">
						<li>
							@paginationArrow(
								props.CurrentPage > 1,
								props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage-1),
								"rounded-s-md",
								"Previous page",
								"Previous",
								svg.PathArrowLeft,
								"prev",
							)
						</li>
						{{ start, end := paginationRange(props.CurrentPage, props.TotalPages, props.MaxVisible) }}
						if start > 1 {
							@paginationPageItem(false, props.pageURL(1), "1", "", "canonical")
							@paginationEllipsisItem()
						}
						for p := start; p <= end; p++ {
							@paginationPageItem(
								p == props.CurrentPage,
								props.pageURL(p),
								fmt.Sprintf("%d", p),
								"relative z-10 inline-flex items-center bg-blue-600 dark:bg-blue-500 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white focus:z-20 focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue-600 dark:focus-visible:outline-blue-500",
								"",
							)
						}
						if end < props.TotalPages {
							@paginationEllipsisItem()
							@paginationPageItem(false, props.pageURL(props.TotalPages), fmt.Sprintf("%d", props.TotalPages), "", "")
						}
						<li>
							@paginationArrow(
								props.CurrentPage < props.TotalPages,
								props.pageURL(props.CurrentPage+1),
								"rounded-e-md",
								"Next page",
								"Next",
								svg.PathArrowRight,
								"next",
							)
						</li>
					</ol>
				</div>
			</div>
		</nav>
	}
}
// Package navigation provides tests for navigation components.
package navigation

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestPaginationRange(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		current    uint
		total      uint
		maxVisible uint
		wantStart  uint
		wantEnd    uint
	}{
		{"small total", 2, 3, 5, 1, 3},
		{"current in middle", 5, 10, 5, 3, 7},
		{"current near start", 2, 10, 5, 1, 5},
		{"current near end", 9, 10, 5, 6, 10},
		{"current beyond total self-corrects to last window", 15, 10, 5, 6, 10},
		{"default max visible", 5, 20, 0, 3, 7},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			start, end := paginationRange(tt.current, tt.total, tt.maxVisible)
			if start != tt.wantStart || end != tt.wantEnd {
				t.Errorf("paginationRange(%d, %d, %d) = (%d, %d), want (%d, %d)",
					tt.current, tt.total, tt.maxVisible, start, end, tt.wantStart, tt.wantEnd)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestPaginationRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	t.Run("renders page numbers", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			CurrentPage: 2,
			TotalPages:  5,
			BaseURL:     "/items",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/items?page=1"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/items?page=3"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="page"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "2")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Previous")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Next")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Showing page")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "of")
	})

	t.Run("first page disables previous", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := renderPagination(t, 1, 3, "/users")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-disabled="true"`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `href="/users?page=0"`)
	})

	t.Run("last page disables next", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := renderPagination(t, 3, 3, "/users")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `href="/users?page=4"`)
	})

	t.Run("hidden when single page", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		assertEmptyPaginationOutput(t, 1, 1, "/users")
	})

	t.Run("custom query param", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			CurrentPage: 2,
			TotalPages:  3,
			BaseURL:     "/search?q=test",
			QueryParam:  "p",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/search?p=1&amp;q=test"`)
	})

	t.Run("zero CurrentPage clamped to 1", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			CurrentPage: 0,
			TotalPages:  3,
			BaseURL:     "/items",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="page"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "1")
	})

	t.Run("CurrentPage beyond TotalPages clamps to last page", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			CurrentPage: 15,
			TotalPages:  10,
			BaseURL:     "/items",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="page"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, ">10<")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "page=15")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "page=14")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, ">15<")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "page=11")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "page=10")
	})

	t.Run("zero TotalPages renders nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		assertEmptyPaginationOutput(t, 1, 0, "/items")
	})

	t.Run("custom ID propagated", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			ID:          "my-pager",
			CurrentPage: 2,
			TotalPages:  3,
			BaseURL:     "/items",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-pager"`)
	})

	t.Run("rel=canonical on first page when ellipsis shown", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
			CurrentPage: 5,
			TotalPages:  20,
			BaseURL:     "/items",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `rel="canonical"`)
	})
}

func renderPagination(t *testing.T, currentPage, totalPages uint, baseURL string) string {
	t.Helper()

	return utils.Render(t, Pagination(PaginationProps{
		CurrentPage: currentPage,
		TotalPages:  totalPages,
		BaseURL:     baseURL,
	}))
}

func assertEmptyPaginationOutput(t *testing.T, currentPage, totalPages uint, baseURL string) {
	t.Helper()

	output := renderPagination(t, currentPage, totalPages, baseURL)
	if output != "" {
		t.Errorf("expected empty output, got: %s", output)
	}
}

// TestMobileMenuNoDoublePrefix verifies the mobile-menu ID does not get
// the "tc-mobile-menu-" prefix applied twice. EnsureID already produces
// "tc-mobile-menu-<hex>", so the template must not prepend it again.
func TestMobileMenuNoDoublePrefix(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, MobileMenu(testNavLinks, "/", "nonce", "my-menu-id", false))
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="my-menu-id"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tc-mobile-menu-tc-mobile-menu-")
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tc-mobile-menu-my-menu-id")
}

// the menu ID without a double prefix.
func TestMobileMenuToggleNoDoublePrefix(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, MobileMenuToggle(true, "my-menu-id", false))
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-controls="my-menu-id"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tc-mobile-menu-my-menu-id")
}

// TestBreadcrumbsCurrentPathAutoDetect verifies that setting CurrentPath
// auto-highlights the matching crumb without needing Active=true.
func TestBreadcrumbsCurrentPathAutoDetect(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, Breadcrumbs(BreadcrumbsProps{
		Items: []BreadcrumbItem{
			{Text: "Home", Href: "/"},
			{Text: "Users", Href: "/users"},
			{Text: "Edit", Href: "/users/1/edit"},
		},
		CurrentPath: "/users/1/edit",
	}))
	// The active crumb should render as a <span> (no <a> tag)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, "text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400")
	// Non-active crumbs should still have links
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/users"`)
	// The active crumb should NOT have an href
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `href="/users/1/edit"`)
}

// TestBreadcrumbsCurrentPathNoMatch verifies that when CurrentPath doesn't
// match any crumb, none are auto-highlighted (except terminal empty-Href crumb).
func TestBreadcrumbsCurrentPathNoMatch(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, Breadcrumbs(BreadcrumbsProps{
		Items: []BreadcrumbItem{
			{Text: "Home", Href: "/"},
			{Text: "Settings", Href: "/settings"},
		},
		CurrentPath: "/completely/different",
	}))
	// Both should be links since neither matches and neither has Active=true
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/settings"`)
}

// TestBreadcrumbsExplicitActiveOverridesCurrentPath verifies that Active=true
// takes priority — an item can be active even when CurrentPath matches a different crumb.
func TestBreadcrumbsExplicitActiveOverridesCurrentPath(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, Breadcrumbs(BreadcrumbsProps{
		Items: []BreadcrumbItem{
			{Text: "Home", Href: "/", Active: true},
			{Text: "Users", Href: "/users"},
		},
		CurrentPath: "/users",
	}))
	// Both should be active: Home via explicit flag, Users via CurrentPath match
	// Neither should render as a link
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `href="/"`)
	utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `href="/users"`)
}
package navigation

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SidebarNavItem is one link in a vertical sidebar navigation.
type SidebarNavItem struct {
	Label  string
	Href   string
	Icon   icons.Name // optional; renders before the label if set
	Active bool
	// Section groups this item under a collapsible header. Items with
	// the same Section value are grouped together. Empty = ungrouped.
	Section string
}

// SidebarNavProps configures a vertical sidebar navigation panel.
type SidebarNavProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps
	// Brand renders at the top of the sidebar (optional).
	Brand templ.Component
	// Header renders between Brand and the nav links (optional).
	// Useful for search/filter inputs.
	Header templ.Component
	// Items are the navigation links.
	Items []SidebarNavItem
	// Footer renders at the bottom of the sidebar (optional).
	Footer templ.Component
	// CurrentPath auto-detects the active item when set. An item is active when
	// its Href matches CurrentPath. Explicit Active=true on an item takes priority.
	CurrentPath string
}

// DefaultSidebarNavProps returns sensible defaults
func DefaultSidebarNavProps() SidebarNavProps {
	return SidebarNavProps{}
}

// sidebarItemActive returns true when the item should be highlighted.
// Explicit Active=true takes priority; otherwise the item is active when its
// Href exactly matches CurrentPath (unified with NavLink via IsActive).
func sidebarItemActive(item SidebarNavItem, currentPath string) bool {
	if item.Active {
		return true
	}
	if currentPath == "" || item.Href == "" {
		return false
	}
	return IsActive(item.Href, currentPath)
}

// sidebarNavGroup is a run of consecutive items with the same Section value.
type sidebarNavGroup struct {
	Section string // empty for ungrouped items
	Items   []SidebarNavItem
}

// sidebarNavGroups partitions items into groups of consecutive items sharing
// the same Section value. Items with empty Section form standalone groups.
func sidebarNavGroups(items []SidebarNavItem) []sidebarNavGroup {
	if len(items) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	var groups []sidebarNavGroup
	current := sidebarNavGroup{Section: items[0].Section}

	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Section != current.Section {
			groups = append(groups, current)
			current = sidebarNavGroup{Section: item.Section}
		}

		current.Items = append(current.Items, item)
	}

	groups = append(groups, current)

	return groups
}

// sidebarNavHasSections reports whether any item has a non-empty Section,
// which triggers the grouped rendering path.
func sidebarNavHasSections(items []SidebarNavItem) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Section != "" {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// sidebarGroupHasActive reports whether any item in a group is active.
func sidebarGroupHasActive(items []SidebarNavItem, currentPath string) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if sidebarItemActive(item, currentPath) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// SidebarNav renders a vertical sidebar with brand, nav links (each with an
// optional icon), and a footer slot. Designed for admin panels and dashboards.
//
//	@navigation.SidebarNav(navigation.SidebarNavProps{
//	   Brand: templ.Raw(`<span class="font-bold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">MyApp</span>`),
//	   Items: []navigation.SidebarNavItem{
//	     {Label: "Dashboard", Href: "/", Icon: icons.Squares2x2, Active: true},
//	     {Label: "Users", Href: "/users", Icon: icons.Users},
//	   },
//	   CurrentPath: "/users",
//	})
templ SidebarNav(props SidebarNavProps) {
	<aside
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("flex h-full w-64 flex-col border-e border-[var(--tc-sidebar-border)] bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-bg)]", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		} else {
			aria-label="Sidebar"
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Brand != nil {
			<div class="flex items-center gap-2.5 px-4 py-5">
				@props.Brand
			</div>
		}
		if props.Header != nil {
			<div class="px-3 pb-1">
				@props.Header
			</div>
		}
		<nav class="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto px-3 py-2" aria-label="Sidebar navigation">
			if sidebarNavHasSections(props.Items) {
				for _, group := range sidebarNavGroups(props.Items) {
					if group.Section != "" {
						{{ hasActive := sidebarGroupHasActive(group.Items, props.CurrentPath) }}
						<details
							class="group"
							if hasActive {
								open
							}
						>
							<summary class="flex cursor-pointer list-none items-center justify-between rounded-lg px-3 pt-3 pb-1 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-[var(--tc-sidebar-muted)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-muted-hover)] [&::-webkit-details-marker]:hidden">
								<span>{ group.Section }</span>
								@icons.Icon(icons.ChevronDown, "h-3 w-3 shrink-0 text-gray-600 transition-transform duration-200 motion-reduce:transition-none group-open:rotate-180 dark:text-gray-500")
							</summary>
							<div class="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
								for _, item := range group.Items {
									{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
									<a
										href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
										class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
											templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
											templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
										if active {
											aria-current="page"
										}
									>
										if item.Icon != "" {
											@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
										}
										{ item.Label }
									</a>
								}
							</div>
						</details>
					} else {
						for _, item := range group.Items {
							{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
							<a
								href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
								class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
									templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
									templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
								if active {
									aria-current="page"
								}
							>
								if item.Icon != "" {
									@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
								}
								{ item.Label }
							</a>
						}
					}
				}
			} else {
				for _, item := range props.Items {
					{{ active := sidebarItemActive(item, props.CurrentPath) }}
					<a
						href={ templ.SafeURL(item.Href) }
						class={ "flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium " + utils.TransitionColors,
							templ.KV("bg-blue-600 text-white dark:bg-blue-500", active),
							templ.KV("text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg)] hover:bg-[var(--tc-sidebar-item-hover-bg)] hover:text-[var(--tc-sidebar-fg-hover)]", !active) }
						if active {
							aria-current="page"
						}
					>
						if item.Icon != "" {
							@icons.Icon(item.Icon, "h-5 w-5 flex-shrink-0")
						}
						{ item.Label }
					</a>
				}
			}
		</nav>
		if props.Footer != nil {
			<div class="px-4 py-3 text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400">
				@props.Footer
			</div>
		}
	</aside>
}
package navigation

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

func TestSidebarNavRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders items with labels", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{
				{Label: "Dashboard", Href: "/"},
				{Label: "Users", Href: "/users"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Dashboard")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Users")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `href="/users"`)
	})

	t.Run("active item gets active styling and aria-current", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{
				{Label: "Dashboard", Href: "/", Active: true},
				{Label: "Users", Href: "/users"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-blue-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="page"`)
	})

	t.Run("currentpath auto-detects active item", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			CurrentPath: "/users",
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{
				{Label: "Dashboard", Href: "/"},
				{Label: "Users", Href: "/users"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "bg-blue-600")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-current="page"`)
	})

	t.Run("icon renders when set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{
				{Label: "Users", Href: "/users", Icon: icons.Users},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "<svg")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Users")
	})

	t.Run("no icon omits svg", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{
				{Label: "Settings", Href: "/settings"},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "<svg")
	})

	t.Run("brand slot renders at top", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Brand: templ.Raw(`<span class="font-bold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">MyApp</span>`),
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{{Label: "Home", Href: "/"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "MyApp")
	})

	t.Run("footer slot renders at bottom", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items:  []SidebarNavItem{{Label: "Home", Href: "/"}},
			Footer: templ.Raw(`<span>v1.0.0</span>`),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "v1.0.0")
	})

	t.Run("default aria-label is Sidebar", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{{Label: "Home", Href: "/"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Sidebar"`)
	})

	t.Run("nav has scroll classes for overflow", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items: []SidebarNavItem{{Label: "Home", Href: "/"}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "overflow-y-auto")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "min-h-0")
	})

	t.Run("propagates BaseProps", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SidebarNav(SidebarNavProps{
			Items:     []SidebarNavItem{{Label: "Home", Href: "/"}},
			ID:        "sidebar",
			Class:     "w-72",
			AriaLabel: "Main navigation",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="sidebar"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "w-72")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-label="Main navigation"`)
	})
}

	})
}

// navMenuIDRe matches the content-derived mobile-menu id: the same
// tc-<prefix>-<16 hex> shape utils.EnsureID mints, so goldens normalize it.
var navMenuIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`tc-mobile-menu-[a-f0-9]{16}`)

// domIDRe matches id="" attributes only (not data-*-id=""), so a duplicate-id
// assertion sees exactly the ids getElementById() resolves.
var domIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?:^|\s)id="([^"]*)"`)

func domIDs(html string) []string {
	matches := domIDRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(html, -1)
	ids := make([]string, 0, len(matches))

	for _, match := range matches {
		ids = append(ids, match[1])
	}

	return ids
}

// TestNavMenuIDIsDeterministic pins the caching contract: the mobile-menu id
// is derived from the nav's content, so rendering the same props twice is
// byte-identical and ETag revalidation can answer 304 instead of re-sending
// a freshly randomized page on every request.
func TestNavMenuIDIsDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	props := NavProps{Links: testNavLinks, CurrentPath: "/"}
	first := utils.Render(t, Nav(props))
	second := utils.Render(t, Nav(props))

	if first != second {
		t.Error("Nav rendered different HTML for identical props — the mobile-menu id must not be render-random")
	}

	if got := navMenuIDRe.FindString(first); got == "" {
		t.Errorf("mobile-menu id missing from the rendered nav:\n%s", first)
	}
}

// TestNavMenuIDTracksContent proves the derived id is content-scoped: two
// navs that differ in links or current path get different menu ids, so their
// toggles cannot resolve to each other's menu.
func TestNavMenuIDTracksContent(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	base := navMenuIDRe.FindString(utils.Render(t, Nav(NavProps{Links: testNavLinks, CurrentPath: "/"})))
	otherPath := navMenuIDRe.FindString(utils.Render(t, Nav(NavProps{Links: testNavLinks, CurrentPath: "/about"})))

	if base == "" || otherPath == "" {
		t.Fatalf("mobile-menu id missing (base=%q otherPath=%q)", base, otherPath)
	}

	if base == otherPath {
		t.Errorf("navs with different current paths share the menu id %q", base)
	}
}

// TestNavMenuIDDerivesFromCallerID pins the duplicate-id fix: the <nav> keeps
// the consumer's id and the mobile menu gets its own derived id, so a document
// never carries the same id twice (invalid HTML, and aria-controls/
// getElementById resolve to the wrong element).
func TestNavMenuIDDerivesFromCallerID(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	output := utils.Render(t, Nav(NavProps{
		ID:          "site-nav",
		Links:       testNavLinks,
		CurrentPath: "/",
	}))

	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="site-nav-mobile-menu"`)
	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-controls="site-nav-mobile-menu"`)

	seen := map[string]int{}
	for _, id := range domIDs(output) {
		seen[id]++
	}

	if seen["site-nav"] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("expected exactly one id=%q, got %d", "site-nav", seen["site-nav"])
	}

	for id, count := range seen {
		if count > 1 {
			t.Errorf("duplicate id %q rendered %d times", id, count)
		}
	}
}

func TestNavContainerAware(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("viewport breakpoints by default", func(t *testing.T) {

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "@sm:flex")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "@sm:hidden")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, " sm:flex")
	})
}

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/icons"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// AuthLayout renders a split-screen authentication page: a centered auth card
// on one side and a branding/feature panel on the other. The branding panel
// hides on mobile (lg: breakpoint), leaving the card centered.
//
// Pass a LoginCard (or any Card-wrapped form) as Card. Set PanelTitle,
// PanelText, and PanelFeatures to fill the branding panel. Set Reverse to flip
// the column order.
//
//	@recipes.AuthLayout(recipes.AuthLayoutProps{
//	   Card:          loginCard,
//	   PanelTitle:    "Acme",
//	   PanelText:     "Build better products, faster.",
//	   PanelFeatures: []string{"SOC 2 compliant", "99.9% uptime SLA"},
//	})
templ AuthLayout(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("min-h-dvh grid lg:grid-cols-2", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		if props.Reverse {
			@authPanel(props)
			@authCardSide(props)
		} else {
			@authCardSide(props)
			@authPanel(props)
		}
	</div>
}

// authCardSide renders the card column — centered vertically and horizontally.
templ authCardSide(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div class="flex items-center justify-center px-4 py-12">
		<div class="w-full max-w-sm">
			if props.Card != nil {
				@props.Card
			}
		</div>
	</div>
}

// authPanel renders the branding column — hidden on mobile, visible from the
// lg breakpoint. Uses a blue-tinted background that adapts to dark mode.
templ authPanel(props AuthLayoutProps) {
	<div class="hidden lg:flex lg:flex-col lg:justify-between bg-blue-600 dark:bg-blue-900 px-12 py-12">
		<div class="max-w-md space-y-6">
			if props.PanelTitle != "" {
				<h2 class="text-3xl font-bold text-white">{ props.PanelTitle }</h2>
			}
			if props.PanelText != "" {
				<p class="text-lg text-blue-100">{ props.PanelText }</p>
			}
			if len(props.PanelFeatures) > 0 {
				<ul class="space-y-3">
					for _, feature := range props.PanelFeatures {
						<li class="flex items-start gap-3">
							@icons.IconWithStrokeWidth(icons.CheckCircle, "w-6 h-6 flex-shrink-0 text-blue-200", 1.5)
							<span class="text-blue-50">{ feature }</span>
						</li>
					}
				</ul>
			}
		</div>
		if props.PanelFooter != nil {
			<div class="mt-8">
				@props.PanelFooter
			</div>
		}
	</div>
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// AuthLayoutProps configures a recipes.AuthLayout screen — the canonical
// split-screen authentication layout: a centered auth card on one side and a
// branding/feature panel on the other. On mobile, the branding panel collapses
// to show only the card.
//
// The card content is consumer-supplied (typically a LoginCard, a signup form,
// or a password-reset form). The branding panel shows an optional title,
// description, feature bullets, and footer.
type AuthLayoutProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Card is the main auth content (typically a LoginCard or forms.Form
	// wrapped in a Card). Required.
	Card templ.Component
	// PanelTitle renders as a large heading in the branding panel. Optional.
	PanelTitle string
	// PanelText renders as body text under the PanelTitle. Optional.
	PanelText string
	// PanelFeatures is a list of bullet points rendered with checkmark icons
	// in the branding panel. Optional.
	PanelFeatures []string
	// PanelFooter renders at the bottom of the branding panel (e.g. a
	// testimonial, copyright, or security badge). Optional.
	PanelFooter templ.Component
	// Reverse flips the layout so the card appears on the right and the
	// branding panel on the left. Default: card left, panel right.
	// (On mobile the panel is always hidden.)
	Reverse bool
}

// DefaultAuthLayoutProps returns sensible defaults (empty).
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultAuthLayoutProps() AuthLayoutProps {
	return AuthLayoutProps{}
}
package recipes

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// errWriter always fails, exercising the generated templates' write-error
// propagation branches (every WriteString error check in *_templ.go).
type errWriter struct{}

func (errWriter) Write([]byte) (int, error) { return 0, errors.New("write failed") }

// TestRenderErrorPropagation proves every recipe propagates writer/context
// failures instead of silently rendering partial output — and covers the
// runtime error branches the happy-path tests cannot reach.
func TestRenderErrorPropagation(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	components := map[string]templ.Component{
		"dashboard": Dashboard(DashboardProps{Title: "X", Sidebar: templ.Raw("<nav>")}),
		"login":     LoginCard(LoginCardProps{Title: "X", FormBody: templ.Raw("<form>")}),
		"auth":      AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{Card: templ.Raw("<form>")}),
		"settings": SettingsLayout(SettingsLayoutProps{
			Title:    "X",
			Sections: []SettingsSection{{ID: "s", Title: "S", Body: templ.Raw("<form>")}},
		}),
	}

	for name, component := range components {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			if err := component.Render(context.Background(), errWriter{}); err == nil {
				t.Errorf("%s rendered without error through a failing writer", name)
			}

			cancelled, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
			cancel()

			if err := component.Render(cancelled, errWriter{}); err == nil {
				t.Errorf("%s rendered without error on a cancelled context", name)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCoverageMatrix renders maximal and minimal prop combinations for every
// recipe so branch-heavy generated templates (slot presence checks, defaults)
// are exercised beyond the happy-path rendering tests. Assertions stay light:
// the point is branch execution, verified by a marker string per slot.
func TestCoverageMatrix(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	marker := templ.Raw(`<div data-test="slot">slot</div>`)

	t.Run("dashboard maximal", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{
			ID:            "dash-id",
			Class:         "dash-class",
			AriaLabel:     "dash-label",
			Attrs:         templ.Attributes{"data-test-root": "dashboard"},
			Title:         "Overview",
			Subtitle:      "Last 30 days",
			Breadcrumb:    marker,
			Sidebar:       marker,
			MobileNav:     marker,
			Header:        marker,
			HeaderActions: marker,
			StatCards:     []templ.Component{marker},
			Charts:        []templ.Component{marker},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output,
			`data-test="slot"`, `data-test-root="dashboard"`, "dash-id", "dash-class", "dash-label")
	})

	t.Run("dashboard sidebar without header", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{
			Title:   "Shell",
			Sidebar: marker,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="slot"`)
	})

	t.Run("dashboard shell only", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{Title: "Bare"}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Bare")
	})

	t.Run("login card full", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LoginCard(LoginCardProps{
			Title:        "Create account",
			Subtitle:     "Start free",
			FormBody:     marker,
			OAuthButtons: marker,
			Footer:       marker,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Create account")
	})

	t.Run("auth layout panel footer", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{
			ID:            "auth-id",
			Class:         "auth-class",
			Attrs:         templ.Attributes{"data-test-root": "auth"},
			Card:          marker,
			PanelTitle:    "Acme",
			PanelText:     "Build better products.",
			PanelFeatures: []string{"SOC 2", "Uptime"},
			PanelFooter:   marker,
			Reverse:       true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, `data-test-root="auth"`, "auth-id", "auth-class", "Acme")
	})

	t.Run("auth layout card only", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{Card: marker}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="slot"`)
	})

	t.Run("settings sections with subtitles", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SettingsLayout(SettingsLayoutProps{
			Title:    "User Settings",
			Subtitle: "Manage your account",
			Aside:    marker,
			Sections: []SettingsSection{
				{ID: "profile", Title: "Profile", Subtitle: "Your details", Body: marker},
				{ID: "security", Title: "Security", Body: marker},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "Your details", `id="security"`)
	})

	t.Run("settings single section no aside", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SettingsLayout(SettingsLayoutProps{
			Title:    "Solo",
			Sections: []SettingsSection{{ID: "only", Title: "Only", Body: marker}},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="only"`)
	})
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/display"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/layout"
)

// Dashboard renders a complete dashboard screen: AppShell with a sidebar,
// sticky header, a page header (title + optional actions), a responsive stat
// card grid, and a charts grid. Every slot is consumer-supplied via
// templ.Component — Dashboard provides the scaffold only.
//
// Pass components for Sidebar (typically navigation.SidebarNav), Header
// (typically navigation.Nav), StatCards (display.StatCard instances), and
// Charts (display.Card-wrapped visualizations). Charts and StatCards slices
// may be empty.
//
//	@recipes.Dashboard(recipes.DashboardProps{
//	   Title:       "Overview",
//	   Subtitle:    "Last 30 days",
//	   Sidebar:     navSidebar,
//	   Header:      navHeader,
//	   StatCards:   []templ.Component{stat1, stat2, stat3, stat4},
//	   Charts:      []templ.Component{chart1, chart2},
//	});
templ Dashboard(props DashboardProps) {
	@layout.AppShell(layout.AppShellProps{
		BaseProps:      props.GetBaseProps(),
		Sidebar:        props.Sidebar,
		MobileNav:      props.MobileNav,
		Header:         props.Header,
		SidebarWidth:   props.SidebarWidth,
		StickyHeader:   true,
		Container:      true,
		ContainerWidth: layout.ContainerWidthDefault,
		Content:        dashboardContent(props),
	})
}

templ dashboardContent(props DashboardProps) {
	<div class="py-6 space-y-6">
		@display.PageHeader(display.PageHeaderProps{
			Title:      props.Title,
			Subtitle:   props.Subtitle,
			Breadcrumb: props.Breadcrumb,
			Action:     props.HeaderActions,
		})
		if len(props.StatCards) > 0 {
			@display.Grid(display.GridProps{
				Cols: display.GridCols4,
				Gap:  display.GridGapMD,
			}) {
				for _, card := range props.StatCards {
					@card
				}
			}
		}
		if len(props.Charts) > 0 {
			@display.Grid(display.GridProps{
				Cols: display.GridCols2,
				Gap:  display.GridGapLG,
			}) {
				for _, chart := range props.Charts {
					@chart
				}
			}
		}
	</div>
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/layout"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// DashboardProps configures a recipes.Dashboard screen. A dashboard is an
// AppShell with a stat-card grid and arbitrary chart/content slots. Every
// slot is a templ.Component so the consumer controls the actual content —
// recipes.Dashboard provides the layout scaffold only.
//
// Pass slots via templ.Component (Card.Body, navigation.Nav, display.Grid, etc.).
// The Sidebar slot is typically navigation.SidebarNav; the Header slot is
// typically navigation.Nav or navigation.SimpleNav. StatCards is a slice of
// display.StatCard components rendered inside a display.Grid. Charts is a
// slice of arbitrary chart components (display.Card-wrapped) rendered below
// the stat grid.
type DashboardProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Title and Subtitle render in a display.PageHeader at the top of the
	// content column.
	Title    string
	Subtitle string
	// Breadcrumb is an optional templ.Component slot (typically
	// navigation.Breadcrumbs) rendered above the title in the PageHeader.
	Breadcrumb templ.Component
	// Sidebar is the desktop sidebar slot (typically navigation.SidebarNav).
	// Required for the dashboard layout; pass nil for a sidebar-less shell.
	Sidebar templ.Component
	// MobileNav is the below-lg mobile navigation slot (typically
	// display.Drawer). Optional.
	MobileNav templ.Component
	// Header is the sticky top header slot (typically navigation.Nav). Optional.
	Header templ.Component
	// HeaderActions is rendered on the right side of the PageHeader (above
	// the stat grid). Use it for "Add" buttons, filters, or time-range
	// pickers. Optional.
	HeaderActions templ.Component
	// StatCards is the slice of display.StatCard components rendered in a
	// responsive 4-up grid at the top of the dashboard body.
	StatCards []templ.Component
	// Charts is the slice of chart/visualization components rendered below
	// the stat grid in a responsive 2-up grid. Each chart should be wrapped
	// in a display.Card by the consumer.
	Charts []templ.Component
	// SidebarWidth controls the AppShell sidebar width. Default
	// layout.SidebarWidthMD (16rem).
	SidebarWidth layout.SidebarWidth
}

// DefaultDashboardProps returns sensible defaults (MD sidebar, no slots).
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultDashboardProps() DashboardProps {
	return DashboardProps{
		SidebarWidth: layout.SidebarWidthDefault,
	}
}
// Package recipes ships composition screens built from the library's existing
// primitives (display, forms, layout, navigation). Each recipe is a screen-level
// component — Dashboard, SettingsLayout, LoginCard — that composes primitives
// into a complete layout via templ.Component slots.

// recipes is a top-of-DAG package: it imports downward only (into display/forms/
// layout/navigation/utils/icons) and is imported by nothing inside the library.
// See docs/adr/0019-recipes-package.md for the design rationale.

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"

// LoginCard renders a centered sign-in card with a header, form body, optional
// OAuth divider + buttons, and a footer. The canonical login screen.
//
// Pass a forms.Form as FormBody (typically with Layout: forms.FormLayoutStack
// for vertical label-above-input layout). Pass display.Button components in
// OAuthButtons for "Continue with X" options.
//
//	@recipes.LoginCard(recipes.LoginCardProps{
//	   Title:    "Sign in to Acme",
//	   Subtitle: "Welcome back",
//	   FormBody: signInForm,
//	   OAuthButtons: templ.Raw(`<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3">…</div>`),
//	   Footer:   templ.Raw(`<p>Need an account? <a href="/signup">Sign up</a></p>`),
//	})
templ LoginCard(props LoginCardProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("min-h-dvh flex items-center justify-center px-4 py-12", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		<div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-sm">
			@display.Card(display.CardProps{
				Title:    props.Title,
				Subtitle: props.Subtitle,
				Padding:  display.CardPaddingMD,
				Body:     loginBody(props),
				Footer:   props.Footer,
			})
		</div>
	</div>
}

templ loginBody(props LoginCardProps) {
	<div class="space-y-4">
		if props.FormBody != nil {
			@props.FormBody
		}
		if props.OAuthButtons != nil {
			<div class="relative py-2">
				<div class="absolute inset-0 flex items-center" aria-hidden="true">
					<div class="w-full border-t border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700"></div>
				</div>
				<div class="relative flex justify-center">
					<span class={ "bg-white dark:bg-gray-800 px-2 text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400" }>OR</span>
				</div>
			</div>
			@props.OAuthButtons
		}
	</div>
}

// LoginCardProps configures a recipes.LoginCard screen — the canonical
// centered Card with email + password form, optional OAuth slots, and
// "remember me" / "forgot password" affordances.
//
// The form body and OAuth buttons are consumer-supplied templ.Component
// slots so the consumer controls the actual input fields, validation, and
// HTMX wiring. LoginCard provides the layout: a centered max-w card with
// a title header and a vertical form stack body.
type LoginCardProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Title renders as the card header. Default: "Sign in".
	Title string
	// Subtitle renders as muted text under the Title. Optional.
	Subtitle string
	// FormBody is the main form content (email + password + submit button).
	// Typically a forms.Form with Layout: forms.FormLayoutStack. Required.
	FormBody templ.Component
	// OAuthButtons renders below the form body, separated by a divider.
	// Use it for "Continue with Google/GitHub" buttons. Optional.
	OAuthButtons templ.Component
	// Footer renders below everything (typically "Don't have an account?
	// Sign up"). Optional.
	Footer templ.Component
}

// DefaultLoginCardProps returns sensible defaults (Title: "Sign in").
//
//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // constructor intentionally sets only non-zero defaults
func DefaultLoginCardProps() LoginCardProps {
	return LoginCardProps{
		Title: loginDefaultTitle,
	}
}

const loginDefaultTitle = "Sign in"
// Package recipes provides rendering tests for the recipes package.
package recipes

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
