func TestDashboardRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders title and stat cards", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{
			Title:    "Overview",
			Subtitle: "Last 30 days",
			StatCards: []templ.Component{
				templ.Raw(`<div data-test="stat1">S1</div>`),
				templ.Raw(`<div data-test="stat2">S2</div>`),
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Overview")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Last 30 days")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="stat1"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="stat2"`)
	})

	t.Run("renders charts when provided", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{
			Title: "X",
			Charts: []templ.Component{
				templ.Raw(`<div data-test="chart1">Chart1</div>`),
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="chart1"`)
	})

	t.Run("omits stat grid when slice empty", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, Dashboard(DashboardProps{Title: "X"}))
		// Still renders title but no chart/stat data attributes
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "X")
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		p := DefaultDashboardProps()
		if p.SidebarWidth == "" {
			t.Error("DefaultDashboardProps().SidebarWidth should not be empty")
		}
	})
}

func TestSettingsLayoutRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders title and sections", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, SettingsLayout(SettingsLayoutProps{
			Title:    "Settings",
			Subtitle: "Manage your account",
			Aside:    templ.Raw(`<nav data-test="aside">aside</nav>`),
			Sections: []SettingsSection{
				{ID: "profile", Title: "Profile", Body: templ.Raw(`<form data-test="profile-form">P</form>`)},
				{ID: "security", Title: "Security", Body: templ.Raw(`<form data-test="security-form">S</form>`)},
			},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Settings")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Manage your account")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="aside"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="profile"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `id="security"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="profile-form"`)
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		_ = DefaultSettingsLayoutProps()
	})
}

func TestLoginCardRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders title, form body, and footer", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, LoginCard(LoginCardProps{
			Title:    "Sign in",
			Subtitle: "Welcome back",
			FormBody: templ.Raw(`<form data-test="form">F</form>`),
			Footer:   templ.Raw(`<p data-test="footer">Need an account?</p>`),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Sign in")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Welcome back")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="form"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="footer"`)
	})

	t.Run("renders oauth divider when OAuthButtons set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, LoginCard(LoginCardProps{
			FormBody:     templ.Raw(`<form>F</form>`),
			OAuthButtons: templ.Raw(`<div data-test="oauth">Google</div>`),
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="oauth"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, ">OR<")
	})

	t.Run("omits oauth divider when OAuthButtons nil", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, LoginCard(LoginCardProps{
			FormBody: templ.Raw(`<form>F</form>`),
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, ">OR<")
	})

	t.Run("default props set Title", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		p := DefaultLoginCardProps()
		if p.Title != "Sign in" {
			t.Errorf("DefaultLoginCardProps().Title = %q, want %q", p.Title, "Sign in")
		}
	})
}

func TestAuthLayoutRender(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("renders card and panel", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{
			Card:          templ.Raw(`<form data-test="login">Login</form>`),
			PanelTitle:    "Acme Corp",
			PanelText:     "Build better products.",
			PanelFeatures: []string{"SOC 2 compliant", "99.9% uptime"},
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `data-test="login"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Acme Corp")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Build better products.")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "SOC 2 compliant")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "99.9% uptime")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "lg:grid-cols-2")
	})

	t.Run("hides panel content on mobile", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{
			Card:       templ.Raw(`<div>card</div>`),
			PanelTitle: "Branding",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "hidden lg:flex")
	})

	t.Run("reverse flips column order", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		normal := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{
			Card:       templ.Raw(`<div id="card">`),
			PanelTitle: "Panel",
		}))
		reversed := utils.Render(t, AuthLayout(AuthLayoutProps{
			Card:       templ.Raw(`<div id="card">`),
			PanelTitle: "Panel",
			Reverse:    true,
		}))
		// In normal mode, card appears before panel in DOM order.
		// In reverse mode, panel appears before card.
		normalCardIdx := indexOf(normal, `id="card"`)

		normalPanelIdx := indexOf(normal, "Panel")
		if normalCardIdx >= normalPanelIdx {
			t.Error("normal layout should have card before panel in DOM")
		}

		reversedCardIdx := indexOf(reversed, `id="card"`)

		reversedPanelIdx := indexOf(reversed, "Panel")
		if reversedPanelIdx >= reversedCardIdx {
			t.Error("reverse layout should have panel before card in DOM")
		}
	})

	t.Run("default props", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		p := DefaultAuthLayoutProps()
		if p.Reverse {
			t.Error("DefaultAuthLayoutProps().Reverse should be false")
		}
	})
}

func indexOf(s, substr string) int {
	for i := 0; i <= len(s)-len(substr); i++ {
		if s[i:i+len(substr)] == substr {
			return i
		}
	}

	return -1
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/display"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/layout"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SettingsLayout renders a titled page with a section-nav aside and a stack
// of Card-wrapped form sections in the main column. The canonical admin
// settings page.
//
//	@recipes.SettingsLayout(recipes.SettingsLayoutProps{
//	   Title:    "Account settings",
//	   Subtitle: "Manage your profile and preferences",
//	   Aside:    sectionNav,
//	   Sections: []recipes.SettingsSection{
//	     {ID: "profile", Title: "Profile", Body: profileForm},
//	     {ID: "security", Title: "Security", Body: securityForm},
//	   },
//	})
templ SettingsLayout(props SettingsLayoutProps) {
	<div
		if props.ID != "" {
			id={ props.ID }
		}
		class={ utils.Class("py-6", props.Class) }
		if props.AriaLabel != "" {
			aria-label={ props.AriaLabel }
		}
		{ props.Attrs... }
	>
		@layout.Container(layout.ContainerProps{Width: layout.ContainerWidthDefault}) {
			<div class="mb-6">
				<h1 class="text-2xl font-bold text-gray-900 dark:text-white">{ props.Title }</h1>
				if props.Subtitle != "" {
					<p class={ utils.Class(mutedSettingsSubtitle, "mt-1") }>{ props.Subtitle }</p>
				}
			</div>
			@layout.Split(layout.SplitProps{
				Ratio: layout.SplitRatio1To3,
				Aside: props.Aside,
				Main:  settingsMain(props.Sections),
			})
		}
	</div>
}

const mutedSettingsSubtitle = "text-sm text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400"

templ settingsMain(sections []SettingsSection) {
	<div class="space-y-6">
		for _, section := range sections {
			@display.Card(display.CardProps{
				BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{ID: section.ID},
				Title:     section.Title,
				Subtitle:  section.Subtitle,
				Body:      section.Body,
			})
		}
	</div>
}
package recipes

import (
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils"
)

// SettingsLayoutProps configures a recipes.SettingsLayout screen — the
// canonical "section nav on the left, form content on the right" pattern
// used by almost every settings page in every admin panel.
//
// The aside is a vertical list of section links; the main is a stack of
// Card-wrapped forms (one per section). Both are consumer-supplied
// templ.Component slots.
type SettingsLayoutProps struct {
	utils.BaseProps

	// Title and Subtitle render at the top of the page.
	Title    string
	Subtitle string
	// Aside is the section navigation slot (typically a Card-wrapped list
	// of links to #section-id anchors). Required.
	Aside templ.Component
	// Sections is the list of form sections rendered in the main column.
	// Each section is rendered as a Card with Title + a form body. The
	// Section.ID becomes the card's id (for anchor navigation from Aside).
	Sections []SettingsSection
}

// SettingsSection is one titled section of a settings page.
type SettingsSection struct {
	// ID is used as the anchor target (id attribute) so the Aside links
	// can jump to it. Optional but recommended.
	ID string
	// Title renders as the Card header.
	Title string
	// Subtitle renders as muted text under the Title. Optional.
	Subtitle string
	// Body is the form content of the section. Typically a forms.Form
	// or a Card.Body slot. Required.
	Body templ.Component
}

// DefaultSettingsLayoutProps returns sensible defaults (empty).
func DefaultSettingsLayoutProps() SettingsLayoutProps {
	return SettingsLayoutProps{} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // intentionally minimal
}
// Command countgen keeps the count-bearing tables in FEATURES.md and
// skill/SKILL.md derived from the tree instead of hand-typed. Check mode (default)
// exits non-zero listing every drift; -w rewrites the docs.
//
//	go run ./tools/countgen/cmd/countgen          # check
//	go run ./tools/countgen/cmd/countgen -w      # write
//
// utils.TestDocsCountDrift is the independent verifier — it re-derives every
// count and asserts the docs without this package's code (see package docs).
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/tools/countgen"
)

func main() {
	write := flag.Bool("w", false, "rewrite FEATURES.md/SKILL.md to match the tree")

	flag.Parse()

	root := "."

	if flag.NArg() > 0 {
		root = flag.Arg(0)
	}

	if *write {
		changed, err := countgen.Apply(root)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "countgen: %v\n", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}

		if len(changed) == 0 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "countgen: docs already match the tree")

			return
		}

		for _, name := range changed {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "countgen: wrote %s\n", name)
		}

		return
	}

	if err := countgen.Check(root); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "countgen: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "countgen: OK — every count-bearing site matches the tree")
}
// Package countgen derives the library's count-bearing numbers from the tree
// and writes them into the three count-bearing docs (FEATURES.md, skill/SKILL.md,
// README.md).
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS: every component addition forced a hand-typed same-commit
// count bump in FEATURES/SKILL (TODO #996) — the tax this generator deletes.
// Run `go run ./tools/countgen/cmd/countgen -w` after any change that moves a
// count; commit the diff in the same commit as the source change.
//
// INDEPENDENT VERIFIER: utils.TestDocsCountDrift re-derives every count with
// its own implementation and asserts the docs directly — it is deliberately
// NOT this package's code, so the two layers cross-check each other. If they
// ever disagree, CI goes red and the reconciliation is the signal.
//
// DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED (no mechanical source; semantics owned by
// docs/count-definitions.md):
//   - the enums TOTAL ("74 typed enums") — "exported closed-set string types"
//     is a semantic judgment; only the IsValid count is mechanical;
//   - the FEATURES.md `utils` row ("0"): utils owns no components by
//     definition, yet utils/dismiss.templ exports a helper templ function —
//     a mechanical count would print 1 against a deliberate 0;
//   - "~31,500 lines of Go/templ source" and "in 5 packages" prose counts;
//   - the "8 components accept ContainerAware" figure (ADR-0018 lookup-map
//     semantics).
package countgen

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

const (
	featuresDoc = "FEATURES.md"
	skillDoc    = "skill/SKILL.md"
	readmeDoc   = "README.md"
)

// countedPackages returns the packages whose exported templ functions compose
// the "N templ components" total (recipes screens counted separately).
func countedPackages() []string {
	return []string{
		"display", "feedback", "forms", "navigation", "errorpage",
		"layout", "htmx", "datastar", "charts/echarts",
	}
}

// tablePackages returns the packages whose exported templ functions countgen
// derives (utils excluded: its FEATURES row is the semantic "owns no
// components", not a templ-function count — utils/dismiss.templ exports
// one helper function and must keep printing 0).
func tablePackages() []string {
	return append([]string{"icons", "recipes"}, countedPackages()...)
}

// Counts holds every number countgen derives from the tree.
type Counts struct {
	Components            int            // exported templ funcs across the 9 counted packages
	PackageCounts         map[string]int // per package (counted 9 + icons + recipes)
	Recipes               int            // recipes/*.templ exported screens
	ComponentsPlusRecipes int            // Components + Recipes
	Icons                 int            // iconPathData entries + Spinner
	IsValid               int            // <Name>IsValid( declarations, library source
	GeneratedFiles        int            // *_templ.go files (website excluded)
	HTMLGoldens           int            // committed .golden baselines (visualtest/website excluded)
	VisualGoldens         int            // visualtest/testdata .png goldens
	ErrorpageConstructors int            // exported constructors in errorpage/constructors.go
}

var (
	templFuncRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^templ\s+([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\s*\(`)
	iconEntryRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\t[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*:\s+("[^"]*"|svg\.Path[A-Za-z]*)`)
	isValidRe     = regexp.MustCompile(`func\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*IsValid\s*\(`)
	constructorRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^func [A-Z]`)
)

// Derive computes every count from the tree rooted at root.
func Derive(root string) (Counts, error) {
	//nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // zero values are the point: every field is filled as it is derived
	counts := Counts{PackageCounts: map[string]int{}}

	for _, pkg := range tablePackages() {
		total, err := countPackageTemplFuncs(root, pkg)
		if err != nil {
			return counts, err
		}

		counts.PackageCounts[pkg] = total
	}

	for _, pkg := range countedPackages() {
		counts.Components += counts.PackageCounts[pkg]
	}

	counts.Recipes = counts.PackageCounts["recipes"]
	counts.ComponentsPlusRecipes = counts.Components + counts.Recipes

	if err := deriveWalkedCounts(root, &counts); err != nil {
		return counts, err
	}

	constructorSource, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, "errorpage", "constructors.go"))
	if err != nil {
		return counts, fmt.Errorf("read errorpage/constructors.go: %w", err)
	}

	counts.ErrorpageConstructors = len(constructorRe.FindAll(constructorSource, -1))

	return counts, nil
}

func deriveWalkedCounts(root string, counts *Counts) error {
	icons, err := countIcons(root)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	counts.Icons = icons

	isValid, err := countMatchesWalk(root, isValidRe, "IsValid")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	counts.IsValid = isValid

	generated, err := countSuffixWalk(root, "_templ.go", "generated")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	counts.GeneratedFiles = generated

	htmlGoldens, err := countGoldenWalk(root)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	counts.HTMLGoldens = htmlGoldens

	visualGoldens, err := countVisualGoldens(root)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	counts.VisualGoldens = visualGoldens

	return nil
}

func countPackageTemplFuncs(root, pkg string) (int, error) {
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, pkg, "*.templ"))
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("glob %s: %w", pkg, err)
	}

	total := 0

	for _, file := range files {
		data, err := os.ReadFile(file)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", file, err)
		}

		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(string(data), "\n") {
			if templFuncRe.MatchString(line) {
				total++
			}
		}
	}

	return total, nil
}

func countIcons(root string) (int, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, "icons", "icon_paths.go"))
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("read icons/icon_paths.go: %w", err)
	}

	return len(iconEntryRe.FindAll(data, -1)) + 1, nil // +1: Spinner
}

// countMatchesWalk mirrors utils' countIsValidMethods: non-test .go files,
// skipping .git, website, and the cmd/tc _sources mirror.
func countMatchesWalk(root string, pattern *regexp.Regexp, label string) (int, error) {
	total := 0

	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if entry.IsDir() {
			if base := filepath.Base(path); base == ".git" || base == "website" || base == "_sources" {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".go") || strings.HasSuffix(path, "_test.go") {
			return nil
		}

		data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // G122: walks the repo's own tree; no untrusted symlinks
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
		}

		total += len(pattern.FindAll(data, -1))

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("walk %s: %w", label, err)
	}

	return total, nil
}

// countSuffixWalk mirrors utils' countGeneratedFiles: skip .git and website.
func countSuffixWalk(root, suffix, label string) (int, error) {
	total := 0

	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if entry.IsDir() {
			if base := filepath.Base(path); base == ".git" || base == "website" {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(path, suffix) {
			total++
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("walk %s: %w", label, err)
	}

	return total, nil
}

// countGoldenWalk mirrors utils' countHTMLGoldens: .golden files, visualtest
// and website excluded.
func countGoldenWalk(root string) (int, error) {
	total := 0

	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if entry.IsDir() {
			if base := filepath.Base(path); base == ".git" || base == "website" || base == "visualtest" {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(path, ".golden") {
			total++
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("walk HTML goldens: %w", err)
	}

	return total, nil
}

// countVisualGoldens mirrors utils' countVisualGoldens: .png files under
// visualtest/testdata, dotted (failure-artifact) dirs skipped.
func countVisualGoldens(root string) (int, error) {
	total := 0
	visualDir := filepath.Join(root, "visualtest", "testdata")

	err := filepath.WalkDir(visualDir, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if entry.IsDir() {
			if strings.HasPrefix(entry.Name(), ".") && entry.Name() != "." && path != visualDir {
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(path, ".png") && !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".fail.png") {
			total++
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("walk visual goldens: %w", err)
	}

	return total, nil
}

// renderFunc rebuilds a site's matched text from the derived counts; prev
// carries the regex's captured groups for numbers countgen does not own
// (hand-typed totals) and exact whitespace (markdown table padding).
type renderFunc func(counts Counts, prev []string) string

// site is one count-bearing doc location: a single-match regex countgen
// rewrites with its render function.
type site struct {
	name    string
	file    string
	pattern *regexp.Regexp
	render  renderFunc
}

func featuresSites() []site {
	backtick := "`"

	return append(featuresTotalsSites(backtick), featuresBulletSites(backtick)...)
}

// featuresTotalsSites returns the Totals line site plus every FEATURES.md
// table-row site (icons, recipes, and one row per counted package).
func featuresTotalsSites(backtick string) []site {
	totals := site{
		name: "Totals line",
		file: featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(
			`\*\*Totals:\*\* (\d+) templ components \(primitives, drift-guard verified\) \+ (\d+) recipe screens = (\d+), (\d+) icon names, (\d+) typed enums \((\d+) with ` + backtick + `IsValid\(\)` + backtick + `, (\d+) generated ` + backtick + `\*_templ\.go` + backtick + ` files`,
		),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf(
				"**Totals:** %d templ components (primitives, drift-guard verified) + %d recipe screens = %d, %d icon names, %s typed enums (%d with %sIsValid()%s, %d generated %s*_templ.go%s files",
				counts.Components,
				counts.Recipes,
				counts.ComponentsPlusRecipes,
				counts.Icons,
				prev[5],
				counts.IsValid,
				backtick,
				backtick,
				counts.GeneratedFiles,
				backtick,
				backtick,
			)
		},
	}

	iconsRow := site{
		name:    "icons table row",
		file:    featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\| (` + backtick + `icons` + backtick + `)(\s+)\| (\d+) \((\d+) icons\)`),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("| %s%s| %d (%d icons)", prev[1], prev[2], counts.PackageCounts["icons"], counts.Icons)
		},
	}

	recipesRow := site{
		name:    "recipes table row",
		file:    featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\| (` + backtick + `recipes` + backtick + `)(\s+)\| (\d+) screens`),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("| %s%s| %d screens", prev[1], prev[2], counts.Recipes)
		},
	}

	packages := countedPackages()
	rows := make([]site, 0, 2+len(packages))
	rows = append(rows, iconsRow, recipesRow)

	for _, pkg := range packages {
		rows = append(rows, countTableRow(pkg))
	}

	return append(rows, totals)
}

// featuresBulletSites returns the FEATURES.md bullet sites that carry derived
// counts (IsValid coverage, HTML baselines, visual goldens).
func featuresBulletSites(backtick string) []site {
	isValidBullet := site{
		name: "Type Safety bullet (IsValid only; enums total is hand-typed)",
		file: featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(
			`(\d+) typed string enums \((\d+) with ` + backtick + `IsValid\(\)` + backtick + ` methods \+ tests\)`,
		),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s typed string enums (%d with %sIsValid()%s methods + tests)",
				prev[1], counts.IsValid, backtick, backtick)
		},
	}

	htmlBaselines := site{
		name:    "Test Coverage bullet (HTML baselines)",
		file:    featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`in 5 packages, (\d+) baselines\)`),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("in 5 packages, %d baselines)", counts.HTMLGoldens)
		},
	}

	visualGoldens := site{
		name:    "Test Coverage bullet (visual goldens)",
		file:    featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`; (\d+) goldens incl\. charts`),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("; %d goldens incl. charts", counts.VisualGoldens)
		},
	}

	return []site{isValidBullet, htmlBaselines, visualGoldens}
}

// countTableRow renders one FEATURES.md package-table row. The captured gap
// preserves the markdown table's column padding byte-for-byte.
func countTableRow(pkg string) site {
	backtick := "`"

	return site{
		name:    "table row " + pkg,
		file:    featuresDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\| (` + regexp.QuoteMeta(backtick+pkg+backtick) + `)(\s+)\| (\d+)`),
		render: func(c Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("| %s%s| %d", prev[1], prev[2], c.PackageCounts[pkg])
		},
	}
}

func skillSites() []site {
	backtick := "`"

	catalogueTotal := site{
		name:    "catalogue total line",
		file:    skillDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^(\d+) components across (\d+) packages \((\w+) counted templ packages, plus`),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			counted := len(countedPackages())

			return fmt.Sprintf("%d components across %d packages (%s counted templ packages, plus",
				counts.Components, counted+2, numberWord(counted))
		},
	}

	componentsPlusIcons := site{
		name:    "components+icons line",
		file:    skillDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^- (\d+) templ components \+ (\d+) icons\. Full signatures`),
		render: func(c Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("- %d templ components + %d icons. Full signatures",
				c.Components, c.Icons)
		},
	}

	errorpageHeading := site{
		name: "errorpage heading",
		file: skillDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(
			`(?m)^(#### ` + backtick + `errorpage` + backtick + ` — )(\d+)( components \+ )(\d+)( constructors \+ handler)`,
		),
		render: func(c Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d%s%d%s",
				prev[1], c.PackageCounts["errorpage"], prev[3], c.ErrorpageConstructors, prev[5])
		},
	}

	chartsHeading := site{
		name: "charts/echarts heading",
		file: skillDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(
			`(?m)^(#### ` + backtick + `charts/echarts` + backtick + ` — )(\d+)( components \(opt-in module\))`,
		),
		render: func(c Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d%s", prev[1], c.PackageCounts["charts/echarts"], prev[3])
		},
	}

	skillPackages := []string{"display", "forms", "feedback", "layout", "navigation", "htmx", "datastar"}
	//nolint:mnd // 4 = catalogueTotal, componentsPlusIcons, errorpageHeading, chartsHeading
	sites := make([]site, 0, 4+len(skillPackages))
	sites = append(sites, catalogueTotal, componentsPlusIcons, errorpageHeading, chartsHeading)

	for _, pkg := range skillPackages {
		sites = append(sites, skillPkgHeading(pkg))
	}

	return sites
}

func skillPkgHeading(pkg string) site {
	backtick := "`"

	return site{
		name:    "heading " + pkg,
		file:    skillDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^(#### ` + regexp.QuoteMeta(backtick+pkg+backtick) + ` — )(\d+)( components)`),
		render: func(c Counts, prev []string) string {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d%s", prev[1], c.PackageCounts[pkg], prev[3])
		},
	}
}

func sites() []site {
	return append(append(featuresSites(), skillSites()...), readmeSites()...)
}

// readmeSites returns the README.md per-package catalogue headings. Every
// counted package plus icons carries "### `pkg` — Prose (N components)" (the
// charts heading adds ", opt-in" inside the parens; icons counts icons, not
// components) — the prose around the number is passthrough, only N is derived.
func readmeSites() []site {
	sites := make([]site, 0, 1+len(countedPackages()))

	for _, pkg := range countedPackages() {
		sites = append(sites, readmeHeadingSite(pkg, "components"))
	}

	return append(sites, readmeHeadingSite("icons", "icons"))
}

func readmeHeadingSite(pkg, noun string) site {
	backtick := "`"

	return site{
		name: "README heading " + pkg,
		file: readmeDoc,
		pattern: regexp.MustCompile(
			`(?m)^(### ` + regexp.QuoteMeta(backtick+pkg+backtick) + ` — [^(]*\()(\d+)( ` + noun + `[^)]*\))`,
		),
		render: func(counts Counts, prev []string) string {
			count := counts.PackageCounts[pkg]
			if noun == "icons" {
				count = counts.Icons
			}

			return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d%s", prev[1], count, prev[3])
		},
	}
}

// numberWord renders small counts as words for the SKILL.md prose.
func numberWord(total int) string {
	words := []string{
		"zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six",
		"seven", "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen",
		"fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty",
	}

	if total >= 0 && total < len(words) {
		return words[total]
	}

	return strconv.Itoa(total)
}

// siteMatch locates the single occurrence of a site in content.
func siteMatch(content []byte, s site) ([]int, error) {
	locations := s.pattern.FindAllIndex(content, -1)
	if len(locations) != 1 {
		//nolint:err113 // leaf diagnostic printed for a human; there is no error to wrap
		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
			"%s: site %q matched %d times (want exactly 1) — structural drift, fix the doc or the site pattern by hand",
			s.file, s.name, len(locations),
		)
	}

	return locations[0], nil
}

// lineAt returns the 1-based line number of a byte offset.
func lineAt(content []byte, idx int) int {
	return strings.Count(string(content[:idx]), "\n") + 1
}

// docContent reads and caches one doc's bytes (cache holds read errors too).
type docContent struct {
	cache map[string][]byte
	errs  map[string]error
	root  string
}

func newDocContent(root string) *docContent {
	return &docContent{cache: map[string][]byte{}, errs: map[string]error{}, root: root}
}

func (d *docContent) get(name string) ([]byte, error) {
	if b, ok := d.cache[name]; ok {
		return b, nil
	}

	if err, ok := d.errs[name]; ok {
		return nil, err
	}

	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(d.root, name))
	if err != nil {
		d.errs[name] = fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", name, err)

		return nil, d.errs[name]
	}

	d.cache[name] = b

	return b, nil
}

// evaluate runs every site against the current docs. It yields, per site, the
// byte location of the match, its current text, and the expected text.
func evaluate(root string) ([]evalResult, error) {
	counts, err := Derive(root)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	docs := newDocContent(root)

	var results []evalResult

	for _, s := range sites() {
		content, err := docs.get(s.file)
		if err != nil {
			return results, err
		}

		location, err := siteMatch(content, s)
		if err != nil {
			return results, err
		}

		prev := captureGroups(content, location, s.pattern)
		results = append(results, evalResult{
			site:     s,
			content:  content,
			location: location,
			current:  string(content[location[0]:location[1]]),
			expected: s.render(counts, prev),
		})
	}

	return results, nil
}

type evalResult struct {
	site     site
	content  []byte
	location []int
	current  string
	expected string
}

// Check verifies both docs against the tree. Every drift is a separate error
// naming the location and telling the user how to fix it mechanically.
func Check(root string) error {
	results, err := evaluate(root)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	var problems []error

	for _, r := range results {
		if r.current == r.expected {
			continue
		}

		problems = append(
			problems,
			fmt.Errorf( //nolint:err113 // leaf diagnostic printed for a human; there is no error to wrap
				"%s:%d: site %q drifts from the tree (expected %q, found %q) — run: go run ./tools/countgen/cmd/countgen -w",
				r.site.file,
				lineAt(r.content, r.location[0]),
				r.site.name,
				r.expected,
				r.current,
			),
		)
	}

	return joinErrors(problems)
}

// Apply rewrites both docs to match the tree, returning the changed file names.
//
// Every site location was captured against the ORIGINAL doc bytes, so the
// replacements splice into a working copy from the end of the file backwards —
// applying them in site order would invalidate later offsets, and building
// each replacement from the pristine content (the 2026-11-02 shape) silently
// dropped all but the last drifted site per file.
func Apply(root string) ([]string, error) {
	results, err := evaluate(root)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	type edit struct {
		location []int
		expected string
	}

	originals := map[string][]byte{}
	editsByFile := map[string][]edit{}

	for _, r := range results {
		if r.current == r.expected {
			continue
		}

		if _, ok := originals[r.site.file]; !ok {
			originals[r.site.file] = r.content
		}

		editsByFile[r.site.file] = append(editsByFile[r.site.file], edit{location: r.location, expected: r.expected})
	}

	updated := map[string][]byte{}

	for name, edits := range editsByFile {
		sort.Slice(edits, func(i, j int) bool { return edits[i].location[0] > edits[j].location[0] })

		content := append([]byte{}, originals[name]...)

		for _, e := range edits {
			next := append([]byte{}, content[:e.location[0]]...)
			next = append(next, e.expected...)
			next = append(next, content[e.location[1]:]...)
			content = next
		}

		updated[name] = content
	}

	var written []string

	for _, name := range []string{featuresDoc, skillDoc, readmeDoc} {
		if _, dirty := updated[name]; !dirty {
			continue
		}

		//nolint:gosec // G306: 0644 matches the docs' tracked file mode
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, name), updated[name], 0o644); err != nil {
			return written, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", name, err)
		}

		written = append(written, name)
	}

	return written, nil
}

// captureGroups extracts the site pattern's capture groups for passthrough.
func captureGroups(content []byte, location []int, pattern *regexp.Regexp) []string {
	match := pattern.FindSubmatch(content[location[0]:location[1]])
	if match == nil {
		return nil
	}

	out := make([]string, 0, len(match))

	for _, m := range match {
		out = append(out, string(m))
	}

	return out
}

func joinErrors(errs []error) error {
	switch len(errs) {
	case 0:
		return nil
	case 1:
		return errs[0]
	default:
		messages := make([]string, 0, len(errs))
		for _, err := range errs {
			messages = append(messages, err.Error())
		}

		return fmt.Errorf( //nolint:err113 // aggregated diagnostic header; there is no error to wrap
			"%d count drifts:\n%s",
			len(errs),
			strings.Join(messages, "\n"),
		)
	}
}
package countgen

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// wrongNumber seeds every count-bearing doc site with a recognizably wrong
// value so Apply has something to fix; the site patterns locate the lines by
// structure, not by the number.
const wrongNumber = "99"

// syntheticTree writes a minimal tree exercising every counted axis:
// exported templ funcs (counted + ignored), icon entries (+Spinner),
// IsValid declarations (in-scope, test-file, .git, _sources, website),
// generated files, HTML goldens (in-scope + website), visual goldens
// (real + dotted-dir + .fail.png), and errorpage constructors.
func syntheticTree(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()

	root := t.TempDir()

	write := func(rel, content string) {
		t.Helper()

		path := filepath.Join(root, rel)
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("mkdir %s: %v", rel, err)
		}

		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", rel, err)
		}
	}

	write("display/alpha.templ", "templ Card() {}\n\ntempl Badge() {}\n\ntempl helper() {}\n")
	write("display/alpha_templ.go", "// generated\n")
	write("display/enums.go", "package display\n\nfunc StatusIsValid(s Status) bool { return true }\n")
	write("display/enums_test.go", "package display\n\nfunc OtherIsValid(s Other) bool { return true }\n")
	write("forms/beta.templ", "templ Input() {}\n")
	write("recipes/gamma.templ", "templ Dashboard() {}\n")

	write("icons/icon_paths.go", "package icons\n\nvar iconPathData = map[string]string{\n"+
		"\tHome:  \"M1 1\",\n"+
		"\tClose: \"M2 2\",\n"+
		"}\n")

	write(
		"errorpage/constructors.go",
		"package errorpage\n\nfunc NotFound() *Error { return nil }\n\nfunc InternalError() *Error { return nil }\n",
	)

	write("display/snapshot.golden", "<div>golden</div>\n")
	write("website/excluded.golden", "<div>excluded</div>\n")
	write("website/excluded_templ.go", "// generated, excluded\n")

	write("visualtest/testdata/routes/dashboard.png", "png")
	write("visualtest/testdata/.fail/route.png", "png")
	write("visualtest/testdata/routes/flaky.fail.png", "png")

	write(".git/ignored.go", "func GitIsValid(s string) bool { return true }\n")
	write("cmd/tc/_sources/ignored.go", "func MirrorIsValid(s string) bool { return true }\n")

	write(featuresDoc, featuresFixture())
	write(skillDoc, skillFixture())
	write(readmeDoc, readmeFixture())

	return root
}

func TestDeriveSyntheticTree(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	counts, err := Derive(syntheticTree(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Derive: %v", err)
	}

	want := Counts{
		Components:            3, // display 2 + forms 1
		PackageCounts:         map[string]int{"display": 2, "forms": 1, "recipes": 1, "icons": 0},
		Recipes:               1,
		ComponentsPlusRecipes: 4,
		Icons:                 3, // 2 entries + Spinner
		IsValid:               1, // enums.go only: test/.git/_sources excluded
		GeneratedFiles:        1, // website's excluded
		HTMLGoldens:           1, // website's excluded
		VisualGoldens:         1, // dotted dir + .fail.png excluded
		ErrorpageConstructors: 2,
	}

	for _, pkg := range countedPackages() {
		if _, ok := want.PackageCounts[pkg]; !ok && pkg != "recipes" && pkg != "icons" {
			want.PackageCounts[pkg] = 0
		}
	}

	if counts.Components != want.Components ||
		counts.Recipes != want.Recipes ||
		counts.ComponentsPlusRecipes != want.ComponentsPlusRecipes ||
		counts.Icons != want.Icons ||
		counts.IsValid != want.IsValid ||
		counts.GeneratedFiles != want.GeneratedFiles ||
		counts.HTMLGoldens != want.HTMLGoldens ||
		counts.VisualGoldens != want.VisualGoldens ||
		counts.ErrorpageConstructors != want.ErrorpageConstructors {
		t.Fatalf("Derive = %+v, want %+v", counts, want)
	}

	for pkg, wantCount := range want.PackageCounts {
		if got := counts.PackageCounts[pkg]; got != wantCount {
			t.Errorf("PackageCounts[%s] = %d, want %d", pkg, got, wantCount)
		}
	}
}

func TestCheckDriftApplyFixesIdempotence(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	root := syntheticTree(t)

	err := Check(root)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Check on drifted docs: want error, got nil")
	}

	for _, site := range []string{"Totals line", "icons table row", "heading display"} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), site) {
			t.Errorf("Check error missing site %q:\n%v", site, err)
		}
	}

	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "go run ./tools/countgen/cmd/countgen -w") {
		t.Errorf("Check error missing the fix command:\n%v", err)
	}

	changed, err := Apply(root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Apply: %v", err)
	}

	if len(changed) != 3 || changed[0] != featuresDoc || changed[1] != skillDoc || changed[2] != readmeDoc {
		t.Fatalf("Apply changed = %v, want [%s %s %s]", changed, featuresDoc, skillDoc, readmeDoc)
	}

	if err := Check(root); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Check after Apply: %v", err)
	}

	if changed, err := Apply(root); err != nil || len(changed) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("second Apply = %v, %v; want no writes (idempotence)", changed, err)
	}

	assertDocContains(
		t,
		root,
		featuresDoc,
		"**Totals:** 3 templ components (primitives, drift-guard verified) + 1 recipe screens = 4, 3 icon names, 74 typed enums (1 with `IsValid()`, 1 generated `*_templ.go` files",
	)
	assertDocContains(t, root, featuresDoc, "| `display` | 2 |")
	assertDocContains(t, root, featuresDoc, "| `icons` | 0 (3 icons)")
	assertDocContains(t, root, skillDoc,
		"3 components across 11 packages (nine counted templ packages, plus `utils` and `icons`)")
	assertDocContains(t, root, skillDoc, "#### `errorpage` — 0 components + 2 constructors + handler")
	assertDocContains(t, root, skillDoc, "#### `display` — 2 components")
	assertDocContains(t, root, readmeDoc, "### `display` — Some Prose (2 components)")
	assertDocContains(t, root, readmeDoc, "### `icons` — SVG Icons (3 icons)")
	assertDocContains(t, root, readmeDoc, "### `charts/echarts` — Some Prose (0 components)")
}

func TestCheckStructuralDriftMultiMatch(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	root := syntheticTree(t)

	features, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, featuresDoc))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", featuresDoc, err)
	}

	totals := strings.Split(string(features), "\n")
	doubled := make([]string, 0, len(totals)+1)

	for _, line := range totals {
		doubled = append(doubled, line)
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "**Totals:**") {
			doubled = append(doubled, line)
		}
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, featuresDoc), []byte(strings.Join(doubled, "\n")), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", featuresDoc, err)
	}

	err = Check(root)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Check with a duplicated totals line: want structural-drift error, got nil")
	}

	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `matched 2 times (want exactly 1)`) {
		t.Errorf("error missing multi-match diagnosis:\n%v", err)
	}
}

		{total: 0, want: "zero"},
		{total: 9, want: "nine"},

func assertDocContains(t *testing.T, root, name, want string) {
	t.Helper()

	content, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", name, err)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(string(content), want) {
		t.Errorf("%s missing %q", name, want)
	}
}

// TestSSEErrorHandlingA11y is the accessibility lens for the global SSE error
// handler: every failure path must reach a non-sighted user even when the
// toast container is missing.
func TestSSEErrorHandlingA11y(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("announcer region exists and is visually hidden", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<div id="tc-datastar-announcer" aria-live="polite" class="sr-only"></div>`)
	})

	t.Run("announcements feed the aria-live region via textContent", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))

		// Screen readers announce textContent changes on aria-live regions.
		// The handler must not use innerHTML (injection) or create/remove
		// nodes (some screen readers miss region creation).
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "announcer.textContent = text")
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "announcer.innerHTML")
	})

	t.Run("announcer is polite, not assertive", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))

		// Stream errors are important but not emergencies: polite queueing
		// avoids interrupting the user mid-sentence. The region is declared
		// once at render time (a11y best practice).
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-live="polite"`)
	})

	t.Run("both failure paths announce through the same region", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `announce('Stream error' + status)`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "announce('Live stream lost. Automatic reconnection failed.')")
	})
}

// TestSSEErrorHandlingCSP pins the security lens: the inline script must be
// nonced (the integration CSP test covers the cross-package invariant; this
// keeps the package-local guarantee explicit).
func TestSSEErrorHandlingCSP(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(SSEErrorHandlingConfig{Nonce: "a11y-nonce"}))

	utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<script nonce="a11y-nonce">`)
}

package datastar

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

// Typed builders for the Datastar runtime's reactive plugins — the CLIENT
// half of the attribute surface (the request half is utils/wire, ADR-0036).
// Every builder returns templ.Attributes: spread them into any element
// (`<span ${ datastar.Text("$user.name") }>`) and templ renders the value
// escaped. Empty names/expressions degrade to nil — a builder without its
// inputs renders nothing instead of a broken binding (the graceful-
// degradation rule every library component follows).
//
// Scope note (JS decision ladder, docs/javascript-guide.md): these builders
// exist for consumers' OWN glue — dashboard widgets, exploratory UIs,
// reactive islands. The library's components stay native-first/htmx-first;
// no component is re-ported to signals.

// signalSegmentGrammar is the attribute-suffix-safe signal grammar: lowercase
// segments (the HTML parser lowercases attribute NAMES, so an uppercase
// segment would silently bind a different signal than the expression reads —
// see runtime-facts §CSP caveats), digits and underscores allowed, dotted
// paths for nested signals. A leading underscore marks a LOCAL signal (never
// sent to the backend: the runtime's default filterSignals exclude
// /(^|\.)_/). Double underscores are banned — they are the MODIFIER delimiter
// (data-on:click__debounce…), so a signal carrying them can never round-trip
// through an attribute suffix.
var signalSegmentGrammar = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9_]+$`)

// SignalName is a validated Datastar signal name for attribute-suffix
// bindings (data-bind:<name>, data-computed:<name>). Not a closed enum — an
// open validated type: there is no fixed value set, so there is no
// SignalNameDefault constant; IsValid is the contract, its test lives in
// attributes_test.go (same commit rule).
type SignalName string

// IsValid reports whether the name is safe to embed in an attribute suffix:
// one or more lowercase word segments separated by dots, no "__" anywhere
// (the modifier delimiter), no empty segments.
func (s SignalName) IsValid() bool {
	name := string(s)
	if name == "" || strings.Contains(name, "__") {
		return false
	}

	for segment := range strings.SplitSeq(name, ".") {
		if !signalSegmentGrammar.MatchString(segment) {
			return false
		}
	}

	return true
}

// eventGrammar constrains handler events to real DOM/custom-event names:
// letters, digits, dashes and dots (e.g. click, keydown, datastar-fetch).
// Anything else cannot be an event and would corrupt the attribute NAME —
// rejected (renders nothing) rather than escaped, unlike expression VALUES
// which escape safely.
var eventGrammar = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$`)

// normalizeExpr makes a consumer expression safe AS AN ATTRIBUTE VALUE: CR/LF
// collapse to spaces (one statement line). Quotes and angle brackets pass
// through VERBATELY — they are expression CODE (string literals like
// @get('/x'), comparisons) that the runtime parses, and the HTML attribute
// layer is escaped by templ at render time. The builders never interpolate
// user input INTO an expression; they only carry one.
func normalizeExpr(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\r", " ")
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\n", " ")

	return s
}

// attrsOrNil collapses an empty attribute map to nil so `…${ nil }…` renders
// nothing.
func attrsOrNil(attrs templ.Attributes) templ.Attributes {
	if len(attrs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	return attrs
}

// exprBinding is the shared body of the single-attribute expression
// builders: an empty expression renders nothing (the graceful-degradation
// rule), everything else passes through the attribute-value normalizer.
func exprBinding(key, expr string) templ.Attributes {
	if expr == "" {
		return nil
	}

	return templ.Attributes{key: normalizeExpr(expr)}
}

// Show binds an element's visibility to an expression (data-show): the
// element renders when the expression is truthy.
//
//	<span ${ datastar.Show("$user.admin") }>secrets</span>
func Show(expr string) templ.Attributes {
	return exprBinding("data-show", expr)
}

// Text binds an element's text content to an expression (data-text): the
// node re-renders whenever any referenced signal changes.
//
//	<dd ${ datastar.Text("$metrics.users") }>0</dd>
func Text(expr string) templ.Attributes {
	return exprBinding("data-text", expr)
}

// Bind two-ways an input element to a signal (data-bind:<name>): element
// edits write the signal, signal patches write the element.
//
//	<input ${ datastar.Bind("email") }>
func Bind(name SignalName) templ.Attributes {
	if !name.IsValid() {
		return nil
	}

	return templ.Attributes{"data-bind:" + string(name): ""}
}

// Computed declares a derived signal (data-computed:<name>): the expression
// re-evaluates when its signal dependencies change.
//
//	<div ${ datastar.Computed("total", "$price * $qty") }>
func Computed(name SignalName, expr string) templ.Attributes {
	if !name.IsValid() || expr == "" {
		return nil
	}

	return templ.Attributes{"data-computed:" + string(name): normalizeExpr(expr)}
}

// Signals declares initial signal values (data-signals): the JSON object
// deep-merges into the signal tree at init. Keys are VALUE-borne (JSON), so
// camelCase keys are safe here — the attribute-name-lowercasing gotcha does
// not apply. A payload that cannot marshal to JSON degrades to nil.
func Signals(values map[string]any) templ.Attributes {
	if len(values) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	buf, err := json.Marshal(values)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}

	return templ.Attributes{"data-signals": string(buf)}
}

// On wires an event to an expression (data-on:<event>) with the runtime's
// modifier groups spelled the pinned-bundle way (data-on:click__debounce.300ms,
// data-on:submit__prevent — groups only parse after __, never as a dotted
// suffix). Chain modifiers with value receivers; the zero-chained form is the
// plain handler. An empty event or expression renders nothing.
//
//	<button ${ datastar.On("click", "$count++").Debounce(300) }>go</button>
type OnExpr struct {
	event      string
	expr       string
	debounceMS int
	throttleMS int
	prevent    bool
}

// On starts an event-handler builder.
func On(event, expr string) OnExpr {
	return OnExpr{event: event, expr: expr} //nolint:exhaustruct_v5 // zero values are the no-modifier defaults
}

// Debounce adds the __debounce.<n>ms modifier (trailing-edge; the runtime's
// leading/notrailing sub-modifiers are not modeled — use raw attrs for those).
func (o OnExpr) Debounce(ms int) OnExpr {
	o.debounceMS = ms

	return o
}

// Throttle adds the __throttle.<n>ms modifier (leading-edge default).
func (o OnExpr) Throttle(ms int) OnExpr {
	o.throttleMS = ms

	return o
}

// Prevent adds the __prevent modifier (suppresses the event's native
// default — required for wired anchors whose href is the no-JS fallback).
func (o OnExpr) Prevent() OnExpr {
	o.prevent = true

	return o
}

// Attrs renders the builder. Modifiers require the explicit event (an orphan
// modifier is dropped by design — see wire.Action's documented rule). An
// event that is not a plausible DOM/custom-event name renders nothing.
func (o OnExpr) Attrs() templ.Attributes {
	if o.event == "" || o.expr == "" || !eventGrammar.MatchString(o.event) {
		return nil
	}

	key := "data-on:" + o.event

	if o.prevent {
		key += "__prevent"
	}

	if o.debounceMS > 0 {
		key += fmt.Sprintf("__debounce.%dms", o.debounceMS)
	}

	if o.throttleMS > 0 {
		key += fmt.Sprintf("__throttle.%dms", o.throttleMS)
	}

	return attrsOrNil(templ.Attributes{key: normalizeExpr(o.expr)})
}
package datastar

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
	templruntime "github.com/a-h/templ/runtime"
)

// Fuzz builders (plan T13): hostile inputs must never panic, never produce
// more than one attribute per builder call, never emit a key that is not a
// plausible data-* attribute name, and never smuggle a URL scheme into a
// NAME position (names are grammar-validated; expressions are consumer code
// carried verbatim). Run: go test -fuzz=FuzzBuilders -time=30s (the seed
// corpus runs in normal `go test` too).

func fuzzCheckAttrs(t *testing.T, name string, attrs templ.Attributes) {
	t.Helper()

	if attrs == nil {
		return
	}

	if len(attrs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: want at most one attribute, got %d (%#v)", name, len(attrs), attrs)
	}

	for key, value := range attrs {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "data-") {
			t.Fatalf("%s: key %q is not a data-* attribute", name, key)
		}

		if strings.Contains(key, "://") || strings.Contains(key, "javascript:") {
			t.Fatalf("%s: key %q smuggles a URL scheme", name, key)
		}

		if _, ok := value.(string); !ok && value != "" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: value %T is not a string", name, value)
		}
	}
}

func FuzzBuilders(f *testing.F) {
	f.Add("$count++", "click", "users")
	f.Add(`'; alert(1); '`, "click", "Users")
	f.Add("@get('/x')", "keydown", "metrics.users")
	f.Add("<script>alert(1)</script>", "datastar-fetch", "__bad")
	f.Add("$a\n$b", "load", "_local")

	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, expr, event, name string) {
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "Show", Show(expr))
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "Text", Text(expr))
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "Bind", Bind(SignalName(name)))
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "Computed", Computed(SignalName(name), expr))

		// Signals: hostile strings ride as JSON VALUES — the payload must
		// marshal or degrade to nil, never panic.
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "Signals", Signals(map[string]any{
			"fuzz": map[string]any{"expr": expr, "name": name},
		}))

		chain := On(event, expr).Prevent().Debounce(100).Throttle(100)
		fuzzCheckAttrs(t, "On", chain.Attrs())
	})
}

// TestBuildersRenderSafeAttributes is the static no-injection guard: for
// hostile seeds, the RENDERED attribute output (what templ writes into HTML)
// stays inside a quoted attribute value — no raw quote, no tag boundary can
// appear outside the value's opening/closing quotes, because templ escapes
// the value at render time. The guard pins that contract for the builders'
// outputs specifically.
func TestBuildersRenderSafeAttributes(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	hostile := map[string]templ.Attributes{
		"show":     Show(`'$x' + "</span><script>alert(1)</script>"`),
		"computed": Computed("ok", `"</div>`+"`"+`"`),
		"on":       On("click", `'; fetch("//evil.example") ; '`).Attrs(),
	}

	var b strings.Builder

	for name, attrs := range hostile {
		b.Reset()

		if _, err := b.WriteString("<span"); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("seed writer: %v", err)
		}

		if err := templruntime.RenderAttributes(context.TODO(), &b, &b, "span", attrs); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: render hostile attrs: %v", name, err)
		}

		if _, err := b.WriteString("></span>"); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("seed writer close: %v", err)
		}

		rendered := b.String()

		// The invariant: the FIRST raw double quote after the value's opening
		// quote must be the value's closing quote, immediately followed by
		// the tag end — templ's HTML escaping (&#34; etc.) must have consumed
		// every hostile quote INSIDE the value, so nothing escapes the
		// attribute boundary.
		_, value, valueFound := strings.Cut(rendered, `="`)
		if !valueFound {
			t.Fatalf("%s: no attribute value found in %q", name, rendered)
		}

		// The FIRST raw double quote must close the value and sit right
		// against the tag end: templ's HTML escaping consumed every hostile
		// quote inside, so nothing escapes the attribute boundary.
		_, afterClose, closeFound := strings.Cut(value, `"`)
		if !closeFound || afterClose != "></span>" {
			t.Errorf("%s: hostile value broke the attribute boundary: %q", name, rendered)
		}
	}
}
package datastar

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

// TestSignalNameIsValid pins the attribute-suffix-safe signal grammar
// (lowercase segments, dotted paths, `_`-local prefix, `__` banned — the
// modifier delimiter). Same-commit rule: no IsValid without a test.
func TestSignalNameIsValid(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, tt := range []struct {
		name  string
		valid bool
	}{
		{"users", true},
		{"metrics.users", true},
		{"_local_draft", true},
		{"metrics._transient", true},
		{"user2.name_2", true},
		{"", false},
		{"Users", false},               // attribute names lowercase — uppercase would silently mismatch
		{"camelCase", false},           // use VALUE-borne data-signals JSON for camelCase keys
		{"metrics__deep", false},       // __ is the modifier delimiter
		{"a..b", false},                // empty segment
		{".users", false},              // leading empty segment
		{"users.", false},              // trailing empty segment
		{"has space", false},           // no spaces
		{"has-dash", false},            // dashes are the attribute key delimiter
		{"javascript:alert(1)", false}, // scheme injection
	} {
		if got := SignalName(tt.name).IsValid(); got != tt.valid {
			t.Errorf("SignalName(%q).IsValid() = %v, want %v", tt.name, got, tt.valid)
		}
	}
}

// TestBuildersDegradeToNil pins the graceful-degradation rule: a builder
// without its inputs renders nothing instead of a broken binding.
func TestBuildersDegradeToNil(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for name, attrs := range map[string]templ.Attributes{
		"Show":        Show(""),
		"Text":        Text(""),
		"Bind":        Bind(""),
		"BindInvalid": Bind("Users"),
		"Computed":    Computed("total", ""),
		"Signals":     Signals(nil),
		"On":          On("", "$count++").Attrs(),
		"OnExpr":      On("click", "").Attrs(),
		"OnBadEvent":  On(`click'`, "$count++").Attrs(),
		"OnNoMods":    On("click", "$x").Attrs(),
	} {
		if name == "OnNoMods" {
			if attrs == nil {
				t.Errorf("On with valid inputs must render")

				continue
			}

			continue
		}

		if attrs != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s with empty/invalid inputs must degrade to nil, got %#v", name, attrs)
		}
	}
}

// TestBuilderSpelling pins the pinned-runtime attribute spellings: plugin
// keys, modifier groups after __ (never a dotted suffix — the
// data-on:click.prevent never-fires trap), and the debounce duration unit.
func TestBuilderSpelling(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		attrs     templ.Attributes
		wantKey   string
		wantValue string
	}{
		{"show", Show("$visible"), "data-show", "$visible"},
		{"text", Text("$user.name"), "data-text", "$user.name"},
		{"bind", Bind("email"), "data-bind:email", ""},
		{"computed", Computed("total", "$price * $qty"), "data-computed:total", "$price * $qty"},
		{"on-plain", On("click", "$count++").Attrs(), "data-on:click", "$count++"},
		{"on-prevent", On("click", "@get('/x')").Prevent().Attrs(), "data-on:click__prevent", "@get('/x')"},
		{"on-debounce", On("input", "@get('/s')").Debounce(300).Attrs(), "data-on:input__debounce.300ms", "@get('/s')"},
		{
			"on-chain", On("submit", "@post('/f')").Prevent().Debounce(120).Throttle(80).Attrs(),
			"data-on:submit__prevent__debounce.120ms__throttle.80ms", "@post('/f')",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range cases {
		value, ok := tt.attrs[tt.wantKey]
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("%s: missing key %q in %#v", tt.name, tt.wantKey, tt.attrs)

			continue
		}

		if value != tt.wantValue {
			t.Errorf("%s: %q = %q, want %q", tt.name, tt.wantKey, value, tt.wantValue)
		}

		if len(tt.attrs) != 1 {
			t.Errorf("%s: want exactly one attribute, got %#v", tt.name, tt.attrs)
		}
	}
}

// TestSignalsBuilder pins the JSON-object form (value-borne keys, so
// camelCase is safe here) and the JSON-marshallable contract.
func TestSignalsBuilder(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	attrs := Signals(map[string]any{"metrics": map[string]any{"users": 5, "camelsRock": true}})
	raw, ok := attrs["data-signals"]

	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("data-signals missing: %#v", attrs)
	}

	var decoded map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw.(string)), &decoded); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("data-signals must be valid JSON: %v (%q)", err, raw)
	}

	if !strings.Contains(raw.(string), `"camelsRock":true`) {
		t.Errorf("camelCase keys must survive verbatim: %q", raw)
	}

	// Non-marshalable payloads degrade to nil (channels, funcs).
	if Signals(map[string]any{"bad": make(chan int)}) != nil {
		t.Error("non-marshalable Signals payload must degrade to nil")
	}
}

// TestNormalizeExpr pins the expression-value contract: CR/LF collapse to
// spaces (one statement line), while quotes and angle brackets pass through
// VERBATIM — they are expression code (string literals like @get('/x'),
// comparisons) that the runtime parses; the HTML attribute layer is escaped
// by templ at render time. Escaping quotes here would MANGLE every
// datastar.Get-constructed expression.
func TestNormalizeExpr(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	expr := Get("/api/x")

	if got := normalizeExpr(expr); got != expr {
		t.Errorf("normalizeExpr must leave expression code verbatim: got %q", got)
	}

	if got := normalizeExpr("a\nb\rc"); got != "a b c" {
		t.Errorf("normalizeExpr must collapse CR/LF to spaces: got %q", got)
	}
}

func TestSDKScriptUserGetsDatastarRuntime(t *testing.T) {

	t.Run("user sees ES module script tag with CDN URL", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `<script type="module"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `src="`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "starfederation/datastar")
	})

	t.Run("user gets self-hosted script when Src is set", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

			Src: "/assets/datastar.js",

		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "cdn.jsdelivr.net")
	})

	t.Run("script always carries CSP nonce for security", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SDKScript(SDKScriptProps{
			Nonce: "nonce-abc-789",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `nonce="nonce-abc-789"`)
	})
}

// --- LiveRegion Behavior ---

func TestLiveRegionUserSeesAutoStreamingContent(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("region auto-connects to SSE on page load", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(LiveRegionProps{
			URL:       "/stream/metrics",
			AutoStart: true,
		}))
		utils.AssertContainsAll(t, output, "data-init", "@get(", "/stream/metrics")
	})

	t.Run("manual start omits data-init attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(LiveRegionProps{
			URL:       "/stream/data",
			AutoStart: false,
		}))
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "data-init")
	})

	t.Run("region announces streamed updates politely by default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(DefaultLiveRegionProps()))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-live="polite"`)
	})

	t.Run("auto-connected region signals loading until the first patch arrives", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(LiveRegionProps{
			URL:       "/stream/metrics",
			AutoStart: true,
		}))
		// aria-busy=true between page load and the first datastar-patch-*
		// event gives screen readers a loading cue instead of silence; the
		// singleton script removes it once patches flow (or the stream
		// fails terminally) so live content is announced.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-busy="true"`)
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "datastar-patch-elements")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "removeAttribute('aria-busy')")
	})

	t.Run("invalid politeness falls back to polite gracefully", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(LiveRegionProps{
			Live: "invalid-value",
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-live="polite"`)
	})

	t.Run("consumer can set assertive for critical alerts", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, LiveRegion(LiveRegionProps{
			Live: LiveAssertive,
		}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `aria-live="assertive"`)
	})
}

// --- SSEErrorHandling Behavior ---

func TestSSEErrorHandlingUserIsToldAboutStreamFailures(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("screen reader hears about an HTTP stream error", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		// The 'error' branch writes to the polite announcer...
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `announce('Stream error' + status)`)
		// ...and includes the HTTP status so the user can judge severity.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `' (HTTP ' + args.status + ')'`)
	})

	t.Run("screen reader hears when reconnection gives up", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "announce('Live stream lost. Automatic reconnection failed.')")
	})

	t.Run("user gets a recovery action when reconnection fails", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		// The toast copy must tell the user HOW to recover, not just that
		// something broke.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "Reload the page to resume.")
	})

	t.Run("transient retries stay quiet for the user", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		// The 'retrying' branch logs to console only: the runtime keeps
		// reconnecting on its own, and announcing every attempt would spam
		// screen readers and toast stacks.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, `detail.type === 'retrying'`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, `announce('Stream interrupted`)
		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "tcShowToast('DataStar stream interrupted")
	})

	t.Run("toast is best-effort: absence of the toast container must not throw", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		// Guards both call sites with a typeof check so pages without
		// feedback.ToastContainer still get console + announcer feedback.
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "typeof tcShowToast === 'function'")
	})

	t.Run("toasts carry the error type so they render as error feedback", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(DefaultSSEErrorHandlingConfig()))
		// tcShowToast(message, type, title, duration) — type 'error' selects
		// the error toast styling (red border, error icon).
		utils.AssertContains(
			t,
			output,
			`tcShowToast('The live stream endpoint returned an error' + status + '.', 'error', 'Stream Error', DURATION)`,
		)
		utils.AssertContains(
			t,
			output,
			`tcShowToast('The live stream was lost and automatic reconnection failed. Reload the page to resume.', 'error', 'Connection Lost', DURATION)`,
		)
	})

	t.Run("toasts auto-dismiss after the configured duration", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		output := utils.Render(t, SSEErrorHandling(SSEErrorHandlingConfig{DurationMS: 4500}))
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "var DURATION = 4500;")
		utils.AssertContains(t, output, "DURATION)")
	})
}

package datastar

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/go-datastar/static"
)

// pinnedBundleSHA256 is the SHA-256 of the embedded runtime bundle
// (static.Bytes()) at go-datastar/static v0.5.0 → v0.6.1 — Datastar 1.0.3,
// 33538 bytes. Re-audited 2026-09-05 on the v0.4.0 → v0.5.0 bump (the bundle
// shrank, 56330 → 33538 bytes, upstream minification refactor; the retry
// machinery retryInterval/retryMax/retryMaxCount + auto/error/never/always
// literals survived) and re-verified 2026-10-02 on the v0.5.0 → v0.6.1 bump:
// BYTE-IDENTICAL (same sha256), so every pinned token carried over.
// Re-audited 2026-11-17 on the v0.6.1 → v0.7.0 bump (Datastar 1.0.3 → 1.0.4,
// 33553 bytes): minifier identifier renames throughout, the error formatter
// rewritten (multi-line `More info:`/`Context:` template), the CSP machinery
// now assembles the data-nonce attribute name at runtime (j("nonce") — the
// bare literal is no longer byte-present), the empty-nonce throw became the
// typed NonceRequired error, and expression compilation gained an explicit
// "Blocked by CSP." throw. Mechanism unchanged; every functional token
// re-verified present.
const pinnedBundleSHA256 = "727844adfc825ee651fb93c544a2a739986f9a21820a94524b35f0cac470cf91"

// TestPinnedRuntimeBundleContract pins the runtime surface this library
// integrates against, as verified byte-for-byte in the embedded bundle.
// SSEErrorHandling was inert for its entire life because it listened for a
// "datastar-sse-error" event that the runtime never dispatched — string
// assertions against our own output cannot catch that class of bug.
//
// A go-datastar/static version bump that renames or removes any pinned
// token fails here, forcing a re-audit of the integration instead of a
// silent breakage in LiveRegion, SSEErrorHandling, or the demo wire format.
func TestPinnedRuntimeBundleContract(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	bundle := string(static.Bytes())

	for _, token := range []string{
		// The only lifecycle observability surface: SSEErrorHandling
		// listens to this document CustomEvent (detail.type is
		// started/finished/error/retrying/retries-failed).
		"datastar-fetch",
		// The only SSE event names with registered handlers in v1.x —
		// the demo stream and go-datastar's PatchElements emit these.
		"datastar-patch-elements",
		"datastar-patch-signals",
		// Retry-mode literals consumed by LiveRegionProps.Retry
		// ("always" also appears in the retry comparison chain).
		`"always"`,
		`"error"`,
		`"never"`,
		// Request-cancellation option consumed by
		// LiveRegionProps.Cancellation — under cleanup mode the runtime
		// aborts the in-flight stream when the element leaves the DOM.
		"requestCancellation",
		// Form-serialization machinery consumed by wire.ContentTypeForm
		// (forms.Form Wires dual-transport submission): the fetch option
		// selecting form-field serialization over the signals-JSON default,
		// and the two failure paths (no enclosing form / unknown type).
		"contentType",
		"FetchFormNotFound",
		"FetchInvalidContentType",
		// Interval-polling plugin consumed by PolledRegion (ADR-0042): the
		// plugin name (attribute data-on-interval), the duration modifier,
		// and the leading flag (an element of the duration mod set, not a
		// separate group — PolledRegion deliberately never emits it).
		`name:"on-interval"`,
		`name:"on-intersect"`,
		"duration",
		"leading",
		// CSP-mode machinery (decoded 2026-11-07, see runtime-facts §CSP;
		// re-audited 2026-11-17 on the 1.0.4 bump): the runtime reads
		// data-nonce from documentElement ONCE at init — as of 1.0.4 the
		// attribute name is ASSEMBLED at runtime (j("nonce") → "data-nonce"),
		// so the byte-provable literals are the "nonce" argument, the typed
		// NonceRequired error (was a literal message), and the explicit
		// "Blocked by CSP." throw on expression-compile rejection. When
		// data-nonce is present and nonempty, expressions execute as nonce'd
		// inline scripts instead of Function() eval, so script-src 'nonce-…'
		// suffices without 'unsafe-eval'. trustedTypes is the self-registered
		// identity policy used under Trusted Types enforcement. A pin bump
		// that drops any of these fails here before a consumer CSP flips.
		`"nonce"`,
		"NonceRequired",
		"Blocked by CSP.",
		"trustedTypes",
		"createPolicy",
		// Verified present but UNMODELED surface (runtime-facts §"Verified
		// present, unmodeled"): the signal-patch listener plugin (attribute
		// data-on-signal-patch; plugin registrations are name:"…" literals,
		// the data- prefixes assemble at runtime, so only this literal is
		// byte-provable), the view-transition-selector dataline, and the
		// fetch options / datalines below.
		`name:"on-signal-patch"`,
		"viewTransitionSelector",
		"filterSignals",
		"openWhenHidden",
		"onlyIfMissing",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(bundle, token) {
			t.Errorf(
				"pinned runtime bundle v%s no longer contains %q — the Datastar integration is broken; re-audit against the new bundle",
				static.Version,
				token,
			)
		}
	}

	// The event SSEErrorHandling originally listened for never existed in
	// v1.x. If a future bundle dispatches it, prefer listening to it again
	// over the datastar-fetch lifecycle approximation.
	if strings.Contains(bundle, "datastar-sse-error") {
		t.Log("bundle now dispatches datastar-sse-error — consider migrating SSEErrorHandling back to it")
	}

	// Byte-integrity pin: the token assertions above tolerate arbitrary new
	// bytes as long as every pinned token survives. This hash closes that
	// gap — any byte-level bundle change fails here and forces a conscious
	// re-audit (docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md) before the pin is updated.
	sum := sha256.Sum256(static.Bytes())
	if got := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]); got != pinnedBundleSHA256 {
		t.Errorf(
			"embedded bundle sha256 changed: got %s, want %s (static v%s) — re-audit per docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md",
			got,
			pinnedBundleSHA256,
			static.Version,
		)
	}
}

// TestDatastarVersionConstantNameMatchesValue guards the literal behind
// DatastarVersion1_0_4. Its value is derived from static.Version, so a
// go-datastar/static bump silently re-points the value while the NAME still
// claims 1.0.4 — a name that lies about its value is worse than none. On
// failure: re-audit the new runtime, rename the constant, update references.
func TestDatastarVersionConstantNameMatchesValue(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if got := string(DatastarVersion1_0_4); got != "1.0.4" {
		t.Errorf(
			"DatastarVersion1_0_4 = %q — static.Version moved and the constant name no longer tells the truth; re-audit the new bundle, rename the constant, and update references",
			got,
		)
	}

	// The compat aliases are deliberate LITERALS (never derived), so their
	// names keep telling the truth even when the pin moves again.
	if got := string(DatastarVersion1_0_3); got != "1.0.3" {
		t.Errorf("DatastarVersion1_0_3 compat alias = %q, want literal %q",
			got, "1.0.3")
	}

	if got := string(DatastarVersion1_0_2); got != "1.0.2" {
		t.Errorf("DatastarVersion1_0_2 compat alias = %q, want literal %q",
			got, "1.0.2")
	}
}
package datastar

// RequestCancellation controls what happens to an in-flight @get stream
// request when the element carrying data-init is removed from the DOM —
// typically an HTMX swap that replaces the region with a new instance
// pointing at a different URL.
type RequestCancellation string

const (
	// CancellationNone is the default: the option is omitted from the
	// action expression and the in-flight request survives element
	// removal. This is the runtime's own default behaviour.
	CancellationNone RequestCancellation = ""
	// CancellationCleanup aborts the request when its initiating element
	// is removed from the DOM. Without it, a swapped-out region's old
	// stream keeps running and re-patches the region with stale content
	// that races the replacement's stream.
	CancellationCleanup RequestCancellation = "cleanup"
)

// validRequestCancellation are the allowed requestCancellation option values.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level validation set
var validRequestCancellation = map[RequestCancellation]bool{
	CancellationNone: true, CancellationCleanup: true,
}

// requestCancellationValue returns c if valid, otherwise falls back to none.
func requestCancellationValue(c RequestCancellation) RequestCancellation {
	if validRequestCancellation[c] {
		return c
	}

	return CancellationNone
}
// Package datastar provides templ components and helpers for integrating
// [Datastar] — a zero-dependency frontend framework that unifies
// HTMX-style backend reactivity with Alpine.js-style frontend reactivity via
// Server-Sent Events (SSE) and reactive signals. The pinned v1.0.4 bundle is
// 33,553 bytes raw; upstream advertises 11.90 KiB on an unverified basis.
//
// This package mirrors the [htmx] package: it emits data-* attributes and
// injects the Datastar runtime <script> tag without importing any server-side
// SDK. The pinned version ([DatastarVersion1_0_4]) is derived from
// [github.com/larsartmann/go-datastar/static].Version so the CDN URL and the
// embedded bundle can never drift.
//
// # Server-side SDK
//
// Consumers who want SSE streaming should use
// [github.com/larsartmann/go-datastar] — a protocol library where every patch
// is a first-class value (not a method call on a live connection). Add it to
// your own go.mod:
//
//	go get github.com/larsartmann/go-datastar
//
// # Self-hosting the Datastar runtime
//
// By default, SDKScript loads the runtime from the jsDelivr CDN. For
// self-hosting, use [github.com/larsartmann/go-datastar/static] (zero
// dependencies — its go.mod requires nothing):
//
//	mux.Handle("GET /datastar.js", http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
//	    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/javascript; charset=utf-8")
//	    _, _ = w.Write(static.Bytes())
//	}))
//	@datastar.SDKScript(datastar.SDKScriptProps{Src: "/datastar.js"})
//
// # Quick start
//
// Inject the runtime once per page (in your layout, alongside or instead of
// the HTMX script):
//
//	@datastar.SDKScript(datastar.DefaultSDKScriptProps())
//
// Establish an SSE-powered live region:
//
//	@datastar.LiveRegion(datastar.LiveRegionProps{
//	    URL:       "/stream/metrics",
//	    AutoStart: true,
//	}) {
//	    @display.StatCard(display.StatCardProps{
//	        BaseProps: utils.BaseProps{ID: "metrics"},
//	        Label:     "Active Users",
//	        Value:     "—",
//	    })
//	}
//
// Two options are load-bearing on real deployments:
//
//   - Retry: RetryAlways — the runtime default ('auto') never reconnects
//     after a clean stream EOF, which is exactly what a server restart
//     produces. Without it the region goes permanently stale.
//   - Cancellation: CancellationCleanup — when an HTMX swap replaces the
//     region (e.g. a filter change re-renders it with a different URL),
//     cleanup aborts the old stream so it cannot keep re-patching the
//     region with stale content. The swapped-region combination renders
//     @get(url, {retry: 'always', requestCancellation: 'cleanup'}).
//
// The server endpoint streams patches using go-datastar. Target a child
// element by selector — patch modes other than the default outer mode
// require one, and the default outer mode matches incoming root elements
// by their id (id-less fragments are dropped with a console warning):
//
//	func streamHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
//	    stream := sse.NewStream(w, r)
//	    defer func() { _ = stream.Close() }()
//	    resp := datastar.NewResponse(stream)
//	    _ = resp.PatchElementsTempl(metricsCardContent(),
//	        datastar.WithSelector("#metrics"), datastar.WithModeInner())
//	}
//
// # Patched fragments carry no executable scripts
//
// The runtime inserts patched elements with innerHTML/morph semantics, and
// script elements inserted via innerHTML are inert — they are NEVER executed.
// This differs from htmx, which re-evaluates scripts in swapped content. A
// server patch therefore cannot ship behavior as an inline <script> tag:
// drive client-side reactions with data-* attributes and expressions on the
// patched elements instead (bundle-proven fact — see
// docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md, "Fragments carry no executable scripts").
//
// # When to choose Datastar over HTMX
//
// See docs/research/datastar-integration-analysis.md for the full analysis.
// Briefly: HTMX is the default (zero JS dependency). Datastar is opt-in for
// real-time streaming, reactive client-side state, or when the consumer's app
// already uses Datastar.
//
// # Re-audit contract (for contributors)
//
// The runtime bundle this package integrates against is an EXTERNAL
// dependency pinned in go.mod (go-datastar/static). Its wire behavior is
// documented in docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md (with a bundle-provenance
// block: pin version, byte size, sha256, extraction commands) and enforced
// by tests:
//
//   - datastar.TestPinnedRuntimeBundleContract pins the bundle sha256 plus
//     every integration token (event names, retry literals) — a pin bump
//     that changes any pinned byte fails there first.
//   - examples/demo/sse_test.go pins the SSE wire format the demo streams.
//
// When bumping the pin, follow docs/external-dependency-bumps.md end to end:
// verify-at-source, diff old-vs-new bundle, bump, re-audit every fact in
// docs/datastar-runtime-facts.md, update pinnedBundleSHA256 in
// bundle_guard_test.go, and warm [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.
//
// [Datastar]: https://data-star.dev/
// [htmx]: https://htmx.org
package datastar
package datastar
