// TestScriptComponentContextNonce is the ADR-0047 pilot proof: the canonical
// script writer resolves the nonce from the render context when the prop is
// empty, an explicit prop always wins, and the omit-empty rule survives.
func TestScriptComponentContextNonce(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	const js = "console.log('x');"

	render := func(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, nonce string) string {
		t.Helper()

		var buf bytes.Buffer

		if err := ScriptComponent(nonce, js, "test script").Render(ctx, &buf); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("render: %v", err)
		}

		return buf.String()
	}

	t.Run("props nonce unchanged", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := render(t, context.Background(), "prop-nonce")
		if !strings.Contains(got, `<script nonce="prop-nonce">`) {
			t.Errorf("props nonce not rendered: %s", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("context fills empty prop", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := render(t, ContextWithNonce(context.Background(), "ctx-nonce"), "")
		if !strings.Contains(got, `<script nonce="ctx-nonce">`) {
			t.Errorf("context nonce not rendered: %s", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("props and context agree byte-identically", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		viaProps := render(t, context.Background(), "same-nonce")

		viaContext := render(t, ContextWithNonce(context.Background(), "same-nonce"), "")

		if viaProps != viaContext {
			t.Errorf("context path diverges from props path:\nprops:    %s\ncontext:  %s", viaProps, viaContext)
		}
	})

	t.Run("disagreement is caught: props win", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := render(t, ContextWithNonce(context.Background(), "ctx-nonce"), "prop-nonce")
		if !strings.Contains(got, `nonce="prop-nonce"`) || strings.Contains(got, "ctx-nonce") {
			t.Errorf("explicit prop must win over context: %s", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("both empty omits the attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := render(t, context.Background(), "")
		if strings.Contains(got, "nonce=") {
			t.Errorf("empty nonce must render no nonce attribute (omit-empty rule): %s", got)
		}

		if !strings.Contains(got, "<script>\n"+js+"</script>") {
			t.Errorf("script body must still render: %s", got)
		}
	})
}

import (

// FuzzScriptComponent pins the writer's contract edges against hostile
// inputs (#360): the nonce attribute is HTML-escaped and never empty when a
// nonce resolves, the script body is written verbatim (templ's own script
// context handles JS-level sanitization upstream of this writer), and no
// input shape panics.
func FuzzScriptComponent(f *testing.F) {
	f.Add(`alert("x");`, "nonce-123")
	f.Add(`</script><script>alert(1)`, "")
	f.Add(`quotes " ' angles < > ampersand &`, `n"ce<&>`)
	f.Add("unicode ünïcödé áéíóú \U0001F642", "n")
	f.Add("", "n")
	f.Add("var tc = `template ${literal}`;", "")

	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, js, nonce string) {
		var sb strings.Builder

		err := ScriptComponent(nonce, js, "fuzz").Render(context.Background(), &sb)

		if strings.Contains(js, "</script>") {
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("script body %q carries a literal close tag and must refuse, got output %q", js, sb.String())
			}

			return
		}

		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("render error: %v", err)
		}

		out := sb.String()

		if strings.Contains(out, `nonce=""`) {
			t.Fatalf("nonce=%q rendered an empty nonce attribute: %q", nonce, out)
		}

		if nonce != "" {
			want := `nonce="` + html.EscapeString(nonce) + `"`
			if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
				t.Fatalf("nonce=%q missing escaped attribute %q in %q", nonce, want, out)
			}
		}

		if !strings.HasSuffix(out, "\n"+js+"</script>\n") {
			t.Fatalf("script body not written verbatim (nonce=%q): %q", nonce, out)
		}

		if !strings.HasPrefix(out, "<script") {
			t.Fatalf("output does not open with <script: %q", out)
		}
	})
}

// TestSemanticColorTokensCompiled extends TestCustomClassTokensCompiled from
// tc-* hooks to semantic color classes: every literal `<utility>-<hue>-<shade>`
// token written into a .templ class attribute must be RESOLVED by the compiled
// demo CSS (examples/demo/static/app.css, which @source-scans every repo
// .templ file). Tailwind v4 emits a color utility only when its theme color
// resolves, so even a freshly compiled stylesheet silently produces nothing
// for a family the consumer theme does not define — the exact mechanism
// behind the invisible accent focus ring the token-axis sweep shipped
// (ADR-0049): the class string was present, the rule never was.
//
// Substring matching against the minified CSS is deliberate, the same choice
// the tc-* guard makes: variant selectors (dark:, focus-visible:,
// peer-checked:*, @sm:…) embed the bare token, and an opacity stem (a token
// with a slash and an alpha percentage, like the accent-600 bar tint) still
// matches the unslashed selector fragment. False
// negatives (dynamically composed class strings) stay out of scope — the
// authoritative full check remains `scripts/ci-repro.sh --css`.
func TestSemanticColorTokensCompiled(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	// unresolvedByDesign lists color tokens that are deliberately absent from
	// the compiled CSS, each with the reason. Everything else must resolve.
	unresolvedByDesign := map[string]string{}

	// colorTokenRe anchors on the canonical hue families (tone.Hue + the
	// accent token family) and a shade: `[a-z-]+-(hue)-(shade)`. Anchoring on
	// families kills the numeric false-positive class (z-50, duration-700,
	// opacity-60) because those never carry a hue name.
	colorTokenRe := regexp.MustCompile(
		`\b[a-z]+[a-z-]*-(?:accent|gray|green|red|yellow|amber|orange|blue|emerald|rose|violet|cyan|pink|purple)-` +
			`(?:50|100|200|300|400|500|600|700|800|900|950)\b`)

	css, err := os.ReadFile("../examples/demo/static/app.css")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("compiled demo CSS not found: %v", err)
	}

	cssText := string(css)

	// class="..." (HTML attribute) and class={ "..." } (templ expression),
	// same extraction contract as TestCustomClassTokensCompiled.
	classAttrRe := regexp.MustCompile(`class=(?:\{[[:space:]]*)?"([^"]*)"?`)

	templFiles := walkTemplFiles(t)

	seen := make(map[string]bool)

	var missing []string

	for _, file := range templFiles {
		src, err := os.ReadFile(file)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", file, err)
		}

		for _, attr := range classAttrRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(string(src), -1) {
			for _, token := range colorTokenRe.FindAllString(attr[1], -1) {
				if seen[token] {
					continue
				}

				seen[token] = true

				if strings.Contains(cssText, token) {
					continue
				}

				if _, ok := unresolvedByDesign[token]; ok {
					continue
				}

				missing = append(missing, token+" ("+file+")")
			}
		}
	}

	if len(missing) > 0 {
		sort.Strings(missing)

		t.Errorf(
			"%d semantic color class(es) referenced in .templ class attributes but not resolved by examples/demo/static/app.css — the rule was never emitted (undefined theme family or stale compile): recompile with `nix run .#css`, define the family in templates/custom.css, or fix the typo:\n%s",
			len(missing),
			strings.Join(missing, "\n"),
		)
	}

	if len(seen) < 20 {
		t.Errorf("expected >=20 distinct color tokens across sources, found %d — the scan is likely broken", len(seen))
	}
}

// TestStarterCSSMatchesTemplates pins the `tc init` starter files to the
// canonical consumer templates. The starter copies are what `tc init`
// scaffolds; the templates/ files are what the README tells consumers to
// copy. They drifted apart once (the starter predated the `.go`-scanning
// @source lesson and several custom.css sections — TODO_LIST #290,
// 2026-09-23), which silently shipped new consumers a worse entry point.
// The starter files must be byte-identical to the canonical ones: fix
// drift by copying templates/ over starter/, never by editing starter/.
func TestStarterCSSMatchesTemplates(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	pairs := [][2]string{
		{"../cmd/tc/_sources/starter/app.css", "../templates/app.css"},
		{"../cmd/tc/_sources/starter/custom.css", "../templates/custom.css"},
		{"../cmd/tc/_sources/starter/safelist.css", "../templates/safelist.css"},
	}

	for _, pair := range pairs {
		starter, err := os.ReadFile(pair[0])
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", pair[0], err)
		}

		canonical, err := os.ReadFile(pair[1])
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", pair[1], err)
		}

		if string(starter) != string(canonical) {
			t.Errorf(
				"%s drifted from %s — copy the canonical file over the starter (never hand-edit the starter)",
				pair[0],
				pair[1],
			)
		}
	}
}

// FillIcon renders a 20×20 filled SVG icon with the given class and path.
templ FillIcon(class string, path string, rotate bool) {
	<svg
		class={ class, templ.KV("rotate-180", rotate) }
		viewBox="0 0 20 20"
		fill="currentColor"
		aria-hidden="true"
	>
		<path fill-rule="evenodd" d={ path } clip-rule="evenodd"></path>
	</svg>
}

// SpinnerSVG renders the inner SVG elements for a loading spinner.
// Wrap in an <svg> tag with animate-spin and desired size.
templ SpinnerSVG() {
	<circle class="opacity-25" cx="12" cy="12" r="10" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4"></circle>
	<path class="opacity-75" fill="currentColor" d="M4 12a8 8 0 018-8V0C5.373 0 0 5.373 0 12h4zm2 5.291A7.962 7.962 0 014 12H0c0 3.042 1.135 5.824 3 7.938l3-2.647z"></path>
}

	t.Run("renders SVG with correct path", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()
		output := utils.Render(t, svg.FillIcon(
			"h-5 w-5",

		t.Parallel()

		utils.AssertNotContains(t, output, "rotate-180")
	})
}

// TestInlineIconPathCompliance enforces the single-source-of-truth rule for
// SVG path data (AGENTS.md "SVG paths"): component sources must never inline
// a path d="M..." literal. Stroke and fill glyphs come from the icons package
// (icons.Icon for markup, icons.IconPathData for JS injection); paths needed
// across module boundaries (utils is a leaf and cannot import icons) live as
// shared constants in utils/svg. The sweep is the drift-guard style used by
// TestMotionReduceCompliance: it scans library sources so a future component
// cannot silently copy-paste path data again (the X glyph was inlined three
// times before this guard existed).
//
// Canonical definitions are exempt: icons/icon_paths.go (the icon table
// itself) and utils/svg (the shared constants + SpinnerSVG primitive).
func TestInlineIconPathCompliance(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	root := ".."
	dirs := []string{
		"display", "forms", "feedback", "layout", "navigation",
		"errorpage", "recipes", "htmx", "datastar", "charts/echarts",
		"icons", "utils",
	}

	violations := 0

	for _, dir := range dirs {
		findings, err := ScanIconPaths(filepath.Join(root, dir))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("scan %s: %v", dir, err)
		}

		violations += len(findings)

		for _, f := range findings {
			t.Errorf(
				"%s:%d inlines SVG path data — single-source violation. "+
					"Render via icons.Icon / icons.IconWithStrokeWidth (markup) or "+
					"icons.IconPathData (JS injection); for cross-module needs add a "+
					"constant in utils/svg.",
				filepath.Join(dir, f.File),
				f.Line,
			)
		}
	}

	if violations == 0 {
		t.Log("inline icon path compliance: OK (no inlined path data in library sources)")
	}
}

// TestInlineIconPathRegexDetectsViolations pins the detector itself: both
// literal forms (template attribute and Go-embedded JS) must match, while
// component-sourced paths stay clean.
func TestInlineIconPathRegexDetectsViolations(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	pathRe := regexp.MustCompile(`d=\\"M[0-9]|d="M[0-9]`)

	mustMatch := []string{
		`<path d="M6 18L18 6M6 6l12 12"></path>`,
		"btn.innerHTML='<svg><path d=\\\"M6 18L18 6M6 6l12 12\\\"></path></svg>'",
	}
	for _, sample := range mustMatch {
		if !pathRe.MatchString(sample) {
			t.Errorf("detector missed violation sample: %q", sample)
		}
	}

	clean := []string{
		`<path d={ svg.PathXMark }></path>`,
		`<path fill-rule="evenodd" d={ p } clip-rule="evenodd"></path>`,
		`<path d={ fmt.Sprintf("M%s", coords) }></path>`,
	}
	for _, sample := range clean {
		if pathRe.MatchString(sample) {
			t.Errorf("detector flagged clean sample: %q", sample)
		}
	}
}

// TestTailwindGoSourceScanning verifies that CSS entry points include @source
// directives for .go files, not just .templ files. Tailwind v4's content
// scanner only scans files matched by @source. Many components define Tailwind
// class lookup maps in Go source (buttonVariantLookup, feedbackStyleMap,
// familyStyleMap, modalSizeLookup, etc.). Without scanning .go files, those
// classes produce silently-missing CSS.
//
// History (2026-07-28): errorpage family classes (amber/orange/purple)
// were entirely missing from the compiled CSS because familyStyleMap lived in
// errorpage/styles.go and the CSS only scanned *.templ.
func TestTailwindGoSourceScanning(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		path string
	}{
		{"consumer template", "../templates/app.css"},
		{"demo CSS", "../examples/demo/demo.css"},
	}

	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			data, err := os.ReadFile(tc.path)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", tc.path, err)
			}

			src := string(data)

			// Must scan .templ files.
			if !strings.Contains(src, "*.templ") {
				t.Errorf("%s missing @source directive for *.templ files", tc.path)
			}

			// Must scan .go files (lookup maps, constants with Tailwind classes).
			if !strings.Contains(src, "*.go") {
				t.Errorf(
					"%s missing @source directive for *.go files — "+
						"Tailwind classes defined in Go source "+
						"(buttonVariantLookup, feedbackStyleMap, familyStyleMap) "+
						"will not get CSS generated",
					tc.path,
				)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestTemplVersionPin pins the github.com/a-h/templ version required by every
// module's go.mod to the templGeneratedWith constant in cmd/tc/doctor.go.
//
// The 2026-10-06 incident: an auto-commit daemon re-applied the templ
// v0.3.1070 bump across 8 go.mod files while the sanctioned generator
// (nixpkgs templ in the dev shell) was still v0.3.1020. That exact bump was
// deliberately rolled back on 2026-10-05 (see AGENTS.md "sweep note"): the
// 0.3.1070 generator changes OUTPUT (icon+label spacing), so the bump needs a
// flake-level generator pin, a golden + pixel re-baseline, and a source-trim
// review first (TODO #335). The migration window landed 2026-11-04
// (v0.3.1100, flake templGen from the upstream tag); the guard keeps
// enforcing the lockstep permanently — generator and go.mod must ALWAYS
// move together. This guard fails on any partial bump — go.mod moving
// without doctor.go's constant, or the constant moving without every module.
func TestTemplVersionPin(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	const doctorFile = "../cmd/tc/doctor.go"

	doctorSrc, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(doctorFile))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", doctorFile, err)
	}

	doctorRe := regexp.MustCompile(`templGeneratedWith = "(v[^"]+)"`)

	m := doctorRe.FindSubmatch(doctorSrc)
	if m == nil {
		t.Fatalf("templGeneratedWith constant not found in %s — constant renamed?", doctorFile)
	}

	expected := string(m[1])

	requireRe := regexp.MustCompile(`github\.com/a-h/templ\s+(v\S+)`)

	for _, mod := range []string{
		".", "utils", "icons", "errorpage", "charts/echarts", "htmx",
		"datastar", "website", "visualtest",
	} {
		t.Run(mod, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			goMod := filepath.Join("..", mod, "go.mod")

			src, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(goMod))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", goMod, err)
			}

			got := requireRe.FindSubmatch(src)
			if got == nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s has no github.com/a-h/templ require line", goMod)
			}

			if string(got[1]) != expected {
				t.Errorf(
					"%s requires templ %s but the generator pin is %s — "+
						"revert the go.mod bump or execute the TODO #335 migration plan "+
						"(flake generator pin + golden re-baseline) in the same commit",
					goMod, string(got[1]), expected,
				)
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("ci workflow generator pin", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		wf := filepath.Clean("../.github/workflows/ci.yaml")

		src, err := os.ReadFile(wf)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", wf, err)
		}

		pinRe := regexp.MustCompile(`github\.com/a-h/templ/cmd/templ@(v\S+)`)

		got := pinRe.FindSubmatch(src)
		if got == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s installs no templ generator pin — CI would regenerate "+
				"committed *_templ.go with an unpinned binary and fail on drift", wf)
		}

		if string(got[1]) != expected {
			t.Errorf(
				"%s installs templ generator %s but the go.mod/doctor lockstep pin is %s — "+
					"CI regenerates with the WRONG binary and reports REAL content drift "+
					"(the 2026-11-05 master red); bump the workflow pin in the SAME commit",
				wf, string(got[1]), expected,
			)
		}
	})
}

// TestTemplGeneratedInSync verifies that every committed *_templ.go file has
// import paths exactly matching its .templ source (both directions, excluding
// templ's auto-injected runtime imports). This catches the drift class where
// a source file's imports change but the generated file is not regenerated —
// or the reverse, where a daemon commits a generated file whose imports no
// longer match the source.
//
// The walk is REPO-WIDE (all modules: root, utils, icons, errorpage,
// charts/echarts, datastar, htmx, website, examples/demo). The 2026-09-17
// incident: website/internal/pages/base_templ.go was flipped to
// encoding/json/v2 while base.templ said v1 — invisible because the guard
// only walked the 8 root-module packages.
//
// Breadcrumbs bug (2026-07-28): source imported encoding/json (v1) but the
// generated file imported encoding/json/v2 — functionally inert under
// GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 but breaks consumers who run templ generate themselves.
func TestTemplGeneratedInSync(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	templFiles := walkTemplFiles(t)
	if len(templFiles) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no .templ files found — glob root is wrong")
	}

	importRe := regexp.MustCompile(`"([^"]+)"`)

	for _, templFile := range templFiles {
		genFile := strings.TrimSuffix(templFile, ".templ") + "_templ.go"

		t.Run(templFile, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			src, err := os.ReadFile(templFile)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", templFile, err)
			}

			gen, err := os.ReadFile(genFile)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read %s: %v (run `templ generate ./...` and commit)", genFile, err)
			}

			srcImports := extractImports(string(src), importRe)
			genImports := extractImports(string(gen), importRe)

			assertImportsMatch(t, templFile, genFile, srcImports, genImports)
		})
	}
}

// assertImportsMatch fails the test for every import present in one file but
// not the other, in both directions. Missing-in-generated means a stale
// generated file; missing-in-source means the generated file was hand-edited
// or generated from a different source. Extracted to keep the driving test's
// cognitive complexity under the gocognit gate.
func assertImportsMatch(t *testing.T, templFile, genFile string, srcImports, genImports map[string]bool) {
	t.Helper()

	onlyInSrc := missingFrom(srcImports, genImports)
	onlyInGen := missingFrom(genImports, srcImports)

	for _, imp := range onlyInSrc {
		t.Errorf(
			"%s imports %q but %s does not — run `templ generate ./...` to sync",
			filepath.Base(templFile), imp, filepath.Base(genFile),
		)
	}

	for _, imp := range onlyInGen {
		t.Errorf(
			"%s imports %q but its .templ source does not — the generated file is stale or hand-edited; run `templ generate ./...` to sync",
			filepath.Base(genFile),
			imp,
		)
	}
}

// missingFrom returns the sorted paths present in want but absent from have.
func missingFrom(want, have map[string]bool) []string {
	var missing []string

	for imp := range want {
		if !have[imp] {
			missing = append(missing, imp)
		}
	}

	sort.Strings(missing)

	return missing
}

// walkTemplFiles returns every .templ file under the repo root (".." from
// utils/) that is expected to have a generated *_templ.go twin. Excluded:
// .git, node_modules, build output (dist), test fixtures, and
// cmd/tc/_sources (the `tc new` scaffolding sources — intentionally
// standalone templates with no generated twins, the same exclusion CI's
// tracked-files check uses).
func walkTemplFiles(t *testing.T) []string {
	t.Helper()

	const repoRoot = ".."

	var files []string

	err := filepath.WalkDir(repoRoot, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if d.IsDir() {
			name := d.Name()

			switch {
			case name == ".git" || name == "node_modules" || name == "dist" || name == "testdata":
				return filepath.SkipDir
			case path == filepath.Join(repoRoot, "cmd", "tc", "_sources"):
				return filepath.SkipDir
			}

			return nil
		}

		if strings.HasSuffix(path, ".templ") {
			files = append(files, path)
		}

		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("walk %s: %v", repoRoot, err)
	}

	sort.Strings(files)

	return files
}

// extractImports pulls quoted import paths from the import section of a Go or
// templ source file. It scans only import (...) blocks and single-line
// import "..." declarations, excluding templ's own runtime imports
// (github.com/a-h/templ and github.com/a-h/templ/runtime) which are always
// injected by the generator.
func extractImports(src string, re *regexp.Regexp) map[string]bool {
	result := make(map[string]bool)

	importBlockRe := regexp.MustCompile(
		`(?s)import\s*\(([^)]*)\)|import\s*"([^"]+)"`,
	)

	for _, match := range importBlockRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(src, -1) {
		var block string

		if match[1] != "" {
			block = match[1]
		} else {
			block = match[2]
		}

		for _, imp := range re.FindAllStringSubmatch(block, -1) {
			path := imp[1]

			if strings.HasPrefix(path, "github.com/a-h/templ") {
				continue
			}

			result[path] = true
		}
	}

	return result
}

// TestTemplGeneratedInSyncCoverage confirms the repo-wide walk actually visits
// the modules whose drift shipped incidents (website: the 2026-09-17
// base_templ.go import flip; examples/demo: the 20:52 stale generated file),
// preventing a silent pass if the skip rules over-exclude after a refactor.
func TestTemplGeneratedInSyncCoverage(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	templFiles := walkTemplFiles(t)

	if len(templFiles) < 100 {
		t.Errorf("expected >=100 .templ files repo-wide (outside _sources), found %d", len(templFiles))
	}

	mustCover := []string{
		"website/internal/pages/",
		"examples/demo/",
		"charts/echarts/",
		"datastar/",
		"icons/",
		"display/",
	}

	for _, dir := range mustCover {
		found := false

		for _, f := range templFiles {
			if strings.Contains(f, dir) {
				found = true

				break
			}
		}

		if !found {
			t.Errorf("walk missed .templ files under %q — skip rules over-exclude", dir)
		}
	}
}
// Test rendering utilities: Render, RenderAll, Assert* helpers for component testing.
package utils

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

// TestReporter is the subset of *testing.T the render helpers use.
// *testing.T satisfies it. The interface exists so this PRODUCTION package
// never imports testing: importing testing here linked the Go test
// framework (testing.init et al.) into every consumer binary that pulls
// utils (found in dnsblockd via `go tool nm`, 2026-09-19). Test-only
// helpers stay importable from _test.go files with zero changes while the
// production import graph stays test-free.
type TestReporter interface {
	Helper()
	Fatalf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}

// Render renders a templ component to a string for testing.
func Render(t TestReporter, c templ.Component) string {
	t.Helper()

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	if err := c.Render(context.Background(), &buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to render component: %v", err)
	}

	return strings.TrimSpace(buf.String())
}

// RenderAll renders multiple templ components into a single concatenated string.
// Useful for integration tests that verify component composition.
func RenderAll(t TestReporter, components ...templ.Component) string {
	t.Helper()

	var sb strings.Builder

	for _, c := range components {
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		if err := c.Render(context.Background(), &buf); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to render component: %v", err)
		}

		sb.WriteString(buf.String())
	}

	return strings.TrimSpace(sb.String())
}

// AssertContains checks that the rendered output contains a substring.
func AssertContains(t TestReporter, output, want string) {
	t.Helper()

	if !strings.Contains(output, want) {
		t.Errorf("output does not contain %q:\n%s", want, output)
	}
}

// AssertNotContains checks that the rendered output does not contain a substring.
func AssertNotContains(t TestReporter, output, notWant string) {
	t.Helper()

	if strings.Contains(output, notWant) {
		t.Errorf("output should not contain %q:\n%s", notWant, output)
	}
}

// AssertEqual checks that got equals want, reporting a test error with context if not.
func AssertEqual[T comparable](t TestReporter, context string, got, want T) {
	t.Helper()

	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", context, got, want)
	}
}

// AssertContainsAll checks that the rendered output contains every substring
// in wants. Reports a single test error per missing substring.
func AssertContainsAll(t TestReporter, output string, wants ...string) {
	t.Helper()

	for _, want := range wants {
		if !strings.Contains(output, want) {
			t.Errorf("output does not contain %q:\n%s", want, output)
		}
	}
}

// AssertContainsClass checks that the rendered output contains every want as
// a WHOLE whitespace- or quote-delimited token. Substring asserts
// false-positive on class affixes ("p-2" matches "p-24", "ring-1" matches
// "ring-10"); token membership closes that gap while staying agnostic to
// tailwind-merge class reordering (each want matches as its own token,
// never as a slice of an ordered class attribute). Quotes split tokens too,
// so `class="p-2"` inside HTML attribute syntax matches; a bare substring
// glued inside a longer token ("p-24") still does not.
func AssertContainsClass(t TestReporter, output string, wants ...string) {
	t.Helper()

	tokens := strings.FieldsFunc(output, func(r rune) bool {
		return r == ' ' || r == '\t' || r == '\n' || r == '\r' || r == '"' || r == '\''
	})

	for _, want := range wants {
		if !slices.Contains(tokens, want) {
			t.Errorf("output does not contain class token %q:\n%s", want, output)
		}
	}
}
package tone

// ColorClass is a complete, scanner-safe color utility string: the light
// class and its dark: half in ONE literal (e.g. "text-blue-600
// dark:text-blue-400"). Chart series, spinners, and progress fills accept
// it so a typo cannot silently render nothing — pass a named constant
// (display.ChartColorBlue, …) or a complete literal of your own; a bare
// "text-blue-600" without the dark half compiles but trips the dark-mode
// guards.
//
// The string kind keeps every existing untyped literal assigning (TODO
// #426 non-breaking); a typed value converts with string(c) where a raw
// string is needed.
type ColorClass string
package tone_test

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

var docUpdate = flag.Bool("update", false, "rewrite the generated tone sections in the docs")

const (
	themeBridgeDoc = "../../docs/recipes/scoped-theme-bridge.md"
	themeLayerCSS  = "../../templates/templ-components-theme.css"

	paletteBegin = "<!-- BEGIN generated: tone palette table (utils/tone/doc_sync_test.go; go test ./utils/tone/ -update) -->"
	paletteEnd   = "<!-- END generated: tone palette table -->"

	familyBegin = "<!-- BEGIN generated: token family table (utils/tone/doc_sync_test.go; go test ./utils/tone/ -update) -->"
	familyEnd   = "<!-- END generated: token family table -->"
)

// tonePaletteTable renders the "Which colors does the library use?" table
// from the tone package's own tables — the single source of truth for the
// library palette (report H4: this was the fifth hand-maintained copy).
func tonePaletteTable() string {
	chartSeries := map[tone.Hue]int{}
	for i, hue := range tone.ChartHues() {
		chartSeries[hue] = i + 1
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("| Hue | Tones rendered in it | Chart palette |\n")
	b.WriteString("| --- | --- | --- |\n")

	for _, hue := range tone.Hues() {
		prefix := string(hue) + "-"

		var tones []string

		for _, t := range tone.Tones() {
			if toneUsesHue(t, prefix) {
				tones = append(tones, string(t))
			}
		}

		tonesCell := "—"
		if len(tones) > 0 {
			tonesCell = strings.Join(tones, ", ")
		}

		chartCell := "—"
		if series, ok := chartSeries[hue]; ok {
			chartCell = fmt.Sprintf("yes (series %d)", series)
		}

		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "| `%s` | %s | %s |\n", hue, tonesCell, chartCell)
	}

	return b.String()
}

// toneUsesHue reports whether any surface of the tone references the hue
// (classes carry the hue as a `hue-shade` token prefix).
func toneUsesHue(t tone.Tone, prefix string) bool {
	return toneUsesPrefix(t, prefix)
}

// toneUsesPrefix reports whether any surface of the tone carries the given
// class prefix (a hue like "blue-" or a token family like "accent-").
func toneUsesPrefix(t tone.Tone, prefix string) bool {
	surfaces := tone.For(t)

	for _, pair := range []tone.Pair{
		surfaces.Dot, surfaces.Text, surfaces.TextSoft, surfaces.Border,
		surfaces.BGTint, surfaces.BGSolid, surfaces.Icon,
	} {
		if strings.Contains(pair.Light, prefix) || strings.Contains(pair.Dark, prefix) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}

// toneFamilyTable renders the token-family table (ADR-0049): tones that
// render through token families instead of palette hues. The accent
// family is derived from the tone tables, like the palette table above —
// adding a family means extending this generator, not hand-editing docs.
func toneFamilyTable() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("| Family | Tones rendered in it |\n")
	b.WriteString("| --- | --- |\n")

	var accentTones []string

	for _, t := range tone.Tones() {
		if toneUsesPrefix(t, "accent-") {
			accentTones = append(accentTones, string(t))
		}
	}

	tonesCell := "—"
	if len(accentTones) > 0 {
		tonesCell = strings.Join(accentTones, ", ")
	}

	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "| `accent` | %s |\n", tonesCell)

	return b.String()
}

// syncGeneratedDocSection verifies (or with -update rewrites) one generated
// section of the theme bridge doc against its derived table. Shared by the
// palette and family table tests; the -update branches read-modify-write
// the same file, so callers must stay sequential (never t.Parallel).
func syncGeneratedDocSection(t *testing.T, begin, end, table string) {
	t.Helper()

	doc, err := os.ReadFile(themeBridgeDoc)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read theme bridge doc: %v", err)
	}

	want := begin + "\n" + table + end

	if *docUpdate {
		updated := replaceGeneratedSection(string(doc), begin, end, want)
		if updated != string(doc) {
			if err := os.WriteFile(themeBridgeDoc, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("rewrite theme bridge doc: %v", err)
			}
		}

		return
	}

	start := strings.Index(string(doc), begin)

	endIdx := strings.Index(string(doc), end)
	if start < 0 || endIdx < start {
		t.Fatalf(
			"theme bridge doc lacks the generated markers %q/%q — run go test ./utils/tone/ -update",
			begin, end,
		)
	}

	have := string(doc)[start : endIdx+len(end)]
	if normalizeGeneratedBlock(have) != normalizeGeneratedBlock(want) {
		t.Errorf(
			"theme bridge doc generated section is stale:\n--- have ---\n%s\n--- want ---\n%s\nRun: go test ./utils/tone/ -update",
			have,
			want,
		)
	}
}

// TestThemeBridgePaletteTableSync keeps the generated palette table in
// docs/recipes/scoped-theme-bridge.md byte-identical to what the tone
// package derives. Any tone/hue table change fails here until the doc is
// regenerated (`go test ./utils/tone/ -run TestThemeBridgePaletteTableSync -update`).
// NOT parallel: the -update branches of both doc-sync tests read-modify-
// write the same file, and interleaved writes clobber each other's fill
// (both tables landed half-filled once — 2026-11-06). Trivial cost.
//
//nolint:paralleltest // sequential on purpose: shared read-modify-write doc target
func TestThemeBridgePaletteTableSync(t *testing.T) {
	syncGeneratedDocSection(t, paletteBegin, paletteEnd, tonePaletteTable())
}

// TestThemeBridgeFamilyTableSync keeps the generated token-family table
// (ADR-0049) in docs/recipes/scoped-theme-bridge.md byte-identical to what
// the tone package derives — same mechanism as the palette table above.
// NOT parallel: shared read-modify-write target (see the palette test).
//
//nolint:paralleltest // sequential on purpose: shared read-modify-write doc target
func TestThemeBridgeFamilyTableSync(t *testing.T) {
	syncGeneratedDocSection(t, familyBegin, familyEnd, toneFamilyTable())
}

// normalizeGeneratedBlock makes the generated-section comparison insensitive to
// markdown table padding. The repo formatter aligns tables; the generator emits
// compact rows. Both express the same table, and comparing padding made the
// guard fail after every formatter run (2026-10-23 recurrence). Semantic drift
// (a missing hue, a changed column value) still fails.
func normalizeGeneratedBlock(block string) string {
	lines := strings.Split(block, "\n")
	normalized := make([]string, 0, len(lines))

	for _, line := range lines {
		if isTableSeparator(line) {
			continue
		}

		line = strings.Join(strings.Fields(line), " ")
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}

		normalized = append(normalized, line)
	}

	return strings.Join(normalized, "\n")
}

// isTableSeparator reports whether the line is a markdown table delimiter row
// (only pipes, dashes, colons, and spaces). Padding differences make the
// delimiter row length vary; the row carries no data, so both sides skip it.
func isTableSeparator(line string) bool {
	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "|") {
		return false
	}

	hasDash := false

	for _, char := range trimmed {
		switch char {
		case '|', ' ':
		case '-':
			hasDash = true
		case ':':
		default:
			return false
		}
	}

	return hasDash
}

// TestThemeTokenLayerInventory pins the tc-* token inventory of
// templates/templ-components-theme.css (ADR-0008): exactly the four semantic
// ramps (primary/danger/success/warning — the accent, danger, success, and
// warning tones) at every shade 50–950, so a ramp that loses a shade or a
// stray token that appears fails loudly instead of silently re-breaking
// consumer overrides.
func TestThemeTokenLayerInventory(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	css, err := os.ReadFile(themeLayerCSS)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read theme layer css: %v", err)
	}

	tokenRe := regexp.MustCompile(`--color-tc-([a-z]+)-(\d+):`)
	shades := []string{"50", "100", "200", "300", "400", "500", "600", "700", "800", "900", "950"}
	want := map[string]bool{}

	for _, ramp := range []string{"primary", "danger", "success", "warning"} {
		for _, shade := range shades {
			want[fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", ramp, shade)] = true
		}
	}

	got := map[string]bool{}
	for _, match := range tokenRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(string(css), -1) {
		got[match[1]+"-"+match[2]] = true
	}

	for token := range want {
		if !got[token] {
			t.Errorf("theme layer css is missing token --color-tc-%s (ramp incomplete)", token)
		}
	}

	for token := range got {
		if !want[token] {
			t.Errorf("theme layer css carries unexpected ramp token --color-tc-%s (inventory drift)", token)
		}
	}
}

func replaceGeneratedSection(doc, begin, end, replacement string) string {
	start := strings.Index(doc, begin)

	finish := strings.Index(doc, end)
	if start < 0 || finish < start {
		return doc + "\n" + replacement + "\n"
	}

	return doc[:start] + replacement + doc[finish+len(end):]
}
package tone

// Hue is the categorical hue family: which Tailwind color palette a class
// draws from, independent of meaning. Thirteen hues are in active use across
// the library's lookup tables (verified 2026-10-15); indigo is deliberately
// absent (nothing renders it).
//
// Hue is for decisions that are genuinely categorical (chart series, kanban
// lanes, stat tiles): "the third series is violet" carries no semantics.
// When a color MEANS something, use Tone and let the tone table pick the
// hue.
type Hue string

const (
	// Chart palette hues first, in canonical series order (line/pie/segment
	// charts cycle this order — chart_geometry.go, pie_chart.go).
	HueBlue    Hue = "blue"
	HueEmerald Hue = "emerald"
	HueAmber   Hue = "amber"
	HueRose    Hue = "rose"
	HueViolet  Hue = "violet"
	HueCyan    Hue = "cyan"
	HueOrange  Hue = "orange"
	HuePink    Hue = "pink"
	// Semantic-dialect hues (the feedback/badge/kanban/stat families).
	HueGray   Hue = "gray"
	HueGreen  Hue = "green"
	HueYellow Hue = "yellow"
	HueRed    Hue = "red"
	HuePurple Hue = "purple"
)

// HueDefault is the canonical default (Gray).
const HueDefault = HueGray

// HueIsValid reports whether h is a recognized Hue.
func HueIsValid(h Hue) bool {
	switch h {
	case HueBlue, HueEmerald, HueAmber, HueRose, HueViolet, HueCyan,
		HueOrange, HuePink, HueGray, HueGreen, HueYellow, HueRed, HuePurple:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// Hues returns every Hue, chart palette first (canonical series order),
// then the semantic-dialect hues.
func Hues() []Hue {
	return []Hue{
		HueBlue, HueEmerald, HueAmber, HueRose, HueViolet, HueCyan,
		HueOrange, HuePink, HueGray, HueGreen, HueYellow, HueRed, HuePurple,
	}
}

// ChartHues returns the eight chart-series hues in canonical cycle order.
// Line/pie/segment palettes are views of this slice (see
// display/chart_geometry.go for the pre-tone constants).
func ChartHues() []Hue {
	return []Hue{HueBlue, HueEmerald, HueAmber, HueRose, HueViolet, HueCyan, HueOrange, HuePink}
}
package tone

// Utilities is the per-hue class grammar: seven utility slots, each a
// complete light/dark Pair. The shade numbers are the library's uniform
// grammar, anchored to what the components actually render today:
//
//	Text           600 / dark:400   (chart series text, icons on tint)
//	TextMuted      500 / dark:400   (muted neutral text — the gray-500 inverted convention)
//	TextStrong     700 / dark:400   (trend arrows, log tags)
//	TextOnTint     800 / dark:200   (body text on 50-tinted backgrounds)
//	BGSolid        500 / dark:400   (status dots, kanban lane dots)
//	BGSolidStrong  600 / dark:400   (segment bars, solid fills)
//	BGTint         50  / dark:900/30 (stat tiles, icon chips)
//	Border         200 / dark:800   (alert and card borders)
//
// Gray carries two deliberate exceptions, kept to match shipped pixels:
// BGSolid is 400/dark:500 (the dot convention renders grays one step
// darker) and Border uses gray-700 in dark mode (the feedback neutral
// fallback). Cells no component uses yet are inert until adopted — the
// tables describe the grammar, the components choose the slots.
type Utilities struct {
	Text          Pair
	TextMuted     Pair
	TextStrong    Pair
	TextOnTint    Pair
	BGSolid       Pair
	BGSolidStrong Pair
	BGTint        Pair
	Border        Pair
}

// Repeated text literals shared across the hue and tone tables (goconst):
// every hue's text slots share the same dark:400 class, and blue's light
// 600 shade appears in both tables. The accent token family (ADR-0049)
// shares the same 600/dark:400 text grammar.
const (
	textBlue600    = "text-blue-600"
	darkTextBlue   = "dark:text-blue-400"
	darkTextGray   = "dark:text-gray-400"
	darkTextGreen  = "dark:text-green-400"
	darkTextYellow = "dark:text-yellow-400"
	darkTextAmber  = "dark:text-amber-400"
	darkTextRed    = "dark:text-red-400"
	textAccent600  = "text-accent-600"
	darkTextAccent = "dark:text-accent-400"
)

		TextStrong:    Pair{"text-yellow-700", darkTextYellow},
		TextOnTint:    Pair{"text-yellow-800", "dark:text-yellow-200"},
		BGSolid:       Pair{"bg-yellow-500", "dark:bg-yellow-400"},
		BGSolidStrong: Pair{"bg-yellow-600", "dark:bg-yellow-400"},
		BGTint:        Pair{"bg-yellow-50", "dark:bg-yellow-900/30"},
		Border:        Pair{"border-yellow-200", "dark:border-yellow-800"},
	},
	HueRed: {
		Text:          Pair{"text-red-600", darkTextRed},
		TextMuted:     Pair{"text-red-500", darkTextRed},
		TextStrong:    Pair{"text-red-700", darkTextRed},
		TextOnTint:    Pair{"text-red-800", "dark:text-red-200"},
		BGSolid:       Pair{"bg-red-500", "dark:bg-red-400"},
		BGSolidStrong: Pair{"bg-red-600", "dark:bg-red-400"},
		BGTint:        Pair{"bg-red-50", "dark:bg-red-900/30"},
		Border:        Pair{"border-red-200", "dark:border-red-800"},
	},
	HuePurple: {
		Text:          Pair{"text-purple-600", "dark:text-purple-400"},
		TextMuted:     Pair{"text-purple-500", "dark:text-purple-400"},
		TextStrong:    Pair{"text-purple-700", "dark:text-purple-400"},
		TextOnTint:    Pair{"text-purple-800", "dark:text-purple-200"},

		BGSolidStrong: Pair{"bg-purple-600", "dark:bg-purple-400"},
		BGTint:        Pair{"bg-purple-50", "dark:bg-purple-900/30"},
		Border:        Pair{"border-purple-200", "dark:border-purple-800"},
	},

// UtilitiesFor returns the class grammar for h. Unknown hues fall back to
// Gray (the neutral default) — same contract as utils.Lookup.
func UtilitiesFor(h Hue) Utilities {
	if u, ok := hueTable[h]; ok {
		return u
	}

	return hueTable[HueGray]
}
package tone

import "strings"

// Pair is one utility in light and dark form. Both halves are COMPLETE
// class literals — Dark carries its own dark: prefix — because Tailwind's
// scanner only emits CSS for tokens it can see in full (the package-level
// scanner-safety contract). Pair makes the halves structural so tests can
// prove every dark half exists.
type Pair struct {
	// Light is the light-mode class literal, without any variant prefix
	// (e.g. "text-green-600").
	Light string
	// Dark is the dark-mode class literal WITH its dark: prefix
	// (e.g. "dark:text-green-400").
	Dark string
}

// Classes returns the renderable class string: light and dark halves joined
// by a single space. Either half may be empty (single-mode utilities); the
// join never leaves leading/trailing whitespace.
func (p Pair) Classes() string {
	return strings.TrimSpace(p.Light + " " + p.Dark)
}

// Complete reports whether both halves are non-empty. Most library pairs
// are complete (every color utility carries a dark: variant — guarded by
// utils.TestDarkModeCompliance); incomplete pairs are deliberate
// single-mode exceptions and must say so at their construction site.
func (p Pair) Complete() bool {
	return p.Light != "" && p.Dark != ""
}
package tone

// Surfaces is the per-tone rendering kit: which classes express a semantic
// tone on each surface kind. Values are anchored to the feedback dialect
// (Alert/Toast — the oldest and most-used semantic renderer), so
// For(ToneSuccess).Text is exactly the Text class feedback renders for
// success today (byte-pinned by feedback.TestToneAdapterEquivalence).
type Surfaces struct {
	// Dot is a solid indicator dot (status dots, kanban lane dots).
	Dot Pair
	// Text is body text on a tinted background (alert message text).
	Text Pair
	// TextSoft is de-emphasized text or an icon on a tinted background.
	TextSoft Pair
	// Border outlines a tinted container (alerts, tinted cards).
	Border Pair
	// BGTint is a soft tinted background (alert fills).
	BGTint Pair
	// BGSolid is a solid saturated fill (progress bars, pills).
	BGSolid Pair
	// Icon is an icon on a tinted background (alert icons).
	Icon Pair
}

// toneTable maps every Tone to its surfaces. The pigment backing each tone:
// neutral=gray, success=green, warning=amber (the #428 decision — the
// one semantic warning hue; categorical yellow survives on the Hue axis
// for Kanban/StatCard), danger=red, info=blue (semantic info keeps the
// palette per ADR-0044 decision 3), accent=the accent token family
// (ADR-0044/0049 emission — the v2 swap this table was built for).
//
// Neutral deviates from the uniform tint grammar where feedback's fallback
// ships it: BGTint uses gray-800/50 in dark mode (not 900/30). Completeness
// is guarded by TestToneTableExhaustive; byte-equivalence with the feedback
// map is guarded by feedback.TestToneAdapterEquivalence.
//
//nolint:gochecknoglobals // package-level lookup table by design
var toneTable = map[Tone]Surfaces{
	ToneNeutral: {
		Dot:      hueTable[HueGray].BGSolid,
		Text:     Pair{"text-gray-800", "dark:text-gray-200"},
		TextSoft: Pair{"text-gray-600", darkTextGray},
		Border:   Pair{"border-gray-200", "dark:border-gray-700"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-gray-50", "dark:bg-gray-800/50"},
		BGSolid:  hueTable[HueGray].BGSolidStrong,
		Icon:     Pair{"text-gray-600", darkTextGray},
	},
	ToneSuccess: {
		Dot:      hueTable[HueGreen].BGSolid,
		Text:     Pair{"text-green-800", "dark:text-green-200"},
		TextSoft: Pair{"text-green-600", darkTextGreen},
		Border:   Pair{"border-green-200", "dark:border-green-800"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-green-50", "dark:bg-green-900/20"},
		BGSolid:  hueTable[HueGreen].BGSolidStrong,
		Icon:     Pair{"text-green-600", darkTextGreen},
	},
	ToneWarning: {
		Dot:      hueTable[HueAmber].BGSolid,
		Text:     Pair{"text-amber-800", "dark:text-amber-200"},
		TextSoft: Pair{"text-amber-600", darkTextAmber},
		Border:   Pair{"border-amber-200", "dark:border-amber-800"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-amber-50", "dark:bg-amber-900/20"},
		BGSolid:  hueTable[HueAmber].BGSolidStrong,
		Icon:     Pair{"text-amber-600", darkTextAmber},
	},
	ToneDanger: {
		Dot:      hueTable[HueRed].BGSolid,
		Text:     Pair{"text-red-800", "dark:text-red-200"},
		TextSoft: Pair{"text-red-600", darkTextRed},
		Border:   Pair{"border-red-200", "dark:border-red-800"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-red-50", "dark:bg-red-900/20"},
		BGSolid:  hueTable[HueRed].BGSolidStrong,
		Icon:     Pair{"text-red-600", darkTextRed},
	},
	ToneInfo: {
		Dot:      hueTable[HueBlue].BGSolid,
		Text:     Pair{"text-blue-800", "dark:text-blue-200"},
		TextSoft: Pair{textBlue600, darkTextBlue},
		Border:   Pair{"border-blue-200", "dark:border-blue-800"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-blue-50", "dark:bg-blue-900/20"},
		BGSolid:  hueTable[HueBlue].BGSolidStrong,
		Icon:     Pair{textBlue600, darkTextBlue},
	},
	ToneAccent: {
		Dot:      Pair{"bg-accent-500", "dark:bg-accent-400"},
		Text:     Pair{textAccent600, darkTextAccent},
		TextSoft: Pair{textAccent600, darkTextAccent},
		Border:   Pair{"border-accent-200", "dark:border-accent-800"},
		BGTint:   Pair{"bg-accent-50", "dark:bg-accent-900/20"},
		BGSolid:  Pair{"bg-accent-600", "dark:bg-accent-400"},
		Icon:     Pair{textAccent600, darkTextAccent},
	},
}

// For returns the rendering surfaces for t. Unknown tones fall back to
// Neutral — same contract as utils.Lookup.
func For(t Tone) Surfaces {
	if s, ok := toneTable[t]; ok {
		return s
	}

	return toneTable[ToneNeutral]
}
package tone

// SurfaceToken names a surface role: which LAYER of the interface a
// background belongs to (canvas / panel / raised). Role-indexed, not
// shade-indexed, so a brand specifies its light+dark surface pairs as
// data: the token's CSS variable is defined in templates/custom.css and
// re-defined under `.dark`, making one class self-dark-aware — no
// dark: variant, no value duplication in Go (ADR-0049 §3).
//
// Class emission starts with the shell conversion (master plan S11);
// until then nothing renders these classes. The type exists now so the
// namespace contract is pinned before any component commits to it.
type SurfaceToken string

const (
	// SurfaceToken0 is the page canvas behind everything.
	SurfaceToken0 SurfaceToken = "surface-0"
	// SurfaceToken1 is a panel resting on the canvas (cards, tables, sheets).
	SurfaceToken1 SurfaceToken = "surface-1"
	// SurfaceToken2 is a raised layer on a panel (inputs, popovers, tooltips).
	SurfaceToken2 SurfaceToken = "surface-2"
)

// SurfaceTokenDefault is the canonical default (the canvas).
const SurfaceTokenDefault = SurfaceToken0

// SurfaceTokenIsValid reports whether t is a recognized SurfaceToken.
func SurfaceTokenIsValid(t SurfaceToken) bool {
	switch t {
	case SurfaceToken0, SurfaceToken1, SurfaceToken2:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// SurfaceTokens returns every SurfaceToken, in stacking order (canvas up).
func SurfaceTokens() []SurfaceToken {
	return []SurfaceToken{SurfaceToken0, SurfaceToken1, SurfaceToken2}
}

// InkToken names a text-ink role: how strongly text reads against the
// surface it sits on. Same variable-flip contract as SurfaceToken
// (ADR-0049 §3): the class is self-dark-aware, values are brand data.
//
// Class emission starts with the surface/ink sweeps (master plan S11);
// the type pins the namespace contract now.
type InkToken string

const (
	// InkToken1 is primary text (headings, body emphasis).
	InkToken1 InkToken = "ink-1"
	// InkToken2 is secondary text (body copy, descriptions).
	InkToken2 InkToken = "ink-2"
	// InkToken3 is muted text (meta, placeholders, footnotes).
	InkToken3 InkToken = "ink-3"
)

// InkTokenDefault is the canonical default (primary).
const InkTokenDefault = InkToken1

// InkTokenIsValid reports whether t is a recognized InkToken.
func InkTokenIsValid(t InkToken) bool {
	switch t {
	case InkToken1, InkToken2, InkToken3:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// InkTokens returns every InkToken, in emphasis order (strong to muted).
func InkTokens() []InkToken {
	return []InkToken{InkToken1, InkToken2, InkToken3}
}
// Package tone is the library's canonical color language: one Tone axis
// ("why is this thing colored"), one Hue axis ("which hue family"), and the
// two tables that map them to complete Tailwind class literals.
//
// Before this package existed, the same semantic was modeled thirteen
// different ways (10 enums, 12 lookup maps, 3 palettes, ~10 fixed-color
// sites) — see docs/reviews/2026-10-15_color-domain-model.html. Phase 0 is
// ADDITIVE ONLY: existing enums gain adapters, existing lookup maps keep
// rendering, and equivalence tests prove the tables describe reality
// byte-for-byte. The maps collapse INTO these tables at v2
// (ADR-0039/0044, TODO #431).
//
// # Scanner-safety contract
//
// Every class string in this package is a COMPLETE LITERAL, including the
// dark: prefixed half. Tailwind's scanner must see the whole token to emit
// CSS; variants are never concatenated at runtime (see AGENTS.md "Tailwind
// variant prefixes must be complete literals"). Pair exists to make the
// light/dark halves structural, not to build strings dynamically.
//
// # Warning dialect (resolved)
//
// The #428 decision (2026-10-30, owner default) landed ONE semantic
// warning hue: AMBER. The tone table, feedback (Alert/Toast), and Badge
// all render warning in amber; the former amber sites (StatusDot,
// ScrollbackLog, errorpage rejection, outline warning button, trend warn)
// already did. Categorical yellow survives on the Hue axis (Kanban lanes,
// StatCard series) — that is a pigment choice, not a semantic warning.
package tone

// Tone is the semantic reason something is colored: what the color MEANS,
// not which pigment it uses. Six values cover every color decision the
// library makes; hue-level (categorical) decisions use Hue instead.
type Tone string

const (
	// ToneNeutral is the absence of semantic emphasis (gray).
	ToneNeutral Tone = "neutral"
	// ToneSuccess confirms a positive outcome (green).
	ToneSuccess Tone = "success"
	// ToneWarning signals caution short of failure (amber; see the
	// package doc's warning-dialect note and TODO #428).
	ToneWarning Tone = "warning"
	// ToneDanger signals failure or destruction (red). Canonical spelling
	// is "danger"; the FeedbackError value ("error") maps here via
	// FeedbackType.Tone() and collapses at v2.
	ToneDanger Tone = "danger"
	// ToneInfo is neutral-emphasis communication (blue).
	ToneInfo Tone = "info"
	// ToneAccent is the brand/primary slot. It renders the accent token
	// family (ADR-0044/0049) — one @theme override re-skins it; blue
	// stays reserved for the semantic info tone.
	ToneAccent Tone = "accent"
)

// ToneDefault is the canonical default (Neutral).
const ToneDefault = ToneNeutral

// ToneIsValid reports whether t is a recognized Tone.
func ToneIsValid(t Tone) bool {
	switch t {
	case ToneNeutral, ToneSuccess, ToneWarning, ToneDanger, ToneInfo, ToneAccent:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// Tones returns every Tone, in declaration (semantic severity) order.
func Tones() []Tone {
	return []Tone{ToneNeutral, ToneSuccess, ToneWarning, ToneDanger, ToneInfo, ToneAccent}
}
package tone_test

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/larsartmann/templ-components/utils/tone"
)

// TestToneTableExhaustive: every Tone in Tones() must carry a complete
// Surfaces entry (all seven pairs, every dark half prefixed dark:), and
// unknown tones must fall back to Neutral.
func TestToneTableExhaustive(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, tn := range tone.Tones() {
		if !tone.ToneIsValid(tn) {
			t.Errorf("%s: ToneIsValid false for a member of Tones()", tn)
		}

		s := tone.For(tn)

		pairs := map[string]tone.Pair{
			"Dot": s.Dot, "Text": s.Text, "TextSoft": s.TextSoft,
			"Border": s.Border, "BGTint": s.BGTint, "BGSolid": s.BGSolid, "Icon": s.Icon,
		}

		for name, p := range pairs {
			if !p.Complete() {
				t.Errorf("tone %s: surface %s is incomplete (Light=%q Dark=%q)", tn, name, p.Light, p.Dark)

				continue
			}

			if !strings.HasPrefix(p.Dark, "dark:") {
				t.Errorf(
					"tone %s: surface %s dark half %q lacks the dark: prefix (scanner-safety contract)",
					tn,
					name,
					p.Dark,
				)
			}

			if got := p.Classes(); got != p.Light+" "+p.Dark {
				t.Errorf("tone %s: surface %s Classes() = %q, want %q", tn, name, got, p.Light+" "+p.Dark)
			}
		}
	}

	if got := tone.For(tone.Tone("bogus")); got != tone.For(tone.ToneNeutral) {
		t.Error("For(unknown) does not fall back to Neutral")
	}
}

// TestAccentRowUsesAccentFamily pins the ADR-0049 emission: the Accent
// tone renders the accent TOKEN family, not the blue palette — the family
// swap is the whole point of ADR-0044 Phase 2 (blue stays reserved for
// the semantic info tone).
func TestAccentRowUsesAccentFamily(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	s := tone.For(tone.ToneAccent)

	pairs := map[string]tone.Pair{
		"Dot": s.Dot, "Text": s.Text, "TextSoft": s.TextSoft,
		"Border": s.Border, "BGTint": s.BGTint, "BGSolid": s.BGSolid, "Icon": s.Icon,
	}

	for name, p := range pairs {
		if !strings.Contains(p.Light, "accent-") || !strings.Contains(p.Dark, "accent-") {
			t.Errorf(
				"tone accent: surface %s = %q / %q, want accent- family literals",
				name, p.Light, p.Dark,
			)
		}

		if strings.Contains(p.Light, "blue-") || strings.Contains(p.Dark, "blue-") {
			t.Errorf(
				"tone accent: surface %s still carries blue- pigments (%q / %q)",
				name, p.Light, p.Dark,
			)
		}
	}
}

// TestHueTableExhaustive: every Hue in Hues() must carry a complete
// Utilities entry, and unknown hues must fall back to Gray.
func TestHueTableExhaustive(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, h := range tone.Hues() {
		if !tone.HueIsValid(h) {
			t.Errorf("%s: HueIsValid false for a member of Hues()", h)
		}

		u := tone.UtilitiesFor(h)

		pairs := map[string]tone.Pair{
			"Text": u.Text, "TextMuted": u.TextMuted, "TextStrong": u.TextStrong, "TextOnTint": u.TextOnTint,
			"BGSolid": u.BGSolid, "BGSolidStrong": u.BGSolidStrong,
			"BGTint": u.BGTint, "Border": u.Border,
		}

		for name, p := range pairs {
			if !p.Complete() {
				t.Errorf("hue %s: utility %s is incomplete (Light=%q Dark=%q)", h, name, p.Light, p.Dark)

				continue
			}

			if !strings.HasPrefix(p.Dark, "dark:") {
				t.Errorf("hue %s: utility %s dark half %q lacks the dark: prefix", h, name, p.Dark)
			}
		}
	}

	if got := tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.Hue("bogus")); got != tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGray) {
		t.Error("UtilitiesFor(unknown) does not fall back to Gray")
	}
}

// TestHueUtilityAnchors pins the cells that components render today,
// byte-for-byte, so the grammar cannot drift from shipped pixels. Anchors:
// chart series text + segment bars (chart_geometry/segment_bar), status and
// kanban dots (status_dot/kanban), feedback alert surfaces (styles.go),
// stat tiles (card.templ), trend arrows (card.templ), log tags
// (scrollback.templ).
func TestHueUtilityAnchors(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	anchors := []struct {
		name string
		got  string
		want string
	}{
		{"chart blue text", tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueBlue).Text.Classes(), "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400"},
		{"chart rose text", tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueRose).Text.Classes(), "text-rose-600 dark:text-rose-400"},
		{
			"segment violet fill",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueViolet).BGSolidStrong.Classes(),
			"bg-violet-600 dark:bg-violet-400",
		},
		{"status dot success", tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGreen).BGSolid.Classes(), "bg-green-500 dark:bg-green-400"},
		{
			"status dot warning (amber dialect)",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueAmber).BGSolid.Classes(),
			"bg-amber-500 dark:bg-amber-400",
		},
		{
			"status dot neutral (gray exception)",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGray).BGSolid.Classes(),
			"bg-gray-400 dark:bg-gray-500",
		},
		{"kanban purple dot", tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HuePurple).BGSolid.Classes(), "bg-purple-500 dark:bg-purple-400"},
		{
			"trend up (green strong)",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGreen).TextStrong.Classes(),
			"text-green-700 dark:text-green-400",
		},
		{
			"trend warn (amber strong)",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueAmber).TextStrong.Classes(),
			"text-amber-700 dark:text-amber-400",
		},
		{
			"stat tile purple tint",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HuePurple).BGTint.Classes(),
			"bg-purple-50 dark:bg-purple-900/30",
		},
		{
			"feedback success border",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGreen).Border.Classes(),
			"border-green-200 dark:border-green-800",
		},
		{"scrollback info tag", tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueBlue).Text.Classes(), "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400"},
		{
			"scrollback neutral tag (muted convention)",
			tone.UtilitiesFor(tone.HueGray).TextMuted.Classes(),
			"text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400",
		},
	}

	for _, a := range anchors {
		if a.got != a.want {
			t.Errorf("%s = %q, want %q", a.name, a.got, a.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestChartHuesOrder pins the canonical series cycle shared by line, pie,
// and segment charts (chart_geometry.go order).
func TestChartHuesOrder(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	want := []tone.Hue{
		tone.HueBlue, tone.HueEmerald, tone.HueAmber, tone.HueRose,
		tone.HueViolet, tone.HueCyan, tone.HueOrange, tone.HuePink,
	}

	got := tone.ChartHues()
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("ChartHues() has %d entries, want %d", len(got), len(want))
	}

	for i := range want {
		if got[i] != want[i] {
			t.Errorf("ChartHues()[%d] = %s, want %s", i, got[i], want[i])
		}
	}
}

// TestPairIncompleteAndJoin exercises the Pair edges: empty halves join
// without dangling spaces, Complete reports honestly.
func TestPairIncompleteAndJoin(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	lightOnly := tone.Pair{Light: "text-gray-500"}
	if lightOnly.Complete() {
		t.Error("light-only Pair reports Complete")
	}

	if got := lightOnly.Classes(); got != "text-gray-500" {
		t.Errorf("light-only Classes() = %q, want %q", got, "text-gray-500")
	}

	empty := tone.Pair{}
	if got := empty.Classes(); got != "" {
		t.Errorf("empty Pair Classes() = %q, want empty", got)
	}
}

// TestValidityRejectsUnknownValues pins the closed-set contract: values that
// are not part of the enum must be reported invalid (consumers gate lookups
// and v2 migrations on these).
func TestValidityRejectsUnknownValues(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	if tone.HueIsValid(tone.Hue("not-a-hue")) {
		t.Error(`HueIsValid("not-a-hue") = true, want false`)
	}

	if tone.ToneIsValid(tone.Tone("not-a-tone")) {
		t.Error(`ToneIsValid("not-a-tone") = true, want false`)
	}

	if tone.SurfaceTokenIsValid(tone.SurfaceToken("not-a-surface")) {
		t.Error(`SurfaceTokenIsValid("not-a-surface") = true, want false`)
	}

	if tone.InkTokenIsValid(tone.InkToken("not-an-ink")) {
		t.Error(`InkTokenIsValid("not-an-ink") = true, want false`)
	}
}
package utils

import (
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	twmerge "github.com/Oudwins/tailwind-merge-go"
	"github.com/a-h/templ"
)

// BaseProps provides common configurable attributes for all components.
type BaseProps struct {
	ID        string
	Class     string
	Attrs     templ.Attributes
	AriaLabel string
	Nonce     string
}

// ComponentProps is the interface implemented by all component props structs
// that embed BaseProps. It enables generic component composition, validation,
// and wrapper functions across the entire component library.
type ComponentProps interface {
	GetBaseProps() BaseProps
	SetBaseProps(props BaseProps)
}

// GetBaseProps returns the embedded BaseProps. This method is promoted to all
// structs that embed BaseProps, satisfying the ComponentProps interface.
func (p *BaseProps) GetBaseProps() BaseProps {
	return *p
}

// SetBaseProps updates the embedded BaseProps. This method is promoted to all
// structs that embed BaseProps, satisfying the ComponentProps interface.
func (p *BaseProps) SetBaseProps(bp BaseProps) {
	*p = bp
}

//nolint:gochecknoglobals // Package-level merge cache + mutex for thread safety
var classMu sync.Mutex

// Class merges Tailwind classes intelligently using tailwind-merge-go.
// Conflicting classes are resolved with later arguments overriding earlier ones.
// Thread-safe via sync.Mutex to protect the shared LRU cache.
func Class(classes ...string) string {
	classMu.Lock()
	defer classMu.Unlock()

	merged := twmerge.Merge(classes...)
	parts := strings.Fields(merged)
	sort.Strings(parts)

	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
}

// CurrentYear returns the current year as a string.
func CurrentYear() string {
	return time.Now().Format("2006")
}

// Ternary returns a if condition is true, otherwise b.
// Note: both a and b are eagerly evaluated (this is a function, not a macro),
// so callers passing function calls or side-effecting expressions should use
// inline if/else in templ instead: { if cond }...{ else }...{ end }.
func Ternary[T any](condition bool, a, b T) T {
	if condition {
		return a
	}

	return b
}

// Coalesce returns the first argument that is not the zero value for its
// type, or the zero value when every argument is zero. It is the generic
// form of the library's override-or-default idiom, the
// `Ternary(x != "", x, fallback)` shape, and reads in precedence order:
// Coalesce(props.AriaLabel, props.Label, "Commands").
//
// Note: like Ternary, all arguments are eagerly evaluated.
func Coalesce[T comparable](values ...T) T {
	var zero T

	for _, v := range values {
		if v != zero {
			return v
		}
	}

	return zero
}

// Lookup returns the map value for key, or fallback if not found.
// Replaces the repetitive if-ok-return pattern used across all enum lookups.
func Lookup[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, key K, fallback V) V {
	if v, ok := m[key]; ok {
		return v
	}

	return fallback
}

// DismissScript returns shared JavaScript for dismissing elements via [data-dismiss]
// click delegation. Used by Alert, Toast, and ErrorAlert components.
// Handles both role="alert" (Alert) and role="status" (Toast) containers.
func DismissScript() string {
	return `if(!window.tcDismissAttached){window.tcDismissAttached=true;document.addEventListener('click',function(e){var btn=e.target.closest('[data-dismiss]');if(btn){var el=btn.closest('[role="alert"],[role="status"]');if(el)el.remove();}});}`
}

const (
	textYes = "yes"
)

func TestCurrentYear(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	got := CurrentYear()

	want := time.Now().Format("2006")
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("CurrentYear() = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestTernary(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		condition bool
		a, b      string
		want      string
	}{
		{name: "true returns a", condition: true, a: textYes, b: "no", want: textYes},
		{name: "false returns b", condition: false, a: "yes", b: "no", want: "no"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := Ternary(tt.condition, tt.a, tt.b)
			if got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("Ternary() = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCoalesce(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("strings: first non-empty wins", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce("", "override", "fallback")
		if got != "override" {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want %q", got, "override")
		}
	})

	t.Run("strings: all empty returns zero", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce("", "", "")
		if got != "" {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want empty", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("strings: single value passthrough", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce("only")
		if got != "only" {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want %q", got, "only")
		}
	})

	t.Run("typed enum: zero value skipped", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce(testEnumA, testEnumB)
		if got != testEnumA {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want %q", got, testEnumA)
		}
	})

	t.Run("typed enum: empty falls through to default", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce(testEnum(""), testEnumB)
		if got != testEnumB {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want %q", got, testEnumB)
		}
	})

	t.Run("ints: zero skipped", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce(0, 0, 7)
		if got != 7 {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %d, want 7", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("no arguments returns zero", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		got := Coalesce[string]()
		if got != "" {
			t.Errorf("Coalesce() = %q, want empty", got)
		}
	})
}

func TestClass(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name           string
		classes        []string
		wantContain    []string
		wantNotContain []string
	}{
		{
			name:           "single string",
			classes:        []string{"a b c"},
			wantContain:    []string{"a", "b", "c"},
			wantNotContain: nil,
		},
		{
			name:           "tailwind merge",
			classes:        []string{"bg-red-500 hover:bg-blue-500", "bg-green-500"},
			wantContain:    []string{"bg-green-500", "hover:bg-blue-500"},
			wantNotContain: []string{"bg-red-500"},
		},
		{
			name:           "empty ignored",
			classes:        []string{"a b", ""},
			wantContain:    []string{"a", "b"},
			wantNotContain: nil,
		},
		{
			name:           "multiple overrides",
			classes:        []string{"p-4", "p-6", "px-8"},
			wantContain:    []string{"p-6", "px-8"},
			wantNotContain: []string{"p-4"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := Class(tt.classes...)
			for _, want := range tt.wantContain {
				if !containsWord(got, want) {
					t.Errorf("Class(%v) = %q, want to contain %q", tt.classes, got, want)
				}
			}

			for _, notWant := range tt.wantNotContain {
				if containsWord(got, notWant) {
					t.Errorf("Class(%v) = %q, should not contain %q", tt.classes, got, notWant)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func containsWord(s, word string) bool {
	return slices.Contains(strings.Fields(s), word)
}

type testEnum string

const (
	testEnumA testEnum = "a"
	testEnumB testEnum = "b"
	testEnumC testEnum = "c"
)

func TestLookup(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	t.Run("string-keyed map with struct value", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		type style struct{ Class string }

		m := map[string]style{"a": {"bold"}, "b": {"italic"}}

		got := Lookup(m, "a", style{"fallback"})
		if got.Class != "bold" {
			t.Errorf("Lookup() = %+v, want bold", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("typed-key map with string value", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		m := map[testEnum]string{testEnumA: "found"}

		got := Lookup(m, testEnumA, "fallback")
		if got != "found" {
			t.Errorf("Lookup() = %q, want %q", got, "found")
		}
	})

	t.Run("missing key returns fallback", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		m := map[string]int{"a": 1}

		got := Lookup(m, "z", 99)
		if got != 99 {
			t.Errorf("Lookup() = %d, want 99", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("empty map returns fallback", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Parallel()

		m := map[string]string{}

		got := Lookup(m, "anything", "default")
		if got != "default" {
			t.Errorf("Lookup() = %q, want %q", got, "default")
		}
	})
}
